summary: Paperwork plan for permanent residence through Express Entry, from profile to landing.
conditions: You're applying for permanent residence through Express Entry
You qualify for one of its programs: Canadian Experience Class, Federal Skilled Worker or Federal Skilled Trades
A provincial nomination through an Express Entry stream is optional
You plan to live outside Quebec

steps.title: Check program eligibility and the CRS score
prepare: Pick the likely program: Federal Skilled Worker, Skilled Trades, or Canadian Experience Class
Estimate the Comprehensive Ranking System score
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC publishes who can apply for each Express Entry program and the CRS criteria.
2. Profiles in the pool are ranked by CRS score.
3. Job offer points were removed from the CRS as of March 25, 2025.
4. The route steps below each apply to one program; the others can be marked "Not for me".

steps.title: Confirm the Canadian Experience Class route
prepare: Dates, hours and NOC code of each Canadian job
Language level: CLB 7 for TEER 0 or 1 jobs, CLB 5 for TEER 2 or 3 jobs
conditions: Only if you have at least 1 year of skilled paid work in Canada in the last 3 years
steps.howTo:
1. The work is at least 1 year full time, or 1,560 hours in total, in the 3 years before applying, in TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3 occupations.
2. It is paid work done in Canada while authorized under temporary resident status.
3. Self-employment and work while studying full time do not count.
4. There is no education requirement and no proof of funds; an ECA only adds CRS points for education from outside Canada.

steps.title: Confirm the Federal Skilled Worker route
prepare: Dates, hours and NOC code of each job in the last 10 years
Language level: CLB 7 in all 4 abilities
conditions: Only if you have 1 year of continuous skilled work, in or outside Canada, in the last 10 years
steps.howTo:
1. The work is 1 year of continuous paid work, or 1,560 hours in total, in one TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3 occupation in the last 10 years.
2. The selection grid needs 67 points or more, separate from the CRS score.
3. Education from outside Canada needs an ECA.
4. Proof of funds is needed unless already authorized to work in Canada with a valid job offer.

steps.title: Confirm the Federal Skilled Trades route
documents: Certificate of qualification or job offer
prepare: Dates and hours of skilled trade work in the last 5 years
A Canadian certificate of qualification, or a full-time job offer of at least 1 year
Language level: CLB 5 speaking and listening, CLB 4 reading and writing
conditions: Only if you have 2 years of skilled trade work in the last 5 years
steps.howTo:
1. The work is at least 2 years full time, or 3,120 hours in total, in a skilled trade in the 5 years before applying.
2. It needs a valid job offer or a certificate of qualification from a Canadian provincial, territorial or federal authority.
3. There is no education requirement; an ECA only adds CRS points.
4. Proof of funds is needed unless already authorized to work in Canada with a valid job offer.

steps.title: Check passport validity
prepare: Renew if it expires during the likely processing period
steps.howTo:
1. Passport details are entered in the profile and again in the application.
2. The COPR details are usually expected to match the passport.

steps.title: Book and sit an approved language test
prepare: Pick an approved test: CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training, PTE Core, TEF Canada or TCF Canada
steps.howTo:
1. Results are accepted if less than 2 years old, both when the profile is completed and when the application is submitted.
2. If results expire before an invitation, a retest is usually needed.
3. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted for Express Entry.

steps.title: Get an Educational Credential Assessment
conditions: Only if you have education from outside Canada and apply as a Federal Skilled Worker, or want CRS points for it in another program
prepare: Pick a designated organization, such as WES, ICAS, IQAS, CES or ICES
Check whether a professional body assesses the occupation instead
steps.howTo:
1. The assessment is done by an IRCC-designated organization, not by IRCC.
2. An ECA counts if less than 5 years old when the profile is completed and when the application is submitted.
3. Processing times vary by organization.

steps.title: Collect employment reference letters
prepare: Reference letters on letterhead with duties, hours and dates
Translations for documents not in English or French
steps.howTo:
1. Work experience details are entered in the profile and evidenced in the application.
2. Claims are usually expected to match what the letters show.

steps.title: Get proof-of-funds letters from the bank
conditions: Only for the Federal Skilled Worker or Federal Skilled Trades routes, unless you are authorized to work in Canada and have a valid job offer
prepare: Official letter on bank letterhead for each account
Account numbers, opening dates, current and 6-month average balances
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Experience Class does not need proof of funds.
2. Funds are usually expected to be available both at application and when the visa is issued.
3. Borrowed money and equity in property are not counted.

steps.title: Submit the Express Entry profile
steps.howTo:
1. The profile is completed in the IRCC secure account; a started profile is kept for 60 days before it has to be restarted.
2. A profile not invited within 12 months expires automatically.
3. The expiry date is shown in the account.

steps.title: Get a provincial nomination through an Express Entry stream
prepare: Check the province's Express Entry streams
conditions: Only if you apply to a province or territory for a nomination
steps.howTo:
1. A nomination accepted in the Express Entry profile adds 600 CRS points.
2. The province runs its own application first; its steps are in the "Provincial nomination · British Columbia" and "Provincial nomination · Ontario" plans.
3. The nomination is accepted in the Express Entry profile in the IRCC account.
4. Dates here are rough placeholders.

steps.title: Receive an invitation to apply (ITA)
steps.howTo:
1. Invitations are issued in rounds; timing is not predictable.
2. Besides general and program rounds, IRCC holds category-based rounds for candidates in categories set by the Minister, such as French-language proficiency or certain occupations; the list changes over time.
3. An invitation is valid for 60 days.
4. If it lapses without an application or a decline, the profile is removed from the pool.
5. Move this step's date to the real invitation date once it arrives.

steps.title: Gather identity and civil documents
prepare: Documents for every family member included
steps.howTo:
1. The application lists the documents it expects once the form is filled in.
2. Documents are usually uploaded as scans.

steps.title: Check which Chinese documents need an apostille
prepare: List the Chinese birth, marriage, degree and other documents going to Canadian offices
Check what each office asks for: IRCC, the credential assessor, a regulator
steps.howTo:
1. China joined the Apostille Convention in November 2023 and it entered into force for Canada on January 11, 2024.
2. Between the two, a Chinese public document that needs authenticating gets an apostille from China's foreign affairs authorities instead of consular legalisation at a Canadian mission.
3. IRCC applications are usually uploaded as scans with translations; an apostille matters where a receiving office asks for authenticated documents, so check each office's list.
conditions: Only if some of your documents were issued in mainland China

steps.title: Order police certificates
prepare: List countries stayed in 6 months in a row or longer in the last 10 years, since age 18
China: national ID card and household register (户口簿) for the Certificate of No Criminal Record (无犯罪记录证明)
steps.howTo:
1. The certificate for the current country of residence counts if issued within 6 months before the application is submitted.
2. Others count if issued after the last stay of 6 months or more there.
3. Colour scans of the originals are uploaded.
4. If one is late, a written explanation with proof of the request is usually attached instead.
5. China: IRCC takes a Certificate of No Criminal Record (无犯罪记录证明), or a notification that one cannot be issued, covering from birth to the present, ideally with a QR code. In China it comes from the Public Security Bureau or police station where the hukou is registered or where you usually live, or through local government apps; from outside China, the hukou office explains how to apply online, by mail or in person.

steps.title: Get the upfront medical exam
steps.howTo:
1. The exam is done by a panel physician, as close as possible to the application date.
2. The physician gives an information sheet or IMM 1017B form to attach.
3. Results are valid for 12 months; a new exam may be needed if landing comes later.

steps.title: Submit the permanent residence application (eAPR)
steps.howTo:
1. The application is submitted online within 60 days of the invitation.
2. Processing fees and biometrics fees are paid at submission.

steps.title: Give biometrics
steps.howTo:
1. Applicants aged 14 to 79 usually give fingerprints and a photo.
2. There are 30 days from the date on the letter to give them.

steps.title: Watch for the decision and pay the right of permanent residence fee
steps.howTo:
1. The decision covers eligibility, medical exam, police certificates and background checks.
2. The right of permanent residence fee is paid before approval is finalized.
3. Dates here are rough placeholders.

steps.title: Land as a permanent resident (COPR)
prepare: Check COPR details against the passport
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC sends the COPR, and a permanent resident visa if the passport needs one.
2. A COPR cannot be extended; travel to Canada happens before its expiry date.
3. The COPR is shown to border services on arrival, or used for government services if already in Canada.
4. Adding a "Became a permanent resident" date with the landing date starts the Citizenship · CA plan.

title: On a work or study permit · Canada
summary: Paperwork plan for living on a Canadian work or study permit once it is granted: its conditions, SIN and health records, family permits, the renewal before expiry, and the route to permanent residence.
conditions: You hold a Canadian work or study permit, new or extended
The date is the day the permit was issued; arrival steps are in the relocation plans
Health steps describe British Columbia and Ontario; other provinces have their own

steps.title: Read the conditions printed on the permit
prepare: Name, dates and conditions on the permit
Offer letter or school letter, to compare
steps.howTo:
1. An employer-specific permit names the employer and often the job and location; working elsewhere needs a new permit or a change of conditions first.
2. An open permit covers most employers, with any exceptions printed on it.
3. A study permit sets the school level and whether off-campus work is allowed; the weekly limit on off-campus hours during school terms changes, so check current.
4. Mistakes on the permit are fixed through IRCC's correction process.

steps.title: Update the SIN expiry with Service Canada
conditions: Only if you already have a SIN starting with 9 from an earlier permit
steps.howTo:
1. A SIN starting with 9 expires with the permit it was issued on.
2. After a new permit, Service Canada updates the expiry online, in person or by mail.
3. The employer can ask to see the new date for payroll.

steps.title: Send the new permit to the provincial health plan
documents: Health card or BC Services Card
conditions: Only if you already have provincial health coverage tied to an earlier permit
steps.howTo:
1. British Columbia: MSP coverage for permit holders is set to end with the permit; sending the new permit to Health Insurance BC extends it.
2. Ontario: a health card for a permit holder expires with the permit; renewing it at ServiceOntario with the new permit keeps OHIP going.
3. A gap between permits can leave a gap in coverage; private insurance can fill it.

steps.title: Check permits for a spouse and children
prepare: Your job's TEER level and permit length
conditions: Only if a spouse, partner or children live with you in Canada or plan to
steps.howTo:
1. Spouses of some workers and students can get an open work permit; since 2025 IRCC limits this by occupation, program and time left on the permit, so check current.
2. Minor children of work or study permit holders can often attend preschool, primary or secondary school without a study permit; post-secondary study needs one.
3. Family permits usually expire with the principal applicant's, so renewals line up.
4. Not immigration advice; the IRCC pages decide eligibility.

steps.title: Get a new permit before changing employer
documents: LMIA or offer of employment number
conditions: Only if you hold an employer-specific permit and plan to change job
steps.howTo:
1. An employer-specific permit covers only the named employer; a new job usually needs a new permit, often with a new LMIA or an employer compliance offer number.
2. Some workers in Canada can start the new job while the application is processed; IRCC lists who qualifies, so check current.
3. The date here is a placeholder; move it to before the planned change.

steps.title: Look at the route to the next permit or permanent residence
prepare: Months of skilled work in Canada
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Experience Class counts 1 year of skilled paid work in Canada in the last 3 years; see the "Skilled migration · CA" plan.
2. Provincial nominee programs have streams for workers and graduates; see the provincial nomination plans for British Columbia and Ontario.
3. Graduates may qualify for a post-graduation work permit; see the graduation plan.
4. Not immigration advice; check the IRCC and provincial pages.

steps.title: Start gathering papers for the permit renewal
prepare: Updated job offer, LMIA or school enrolment letter
conditions: Only if you plan to stay past the permit expiry date
steps.howTo:
1. About 90 days before expiry leaves time for new letters, an LMIA if needed, and passport renewal.
2. A permit cannot run past the passport's expiry, so an expiring passport shortens it.
3. This date assumes a 1-year permit; move it to about 90 days before the printed expiry.

steps.title: Apply to extend the permit before it expires
conditions: Only if you plan to stay past the permit expiry date
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC suggests applying at least 30 days before the permit expires.
2. Applying before it expires gives maintained status: work or study can continue under the same conditions until a decision.
3. Leaving Canada while waiting can end maintained status, so check the IRCC page before travelling.
4. This date assumes a 1-year permit; move it to 30 or more days before the printed expiry. Renewals repeat for each permit.

steps.title: Pass the new permit to Service Canada, the health plan and the employer
conditions: Only once a new permit is issued
steps.howTo:
1. Service Canada updates the SIN expiry; Health Insurance BC or ServiceOntario updates health coverage; payroll or the school updates its records.
2. A new permit restarts this plan from its issue date.

title: Life as a permanent resident · Canada
summary: Paperwork plan for the years after landing as a permanent resident: the PR card, SIN and health records, benefits that open up, family sponsorship, the residency obligation and the card renewal.
conditions: You became a permanent resident of Canada, at a port of entry or from inside Canada
Health and benefit steps describe British Columbia and Ontario; other provinces have their own
Some steps apply only to people who held a permit before, or have family abroad

steps.title: Give IRCC a Canadian mailing address and photo for the PR card
prepare: PR card photo to IRCC specifications
Permanent Residence Portal sign-in, if landing from inside Canada
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC sends the first PR card automatically when it has a Canadian mailing address and photo within 180 days of becoming a permanent resident; the first card is then free.
2. At a port of entry, the officer usually takes the address; landing from inside Canada, the portal asks for it.
3. An address change before the card arrives goes to IRCC through its web form.

steps.title: Update the Social Insurance Number record with Service Canada
conditions: Only if your SIN starts with 9 (issued while on a permit)
steps.howTo:
1. A SIN starting with 9 is for temporary residents and expires with the permit; permanent residents hold a SIN that does not expire.
2. Service Canada updates the record online, in person or by mail with the COPR; check whether a new number is issued.
3. Applying and updating are free.

steps.title: Give the updated SIN to the employer
conditions: Only if your SIN starts with 9 and you are employed
steps.howTo:
1. Payroll uses the SIN and its expiry for the T4 and the Record of Employment.
2. The employer no longer needs a work permit on file once PR status is shown.

steps.title: Update health coverage to permanent resident status
documents: Health card or BC Services Card
conditions: Only if your provincial health coverage was tied to a permit, or you have none yet
steps.howTo:
1. British Columbia: send the COPR to Health Insurance BC so MSP coverage is no longer set to end with a permit; newcomers without MSP apply, and coverage usually starts after a waiting period of up to 3 months.
2. Ontario: take the COPR and two other documents to ServiceOntario for a health card tied to PR status; there is no waiting period for OHIP.
3. Other provinces have their own health plans.

steps.title: Tell the CRA about the new immigration status
prepare: Form RC66 if applying for child benefits for the first time
conditions: Only if you or your spouse get, or could get, the Canada Child Benefit or other CRA benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Canada Child Benefit eligibility depends partly on immigration status; the CRA can ask for proof of it.
2. Status can be updated in CRA My Account or on form RC66SCH.
3. Provincial child benefits (BC Family Benefit, Ontario Child Benefit) are paid through the same CCB account.

steps.title: Re-check benefits, tuition and student aid that PR status opens
prepare: School or college registration, if studying
steps.howTo:
1. Permanent residents usually pay domestic tuition rather than international fees; the school sets when the change takes effect.
2. Federal and provincial student aid (StudentAid BC, OSAP) open to permanent residents.
3. The Canadian Dental Care Plan covers residents without private dental insurance and with adjusted family net income under $90,000, once tax returns are filed.
4. British Columbia: Healthy Kids and Fair PharmaCare rely on MSP and income; Ontario: OHIP+ covers many drugs for those under 25 without a private plan.
5. Rules change; check the current pages.

steps.title: Look into sponsoring family members
prepare: Income for the last years, for parents and grandparents
conditions: Only if a spouse, partner, dependent child, parent or grandparent lives outside Canada or without status
steps.howTo:
1. Permanent residents living in Canada can sponsor a spouse, common-law or conjugal partner, and dependent children.
2. Parents and grandparents go through the Parents and Grandparents Program, which opens only to people invited from an interest-to-sponsor pool, with a minimum income over several tax years; the super visa is the alternative for long visits.
3. Sponsors sign an undertaking to support the person for a set number of years.
4. Not immigration advice; the IRCC pages decide eligibility.

steps.title: Apply for a PR travel document before returning without a card
conditions: Only if you are outside Canada, or leaving, without a valid PR card
steps.howTo:
1. Airlines and other commercial carriers ask for a valid PR card or a PRTD before boarding for Canada.
2. The PRTD is applied for from outside Canada; IRCC checks the residency obligation when deciding.
3. By land in a private vehicle, a PR can present other proof of status at the border.
4. The date here is a placeholder; move it to before the trip.

steps.title: Check the 730-day residency obligation
prepare: Travel history: entry and exit dates
Passport stamps or a CBSA travel history request
steps.howTo:
1. Permanent residents stay in Canada at least 730 days in any 5-year period; the days need not be in a row.
2. Some days abroad count, for example accompanying a Canadian citizen spouse, or working abroad full-time for a Canadian business; IRCC has a tool to check.
3. An expired PR card does not end PR status; status ends only by a formal decision, renunciation, a removal order or becoming a citizen.
4. This check repeats before any long stay abroad.

steps.title: Renew the PR card
prepare: Travel history for the last 5 years
conditions: Only if you are not yet a Canadian citizen
steps.howTo:
1. PR cards are usually valid for 5 years; the expiry is printed on the card.
2. IRCC takes renewals when the card expires in less than 9 months, or has expired.
3. Apply through the online portal; processing times are listed on the IRCC page.
4. This date assumes a 5-year card from landing; move it to 9 months before the printed expiry. Renewals repeat every card term.

steps.title: Follow up if the first PR card has not arrived
conditions: Only if the first PR card has not arrived
steps.howTo:
1. Without an address and photo sent within 180 days of landing, the first card goes through a regular application on form IMM 5444 in the Permanent Residence Portal.
2. IRCC's card processing times and web form are the ways to follow up.

title: Citizenship · CA
summary: Paperwork plan for citizenship by grant as an adult permanent resident, from the day of becoming a permanent resident to the oath.
conditions: You became a permanent resident and are applying as an adult
1,095 days physically in Canada in the 5 years before you apply; days there before permanent residence count as half, up to 365
Taxes filed for 3 of those 5 years, if you had to file

steps.title: Start a log of days spent outside Canada
prepare: Keep boarding passes or passport stamps
Save the Confirmation of Permanent Residence
steps.howTo:
1. Days in Canada as a permanent resident count in full; days outside Canada do not count.
2. IRCC offers an optional travel journal for trips outside Canada; it is not sent with the application.

steps.title: Work out the earliest date with the IRCC physical presence calculator
prepare: Dates as a temporary resident or protected person before that
steps.howTo:
1. The requirement is at least 1,095 days physically in Canada in the 5 years right before applying.
2. Each day in Canada as a temporary resident or protected person in those 5 years, before becoming a permanent resident, counts as half a day, up to 365 days of credit.
3. So with 730 or more such days, the earliest date can be up to a year sooner than 1,095 days after landing; with none, it is 1,095 days as a permanent resident.
4. The calculator (in the IRCC online account, or the standalone one for paper applications) does the counting; move the application date to the date it shows.
5. Absences change the result, so the calculation is run again at application time; an application without it is returned.

steps.title: Check tax returns are filed for 3 of the last 5 years
steps.howTo: 1. Filing Canadian income taxes for at least 3 of the 5 years before applying is part of the requirement, if the applicant had to file.

steps.title: Gather language proof (ages 18 to 54)
prepare: A diploma, transcript or certificate from study in English or French
steps.howTo:
1. Skip if under 18 or 55 and over.
2. The level is CLB 4 or higher in speaking and listening, in English or French.

steps.title: Gather passports, ID and photos
prepare: Colour copies of identity pages of every passport held during the 5 years
steps.howTo:
1. The document checklist (CIT 0007) lists what the application includes.
2. A police certificate may be needed for any country where 183 days or more in a row were spent in the 4 years before applying.

steps.title: Apply for citizenship online
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC encourages online applications; paper is for specific cases.
2. Fees include a processing fee and a right of citizenship fee.
3. This date is an estimate: 1,095 days as a permanent resident plus a short buffer, with no absences and no credit for earlier time in Canada; move it to the date the calculator shows.
4. The physical presence calculation is included with the application.

steps.title: Include children under 18 in the application
prepare: Proof you are the parent or legal guardian
Each child's identity documents and photos
steps.howTo:
1. A parent or legal guardian applies for a child under 18; when a parent is a citizen or applying at the same time, the child can be added to the parent's application.
2. A minor applying without a Canadian parent needs 1,095 days of physical presence, like an adult.
3. The minor application form number (CIT 0003 for paper) and the fees are on the IRCC forms page; check current.
4. Children do not take the test.
conditions: Only if you have children under 18 who are permanent residents

steps.title: Watch for the acknowledgement of receipt
prepare: Check the IRCC account and email
steps.howTo:
1. An online application gets an email confirmation straight away.
2. The acknowledgement of receipt follows once processing starts.
3. Dates here are rough placeholders.

steps.title: Study Discover Canada for the test
prepare: Practice questions on the IRCC site
steps.howTo:
1. Questions cover rights and responsibilities, history, geography and government, from the official study guide Discover Canada.
2. Applicants aged 18 to 54 usually take the test.

steps.title: Take the online citizenship test
prepare: Quiet room and a working device
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC sends an invitation with the test window.
2. The test is online: 20 questions in 45 minutes, and 15 correct answers pass.
3. Move this date to the invitation date once known.

steps.title: Watch for the application decision
prepare: Check the IRCC account and email
steps.howTo:
1. An interview or hearing may follow, depending on the test result.
2. Dates here are rough placeholders.

steps.title: Take the oath at the citizenship ceremony
prepare: Check whether it is virtual or in person
steps.howTo:
1. Adults approved for citizenship take the oath; citizenship takes effect once it is taken.
2. The PR card is collected at the ceremony.
3. An electronic certificate is usually in the IRCC portal within 5 business days of the signed oath form; paper certificates come at in-person ceremonies or by mail.

steps.title: Hand in the PR card and update the SIN record
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC says the PR card is destroyed or collected at the ceremony; if it is still in hand, check IRCC's current instructions for it.
2. The PR card is no longer a travel document once the oath is taken.
3. Service Canada lists a change of immigration status as a reason to update the SIN record; the citizenship certificate is the proof.

steps.title: Settle Chinese passport, hukou and visa after naturalising
prepare: Family member who can visit the hukou police station
Plans for the next trip to China
steps.howTo:
1. China's Nationality Law (中华人民共和国国籍法), Article 9: a Chinese national settled abroad who takes a foreign nationality of their own free will loses Chinese nationality automatically; China does not recognise dual nationality (Article 3).
2. The Chinese passport is no longer used to travel after the oath; trips to China then use the Canadian passport with a Chinese visa (签证), or a visa-free arrangement if one covers Canadian passports; check current.
3. The hukou (户口) is cancelled (户口注销) at the local police station where it is registered; the local requirements and who can apply on your behalf vary, so check current.
4. Bank accounts, property and pensions in China tied to the ID card number may need updating; ask each institution.
conditions: Only if you held Chinese nationality

steps.title: Register to vote with Elections Canada
steps.howTo:
1. Federal voter registration is with Elections Canada.
2. Provincial and local elections have their own lists.

steps.title: Apply for a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. The citizenship certificate comes first; it is not a travel document.
2. Adult passports come with 5- or 10-year validity; this step assumes 10.

Tenancy deposits and fees — Province of British Columbia
Moving from outside Canada — ICBC
Canadian Experience Class — Canada.ca
Immigrate to B.C. as a worker — WelcomeBC

steps.title: Pick the permit route
prepare: Study permit: a program at a designated learning institution (DLI) in B.C.
Employer-specific work permit: a job offer, with or without an LMIA
Open work permit: only in certain situations, such as the IEC Working Holiday category
Check the passport stays valid for the whole stay
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC lists the permit types: an employer-specific work permit needs a job offer, and the employer may need a labour market impact assessment (LMIA).
2. An open work permit needs no job offer, but is only available in certain situations.
3. A study permit needs a letter of acceptance from a DLI.
4. The 10 months before arrival here is a planning estimate; check current IRCC processing times.

steps.title: Get proof of funds
prepare: Bank letters or statements in your name
Check the current amount IRCC lists for your permit type
Translations for documents not in English or French
steps.howTo:
1. Study permit applications include proof of financial support; IRCC updates the amount, so check it on the study permit documents page.
2. Proof of funds is also carried at the port of entry.
3. Keep copies with the other travel documents.

steps.title: Get the letter of acceptance and the Provincial Attestation Letter
prepare: Accept the offer from the DLI
Pay the tuition deposit the school asks for
Ask the school for the PAL
steps.howTo:
1. A letter of acceptance from a DLI is always needed for a study permit.
2. A provincial attestation letter (PAL) is needed in most cases; the school issues it, usually after the offer is accepted and tuition is paid in part or in full.
3. Check the IRCC documents page for whether a PAL still applies to your program.
conditions: Only if you came on a study permit

steps.title: Line up the job offer and the employer paperwork
documents: LMIA or offer of employment details from the employer
prepare: Signed job offer with duties, wage and location
Ask the employer whether the job needs an LMIA or is LMIA-exempt
Get the reference numbers the application asks for
steps.howTo:
1. An employer-specific work permit ties you to one employer and one job.
2. The employer may need an LMIA first; some jobs are exempt.
3. LMIA timing depends on the employer and Employment and Social Development Canada, so the 2 months here is an estimate.
conditions: Only with a job offer
Only if you have an LMIA-based or LMIA-exempt employer-specific work permit

steps.title: Get an IEC invitation and accept it
prepare: Check your country has an IEC arrangement and the age limit (18 to 35, or 18 to 30 in some countries)
Create the IEC profile and enter the pool
Watch the IRCC account for an invitation
steps.howTo:
1. Working Holiday gives an open work permit; Young Professionals and International Co-op give an employer-specific one.
2. After an invitation there are 10 days to accept or decline it, then 20 days to submit the work permit application.
3. Invitations come in rounds, so the timing here is an estimate.
conditions: Only if you came on IEC / Working Holiday

steps.title: Apply for the study permit
steps.howTo:
1. The application is made online with the letter of acceptance, the PAL and proof of financial support.
2. The permit itself is issued at the port of entry after approval.
conditions: Only if you came on a study permit

steps.title: Apply for the employer-specific work permit
steps.howTo:
1. The application is made online with the employer details and the LMIA or offer of employment information.
2. The permit itself is issued at the port of entry after approval.
conditions: Only with a job offer
Only if you have an LMIA-based or LMIA-exempt employer-specific work permit

steps.title: Apply for the open work permit
prepare: Note the 20-day deadline after accepting an IEC invitation
steps.howTo:
1. For IEC, the application is submitted within 20 days of accepting the invitation.
2. The permit itself is issued at the port of entry after approval.
conditions: Only if you came on IEC / Working Holiday

steps.title: Apply for the spouse's work permit and the children's study permits
prepare: Check whether your job or program lets a spouse get an open work permit
Check whether the children need a study permit or can study without one
Apply at the same time as the main permit if possible
steps.howTo:
1. Spouses and common-law partners of some workers and students can apply for an open work permit; IRCC narrowed who qualifies in 2024, depending on the job's TEER level or the study program, so check current rules.
2. Minor children can often attend preschool, primary or secondary school without a study permit when a parent is allowed to work or study in Canada; a study permit can still be applied for.
3. Family applications sent together with the main one are usually processed together.
conditions: Only if a spouse, partner or children are coming with you

steps.title: Give biometrics
steps.howTo:
1. Study and work permit applicants usually give fingerprints and a photo, unless exempt.
2. Temporary residence applicants give biometrics once every 10 years, so earlier biometrics may still count.
3. The instruction letter arrives after the application is submitted.

steps.title: Receive the approval and the port of entry letter
documents: Port of entry letter of introduction
prepare: Check the letter details against the passport
steps.howTo:
1. Processing times on the IRCC site are estimates and are updated weekly for temporary residence; they are not a maximum.
2. The 11 weeks here is a placeholder; move this date once the approval arrives.
3. The letter of introduction is shown at the border to get the permit.

steps.title: Check the visitor visa in the passport
prepare: Check the visa dates and entries
steps.howTo:
1. When a permit application is approved, IRCC issues the visitor visa automatically if your passport needs one.
2. The passport is sent for the visa counterfoil; check it is back before travel.
conditions: Only if your passport needs a visitor visa (TRV)

steps.title: Check the eTA is linked to the passport
prepare: Check the approval letter mentions the eTA
Fly with the same passport used in the application
steps.howTo:
1. When a permit application is approved, IRCC issues the eTA automatically if your passport needs one.
2. The eTA is linked electronically to the passport.
conditions: Only if your passport is visa-exempt and needs an eTA

steps.title: Buy private medical insurance for the MSP wait
prepare: Cover at least the rest of the arrival month plus 2 months
Check if the school or employer offers a plan
steps.howTo:
1. MSP coverage for new residents starts after the rest of the arrival month plus 2 months.
2. The province suggests private health insurance for that wait.

steps.title: Book temporary housing for the first weeks
prepare: 2 to 4 weeks near work or school
An address for the SIN, bank and MSP forms
steps.howTo:
1. A short stay gives time to view rentals in person before signing.
2. The length here is an estimate.

steps.title: List the goods you bring and the goods to follow
prepare: Two lists: goods carried now and goods to follow, with values and serial numbers
Proof of ownership for valuable items
Total of cash and monetary instruments carried
steps.howTo:
1. Settlers list their goods on form BSF186 at the first arrival; goods to follow come in duty- and tax-free only if they were on that list.
2. The CBSA treats someone coming to work for more than 36 months as a settler; a shorter stay is not, so check which rules apply.
3. Currency and monetary instruments worth CAN$10,000 or more are declared at the border.

steps.title: Get the permit from the officer at the port of entry
documents: Port of entry letter of introduction
prepare: Carry the letter of introduction, the letter of acceptance or job offer, and proof of funds in hand luggage
Check the name, dates, conditions and expiry on the permit before leaving the counter
Check a study permit says it allows off-campus work, if that applies
steps.howTo:
1. A border services officer checks the documents and issues the permit.
2. Errors are easiest to fix on the spot.
3. A study permit that allows off-campus work carries a condition line that lets you apply for a SIN; without it, an amendment can be requested.

steps.title: Register the children at the school district's welcome centre
prepare: Find the school district for the home address
Past school reports, translated if needed
steps.howTo:
1. Many B.C. school districts register newcomer students through a welcome or newcomer centre, which also assesses English level for English language learning support.
2. The district then places the child at a school, usually the catchment school for the address.
3. Each district sets its own papers and whether fees apply to children of temporary residents; check with the district.
conditions: Only if you have school-age children

steps.title: Start licensing for a regulated occupation
prepare: Find the regulator for the occupation, such as Engineers and Geoscientists BC, the BC College of Nurses and Midwives, or SkilledTradesBC
steps.howTo:
1. Regulated occupations, such as engineering, nursing and many trades, need a licence or certificate from the B.C. regulator to practise under that title.
2. The regulator assesses foreign credentials and may ask for exams, supervised work or Canadian experience.
3. The whole process often takes months; the date here is when to start.
conditions: Only if you work in a regulated occupation

steps.title: Get a Canadian SIM and phone plan
steps.howTo:
1. A local number is asked for by banks, landlords and government forms.
2. Prepaid plans usually need no credit history.

steps.title: Apply for a Social Insurance Number
prepare: Apply online, in person at Service Canada, or by mail
steps.howTo:
1. A work permit, or a study permit that says you may work, is the primary document.
2. There is no fee.
3. A temporary resident's SIN starts with 9 and expires with the immigration document; update it when the permit is extended.

steps.title: Apply for MSP
prepare: Apply as soon as you arrive
Check the permit is valid for 6 months or more
Note the date coverage will start
steps.howTo:
1. Study and work permit holders with a permit valid 6 months or more may be deemed residents for MSP.
2. Coverage starts after the rest of the arrival month plus 2 months.
3. International students may be charged the international student health fee; check the MSP pages.

steps.title: Open a bank account
prepare: Compare newcomer packages from several banks
steps.howTo:
1. Many banks offer newcomer accounts; compare fees and credit card terms.
2. Account details are needed for payroll and for CRA direct deposit.

steps.title: Rent a home
prepare: View the unit in person or by live video before paying anything
Check the landlord owns or manages the unit
Walk through the move-in inspection with the landlord and sign the report
steps.howTo:
1. Landlords in B.C. prepare a written tenancy agreement for every tenancy; the Residential Tenancy Branch has a standard form.
2. The security deposit is at most half of one month's rent, and the pet damage deposit the same.
3. The move-in condition inspection decides who pays for damage later.
4. Paying before seeing a unit or signing is a common pattern in rental scams.

steps.title: Get the BC Services Card photo at ICBC
prepare: Combine it with the driver's licence if exchanging one
steps.howTo:
1. After enrolling in MSP, the photo card is made at an ICBC driver licensing office.
2. The card itself has no fee.
3. The card shows the Personal Health Number.

steps.title: Apply for newcomer benefit payments
prepare: Arrival date and world income for the year
steps.howTo:
1. Newcomers can apply for benefits without first filing a return.
2. People without children apply for the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB), which replaced the GST/HST credit in July 2026, with form RC151; there is a web form.
3. Families with children under 19 use form RC66 for the Canada child benefit; the CRA uses it for the CGEB and the BC family benefit too.
4. The B.C. climate action tax credit ended with the April 2025 payment.
conditions: Only if you are a resident of Canada for tax purposes

steps.title: Register for Fair PharmaCare
prepare: Proof of Income Affidavit if there is no Canadian tax return yet
steps.howTo:
1. Fair PharmaCare helps B.C. residents enrolled in MSP pay for eligible prescription drugs; the help depends on family income, not age.
2. Coverage is based on income from 2 years before, from the CRA; new residents without that can use the Fair PharmaCare Proof of Income Affidavit.
3. Register once, online or by phone.

steps.title: Join the Health Connect Registry for a family doctor
steps.howTo:
1. The registry is how B.C. matches people with a family doctor or nurse practitioner.
2. Registering online takes a few minutes, or call 8-1-1.
3. The local team makes contact when a provider becomes available; waits vary.

steps.title: Exchange the driver's licence at ICBC
prepare: Check whether your licence is on ICBC's licence exchange list
Book an ICBC-approved translation if needed
Book the knowledge and road tests early if it is not on the list
steps.howTo:
1. New residents can drive on a valid licence for up to 90 days, then switch to a B.C. licence.
2. Licences from exchange jurisdictions switch without tests; others take a knowledge test and a road test.
3. Full-time students at a designated institution can keep driving on their own valid licence.
4. The foreign licence is surrendered.
conditions: Only if you drive and hold a licence from outside Canada

steps.title: Apply to extend the permit before it expires
prepare: Keep a copy of the submission receipt
steps.howTo:
1. Move this step to about 30 days before the real expiry date; IRCC suggests applying at least 30 days before a work permit expires.
2. Applying before expiry and staying in Canada keeps you on maintained status while IRCC decides.
3. Update the SIN and MSP once the new permit arrives.

steps.title: Send the new permit to Health Insurance BC
prepare: A copy of the new permit
steps.howTo:
1. MSP for a permit holder is tied to the permit; send each new permit to Health Insurance BC so coverage carries on.
2. Move this step to when the new permit arrives; it repeats after every extension.
3. Update the SIN record at Service Canada at the same time.
conditions: Only if your permit was extended

steps.title: File the first Canadian tax return
steps.howTo:
1. The return is usually due by April 30 of the year after arrival; move this date to that deadline.
2. Filing keeps benefit payments going.
conditions: Only if you are a resident of Canada for tax purposes

steps.title: Check whether form T1135 for foreign property applies
prepare: Cost of property held outside Canada: bank accounts, shares, rental property
steps.howTo:
1. Residents of Canada whose specified foreign property cost more than CAN$100,000 at any time in the year file form T1135 with the return.
2. It is not needed for the year you first become resident.
3. Late filing has a penalty for each day late, up to a maximum; check the current amounts.
4. It repeats every year with the return.
conditions: Only if you are a resident of Canada for tax purposes
Only if you hold property outside Canada

steps.title: Claim the B.C. renter's tax credit on the return
prepare: Total rent paid and months rented
steps.howTo:
1. The credit is up to $400 a year for low- and moderate-income renters; it phases out above an income threshold that changes each year.
2. It counts renters who lived in an eligible B.C. rental unit for at least 6 one-month periods in the year and were B.C. residents on December 31.
3. It is claimed on form BC479 with the return, and repeats each year.
conditions: Only if you rent
Only if you are a resident of Canada for tax purposes

steps.title: Check eligibility for the BC PNP
prepare: See the Provincial nomination · British Columbia plan
steps.howTo:
1. BC PNP Skills Immigration streams need a full-time job offer from an eligible B.C. employer.
2. The steps are in the Provincial nomination · British Columbia plan.
conditions: Only with a job offer

steps.title: Check eligibility for the Canadian Experience Class
prepare: Count paid skilled hours in Canada
See the Skilled migration · CA plan
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Experience Class counts at least 1 year, or 1,560 hours, of skilled paid work in Canada (TEER 0 to 3) in the 3 years before applying.
2. Work done while a full-time student, co-op terms and self-employment usually do not count.
3. The Express Entry steps are in the Skilled migration · CA plan.
conditions: Only after 12 months of skilled Canadian work

title: Relocating to China · Canadian with Chinese family
summary: Routes into China for a Canadian national with a Chinese-citizen parent, spouse or close relative, from the family-reunion visa to permanent residence or nationality, then the first months after arrival.
conditions: Holds a foreign nationality, such as Canadian
Has a Chinese-citizen parent, spouse or close relative

sources.title: Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China (National Immigration Administration)
Exit and Entry Administration Law of the People's Republic of China
Regulations on Administration of Entry and Exit of Foreigners
NIA: Service Guide on Issuance of Residence Permit for Foreigners
NIA: 外国人居留证件签发、延期、换发、补发服务指南
NIA: Guidelines for Approval of Foreign Nationals' Eligibility for Permanent Residence
NIA: 外国人永久居留资格审批服务指南
NIA: Instructions on Application for Naturalization as a Chinese National
NIA: Policy interpretation on nationwide online accommodation registration
NIA: 外国人住宿登记 policy explanation
Chinese Embassy in Canada: visa application guide (申办须知)
Chinese Embassy in Canada: visa introduction and Q&A
Chinese Embassy in Canada: online Chinese visa application
Consulate General in Toronto: China visa application guide
Consulate General in Toronto: passport and travel document application guide (申办护照旅行证须知)
Consulate General in Toronto: passport and travel document FAQ
Chinese Embassy in Canada: Guide to Payment Services in China
Renounce Canadian citizenship: who can apply

steps.title: Confirm the nationality position and pick the entry route
prepare: Parents' passports and status documents from the time of the birth
The Chinese relative's ID and household register (户口簿) details
steps.howTo:
1. For someone born in Canada to a Chinese parent, the plan "Born in Canada to a Chinese parent" covers the nationality background.
2. Under Article 5 of the Nationality Law (中华人民共和国国籍法), a child born abroad to a Chinese-national parent has Chinese nationality, unless a Chinese-national parent had settled abroad (定居国外) and the child acquired a foreign nationality at birth.
3. China does not recognise dual nationality for Chinese nationals (Article 3).
4. The routes below each apply in one situation: A, family-reunion visa; B, permanent residence; C, naturalization; D, Chinese travel document and household registration. Mark the others "Not for me".
5. Confirm the status with the Chinese embassy or a consulate in Canada; this plan does not decide it.

steps.title: Route A: gather the Q1 family-reunion visa documents
prepare: Invitation letter from the Chinese-citizen relative living in China
Copy of the relative's Chinese ID card
Original proof of relationship: birth certificate, marriage certificate or notarial certificate
Canadian passport valid for the stay
conditions: Only if entering on a Q1 family-reunion visa as a foreign national
steps.howTo:
1. The Q1 visa (团聚签证) is for family members of Chinese citizens, or of foreigners with Chinese permanent residence, who apply to reside in China for family reunion for more than 180 days.
2. Family members include spouses, parents, parents-in-law, children, children's spouses, siblings, grandparents and grandchildren.
3. The Embassy's list names an invitation letter from the relative living in China, the relative's Chinese ID copy, and original proof of the relationship; check the current list with the visa centre for anything else, such as household register (户口簿) pages.
4. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Route A: apply for the Q1 visa at a Chinese Visa Application Service Center
conditions: Only if entering on a Q1 family-reunion visa as a foreign national
steps.howTo:
1. Ordinary visas are applied for through a Chinese Visa Application Service Center in Canada; forms are filled online at visaforchina.cn.
2. Standard processing is about 4 business days from the day the paper documents are submitted.
3. A Q1 visa is marked for a residence permit to be applied for within 30 days of entry.
4. The date here is a planning estimate; allow time for appointments and mail.

steps.title: Route B: check eligibility for Chinese permanent residence
prepare: Housing and income proof, for a spouse
conditions: Only if applying for Chinese permanent residence as a minor child or a spouse of a Chinese citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Chinese permanent residence (外国人永久居留) is approved by public security; the card is the Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card (外国人永久居留身份证).
2. A minor child: under 18, unmarried and dependent on a parent who is a Chinese citizen (or a foreign permanent resident).
3. A spouse: married to a Chinese citizen for at least 5 years, with at least 5 consecutive years of residence in China, at least 9 months each year, and a stable income and home.
4. The application goes to the city public security bureau where the applicant lives long term in China, so it is made after entry; a parent can file for a child under 18.
5. Confirm eligibility with the local exit-entry office.

steps.title: Route C: look into Chinese nationality (入籍)
prepare: Proof of the Chinese-national close relative
conditions: Only if considering naturalization as a Chinese national
steps.howTo:
1. A foreign national who has Chinese-national close relatives, has settled in China, or has other legitimate reasons can apply to be naturalized (Nationality Law, Article 7).
2. A person naturalized as Chinese does not keep a foreign nationality (Article 8); the application includes a written declaration giving up the foreign nationality.
3. The application goes to the city or county public security bureau in China, or to a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad; the Ministry of Public Security approves it. Parents can file for a child under 18 (Article 14).
4. Canada accepts renunciation of Canadian citizenship from someone at least 18 who is, or will become, a citizen of another country and does not live in Canada.
5. No processing time is published; confirm the process with the Chinese embassy or a consulate in Canada.

steps.title: Route D: get a Chinese travel document (旅行证) for the move
prepare: China Consular (中国领事) app account
Both parents' passports and residence documents at the birth
conditions: Only if the embassy or consulate treats the person as a Chinese national
steps.howTo:
1. Under Article 5 of the Nationality Law, a child born abroad to a Chinese-national parent who had not settled abroad at the birth has Chinese nationality; the consulates issue such a child a travel document.
2. Apply through the China Consular app while in Canada; the consulates quote about 4 to 10 business days from complete materials.
3. A person treated as Chinese enters China on the Chinese document, not on a visa.
4. Confirm the status with the Chinese embassy or a consulate in Canada before applying.
5. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Register the address with the local police within 24 hours (住宿登记)
conditions: Only if entering as a foreign national and staying outside a hotel
steps.howTo:
1. A foreign national staying outside a hotel is registered with the police station for the address within 24 hours of arriving, by the host or the person themselves.
2. Hotels register their guests themselves.
3. Online registration through the NIA government service platform, the NIA 12367 app or its mini programs has the same effect as registering in person.
4. Registration is done again after moving address.

steps.title: Get a real-name mobile number with the passport
steps.howTo:
1. Mobile numbers in China are registered in the holder's real name; a foreign national shows the passport at a carrier's own shop.
2. A local number makes bank, payment app and government app sign-ups simpler.
3. Rules and accepted documents can differ by carrier; ask in the shop.

steps.title: Open a bank account with the passport
steps.howTo:
1. According to the Embassy's payment guide, a bank account can be opened with a passport or other valid ID at a bank branch, such as ICBC, ABC, Bank of China, CCB or Bank of Communications.
2. Ask the branch what else it asks for; requirements differ between banks.
3. The account can be linked to mobile payment apps.

steps.title: Route A: convert the Q1 visa into a family-reunion residence permit
documents: Family-reunion residence permit (团聚类居留许可)
prepare: Relative's ID and a letter explaining the family relationship
Health certificate, if asking for a permit over 1 year
conditions: Only if entered on a Q1 family-reunion visa
steps.howTo:
1. A visa marked for a residence permit is converted by applying to the local public security exit-entry office within 30 days of entry.
2. Applicants apply in person; a representative can file for someone under 16.
3. A decision comes within the validity of the acceptance receipt, up to 15 working days.
4. Family-reunion permits for people under 18 or 60 and over are issued for up to 3 years, not past the 18th birthday for a minor; for others, up to 2 years.
5. Confirm the current rules with the local exit-entry office.

steps.title: Route D: register in the family's household register (户口)
prepare: Chinese travel document with the entry record
Birth certificate, with any translation or certification the police station asks for
Parent's household register and ID card
conditions: Only if the person is treated as a Chinese national and will live in China
steps.howTo:
1. A Chinese national living in China is registered in a household register (户口) through the local public security police station.
2. For a child born abroad, the police station for the parent's registered address says what it asks for; this varies by city.
3. An expired travel document can't be renewed by the local police in China; for exit, they can issue a one-time exit-entry permit (出入境通行证).
4. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Arrange health insurance
conditions: Only if not covered through an employer in China
steps.howTo:
1. Foreign nationals who are not employed in China often arrange a private medical plan; whether a family member on a residence permit can join a local scheme varies by city.
2. Ask the local social insurance office what applies in your city.
3. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Join social insurance through the employer
conditions: Only if employed in China
steps.howTo:
1. Foreign nationals employed in China are enrolled in the social insurance schemes through the employer.
2. Ask the employer's HR team when enrolment happens.
3. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Apply to a local public school as a foreign student
conditions: Only if a school-age child with foreign nationality is moving
Only if looking at public schools
steps.howTo:
1. Admission of foreign-national students to public primary and secondary schools follows the rules of the city and district education bureau; they vary by city.
2. Ask the district education bureau which schools admit foreign students and what they ask for.
3. A child treated as a Chinese national with a household registration enrols like other local children.
4. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Apply to an international school
conditions: Only if a child with foreign nationality is moving
Only if looking at international schools
steps.howTo:
1. Schools for children of foreign nationals (外籍人员子女学校) admit holders of foreign passports
2. Ask each school about deadlines and entry tests.
3. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Route B: apply for permanent residence once eligible
documents: Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card (外国人永久居留身份证)
prepare: Birth certificate or proof of parentage, for a minor child
Chinese parent's ID copy, for a minor child
Marriage certificate, spouse's ID, housing and income proof, for a spouse
conditions: Only if eligible for permanent residence as a minor child or a spouse of a Chinese citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Apply to the city public security bureau where you live long term in China; a parent can apply for a child under 18.
2. A decision is made within 6 months of acceptance.
3. A spouse becomes eligible only after 5 years of marriage and 5 consecutive years of residence in China, so move this date to when that is met.
4. The date here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Route A: renew the residence permit before it expires
conditions: Only if living in China on a residence permit
steps.howTo:
1. An extension is applied for at the local exit-entry office within 30 days before the permit expires.
2. The date here is a planning estimate for a 2-year permit; move it to 30 days before the expiry date on your permit.

You aren't a Canadian citizen or permanent resident yet
