steps.title: Pick the permit route
prepare: Study, employer-specific work or open work permit
Check the passport stays valid for the whole stay
Use the IRCC "find out if you need a permit" tool
steps.howTo:
1. A study permit needs a letter of acceptance from a designated learning institution (DLI).
2. An employer-specific work permit needs a job offer; the employer may need a labour market impact assessment (LMIA).
3. An open work permit needs no job offer and lets you work for most compliant employers, but only certain situations qualify, e.g. International Experience Canada (IEC) Working Holiday.
4. Not immigration advice; the IRCC pages decide which route fits.

steps.title: Get the letter of acceptance and the PAL
conditions: Only if you are coming to study
prepare: Apply to a designated learning institution (DLI)
Accept the offer and pay the tuition deposit the school asks for
Ask the school for the PAL
steps.howTo:
1. The school issues the letter of acceptance; it is uploaded with the study permit application.
2. Most applicants also need a provincial attestation letter (PAL) from the school; it usually comes after you accept the offer and pay some or all of the tuition.
3. A PAL is linked to the school and in most cases is used in the year it was issued.
4. As of 2026, IRCC lists exemptions, including primary and secondary school and master's or doctoral programs at public institutions; check the PAL page before applying.

steps.title: Get the job offer and the LMIA or offer number
conditions: Only if you are coming on an employer-specific work permit
documents: LMIA or offer of employment number
prepare: Signed job offer with duties, wage and dates
Ask the employer whether the job needs an LMIA or is LMIA-exempt
steps.howTo:
1. An employer-specific permit names the employer, and often the job and location.
2. Either the employer gets an LMIA from Employment and Social Development Canada, or, for an LMIA-exempt job, submits the offer through the IRCC Employer Portal and gives you an offer of employment number.
3. The 60 days is an estimate; LMIA times vary by stream.

steps.title: Enter the IEC pool and wait for an invitation
conditions: Only if you are coming through International Experience Canada (IEC)
prepare: Check your country has an IEC agreement and your age fits (18 to 35, or 18 to 30 for some countries)
Pick the pools: Working Holiday, Young Professionals or International Co-op
steps.howTo:
1. Submit an IEC profile and choose the pools.
2. Working Holiday leads to an open work permit; Young Professionals and International Co-op lead to employer-specific permits.
3. Invitations come in rounds; the 60 days here is an estimate.
4. After an invitation there are 10 days to start the application.

steps.title: Gather proof of funds
prepare: Bank statements for the last 6 months
Tuition receipts, education loan or scholarship letters, if studying
Check the current amount on the IRCC page for your route
steps.howTo:
1. For a study permit, show enough for the first year: tuition, living costs for you and any family, and travel to and from Canada.
2. For longer programs, explain how the rest of the studies will be paid for.
3. IRCC updates the living-cost amounts each year; use the figure in force on the day you apply.
4. Work permit routes, including IEC, can ask for funds too; check the route's own page.

steps.title: Apply for the study permit
conditions: Only if you are coming to study
prepare: Check the current fee and processing time
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online in the IRCC account and upload the letter of acceptance, the PAL and proof of funds.
2. Travel later on the passport used for the application.
3. Processing times are estimates that IRCC updates weekly; check them before picking this date.

steps.title: Apply for the employer-specific work permit
conditions: Only if you are coming on an employer-specific work permit
documents: LMIA or offer of employment number
prepare: Proof of qualifications for the job
Check the current fee and processing time
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online with the LMIA copy or the offer of employment number.
2. Most people apply before travelling; only some can apply at a port of entry.
3. Processing times are estimates that IRCC updates weekly.

steps.title: Apply for the open work permit
conditions: Only if you qualify for an open work permit, e.g. IEC Working Holiday
prepare: Police certificates and medical exam, if the route asks
steps.howTo:
1. For IEC, once the application is started there are 20 days to complete it, submit it and pay the fee.
2. Other open work permits (e.g. for some spouses) have their own IRCC eligibility pages.
3. Processing times are estimates that IRCC updates weekly.

steps.title: Apply for the spouse's work permit and the children's study permits
prepare: Check whether your job or program lets a spouse get an open work permit
Check whether the children need a study permit or can study without one
Apply at the same time as the main permit if possible
steps.howTo:
1. Spouses and common-law partners of some workers and students can apply for an open work permit; IRCC narrowed who qualifies in 2024, depending on the job's TEER level or the study program, so check current rules.
2. Minor children can often attend preschool, primary or secondary school without a study permit when a parent is allowed to work or study in Canada; a study permit can still be applied for.
3. Family applications sent together with the main one are usually processed together.
conditions: Only if a spouse, partner or children are coming with you

steps.title: Give biometrics
prepare: Book a collection point as soon as the letter arrives
steps.howTo:
1. Most applicants give fingerprints and a photo; children under 14 and people over 79 are exempt.
2. Temporary residence applicants give them once every 10 years; a permit can't run more than 10 years past that date.
3. Skip this step if your earlier biometrics are still valid.

steps.title: Receive the approval and port of entry letter
documents: Port of entry letter of introduction
steps.howTo:
1. On approval IRCC sends a port of entry letter of introduction; it is not the permit itself.
2. The 120 days is an estimate; move this step to the real date.

steps.title: Check the visitor visa or eTA
conditions: Only if you aren't a US citizen
prepare: Check which one your passport needs
Check the visa is in the passport you will travel on
steps.howTo:
1. With an approved work or study permit IRCC issues the visitor visa (TRV) or eTA automatically; there is no separate application.
2. A visa-required passport gets a visitor visa in the passport; a visa-exempt passport gets an eTA for flying in.
3. An eTA is valid for up to 5 years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.

steps.title: Arrange health insurance until OHIP or a school plan starts
prepare: For university students, check the UHIP enrolment
For college students, ask the school which plan it uses
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario has no OHIP waiting period any more; eligible people are covered as soon as they qualify.
2. Work permit holders qualify if working full-time in Ontario for an Ontario employer for at least 6 months; the card still has to be applied for in person, so private cover bridges the gap.
3. Study permit holders are not listed as OHIP-eligible; Ontario universities enrol international students in UHIP, a compulsory plan.
4. Private cover is usually needed for anyone not eligible for either.

steps.title: Book temporary housing
prepare: 2 to 4 weeks near work or school
An address to give the border officer
steps.howTo:
1. A short stay gives time to view places in person before signing a lease.
2. The length here is an estimate; rental markets vary across Ontario.

steps.title: List the goods you bring and the goods to follow
prepare: Two lists: goods carried now and goods to follow, with values and serial numbers
Proof of ownership for valuable items
Total of cash and monetary instruments carried
steps.howTo:
1. Settlers list their goods on form BSF186 at the first arrival; goods to follow come in duty- and tax-free only if they were on that list.
2. The CBSA treats someone coming to work for more than 36 months as a settler; a shorter stay is not, so check which rules apply.
3. Currency and monetary instruments worth CAN$10,000 or more are declared at the border.

steps.title: Get the permit at the port of entry and check it
documents: Port of entry letter of introduction
prepare: Carry the letter, passport, proof of funds and the letters behind the application
Read the permit before leaving the counter
steps.howTo:
1. Show the port of entry letter to the border services officer, who issues the permit.
2. Before leaving, check the name, the conditions (employer, school, work rights) and the expiry date.
3. Point out any mistake to the officer before leaving.
4. Note the expiry date; the extension step counts back from it.

steps.title: Register the children at the school board's welcome centre
prepare: Find the school board for the home address
Past school reports, translated if needed
steps.howTo:
1. Many Ontario school boards register newcomer students through a welcome or reception centre, which also assesses English level for English language learner support.
2. The board then places the child at a school, usually the one for the address.
3. Each board sets its own papers and whether fees apply to children of temporary residents; check with the board.
conditions: Only if you have school-age children

steps.title: Start licensing for a regulated occupation
prepare: Find the regulator for the occupation, such as Professional Engineers Ontario, the College of Nurses of Ontario, or Skilled Trades Ontario
steps.howTo:
1. Regulated occupations, such as engineering, nursing and many trades, need a licence or certificate from the Ontario regulator to practise under that title.
2. The regulator assesses foreign credentials and may ask for exams, supervised work or Canadian experience.
3. The whole process often takes months; the date here is when to start.
conditions: Only if you work in a regulated occupation

steps.title: Get a Social Insurance Number
prepare: One more ID, e.g. the passport
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online (fastest), by mail or in person at a Service Canada office.
2. Online confirmation takes about 5 business days; by mail about 20.
3. A temporary resident's SIN starts with 9 and expires with the immigration document.
4. Work can start as soon as you have applied.

steps.title: Get a SIM or phone plan
steps.howTo:
1. A local number is asked for by banks, landlords and employers.
2. Prepaid avoids a credit check while you have no Canadian credit history.

steps.title: Open a bank account
prepare: Two IDs, or one ID and someone the bank trusts to vouch for you
An address, even a temporary one
steps.howTo:
1. You can open an account without a job or money to deposit.
2. Banks accept two documents from reliable sources, one with your name and address and one with your name and date of birth.
3. Many banks run newcomer packages; compare the fees.

steps.title: Rent a home on Ontario's standard lease
prepare: View the place in person or by live video before paying
Check the landlord owns or manages it
Never wire a deposit to hold a place you haven't seen
steps.howTo:
1. Most private landlords use Ontario's standard lease for new leases; ask in writing if you don't get it, and the landlord has 21 days to provide it.
2. The only rent deposit allowed is for the last month's rent, no more than one month; a refundable key deposit is also allowed.
3. Pet or damage deposits aren't allowed; the landlord pays interest on the rent deposit each year.
4. The Landlord and Tenant Board settles disputes; overpaid deposits can be claimed back there.
5. Scams often ask for money before a viewing or push you to sign quickly.

steps.title: Apply for OHIP at ServiceOntario
conditions: Only if you work full-time for an Ontario employer on a permit of at least 6 months, or are the spouse or dependent of someone who does
prepare: Three original documents: immigration status, Ontario residency and identity
Registration for Ontario Health Insurance Coverage form
steps.howTo:
1. Apply in person at ServiceOntario with the form and three separate original documents.
2. There is no waiting period; coverage starts once eligibility is accepted.
3. Study permit holders aren't listed as eligible; use UHIP or the school plan instead.

steps.title: Exchange the driver's licence at DriveTest
conditions: Only if you hold a driver's licence from outside Ontario and want to drive
prepare: Proof of driving experience in English or French
steps.howTo:
1. A valid licence from elsewhere can be used for 60 days after moving to Ontario.
2. Ontario exchanges licences from other provinces, US states and some countries, including Australia, France, Germany, Great Britain, Ireland, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, Switzerland and Taiwan; check the full list.
3. Other countries: an official authentication letter from the issuing agency can credit up to one year of experience toward graduated licensing.
4. Expect a vision test and a knowledge test.

steps.title: Find a family doctor through Health Care Connect
conditions: Only once you have an Ontario health card
steps.howTo:
1. Register yourself and your family online or through 811.
2. A Care Connector searches for a clinician and a referral letter comes by mail.
3. A match can take a long time; walk-in clinics fill the gap.

steps.title: Apply for newcomer benefits with the CRA
conditions: Only if you are resident in Canada for tax and have a low or modest income or children
prepare: Income from the year before arrival
Form RC66 if you have children
steps.howTo:
1. Newcomers can apply for benefit payments as soon as they arrive, before the first tax return.
2. People without children apply for the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB, formerly the GST/HST credit) with form RC151; there is a web form.
3. Families with children under 19 use form RC66 for the Canada Child Benefit; the CRA uses it for the CGEB too.
4. Eligibility depends on being a Canadian resident for tax purposes; check the CRA newcomers page.

steps.title: File the first tax return
steps.howTo:
1. The return is usually due April 30 of the year after arrival; move this step to that date.
2. Filing opens ongoing benefits, including the Ontario Trillium Benefit.
3. The date here is an estimate.

steps.title: Extend the permit before it expires
conditions: Only if you plan to stay past the permit expiry date
prepare: New job offer, LMIA or school letter, if the route needs one
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC suggests applying at least 30 days before the permit expires; move this step to that date.
2. If you apply before it expires, you can keep working under the same conditions until a decision; IRCC calls this maintained status.
3. Check the IRCC page before travelling while waiting.

steps.title: Renew the health card at ServiceOntario with the new permit
steps.howTo:
1. OHIP for a permit holder is tied to the permit; bring each new permit to ServiceOntario so coverage carries on.
2. Move this step to when the new permit arrives; it repeats after every extension.
3. With maintained status while waiting, ServiceOntario confirms eligibility case by case.
4. Update the SIN record at Service Canada at the same time.
conditions: Only if your permit was extended
Only if you have OHIP

steps.title: Check whether form T1135 for foreign property applies
prepare: Cost of property held outside Canada: bank accounts, shares, rental property
steps.howTo:
1. Residents of Canada whose specified foreign property cost more than CAN$100,000 at any time in the year file form T1135 with the return.
2. It is not needed for the year you first become resident.
3. Late filing has a penalty for each day late, up to a maximum; check the current amounts.
4. It repeats every year with the return; move it with the tax return step.
conditions: Only if you are resident in Canada for tax
Only if you hold property outside Canada

steps.title: Claim the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit on rent (ON-BEN)
prepare: Total rent paid in the year
steps.howTo:
1. The credit is part of the Ontario Trillium Benefit; renters apply by filling in the ON-BEN form in the tax return, due April 30.
2. It counts renters who were Ontario residents on December 31 and whose landlord paid property tax on the home.
3. Payments start in July; the ON-BEN form is filled in every year with the return.
conditions: Only if you rent
Only if you are resident in Canada for tax

steps.title: Check the Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program
conditions: Only if you hold a full-time, permanent job offer from an Ontario employer
prepare: Job offer and its TEER level
steps.howTo:
1. Since June 2026 the OINP runs one main stream, Ontario Workforce Priority; the older streams are closed.
2. For TEER 0 to 3 jobs, it asks for 6 months of full-time work in the offered job within the last 12 months, among other criteria.
3. See the "Provincial nomination · Ontario" plan for the steps.
4. Not immigration advice; the OINP pages decide eligibility.

steps.title: Check Express Entry after 12 months of skilled Canadian work
conditions: Only if you work in a TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3 job in Canada
prepare: Count paid hours worked in Canada
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Experience Class counts 1 year (1,560 hours) of paid skilled work in Canada in the 3 years before applying.
2. Work done while studying full-time, including co-op terms, doesn't count.
3. See the "Skilled migration · CA" plan for the Express Entry steps.
4. Not immigration advice; check the IRCC pages.

title: Provincial nomination · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for a BC PNP Skills Immigration nomination, from registration and the invitation to the nomination and the permanent residence application.
conditions: You work in British Columbia, or plan to, and want permanent residence through the BC PNP
You have, or expect, a full-time job offer from an eligible B.C. employer
This is a planning aid, not immigration advice; the BC PNP program guide and IRCC are the reference

sources.title: Immigrate to B.C. as a worker — WelcomeBC
BC PNP Skills Immigration Program Guide (effective June 10, 2026) — WelcomeBC
BC PNP Skills Immigration Post-Nomination Guide — WelcomeBC
BC PNP Invitations to Apply — WelcomeBC
BC PNP Online User Portal — WelcomeBC
Provincial Nominee Program: How it works — Canada.ca
Canadian Experience Class — Canada.ca
Check processing times — Canada.ca

steps.title: Check stream eligibility and the job offer
prepare: Find the NOC code and TEER of the job
Skilled Worker: TEER 0 to 3 and 2 years of full-time skilled work experience
Health Authority: a job with a B.C. public health authority
Check the job is not on the ineligible occupations list
steps.howTo:
1. The current Skills Immigration streams are Skilled Worker and Health Authority; both have an Express Entry BC (EEBC) option.
2. Both need a full-time, indeterminate job offer from an eligible B.C. employer, with a few listed occupations eligible on limited-term offers.
3. The earlier graduate streams are not in the June 2026 program guide; check the guide for the current list.
4. EEBC also needs eligibility for a federal Express Entry program: Federal Skilled Worker, Federal Skilled Trades or Canadian Experience Class.
conditions: Only with a full-time job offer from an eligible B.C. employer

steps.title: Get valid language test results
prepare: Check which tests the BC PNP accepts
steps.howTo:
1. Results count for 2 years from the date of issue.
2. For registration points, results are valid when registering; they are also valid when applying.
3. Express Entry needs its own approved test; one test can serve both if it is on both lists.

steps.title: Create the Express Entry profile for the EEBC option
prepare: Indicate interest in settling in B.C.
See the Skilled migration · CA plan
steps.howTo:
1. EEBC needs a valid Express Entry profile number and job seeker validation code.
2. The profile stays valid for 12 months; if it expires, or IRCC invites you first, the BC PNP can no longer nominate through EEBC.
3. The Express Entry steps are in the Skilled migration · CA plan.
conditions: Only for the Express Entry BC option

steps.title: Line up the employer's support
prepare: Confirm the employer meets the BC PNP employer requirements
Agree the wage and job title
Health Authority: the health authority support letter
steps.howTo:
1. Streams with a job offer need the employer's support throughout.
2. Organisations that provide immigration services are ineligible employers.
3. The employer's details go into the registration and the application.

steps.title: Register in BC PNP Online and get a score
prepare: Job, wage, location and work history
Keep entries consistent with later documents
steps.howTo:
1. Registering is free; the registration gets a score from the published scoring factors.
2. A registration stays in the pool for up to 12 months, or until invited.
3. Only one active registration or application is allowed at a time.
4. Health Authority applicants skip registration and apply directly.
conditions: Only for the Skilled Worker stream

steps.title: Receive an invitation to apply (ITA)
prepare: Check recent draws on the invitations page
steps.howTo:
1. Invitations are issued periodically and may target occupations, wages, regions or priorities.
2. After an invitation there are 30 calendar days to submit a complete application; this cannot be extended.
3. Timing is not predictable; move this date to the real invitation date.
conditions: Only for the Skilled Worker stream

steps.title: Gather application documents
prepare: Use the document list in the Skills Immigration Application Guide
steps.howTo:
1. The application guide lists the documents per stream.
2. Details that differ from the registration can lead to a refusal if the score drops below the draw.

steps.title: Submit the BC PNP application
prepare: Re-check every entry against the registration
steps.howTo:
1. The application and fee go through BCPNP Online.
2. Changes in job, wage or family after applying are reported within 15 calendar days.

steps.title: Get the BC PNP decision and nomination
steps.howTo:
1. Processing times are on the BC PNP Process page; the 2 months here is a planning estimate.
2. A nomination is valid for 180 days; the PR application to IRCC is made before it expires.
3. A refusal can be reviewed if requested within 30 days in Canada, or 60 days outside.

steps.title: Request a work permit support letter
steps.howTo:
1. The BC PNP may issue a support letter to get or renew a work permit while PR is processed.
2. A nominee without a valid work permit usually applies for one within 3 months of nomination.
conditions: Only if your work permit is expiring or you have none

steps.title: Accept the nomination in the Express Entry profile
prepare: Log in to the IRCC account
steps.howTo:
1. An EEBC nomination adds 600 points to the Comprehensive Ranking System score.
2. This normally ranks the profile high enough for an invitation from IRCC.
conditions: Only for the Express Entry BC option

steps.title: Receive the IRCC invitation to apply
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC invites from the pool in rounds.
2. After the invitation there are 60 days to submit the PR application.
3. Move this date to the real invitation date.
conditions: Only for the Express Entry BC option

steps.title: Order police certificates and the medical exam
prepare: Each country lived in 6 months or more since age 18
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC gives a personalised document checklist with the application.
2. The Skilled migration · CA plan has the details for police certificates and medicals.

steps.title: Apply to IRCC for permanent residence
prepare: Check the nomination is not expired
steps.howTo:
1. EEBC nominees apply through Express Entry within 60 days of the IRCC invitation.
2. Otherwise, the base PNP application goes to IRCC outside Express Entry with the nomination; processing usually takes longer.
3. IRCC processing times are estimates; check the processing times page.

steps.title: Keep to the conditions of nomination until landing
prepare: Stay with the supporting employer, in the same occupation and wage
Report changes to the BC PNP
steps.howTo:
1. Conditions apply from nomination until becoming a permanent resident or a refusal by IRCC.
2. Breaking them can lead to the nomination being cancelled, which affects the PR application.
3. The 6 months here is a placeholder for IRCC processing.

title: Provincial nomination · Ontario
summary: Paperwork plan for permanent residence through the Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program, from the job offer and Expression of Interest to the nomination and the IRCC application.
conditions: You're applying for permanent residence through the Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP)
You have a full-time, permanent job offer from an Ontario employer, or you are a self-employed physician in Ontario
You plan to live and work in Ontario after becoming a permanent resident

sources.title: Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program (OINP) — Ontario.ca
Ontario Workforce Priority stream — Ontario.ca
2026 Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program updates — Ontario.ca
OINP closed streams — Ontario.ca
How the Provincial Nominee Program works — Canada.ca
Provincial nominees: Express Entry — Canada.ca
Provincial nominees: Non-Express Entry — Canada.ca
Express Entry: Submit your profile — Canada.ca
Express Entry: Language test results — Canada.ca
Express Entry: Educational credential assessment — Canada.ca
Express Entry: Police certificates — Canada.ca
Medical exam requirements for permanent residents — Canada.ca
Check processing times — Canada.ca

steps.title: Check Ontario Workforce Priority eligibility
prepare: The job offer's NOC code and TEER level
Months of full-time paid work in that job
Whether the wage meets the level for the job location
steps.howTo:
1. Since June 26, 2026 the OINP runs one stream, Ontario Workforce Priority; the Employer Job Offer, Master's and PhD Graduate, and Express Entry (Human Capital Priorities, French-Speaking Skilled Worker, Skilled Trades) streams are closed.
2. It has pathways for TEER 0 to 3 jobs, TEER 4 and 5 jobs, and self-employed physicians (no job offer).
3. TEER 0 to 3: usually 6 months of consecutive full-time work in the offered job within the last 12 months, 3 months for recent Ontario graduates, or 2 years cumulative experience.
4. TEER 4 and 5: at least 9 months of cumulative full-time work within 2 years.
5. Legal status in Canada is needed if you are here.
6. Not immigration advice; the OINP pages decide eligibility, and more changes were announced.

steps.title: Take an approved language test
conditions: Not needed if you're a recent Ontario graduate and won't use the Express Entry option
steps.howTo:
1. Minimums in all four abilities: CLB 6 for TEER 0 to 3 jobs, CLB 5 for skilled trades, CLB 4 for TEER 4 and 5.
2. Higher levels, and a second official language at CLB 6, raise the EOI score.
3. Express Entry counts results less than 2 years old.

steps.title: Get an Educational Credential Assessment
conditions: Only if your qualifying education is from outside Canada
steps.howTo:
1. Credentials from outside Canada need an ECA report less than 5 years old.
2. TEER 0 to 3 non-trades jobs ask for a postsecondary credential of at least 1 year; trades and TEER 4 and 5 ask for secondary school.
3. Processing time varies by organization; the 120 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Get the full-time, permanent job offer
conditions: Only for the job offer pathways, not self-employed physicians
prepare: Wage at or above the level for the location
steps.howTo:
1. The employer has been in business for at least 3 years, has premises in Ontario and meets revenue and staffing minimums for its location.
2. If you are outside Canada, the employer shows it tried to recruit Canadians or permanent residents first.

steps.title: Employer submits the job offer in the Employer Portal
conditions: Only for the job offer pathways, not self-employed physicians
prepare: Ask the employer to register in the OINP Employer Portal
steps.howTo:
1. The employer registers and submits the job offer, then gives you a job offer ID.
2. The EOI is registered within 30 calendar days of that submission.

steps.title: Keep a valid Express Entry profile
conditions: Only if your job is TEER 0 to 3 and you choose the Express Entry option
prepare: Check you meet a federal Express Entry program
steps.howTo:
1. The Express Entry option is open to TEER 0 to 3 jobs only.
2. You meet the minimum criteria of a federal Express Entry program and keep the profile valid.
3. A profile expires after 12 months; see the "Skilled migration · CA" plan.

steps.title: Register the Expression of Interest
steps.howTo:
1. Register in the OINP e-filing portal; physicians contact the OINP to register.
2. The score adds up: job and wage (up to 61), education (up to 20), language (up to 25), and region (up to 15; Toronto 0, Northern Ontario 15).
3. A valid work permit adds 10 points, a study permit 5.
4. Invitations go to the highest scores; there is no set wait.

steps.title: Gather the documents on the OINP checklist
prepare: Download the checklist for your pathway
Translations for documents not in English or French
steps.howTo:
1. The window after an invitation is short, so collect documents before it arrives.
2. The checklist is on the stream page.

steps.title: Receive an invitation to apply
prepare: Tell the employer the same day
steps.howTo:
1. Draw timing isn't predictable; the 30 days is an estimate.
2. Move this step to the real invitation date.

steps.title: Submit the OINP application within 17 days
steps.howTo:
1. The employer submits its application within 14 calendar days of the invitation.
2. You submit yours within 17 calendar days, and only after the employer has.
3. Physicians have 17 calendar days.

steps.title: Watch for the nomination decision
steps.howTo:
1. The OINP doesn't publish a fixed processing time; the 60 days is an estimate.
2. After nomination, apply to IRCC within 6 months.
3. The nomination stays valid until IRCC approves or refuses the permanent residence application.

steps.title: Accept the nomination in the Express Entry profile (+600 CRS)
conditions: Only if you chose the Express Entry option
prepare: Log in to the IRCC account
steps.howTo:
1. The OINP enters the nomination in the Express Entry system.
2. There are 30 calendar days to accept or refuse it.
3. Accepting adds 600 points, which usually leads to an invitation in a later round.

steps.title: Receive the Express Entry invitation
conditions: Only if you chose the Express Entry option
steps.howTo:
1. After the invitation there are 60 days to submit the application to IRCC.
2. Timing is an estimate; move this step to the real date.

steps.title: Order police certificates and the medical exam
prepare: List countries lived in 6 months or more since 18
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC asks for these with the permanent residence application.
2. Police certificates take different times by country; the 45 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Apply to IRCC for permanent residence
prepare: Re-check details against the OINP application
steps.howTo:
1. Express Entry option: submit the eAPR within 60 days of the invitation.
2. Base route: apply through the IRCC Permanent Residence Portal within 6 months of nomination.
3. IRCC makes the final decision; processing times are estimates on the IRCC page.

steps.title: Keep the nomination conditions and watch for the IRCC decision
prepare: Keep living and working in Ontario as the nomination describes
steps.howTo:
1. The OINP follows up with nominees to confirm the nomination conditions are met.
2. Dates here are rough placeholders.

title: Leaving Canada · moving abroad
summary: Paperwork plan for moving from Canada to another country: tax residency and departure tax, benefits and health coverage that stop, registered accounts as a non-resident, PR status, pensions and the final return.
conditions: You lived in Canada and are moving abroad for the long term
The date is the day you leave Canada
Health steps describe British Columbia and Ontario; other provinces have their own

Apply for OHIP and get a health card — Ontario.ca

steps.title: Work out when you stop being a Canadian tax resident
documents: Form NR73, if asking the CRA for an opinion
prepare: Home, spouse and dependants staying or leaving
Bank accounts, cards, licence and health card
Tax treaty with the new country
steps.howTo:
1. Residency for tax depends on residential ties: a home, a spouse or dependants, and secondary ties such as belongings, accounts, a licence and health coverage.
2. The departure date is usually the latest of leaving, the spouse or dependants leaving, or becoming resident in the new country.
3. Form NR73 asks the CRA for an opinion; it is optional.
4. A tax treaty can settle cases where both countries claim residence.

steps.title: List property for the deemed disposition on leaving
documents: Form T1161, if property is over $25,000
Form T1244, if deferring the tax
prepare: Fair market value of shares, funds, crypto and collections on the departure date
steps.howTo:
1. On leaving, most property is treated as sold at fair market value, and any gain is taxed on the final return; this is often called departure tax.
2. Canadian real estate, RRSPs, RRIFs, TFSAs and pensions are generally not part of it.
3. Form T1161 lists property worth more than $25,000 in total; T1243 works out the gain.
4. The tax on the gain can be deferred with security using form T1244.

steps.title: Check the rules for RRSP, TFSA and FHSA as a non-resident
prepare: Home Buyers' Plan or Lifelong Learning Plan balance
steps.howTo:
1. A TFSA can stay open, but contributions while non-resident are taxed 1% a month until withdrawn, and no new room builds.
2. RRSPs can stay; withdrawals as a non-resident face non-resident withholding tax, which a treaty can lower.
3. An unpaid Home Buyers' Plan or Lifelong Learning Plan balance has special repayment rules on leaving; check current.
4. FHSA rules for non-residents limit tax-free home purchase withdrawals; check current.
5. The new country may tax these accounts differently.

steps.title: Tell banks and payers you are becoming a non-resident
prepare: List of Canadian accounts, investments and payers
steps.howTo:
1. Canadian payers take non-resident withholding tax from interest, dividends, pensions and RRSP payments to non-residents; a treaty may lower the rate.
2. Some brokers limit trading or new products for non-residents.
3. NR4 slips replace T5 and similar slips from then on.

steps.title: Decide what to do with permanent resident status
prepare: Days in Canada in the last 5 years
conditions: Only if you are a permanent resident, not a citizen
steps.howTo:
1. PR status is kept while the 730-days-in-5-years residency obligation can still be met; some time abroad with a Canadian citizen spouse or for a Canadian employer counts.
2. Status is not lost automatically; it ends by a formal decision, a removal order, or voluntary renunciation.
3. Voluntary renunciation is an IRCC application, useful for example to visit later as a visitor without questions about residency.
4. Not immigration advice; check the IRCC pages.

steps.title: Tell the provincial health plan you are leaving
documents: Health card or BC Services Card
steps.howTo:
1. British Columbia: Health Insurance BC is told of a permanent move; MSP ends and the BC Services Card is no longer used for health.
2. Ontario: ServiceOntario is told of the move; OHIP ends once someone no longer lives in Ontario.
3. Coverage in the new country, or private insurance, fills the gap from the departure date.

steps.title: Tell the CRA your departure date and stop benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Non-residents generally cannot get the Canada Child Benefit or the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit; provincial payments through the CRA stop too.
2. The CRA asks to be told the departure date promptly; payments received after leaving are paid back.
3. A foreign mailing address keeps CRA letters arriving.

steps.title: Update Service Canada for CPP and OAS
steps.howTo:
1. CPP is paid abroad once someone qualifies, wherever they live.
2. OAS is paid abroad indefinitely after at least 20 years in Canada after age 18; with less, it stops after 6 months away. GIS stops after 6 months abroad.
3. Canada has social security agreements with many countries, which can count time in both toward eligibility.
4. A copy of the CPP Statement of Contributions is worth keeping.

steps.title: Register to vote from abroad
conditions: Only if you are a Canadian citizen aged 18 or over
steps.howTo:
1. Elections Canada keeps an International Register of Electors; citizens abroad vote by special ballot in federal elections.
2. Provincial elections have their own rules.

steps.title: File the departure-year tax return
prepare: Forms T1161 and T1243, if they apply
World income after leaving, for credits
steps.howTo:
1. The final return is due April 30 of the year after leaving and shows the departure date in the residence section.
2. Income up to the departure date is taxed as a resident; credits may be prorated.
3. Later years: a Canadian return is filed only for some Canadian income, such as employment in Canada or a section 217 election on pensions.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to April 30.

title: Leaving China · moving abroad
summary: Paperwork plan on the China side of moving abroad to work, study or settle: notarised and apostilled documents, the police certificate, a driving record, property and a power of attorney, moving money, then the hukou, tax clearance, housing provident fund, pension and medical insurance once settled. Study-abroad steps are marked.
conditions: You are a Chinese citizen living in mainland China and moving to another country
Some steps apply only once you settle abroad or take another nationality, or only to students
The destination's own immigration steps are in its plans; this is a planning aid, not immigration or legal advice

sources.title: China Consular Service Network: apostille and consular legalisation (领事认证) — Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China (National Immigration Administration)
Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC — State Taxation Administration law library
Regulations on the Management of Housing Provident Fund — gov.cn
Housing Provident Fund Regulations, consolidated text (check current) — Ministry of Justice regulations database
Social Insurance Law of the PRC — State Taxation Administration law library
National Social Insurance Public Service Platform
National Healthcare Security Administration
Motor Vehicle Driving Licence Application and Use Provisions (MPS Order 162) — gov.cn
Notice on further facilitating personal current account foreign exchange business — State Administration of Foreign Exchange
China Higher Education Student Information (学信网) — degree and transcript verification
Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange: foreign degree recognition (学历认证)

steps.title: Get certified transcripts and degree reports for study applications
prepare: List of the schools' document rules
conditions: Only if you are going abroad to study
steps.howTo:
1. Schools abroad usually want sealed transcripts from the school or a notarised copy with translation.
2. 学信网 (CHSI) issues online verification reports for Chinese degrees and records that many schools and credential evaluators accept.
3. Each school and country sets its own rules; check them before ordering.
4. The 30 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Notarise birth, marriage, degree and other records (公证)
steps.howTo:
1. A notary office (公证处) issues notarial certificates for birth, kinship, marriage, degrees, no criminal record and similar facts, usually with an English translation attached.
2. The destination's immigration or school rules list which ones they want.
3. People born before birth medical certificates were common get a birth notarisation based on the hukou record.
4. The 30 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Get the no-criminal-record certificate (无犯罪记录证明)
steps.howTo:
1. Issued by the public security police station where the hukou or residence is; many cities also take applications online.
2. For use abroad it is usually notarised, then apostilled or legalised.
3. Destinations often accept only recent certificates, e.g. within 6 months; check their rule before applying.
4. Anyone who lived in other countries may need their certificates too.

steps.title: Apostille or legalise the notarised documents (附加证明书 / 领事认证)
prepare: Whether the destination is a party to the Apostille Convention
steps.howTo:
1. China joined the Hague Apostille Convention with effect from November 7, 2023.
2. For other party countries, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or an authorised local foreign affairs office adds an apostille to the notarised document; no embassy legalisation follows.
3. For countries outside the convention, documents go through consular legalisation: the foreign affairs office, then that country's embassy.
4. Notary offices often arrange this; the 21 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Get a driving record for exchanging the licence abroad
documents: Driving record or certificate from the vehicle management office
conditions: Only if you drive and want to exchange or use your licence abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Many countries let a licence holder exchange or shorten tests using proof of years of driving.
2. The vehicle management office or 交管12123 can give a record of the licence and driving history; ask which form the destination accepts.
3. A notarised translation is often asked for.
4. Keep the Chinese licence valid; it can be renewed through the app while abroad in many cases.

steps.title: Decide to keep, rent out or sell property
documents: Real estate ownership certificate (不动产权证书)
prepare: Mortgage and provident fund loan balance
conditions: Only if you own a home or other property in China
steps.howTo:
1. Owners abroad can keep property; a sale or rental needs someone in China or a power of attorney.
2. A sale follows the local online signing and transfer process; see the "Sold a home" plan if one exists for your region.
3. Tax on a sale depends on years held and whether it is the only home; check current rules. Not financial advice.

steps.title: Make a notarised power of attorney (委托公证)
documents: Notarised power of attorney (委托书公证)
prepare: Who will act for you, and their ID
Exactly which matters: property, bank, pension, hukou
conditions: Only if someone in China will handle matters for you
steps.howTo:
1. Many offices accept an agent only with a notarised power of attorney naming specific matters.
2. Before leaving, do it at a notary office in China; from abroad, a Chinese embassy or consulate, or a local notary plus apostille, can do it.
3. Property transfers usually want a separate, specific authorisation.

steps.title: Plan moving money abroad (购汇 and transfers)
prepare: Proof of purpose, e.g. tuition invoices
conditions: Only if you are taking savings with you
steps.howTo:
1. Individuals can buy foreign currency within a yearly convenience quota (年度便利化额度), currently US$50,000 a person; check current with the bank or SAFE.
2. The quota is for current items such as study, travel and living costs; capital items like buying property abroad are not allowed under it.
3. Tuition and living costs for study can be bought with proof beyond the quota in many banks; ask the bank.
4. Not financial advice; the bank and SAFE rules are the reference.

steps.title: Arrange the hukou and personnel file while studying (档案)
documents: File receipt from a talent centre or the school
prepare: Whether you will come back after the studies
conditions: Only if you are going abroad to study
steps.howTo:
1. Students abroad usually keep their hukou; it is not cancelled for study.
2. A personnel file (档案) can stay with the school or go to a talent exchange centre, so it is ready for a job, civil service or settlement on return.
3. Cities often have returnee (留学回国人员) settlement and job support that asks for the file and hukou records.

steps.title: Register with the Chinese embassy or consulate abroad
steps.howTo:
1. The 中国领事 (China Consular) app has voluntary registration and handles passport renewals, notarisation and pension life certificates from abroad.
2. Save the consulate for your area; it serves Chinese citizens there.

steps.title: Clear income tax before cancelling the hukou (税款清算)
conditions: Only if you settle abroad and cancel your hukou
steps.howTo:
1. The Individual Income Tax Law has people who cancel their Chinese hukou because they moved abroad settle their taxes before the cancellation.
2. Ask the local tax office or use the app; the police may ask for proof when cancelling.
3. The date is an estimate for once you settle abroad.

steps.title: Cancel the hukou once settled abroad (户口注销)
documents: Hukou cancellation certificate (注销户口证明)
prepare: Foreign permanent residence card or passport
Power of attorney, if someone else applies
conditions: Only once you settle abroad for good or take another nationality
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Nationality Law, a Chinese citizen settled abroad who voluntarily takes another nationality loses Chinese nationality automatically (Article 9); Article 3 says China does not recognise dual nationality.
2. The hukou and resident ID card of someone who has settled abroad or lost Chinese nationality are then cancelled at the police station.
3. Do the provident fund, pension, medical insurance and bank steps first where they ask for a valid ID or hukou; some ask for the cancellation proof instead.
4. The date is an estimate; move it to when you settle.

steps.title: Withdraw the housing provident fund on settling abroad (出境定居提取)
prepare: Proof of settling abroad, e.g. hukou cancellation or foreign residence
Power of attorney, if an agent applies
conditions: Only if you have a housing provident fund account and settle abroad
steps.howTo:
1. The provident fund regulations list settling abroad (出境定居) as a ground to withdraw the whole balance and close the account.
2. Fund centres set the proof they accept; ask before applying.
3. An outstanding provident fund loan is dealt with first.
4. Check current rules with the fund centre, including any recent amendment to the regulations.

steps.title: Ask what happens to the pension record (养老保险)
prepare: Power of attorney, if an agent applies
conditions: Only if you paid into the employee basic pension in China
steps.howTo:
1. A pension record normally stays in place after moving abroad, and can be claimed at retirement age with the minimum contribution years; pensions are paid abroad with a yearly life certificate.
2. The rules on ending the record and paying out the personal account in one sum depend on settling abroad or giving up Chinese nationality; ask the local social insurance office for the current rule before deciding.
3. China has social insurance agreements with some countries that can avoid double contributions for posted workers.
4. Not financial advice.

steps.title: Settle medical insurance and the personal account (医保)
prepare: Family members who share the account
conditions: Only if you have medical insurance in China
steps.howTo:
1. Basic medical insurance in China generally does not pay for care abroad.
2. Ask the local medical insurance office what happens to the personal account balance on settling abroad, and whether it can be used by family members first.
3. Stop the residents' medical insurance renewal if no one in China uses it.

steps.title: Get the foreign degree recognised on return (留服学历学位认证)
prepare: Passport with entry and exit records
conditions: Only if you studied abroad and return to China
steps.howTo:
1. The Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) certifies foreign degrees online; employers, civil service exams and city settlement schemes often ask for it.
2. Apply after the degree is awarded; check current documents and times on its site.
3. The date assumes a 4-year course; move it to after graduation.

title: Visiting Canada · Chinese passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a short visit to Canada on a Chinese passport: the visitor visa (TRV) or super visa, the online IRCC application, biometrics in China or abroad, arrival, visitor record and leaving on time.
conditions: You travel on a passport of the People's Republic of China
The visit is for tourism, visiting family or friends, or a short business trip
Not for study, work or moving to Canada
The date is the day you arrive in Canada

sources.title: Find out if you need a visa or eTA — Canada.ca
Entry requirements by country or territory — Canada.ca
Apply for a visitor visa — Canada.ca
Letter of invitation — Canada.ca
Parent and grandparent super visa — Canada.ca
Super visa: Host financial support and minimum income — Canada.ca
Medical exam requirements for visitors — Canada.ca
Biometrics: Where to give them — Canada.ca
Biometrics: When to give them — Canada.ca
IRCC fee list
Check processing times — Canada.ca
Minor children travelling to Canada — Canada.ca
Prepare for arrival as a visitor — Canada.ca
Extend your stay in Canada as a visitor — Canada.ca

steps.title: Confirm the visitor visa (TRV) is the route
prepare: How long you plan to stay
Whether a parent or grandparent is visiting a child or grandchild in Canada
steps.howTo:
1. China is on IRCC's list of visa-required countries, so a Chinese passport holder needs a visitor visa, also called a temporary resident visa (TRV); the eTA is not an option on this passport.
2. A TRV can be valid for up to 10 years, or until the passport or biometrics expire, whichever comes first; the officer decides single or multiple entry.
3. A valid TRV in an old passport can still be used alongside the new one while the visa is valid; check current on IRCC.
4. A parent or grandparent of a Canadian citizen or permanent resident who wants to stay longer than 6 months at a time can look at the super visa in the next step.
5. Run IRCC's "Find out if you need a visa or eTA" tool once to confirm; the answer decides the rest of this plan.

steps.title: Decide on a super visa instead
conditions: Only if you are a parent or grandparent of a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and want to stay longer than 6 months at a time
documents: Proof of host's Canadian citizenship or permanent residence
prepare: Your child's or grandchild's family size, counted the way IRCC asks
Their income against the minimum on the host financial support page
Proof of your relationship, such as the birth certificate (出生医学证明) or household register (户口簿)
steps.howTo:
1. The super visa lets a parent or grandparent stay for 5 years at a time, with multiple entries for up to 10 years.
2. For 6 months or less, IRCC points to the regular visitor visa instead.
3. The child or grandchild in Canada meets a minimum income for their family size and signs a promise of financial support; check the current table on the host financial support page.
4. The super visa also asks for private medical insurance and an immigration medical exam; the next steps cover them.
5. The application fee is the same as a visitor visa on the IRCC fee list.

steps.title: Gather passport, funds and ties papers
prepare: Passport valid at least 6 months past the travel date
Bank statements with several months of history, deposit or property certificates
Employment letter with approved leave, business licence (营业执照), or retirement certificate (退休证)
Previous passports and visas used to travel in the last 10 years
Certified English or French translations of Chinese documents
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC suggests renewing the passport first if it expires within 6 months of the travel date.
2. The officer looks at funds for the trip and ties that bring you back: job, family, property.
3. Documents not in English or French are uploaded with a translation and the translator's affidavit or certification; check current rules on IRCC.
4. After a short questionnaire, the IRCC account gives a personalized checklist; follow it over this list.

steps.title: Ask your host for an invitation letter and status proof
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends in Canada
documents: Copy of host's Canadian status document
prepare: Host's full name, date of birth, address, phone and job title
Copy of the host's Canadian passport, citizenship certificate, PR card or permit
Purpose and length of the visit, where you will stay and who pays
Names and dates of birth of the host's spouse and dependants
steps.howTo:
1. A letter of invitation helps but does not decide the application.
2. IRCC suggests it covers you (name, date of birth, address, relationship, purpose, length, where you stay, how you pay, when you leave) and the host (name, date of birth, address and phone, job, status in Canada with a copy of proof, family details).
3. For a super visa, it adds the host's signed promise of financial support for the whole visit and proof of income.
4. The host sends a signed scan to upload.

steps.title: Prepare a child's birth certificate and consent letter
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Both parents' names, addresses and phone numbers
Signed consent from the parent not travelling, or from both if the child travels with someone else
Copies of both parents' ID or passports
steps.howTo:
1. Each child applies on their own, with their own passport.
2. IRCC and border officers may ask for a consent letter when a child travels with one parent or with another adult; include contact details of the parent or parents not travelling.
3. Children under 14 are exempt from biometrics.
4. The IRCC page on minor children travelling lists what to bring.

steps.title: Buy the 1-year medical insurance for the super visa
conditions: Only if you are applying for a super visa
prepare: A Canadian insurer, or an insurer outside Canada approved by the minister
steps.howTo:
1. The super visa asks for private medical insurance valid for at least 1 year from entry, with at least $100,000 of emergency coverage.
2. It comes from a Canadian insurance company or a company outside Canada approved by the minister; a Chinese insurer only counts if it is on that list.
3. It is paid in full, or in instalments with a deposit; IRCC does not accept quotes.

steps.title: Take the immigration medical exam with a panel physician
conditions: Only if you are applying for a super visa, or IRCC asks for an exam
prepare: An IRCC panel physician clinic in China or where you live
Passport, glasses, medical records and list of medications
steps.howTo:
1. Super visa applicants take an immigration medical exam with an IRCC-approved panel physician; there are panel clinics in several Chinese cities, listed on IRCC.
2. Visitors staying 6 months or less usually need none; for longer stays IRCC checks where you lived in the past year.
3. Results are valid for 12 months, so book close to the application.

steps.title: Submit the application online through IRCC
prepare: Visa fee and biometrics fee, paid together
Scans of everything on the personalized checklist
steps.howTo:
1. Visitor visas are applied for online through the IRCC account; paper is only for people who cannot apply online, such as for a disability.
2. The IRCC fee list shows CAD $100 for a visitor visa (super visa included) and CAD $85 for biometrics per person, with family maximums; check current before paying.
3. Pay the biometrics fee with the application, or processing waits.
4. Applying from China or from a third country uses the same online form; only where you give biometrics and send the passport changes.

steps.title: Give biometrics at a visa application centre in China
conditions: Only if you are in mainland China when applying, aged 14 to 79
prepare: Check whether biometrics from the last 10 years are still on file
steps.howTo:
1. After the fee, IRCC sends a biometric instruction letter; you have 30 days from getting it to give fingerprints and photo.
2. Canada visa application centres (VAC) in China are in cities including Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Chongqing, Wuhan, Shenyang, Hangzhou, Jinan, Kunming and Nanjing; book on the VAC site.
3. Biometrics are given once every 10 years for temporary residence; a valid set on file means no new appointment.
4. The VAC also handles sending the passport in later.

steps.title: Give biometrics in the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally outside China, aged 14 to 79
documents: Residence permit or visa for that country
prepare: Proof of legal status where you live
Proof of ties there: job, study, lease
steps.howTo:
1. The online application is the same from any country; in it, give your current country of residence and status there.
2. Biometrics go to a VAC in the country you apply from; IRCC says that if there is none, any other VAC can be used.
3. People legally in the US can give biometrics at a US Application Support Center instead.
4. The officer weighs ties to where you live; upload the residence permit.

steps.title: Wait for the decision and send the passport
prepare: Check the IRCC processing time for your country of residence
Watch the IRCC account for requests
steps.howTo:
1. Processing times vary by country of residence; IRCC posts current estimates.
2. The 50 days here is only a planning estimate; move it to the posted time.
3. If approved, IRCC asks for the passport; it goes through a VAC so the visa counterfoil can be put in, then comes back.
4. Super visa holders get the visa counterfoil the same way; check the length and entries printed on it.

steps.title: Book flights and travel medical insurance
prepare: Visa dates and number of entries
Insurance for the whole stay, unless the super visa policy already covers it
steps.howTo:
1. Book after the visa is in the passport, so a refusal or delay does not cost the fare.
2. Visitors are generally not covered by provincial health insurance; travel medical insurance for a regular visitor visa is recommended rather than asked for.
3. Match the return date to the stay in the invitation letter.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: meet the border officer
prepare: Host address and phone in Canada
Return ticket and proof of funds in carry-on
For a super visa, ask for a passport stamp
steps.howTo:
1. A Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) officer checks identity, documents, funds, ties and plans to leave.
2. Most visitors can stay up to 6 months; the officer may stamp the passport or issue a visitor record with the leave-by date.
3. With no stamp, the stay ends 6 months after arrival, or when the passport expires if sooner.
4. A super visa holder can stay 5 years at a time; at a kiosk airport, ask for a stamp as proof of the entry date.

steps.title: Apply for a visitor record to extend the stay
conditions: Only if you want to stay past the date the officer gave you
prepare: Leave-by date from the stamp or visitor record
Funds and insurance for the extra time
steps.howTo:
1. To stay longer as a visitor, apply online for a visitor record from inside Canada.
2. IRCC asks for it at least 30 days before the current status expires; the IRCC fee list shows CAD $100 per person, check current.
3. The date here assumes a 6-month stay; move it to 30 days before your real leave-by date.
4. A visitor record is not a visa; leaving Canada and coming back still needs a valid visa.

steps.title: Leave on time and keep the records
prepare: Copies of the visa, stamps and visitor record
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the date on the stamp or visitor record, or 6 months after arrival if there is neither.
2. Keep the visa, stamps and boarding passes; the next application asks about travel in the last 10 years.
3. A multiple-entry visa can be used again while it and the passport are valid.
4. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 180 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting Canada · Philippine passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a Philippine passport holder visiting Canada for tourism or family: eTA or visitor visa, biometrics in Manila, Cebu or abroad, the super visa for parents, leaving the Philippines, arrival, visitor record and coming home.
conditions: You hold a Philippine passport and are not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident
You are visiting for tourism or to see family or friends, not to work, study or immigrate
The date is the day you arrive in Canada
This is a planning aid, not immigration advice; the IRCC and Philippine agency pages are the reference

eTA for certain visa-required travellers — Canada.ca
Apply for a visitor visa — Canada.ca
Letter of invitation — Canada.ca
Parent and grandparent super visa — Canada.ca

steps.title: Check whether you can use an eTA or need a visitor visa
prepare: Whether you held a Canadian visitor visa in the past 10 years
Whether you hold a US non-immigrant visa that is valid today
Whether you are flying in, or coming by land or sea
steps.howTo:
1. The Philippines is a visa-required country for Canada, but it is on IRCC's list of countries whose citizens can get an electronic travel authorization (eTA) instead, when all conditions are met.
2. The eTA route: you held a Canadian visitor visa (temporary resident visa, TRV) in the past 10 years, or you hold a valid US non-immigrant visa when you apply, and you fly to or through a Canadian airport.
3. Arriving by car, bus, train or boat, including a cruise, needs a visitor visa even if you qualify for the eTA.
4. Everyone else on a Philippine passport applies for a visitor visa; it can be valid for up to 10 years, or until the passport or biometrics expire.
5. A parent or grandparent of a Canadian citizen or permanent resident wanting to stay longer than 6 months at a time can look at the super visa next.

steps.title: Renew the Philippine passport if it runs short
conditions: Only if your passport expires within 6 months of the travel date
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC asks for a passport valid for at least 6 months from the date you plan to travel, and a visa is not issued past the passport expiry.
2. Book a renewal on the DFA online appointment system.
3. An eTA is linked to the passport number, so a new passport needs a new eTA.

steps.title: Apply for the eTA online
conditions: Only if you are flying and held a Canadian visitor visa in the past 10 years or hold a valid US non-immigrant visa
prepare: US visa or old Canadian visa details
Check the current fee (CAD 7 when this plan was reviewed)
steps.howTo:
1. Apply only on the official Government of Canada eTA page; other sites charge extra.
2. Most approvals come by email within minutes, but some take several days and ask for documents.
3. The eTA is valid for up to 5 years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.
4. Skip the visitor visa steps below, apart from the invitation letter if visiting family.

steps.title: Decide on a super visa
conditions: Only if you are a parent or grandparent of a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and want to stay longer than 6 months at a time
prepare: Your child or grandchild's proof of income for their family size
A 1-year Canadian or approved medical insurance policy
An immigration medical exam with a panel physician in the Philippines
steps.howTo:
1. The super visa lets a parent or grandparent stay up to 5 years at a time, with multiple entries for up to 10 years.
2. The host in Canada meets a minimum income, signs a promise of financial support, and sends an invitation letter.
3. You buy private medical insurance valid for at least 1 year with at least CAD 100,000 of emergency coverage, and take an immigration medical exam.
4. The host side is covered in detail in the "Visitors to Canada" plan; for 6 months or less, the regular visitor visa is the usual route.

steps.title: Gather proof of ties and funds
conditions: Only if you need a visitor visa or super visa
prepare: Certificate of employment with position, salary and approved leave dates
Bank statements with at least 6 months of history
Business registration (DTI or SEC) if self-employed
Property titles or other ties to the Philippines
Previous passports and visas used in the last 10 years
steps.howTo:
1. The officer weighs whether you will leave Canada at the end of the visit: work, family, property and funds.
2. Scan everything clearly; IRCC takes these as uploads, not paper.
3. Translate documents that are not in English or French and include the translator's declaration.

steps.title: Get an invitation letter and your host's status proof
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends
documents: Copy of host's Canadian passport, PR card or permit
prepare: Host name, date of birth, address, phone, job and status in Canada
Your relationship, with PSA birth or marriage certificates if family
Purpose, dates, where you will stay and who pays
Host's proof of income if they are supporting the trip
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC says an invitation letter may help but does not decide the application.
2. The host writes and signs it, covering your details, theirs, the purpose and length of the trip, where you will stay and how it is paid for.
3. For a super visa, the letter adds a signed promise of financial support and the host's family size.
4. The host sends a signed scan for you to upload.

steps.title: Prepare a child's travel papers
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: A consent letter signed by any parent not travelling, with their contact details and ID copy
Custody or guardianship papers if they apply
steps.howTo:
1. Each child has their own passport and their own eTA or visa application.
2. IRCC says a child under 18 may need a letter authorizing the travel, plus custody or adoption papers where they apply, when travelling alone or with only one parent or another adult; officers can ask for it.
3. The PSA birth certificate shows who the parents are.
4. Children under 14 do not give biometrics.

steps.title: Take the immigration medical exam
conditions: Only if you are applying for a super visa, or staying over 6 months in some cases
prepare: An IRCC panel physician in the Philippines, from the IRCC list
steps.howTo:
1. Super visa applicants take an upfront immigration medical exam with an IRCC panel physician; the clinic sends results to IRCC.
2. Results are valid for 12 months, so book close to the application.

steps.title: Submit the visitor visa application online
conditions: Only if you need a visitor visa or super visa
prepare: Digital photo meeting the IRCC specifications
Check the current fees (CAD 100 visa plus CAD 85 biometrics per person when this plan was reviewed)
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online through the IRCC account; paper applications are only for people who cannot apply online, such as for a disability.
2. The questionnaire builds a personalised document checklist.
3. Pay the visa and biometrics fees together to avoid delays; a family applying together pays capped amounts.
4. You can apply online from wherever you are; the country you apply from sets which visa office and processing time apply.

steps.title: Give biometrics at VFS in Manila or Cebu
conditions: Only if you need a visitor visa or super visa, are aged 14 to 79, apply from the Philippines, and have no biometrics on file from the last 10 years
prepare: Book a VFS appointment as soon as the biometric instruction letter arrives
steps.howTo:
1. After the fee is paid, IRCC sends a biometric instruction letter; you have 30 days to give fingerprints and a photo.
2. The Philippines has Canada visa application centres in Manila and Cebu, run by VFS Global.
3. Bring the letter and passport; VFS can also handle passport submission later for a fee.
4. Biometrics count for 10 years for visitor applications.

steps.title: Give biometrics in the country where you are
conditions: Only if you need a visitor visa or super visa, are aged 14 to 79, and are living or staying outside the Philippines
prepare: The nearest visa application centre that offers biometrics
Proof of legal status in that country, such as a residence or work permit
steps.howTo:
1. Biometrics can be given at any visa application centre worldwide that offers the service; check the centre on the IRCC list before booking.
2. In the US, Application Support Centers take IRCC biometrics, but only for people already legally in the US.
3. Applying from a country where you live legally is common; IRCC may look at your status and ties there as well as in the Philippines.
4. The processing time is the one for the country you apply from; check it on the IRCC page.

steps.title: Wait for the decision and send the passport for the visa
conditions: Only if you applied for a visitor visa or super visa
prepare: Check the IRCC processing time for the Philippines or your country of residence
Watch the IRCC account for requests
steps.howTo:
1. Processing times change often; the 50 days here is only an estimate, so move this date to the posted time.
2. If approved, IRCC asks for the passport; submit it through VFS in Manila or Cebu, or the centre where you are.
3. Check the visa counterfoil: name, dates, number of entries.
4. Book flights once the visa is in the passport.

steps.title: Get a DSWD travel clearance for a child
conditions: Only if a Filipino child under 18 is leaving without a parent, or with someone other than a parent
prepare: Details of the adult travelling with the child
steps.howTo:
1. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) issues travel clearances for Filipino minors travelling abroad alone or with an adult who is not a parent.
2. A child travelling with a parent generally does not need one; check current exemptions on the DSWD site.
3. Apply online or at a DSWD field office; check current processing time and validity, and apply earlier if you can.

steps.title: Check whether a CFO certificate applies
conditions: Only if you are going to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), or emigrating, rather than just visiting
prepare: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship
steps.howTo:
1. The Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO) runs guidance and counselling for Filipinos leaving to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), and registration for emigrants; the Bureau of Immigration checks the CFO certificate at departure.
2. A short visit on a visitor visa or eTA is generally not an emigrant departure, but visiting a foreign partner can prompt questions at the counter; check with the CFO which case yours is before flying.
3. Moving to Canada as a permanent resident is outside this plan.

steps.title: Pay the Philippine travel tax or check the exemption
prepare: Proof of exemption or reduced rate, if any
steps.howTo:
1. Filipinos and some residents leaving the Philippines pay travel tax to TIEZA: PHP 1,620 economy or PHP 2,700 first class at the full rate when this plan was reviewed.
2. Many airline tickets bought in the Philippines include it; check the fare breakdown.
3. Reduced rates and exemptions exist, for example for some minors and overseas Filipino workers; check TIEZA.
4. If not included, pay online on the TIEZA site or at the airport counter before check-in.

steps.title: Pack papers for the Bureau of Immigration departure check
prepare: eTA approval email, if travelling on an eTA
Proof of work, approved leave, business or school
Invitation letter and relationship proof if visiting family or friends
Affidavit of support from the sponsor if someone else pays
steps.howTo:
1. At departure, a Bureau of Immigration (BI) officer checks the passport, visa or eTA, boarding pass and return ticket, following inter-agency (IACAT) departure guidelines meant to stop trafficking and illegal recruitment.
2. Some travellers are sent to secondary inspection and asked for supporting papers; being refused departure is called offloading.
3. Keep the papers in the carry-on, not the checked bag.
4. Check the current IACAT guidelines on the BI site before the trip.

steps.title: Leave the Philippines
prepare: Arrive at the airport early for immigration lines
Check any eTravel or e-Gate registration the BI currently asks departing travellers for
steps.howTo:
1. Check in, then go through BI departure; answer questions about the trip plainly.
2. If referred to secondary inspection, show the papers from the previous step.
3. The date here is the day before arrival; move it to the real flight.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: meet the border officer
prepare: For a super visa, the insurance policy
steps.howTo:
1. A Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) officer decides entry and the length of stay.
2. Most visitors can stay up to 6 months; the officer may stamp the passport or issue a visitor record with a leave-by date.
3. With no stamp, the stay ends 6 months after arrival, or when the passport expires if sooner.
4. A super visa holder can stay up to 5 years at a time; ask for a passport stamp as proof of entry.

steps.title: Apply for a visitor record to extend the stay
conditions: Only if you want to stay past the date the officer gave you
prepare: Proof of funds and insurance for the extra time
Check the current fee (CAD 100 when this plan was reviewed)
steps.howTo:
1. To stay longer as a visitor, apply online for a visitor record from inside Canada.
2. IRCC asks for the application at least 30 days before the current status expires; you can stay while it is processed if applied for in time.
3. A visitor record is not a visa; to re-enter Canada after leaving, a valid visa or eTA is still needed.
4. The date here assumes a 6-month stay; move it to 30 days before the real leave-by date.

steps.title: Register on eTravel before flying home
steps.howTo:
1. eTravel is the Philippine government's free online travel declaration; arriving travellers, Filipinos included, register before landing, usually within 72 hours of the flight; check the current window.
2. Use etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app only; look-alike sites charge fees.
3. Show the QR code on arrival in the Philippines.

steps.title: Leave Canada on time and keep the records
prepare: Copies of the visa, eTA, stamps and visitor record
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the stamped or visitor record date, or 6 months after arrival if there is neither.
2. Keep the visa, stamps and boarding passes; a Canadian visa held in the past 10 years is what makes a later eTA possible.
3. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 30 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting the United States · Chinese passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a short US visit on a Chinese passport: the B1/B2 visitor visa, DS-160, interview in China or a third country, EVUS, arrival, extending the stay and leaving on time.
conditions: You travel on a passport of the People's Republic of China
The visit is short: tourism, visiting family or friends, or business on the same B1/B2 visa
Not for study, work or moving to the United States
The date is the day you arrive in the United States

sources.title: Visitor visa — U.S. Department of State
Online Nonimmigrant Visa Application (DS-160) — U.S. Department of State
Photo requirements — U.S. Department of State
Fees for visa services — U.S. Department of State
Visa reciprocity: China — U.S. Department of State
Global visa wait times — U.S. Department of State
Nonimmigrant visas — U.S. Embassy and Consulates in China
Electronic Visa Update System (EVUS) — U.S. Customs and Border Protection
I-94 arrival record — U.S. Customs and Border Protection
Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status — USCIS
Fee schedule (G-1055) — USCIS
