Know before you visit — U.S. Customs and Border Protection
Border search of electronic devices — U.S. Customs and Border Protection

steps.title: Check which visa the trip needs
prepare: How long you plan to stay
Any earlier US visas, refusals or overstays
steps.howTo:
1. China is not in the Visa Waiver Program, so ESTA is not an option on a Chinese passport; a short visit for tourism, family or business uses the B1/B2 visitor visa.
2. The same applies when only changing planes in the US: transit uses a C visa or a valid B1/B2 visa; check current.
3. The State Department reciprocity page for China lists B1/B2 visas for Chinese nationals as multiple entry for up to 10 years; the officer decides what is issued.
4. A valid B1/B2 visa already in an old passport can still be used with the new passport; check that it has not expired.
5. Birth tourism is not a permitted purpose on a visitor visa.

steps.title: Gather passport, photo and supporting papers
prepare: Passport valid at least 6 months beyond the planned stay
A digital photo meeting the State Department photo rules
Recent bank statements, property or deposit certificates
Employment letter with approved leave, or school or retirement papers
Rough itinerary and where you will stay
Previous passports with US or other visas
steps.howTo:
1. The State Department asks for a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the stay, unless a country agreement exempts it; renew first if it will be close.
2. The photo is uploaded in the DS-160; it follows the State Department photo rules.
3. The interview focuses on the purpose of the trip, the ability to pay, and ties that bring you back to China or the country where you live: job, family, property, study.
4. Supporting papers are not always asked for, but having them ready at the interview helps; bring originals.

steps.title: Ask your host for an invitation letter and status proof
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends in the United States
documents: Copy of host's US status document
prepare: Host's full name, address, phone and relationship to you
Copy of the host's US passport, green card, or visa and I-94
Dates of the visit and where you will stay
Host's proof of income, if the host is paying for the trip
steps.howTo:
1. The State Department does not list an invitation letter as a requirement; officers decide mainly on the interview and the applicant's own ties.
2. A short letter from the host with the relationship, dates and where you will stay, plus a copy of the host's status, still helps explain the trip.
3. If the host is paying, add their recent pay slips, tax return or bank statement.
4. For the host: keep the letter factual; the visitor answers the questions at the interview.

steps.title: Prepare a child's birth certificate and parents' consent
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Both parents' passports or ID cards and household register (户口簿)
Signed consent from the parent not travelling, or from both if the child travels with someone else
The travelling parents' visas, if the child is going with them
steps.howTo:
1. Each traveller, including a baby, needs their own passport, DS-160 and visa.
2. Bring the birth certificate to show the parents; with one parent absent, a signed consent letter with a copy of their ID answers the usual question.
3. The June 2025 State Department page said an interview is generally not asked of applicants 13 and younger; check current, as waiver rules changed in 2025.
4. A parent usually goes with the child to the appointment.

steps.title: Fill in the DS-160 online
prepare: Travel history for the last 5 years
US address or hotel for the stay
Social media handles used in the last 5 years
steps.howTo:
1. Fill in Form DS-160 in English on the State Department Consular Electronic Application Center; save the application ID, as the session times out.
2. Choose the post where you will be interviewed; it matches the next step.
3. Upload the photo in the form.
4. Print or save the confirmation page with the barcode; the appointment and interview use it.
5. Answers are checked against earlier applications and the interview; keep them consistent.

steps.title: Pay the fee and book the interview in China
conditions: Only if you are applying in mainland China
prepare: The consular district for where you live or your hukou
Check current wait times at each post
steps.howTo:
1. In mainland China the embassy in Beijing and the consulates (such as Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenyang) handle visitor visas; check current which posts are interviewing.
2. Register on the appointment website linked from the embassy's visa pages, pay the application fee, then pick a date.
3. The B1/B2 application fee was US$185 when the State Department page was checked in 2025; a separate visa integrity fee has also been legislated, so check current fees before paying.
4. Waits for an interview can run to months; the 280-day start in this plan is an estimate to cover that. Check the State Department wait-time tool.
5. Renewals of an earlier B1/B2 visa may qualify for an interview waiver (dropbox); the rules changed in 2025, so check current eligibility.

steps.title: Pay the fee and book the interview where you live abroad
conditions: Only if you live legally in another country, such as Canada, and are applying there
documents: Residence permit or visa for that country
prepare: Proof of legal status there: permit, PR card or long-stay visa
Proof of ties there: job, study, lease
Check the local embassy page for third-country nationals
steps.howTo:
1. A Chinese citizen living legally abroad (for example in Canada) can apply at a US embassy or consulate in that country; register on that country's appointment website and pay the fee in its currency.
2. The State Department has tightened where applicants may apply; applying in a country where you are only visiting may not be accepted. Check the local embassy page for the current rule.
3. Bring your residence permit; the officer weighs ties to where you live, not only to China.
4. Wait times differ by city; compare them with the wait-time tool.

steps.title: Attend the visa interview
prepare: Invitation letter and host documents, if visiting family
Short, honest answers about the trip and when you come back
steps.howTo:
1. Fingerprints are taken and a consular officer asks about the trip, money and ties at home.
2. At the end the officer approves, refuses (usually under section 214(b)), or hands a form for administrative processing (section 221(g)).
3. If approved, the passport stays with the post for the visa to be printed; delivery or pickup follows the embassy instructions.
4. The 90-day date is an estimate; move it to your real appointment.

steps.title: Get the passport back and check the visa
prepare: Check name, date of birth, visa type, entries and expiry
steps.howTo:
1. Check the printed visa for mistakes before booking; report errors to the post straight away.
2. Administrative processing (221(g)) can take weeks or longer; wait for the result before paying for flights.
3. The visa lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides entry and length of stay.

steps.title: Enrol in EVUS before flying
steps.howTo:
1. Holders of a PRC passport with a 10-year B1/B2 visa update their details through EVUS on the official site evus.gov before travel.
2. The State Department says an enrolment lasts 2 years, or until a new passport or new B1/B2 visa, whichever comes first.
3. Airlines check EVUS before boarding; without it you can be denied boarding.
4. Use only evus.gov; third-party sites charge extra. Check the current fee there.
5. It repeats: enrol again every 2 years or after a new passport or visa.

steps.title: Book flights and travel medical insurance
prepare: Return date inside the planned stay
Insurance covering US medical costs for the whole stay
steps.howTo:
1. Book after the visa is in hand, so a refusal or delay does not cost the fare.
2. US medical care is expensive and visitors are generally not covered by any public plan; travel medical insurance is not asked for by the visa but is widely bought.
3. Keep the return booking consistent with what you said at the interview.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
Phones and laptops you are comfortable having inspected
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.
5. US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) can inspect phones, laptops and other devices at the border, US citizens included; see its page on border searches of electronic devices.
6. Cash and monetary instruments over USD 10,000 in total are reported on FinCEN Form 105.
7. Visa forms ask for social media identifiers; keep what you give at the border consistent with the application.

steps.title: Arrival: entry inspection and the I-94 record
prepare: Return ticket and proof of funds in carry-on
Invitation letter and host contact, if visiting family
steps.howTo:
1. A CBP officer asks about the purpose and length of the trip and decides whether to admit you and until when.
2. B2 visitors are commonly admitted for up to 6 months; the real limit is the date on the electronic I-94, not the visa expiry.
3. Look up the I-94 on the CBP site a few days after arrival and check the admit-until date.
4. The visa can outlast the stay; each entry gets its own I-94.

steps.title: File Form I-539 to extend the stay
conditions: Only if you need to stay past the I-94 admit-until date
prepare: Reason for staying longer, with papers such as medical letters
Proof of funds for the extra time
Return ticket or plan to leave
Current USCIS fee from the G-1055 fee schedule
steps.howTo:
1. Extending a B1/B2 stay, or changing to another status, is filed with USCIS on Form I-539 from inside the US.
2. It is filed before the admit-until date on the I-94; USCIS suggests at least 45 days before.
3. The date here assumes a 6-month admission; move it to 45 days before your real I-94 date.
4. Check the fee on the USCIS fee schedule; processing can outlast the extra time asked for.
5. Not immigration advice; the USCIS page is the reference.

steps.title: Leave on time and keep the records
prepare: Copy of the I-94 and travel history from the CBP site
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the I-94 date, or by the date USCIS grants if an extension was approved.
2. Staying past it, even by a day, voids the visa and makes later visas harder to get.
3. Keep boarding passes and the I-94 history; the next DS-160 asks about earlier trips.
4. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 180 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

steps.title: Check the I-94 shows the departure
steps.howTo:
1. Look up the travel history on the CBP I-94 site; the departure shows once the airline reports it.
2. If it is missing, the CBP site explains how to send proof of departure, such as boarding passes and passport stamps.
3. A missing departure can read as an overstay at the next visa application.

title: Visiting the United States · Philippine passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a Philippine passport holder visiting the US for tourism, family or a business trip on a B1/B2 visa: DS-160, the interview in Manila or abroad, leaving the Philippines, arrival, extensions and coming home.
conditions: You hold a Philippine passport and no US passport or green card
You are visiting for tourism, family or friends, or a short business trip, not to work or study
The date is the day you arrive in the United States
This is a planning aid, not immigration advice; the State Department, US Embassy Manila and Philippine agency pages are the reference

sources.title: Visitor visa — travel.state.gov
DS-160: Online nonimmigrant visa application — travel.state.gov
Photo requirements — travel.state.gov
Fees for visa services — travel.state.gov
Visa appointment wait times — travel.state.gov
Visa Waiver Program — travel.state.gov
Nonimmigrant visas — U.S. Embassy in the Philippines
I-94 arrival/departure record — U.S. Customs and Border Protection
I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status — USCIS
Philippine passport appointments — Department of Foreign Affairs
Travel tax — TIEZA
Bureau of Immigration — Philippines
Commission on Filipinos Overseas
Travel clearance for minors — DSWD
eTravel — Philippine travel information system
Know before you visit — U.S. Customs and Border Protection
Border search of electronic devices — U.S. Customs and Border Protection

steps.title: Check which US visa fits the trip
prepare: How long you plan to stay
Any earlier US visa, and when it expired
steps.howTo:
1. The Philippines is not in the US Visa Waiver Program, so ESTA is not an option on a Philippine passport; a visitor visa is needed.
2. The B1/B2 visitor visa covers tourism, visiting family or friends, medical treatment and business meetings; work and study need other visas.
3. If you hold an unexpired B1/B2 visa in a valid or old passport, you can travel on it; carry both passports if the visa is in the old one.
4. The officer decides the visa length and entries; check the reciprocity table on travel.state.gov for what is typical for the Philippines.
5. Holders of another passport that is in the Visa Waiver Program can check ESTA instead of this plan.

steps.title: Renew the Philippine passport if it runs short
conditions: Only if your passport expires within about 6 months after the trip, or has few blank pages
steps.howTo:
1. Book a renewal on the DFA online appointment system; walk-in lanes exist for some groups.
2. The US generally expects the passport to be valid for 6 months past the stay unless the country has an agreement; check the current rule for the Philippines on travel.state.gov.
3. Renew before the DS-160, since the form asks for the passport number.
4. Processing times vary by site; check current.

steps.title: Gather proof of ties and funds
prepare: Certificate of employment with position, salary and approved leave dates
Recent bank statements or a bank certificate
Business registration (DTI or SEC) if self-employed
Property titles, school enrolment or other ties to home
Rough itinerary and where you will stay
steps.howTo:
1. A B1/B2 interview mainly weighs whether you will return home: work, family, property and study in the Philippines.
2. The officer may not look at papers; bring them anyway, organised so you can hand over one quickly.
3. Old passports with earlier US or other visas help show travel history.
4. If someone else pays, bring their letter and proof of funds.

steps.title: Get an invitation letter and your host's status proof
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends
documents: Copy of host's US passport, green card or visa
prepare: Host name, US address, phone and status in the US
Your relationship, with PSA birth or marriage certificates if family
Dates of the visit and who pays for what
Host's proof of income if they are supporting the trip
steps.howTo:
1. The US does not ask for an invitation letter for a B2 visa, but it can back up the purpose of the trip.
2. The host writes a short signed letter: who you are, the relationship, dates, where you will stay and who pays.
3. If the host sponsors the trip, add their recent bank statement or tax return; Form I-134 is not used for ordinary visitor visas.
4. Relationship documents help if the officer asks how you are related.

steps.title: Prepare a child's application papers
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Both parents' passports and visas, or proof of their status
Written consent from a parent who is not travelling or not attending
School enrolment and the school break dates
steps.howTo:
1. Each child, including babies, needs their own passport, DS-160 and visa.
2. A parent or legal guardian fills in the DS-160 for a young child and usually attends with them; check current rules on which children still need to appear in person.
3. The PSA birth certificate shows who the parents are.
4. If only one parent travels, bring a signed consent letter from the other; the Philippine departure side is in the DSWD step below.

steps.title: Fill in the DS-160 and pay the visa fee
prepare: Passport, travel history for the last 5 years, and past US visas
Work and education history, family details, US address
A recent photo meeting the State Department photo rules
Check the current B1/B2 fee (MRV fee) and whether a separate visa integrity fee applies
steps.howTo:
1. Complete the DS-160 online and save the application ID; the form times out, so save often.
2. Answers are checked against the interview, so keep them consistent and truthful.
3. Create a profile on the embassy's appointment site, then pay the application fee; it is not refundable and is usually valid for a limited time to book, so check the current rule.
4. US law passed in 2025 added a visa integrity fee paid when a visa is issued; check current status and amount on travel.state.gov.
5. Each traveller, including children, has their own DS-160 and fee.

steps.title: Book the interview, or check for an interview waiver
prepare: The current appointment wait for Manila on travel.state.gov
Whether your last B1/B2 visa qualifies for renewal without an interview
steps.howTo:
1. Waits for a first visitor-visa interview in Manila have often been many months; the 300 days this plan starts ahead is an estimate, so check the current wait tool and book as early as you can.
2. Since 2025 the State Department has narrowed interview waivers; the main remaining case is renewing a full-validity B1/B2 that expired within the last 12 months and was issued when you were 18 or older. Check current eligibility on the appointment site.
3. If a waiver applies, the site gives a document drop-off option instead of an interview.
4. Expedited appointments exist for urgent reasons such as a family emergency; a tourist trip normally does not qualify.

steps.title: Attend the interview at the US Embassy in Manila
conditions: Only if you are applying in the Philippines and need an interview
prepare: Old passports with earlier US visas
The supporting papers from the earlier steps, in one folder
Check the embassy list of items not allowed inside; bags and electronics are restricted
steps.howTo:
1. Visa interviews in the Philippines take place at the consular section of the US Embassy on Roxas Boulevard, Manila.
2. Fingerprints are taken, then a short interview; answer briefly and truthfully.
3. If approved, the passport stays for visa printing and is sent back by courier or held for pick-up as chosen on the appointment site.
4. A refusal under section 214(b) means the officer was not convinced of ties to home; you can reapply with a new fee when circumstances change.
5. A 221(g) slip means more papers or administrative processing; follow its instructions.

steps.title: Apply at a US embassy in the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally in a country other than the Philippines
prepare: Residence permit or visa for that country, valid well past the interview
Proof of work or study there
That country's appointment site and its local fee payment method
steps.howTo:
1. Since September 2025 the State Department asks nonimmigrant visa applicants to apply in their country of nationality or of residence; check current rules.
2. If you live legally in, for example, Canada, Japan or the UK, you can apply at the US embassy or consulate there and show proof of residence.
3. A short stay somewhere as a tourist is generally not residence for this purpose; check with that post before booking.
4. Ties the officer weighs are then to the country where you live, plus the Philippines.
5. Wait times differ by post; check the wait tool for that city.

steps.title: Drop off documents for a renewal without interview
conditions: Only if the appointment site confirms you qualify for an interview waiver
prepare: The drop-off appointment and its document list
Old passport with the previous visa
steps.howTo:
1. Deliver the passport and documents to the drop-off location the appointment site names.
2. The consular officer may still call you in for an interview.
3. Processing time varies; plan without the passport for several weeks.

steps.title: Get the passport back and check the visa
prepare: Check name, date of birth, passport number, visa type, entries and expiry
steps.howTo:
1. Check the visa foil for errors right away and report them to the embassy.
2. The visa expiry date is the last day to enter, not how long you can stay; the stay is set at the border.
3. Book flights only once the visa is in hand, so a refusal or delay does not cost the fare.

steps.title: Get a DSWD travel clearance for a child
conditions: Only if a Filipino child under 18 is leaving without a parent, or with someone other than a parent
prepare: Details of the adult travelling with the child
steps.howTo:
1. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) issues travel clearances for Filipino minors travelling abroad alone or with an adult who is not a parent.
2. A child travelling with a parent generally does not need one; check current exemptions on the DSWD site.
3. Apply online or at a DSWD field office; check current processing time and validity.

steps.title: Check whether a CFO certificate applies
conditions: Only if you are going to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), or emigrating, rather than just visiting
prepare: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship
steps.howTo:
1. The Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO) runs guidance and counselling for Filipinos leaving to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), and registration for emigrants; the Bureau of Immigration checks the CFO certificate at departure.
2. A short visit on a B1/B2 visitor visa is generally not an emigrant departure, but visiting a foreign partner can prompt questions at the counter; check with the CFO which case yours is before flying.
3. Registration is booked online on the CFO site; check current requirements and fees.

steps.title: Pay the Philippine travel tax or check the exemption
prepare: Proof of exemption or reduced rate, if any
steps.howTo:
1. Filipinos and some residents leaving the Philippines pay travel tax to TIEZA: PHP 1,620 economy or PHP 2,700 first class at the full rate when this plan was reviewed.
2. Many airline tickets bought in the Philippines include it; check the fare breakdown.
3. Reduced rates and exemptions exist, for example for some minors and overseas Filipino workers; check TIEZA.
4. If not included, pay online on the TIEZA site or at the airport counter before check-in.

steps.title: Pack papers for the Bureau of Immigration departure check
prepare: Proof of work, approved leave, business or school
Invitation letter and relationship proof if visiting family or friends
Affidavit of support from the sponsor if someone else pays
steps.howTo:
1. At departure, a Bureau of Immigration (BI) officer checks the passport, visa, boarding pass and return ticket, following inter-agency (IACAT) departure guidelines meant to stop trafficking and illegal recruitment.
2. Some travellers are sent to secondary inspection and asked for supporting papers; being refused departure is called offloading.
3. Keep the papers in the carry-on, not the checked bag.
4. Check the current IACAT guidelines on the BI site before the trip.

steps.title: Leave the Philippines
prepare: Arrive at the airport early for immigration lines
Check any eTravel or e-Gate registration the BI currently asks departing travellers for
steps.howTo:
1. Check in, then go through BI departure; answer questions about the trip plainly.
2. If referred to secondary inspection, show the papers from the previous step.
3. The date here is the day before arrival; move it to the real flight.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
Phones and laptops you are comfortable having inspected
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.
5. US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) can inspect phones, laptops and other devices at the border, US citizens included; see its page on border searches of electronic devices.
6. Cash and monetary instruments over USD 10,000 in total are reported on FinCEN Form 105.
7. Visa forms ask for social media identifiers; keep what you give at the border consistent with the application.

steps.title: Arrival: meet US Customs and Border Protection
prepare: Return ticket and proof of funds in carry-on
steps.howTo:
1. A visa lets you ask to enter; the Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer decides admission and the length of stay.
2. B2 visitors are often admitted for up to 6 months; the date is on the electronic I-94 record.
3. Look up the I-94 on the CBP site after arrival and note the admit-until date; the rest of this plan uses it.
4. Declare food, cash over USD 10,000 and other items as the customs form asks.

steps.title: File I-539 to extend the stay
conditions: Only if you need to stay past the I-94 date
prepare: Proof of funds for the extra time
steps.howTo:
1. File Form I-539 with USCIS before the I-94 date passes; USCIS suggests filing well ahead, at least 45 days before if possible.
2. Changing from B1/B2 to another status, such as student, is filed on the same form but has its own limits; check USCIS.
3. Staying past the I-94 date without a pending timely application can void the visa and lead to bars on returning.
4. The date here assumes a 6-month admission; move it to 45 days before the real I-94 date.

steps.title: Register on eTravel before flying home
steps.howTo:
1. eTravel is the Philippine government's free online travel declaration; arriving travellers, Filipinos included, register before landing, usually within 72 hours of the flight; check the current window.
2. Use etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app only; look-alike sites charge fees.
3. Show the QR code on arrival in the Philippines.

steps.title: Leave the US on time and keep the records
prepare: Copies of the visa, I-94 and boarding passes
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the I-94 date; the airline reports the departure to CBP.
2. Keep boarding passes and the I-94 printout; later visa applications ask about US travel history.
3. A multiple-entry visa can be used again while it is valid, but each entry has its own I-94 date.
4. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 30 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

steps.title: Check the I-94 shows the departure
steps.howTo:
1. Look up the travel history on the CBP I-94 site; the departure shows once the airline reports it.
2. If it is missing, the CBP site explains how to send proof of departure, such as boarding passes and passport stamps.
3. A missing departure can read as an overstay at the next visa application.

title: Visiting China · Philippine passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a Philippine passport holder visiting mainland China for tourism or family, from checking the few visa-free options to the L or Q2 visa in Manila or abroad, leaving the Philippines, the arrival card, registration, extensions and coming home.
conditions: You hold a Philippine passport
You are visiting mainland China for tourism or to see family or friends
Not for work, study or moving to China; those use other visas
The date is the day you arrive in China
This is a planning aid, not immigration advice; the Chinese embassy, NIA and Philippine agency pages are the reference

sources.title: List of Countries Covered by Unilateral Visa Exemption Policies (as of February 17, 2026) — National Immigration Administration
Visa-Free Transit Policies (August 20, 2026) — National Immigration Administration
Visa for China (Mainland Only) — Chinese Embassy in the Philippines
China Expands Allowed Purposes of Visa-Free Entry to Hainan for 59 Countries — Chinese Embassy in the Philippines
Notice on the Opening of the Chinese Visa Application Service Center in Manila — Chinese Embassy in the Philippines
Notice on Launching the China Online Visa Processing System — Chinese Embassy in the Philippines
Notice: reduced visa fees until December 31, 2026 — Chinese Embassy in the Philippines
Chinese Visa Application Service Center, Manila
Online Arrival Card Filling — National Immigration Administration
Policy Interpretation of the Nationwide Online Accommodation Registration for Foreigners — National Immigration Administration
Exit and Entry Administration Law of the PRC — National Immigration Administration
Philippine passport appointments — Department of Foreign Affairs
Travel tax — TIEZA
Reduced travel tax — TIEZA
Bureau of Immigration — Philippines
Commission on Filipinos Overseas
Travel clearance for minors — DSWD
eTravel — Philippine travel information system

steps.title: Check whether any visa-free entry covers the trip
prepare: Purpose of the trip and number of days
Onward ticket, if only passing through
steps.howTo:
1. China's unilateral visa exemption (免签, miǎnqiān) list from the National Immigration Administration (NIA), as of February 17, 2026, does not include the Philippines; check the list again before booking, since it changes often.
2. The 240-hour visa-free transit (过境免签, guòjìng miǎnqiān) list (NIA, August 20, 2026, 57 countries) does not include the Philippines either.
3. Any nationality can transit for up to 24 hours without a visa if staying in the airport's restricted area with a confirmed onward ticket to a third country.
4. The embassy lists Hainan visa-free entry for 59 countries including the Philippines: up to 30 days in Hainan province only, arriving directly or via a third country, Hong Kong or Macao (announced 2024; check current).
5. For the rest of the mainland, plan on an L (tourism) or Q2 (visiting relatives) visa. If a visa-free option fits, mark the visa steps "Not for me".

steps.title: Check passport validity and blank pages
conditions: Only if your passport has less than 6 months left or no blank visa pages
steps.howTo:
1. Chinese missions generally ask for a passport with at least 6 months of validity and blank visa pages (check the current checklist).
2. Book a renewal on the DFA online appointment system before applying.

steps.title: Choose L or Q2 and gather your documents
conditions: Only if you need a visa
prepare: L (tourism): round-trip booking and hotel reservations, or an invitation from someone in China
Q2 (visiting relatives): the invitation letter and the relative's ID (next step)
Copy of the passport data page and any previous Chinese visas
Proof of work or funds if the centre checklist asks
steps.howTo:
1. L is for tourism, including visiting friends; Q2 is for short visits to relatives who are Chinese citizens or foreigners with permanent residence in China (up to 180 days).
2. The embassy decides the validity, stay per entry and number of entries; the duration printed on the visa is what counts.
3. Check the Manila centre's current checklist; lists for Philippine applicants may differ from other countries'.

steps.title: Get the invitation letter and the inviter's ID copy
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends in China
documents: Copy of inviter's Chinese ID card or permanent residence card
prepare: Your details, the visit (purpose, dates, places, relationship, who pays)
The inviter's name, phone, address and signature
Proof of the family relationship for Q2: PSA birth or marriage certificate, or a kinship certificate
steps.howTo:
1. The inviter writes a letter with your details, the visit and their own details, and adds a copy of their Chinese ID card (身份证, shēnfènzhèng) or foreign permanent residence card.
2. For Q2, proof of the family relationship is usually asked for; check whether your centre also asks for the relative's household register (户口本, hùkǒu běn).
3. The same host usually registers your stay after arrival (see below).

steps.title: Prepare a child's application
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Copies of both parents' passports or IDs
A parent's signature on the child's form
Consent letter if a parent is not travelling (check current)
steps.howTo:
1. Each child has their own application.
2. The PSA birth certificate shows the parents; a parent signs a minor's form.
3. A child with a Chinese-citizen parent may be treated as a Chinese citizen and not get a visa; check with the embassy first.
4. The Philippine departure side for minors is in the DSWD step below.

steps.title: Fill in the online form and submit at the Manila visa centre
conditions: Only if you need a visa and are applying from the Philippines
prepare: Printed and signed form and confirmation page
Scans of the documents to upload
Visa fee (reduced rates in PHP until December 31, 2026) plus the centre service fee
steps.howTo:
1. Since October 13, 2025, the embassy's China Online Visa Processing System lets applicants fill in the form and upload documents on visaforchina.cn (Manila site), then go to the centre.
2. Since January 29, 2024, the Chinese Visa Application Service Center in Manila (Noble Square, Ayala Avenue, Makati) takes ordinary-passport applications; the embassy no longer does, and says it has entrusted no other agent.
3. Living near Cebu, Davao or Laoag: check which centre or consulate serves your district.
4. Short-term applicants have been exempt from fingerprints until December 31, 2026 under China's global measure; check current at the centre.
5. Express and rush services cost extra; the centre may ask for more papers or an interview.

steps.title: Apply where you live outside the Philippines
conditions: Only if you need a visa and live legally outside the Philippines, e.g. working in Canada or the Gulf
prepare: Proof of legal status there (work, study or residence permit)
The Chinese embassy or consulate that covers where you live
steps.howTo:
1. Chinese missions generally accept applications from foreigners living legally in their country, with a copy of that status document; check the local checklist.
2. Many now use the same online form and a local Chinese Visa Application Service Center.
3. Fees are set in local currency and differ from the Philippine rates.

steps.title: Collect the passport and check the visa
conditions: Only if you need a visa
prepare: Check entries, "enter before" date and duration of each stay
steps.howTo:
1. Processing time is an estimate; check the centre site for regular, express and rush times.
2. Check the visa: entries, the date to enter by, and the duration of each stay (often counted from the day after entry).
3. Book flights once the visa is issued.

steps.title: Get a DSWD travel clearance for a child
conditions: Only if a Filipino child under 18 is leaving without a parent, or with someone other than a parent
prepare: Details of the adult travelling with the child
steps.howTo:
1. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) issues travel clearances for Filipino minors travelling abroad alone or with an adult who is not a parent.
2. A child travelling with a parent generally does not need one; check current exemptions on the DSWD site.
3. Apply online or at a DSWD field office; check current processing time and validity, and apply earlier if you can.

steps.title: Check whether a CFO certificate applies
conditions: Only if you are going to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), or emigrating, rather than just visiting
prepare: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship
steps.howTo:
1. The Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO) runs guidance and counselling for Filipinos leaving to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), and registration for emigrants; the Bureau of Immigration checks the CFO certificate at departure.
2. A short L or Q2 visit is generally not an emigrant departure, but visiting a Chinese partner can prompt questions at the counter; check with the CFO which case yours is.
3. Moving to China on a Q1 family-reunion visa is outside this plan.

steps.title: Pay the Philippine travel tax or check the exemption
prepare: Proof of exemption or reduced rate, if any
steps.howTo:
1. Filipinos and some residents leaving the Philippines pay travel tax to TIEZA: PHP 1,620 economy or PHP 2,700 first class at the full rate when this plan was reviewed.
2. Many airline tickets bought in the Philippines include it; check the fare breakdown.
3. Children over 2 and under 12 pay the reduced rate, infants up to 2 are exempt, and overseas Filipino workers and some permanent residents abroad are exempt; check TIEZA.
4. If not included, pay online on the TIEZA site or at the airport counter before check-in.

steps.title: Pack papers for the Bureau of Immigration departure check
prepare: Hotel booking or host address in China
Proof of work, approved leave, business or school
Invitation letter and relationship proof if visiting family or friends
steps.howTo:
1. At departure, a Bureau of Immigration (BI) officer checks the passport, visa, boarding pass and return ticket, following inter-agency (IACAT) departure guidelines meant to stop trafficking and illegal recruitment.
2. Some travellers are sent to secondary inspection and asked for supporting papers; being refused departure is called offloading.
3. Keep the papers in the carry-on, not the checked bag.
4. Check the current IACAT guidelines on the BI site before the trip.

steps.title: Leave the Philippines
prepare: Arrive at the airport early for immigration lines
Check any eTravel or e-Gate registration the BI currently asks departing travellers for
steps.howTo:
1. Check in, then go through BI departure; answer questions about the trip plainly.
2. If referred to secondary inspection, show the papers from the previous step.
3. The date here is the day before arrival; move it to the real flight.

steps.title: Fill in the arrival card online
steps.howTo:
1. Since November 20, 2025, foreigners can submit the arrival card (入境卡, rùjìng kǎ) before travelling on the NIA website, the "NIA 12367" app, or WeChat and Alipay mini-programs.
2. It is free; use only the official channels.
3. Kiosks and paper cards are still available at the port.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Enter China and note your stay limit
prepare: Address and phone of where you stay
steps.howTo:
1. The border officer checks the passport, visa and arrival card, and may take fingerprints.
2. The stay is the duration printed on the visa; Hainan visa-free stays are 30 days counted from the day after arrival.
3. Write down the last day you can stay; the rest of this plan uses it.

steps.title: Register where you stay within 24 hours
steps.howTo:
1. Accommodation registration (住宿登记, zhùsù dēngjì): hotels register guests for you.
2. Staying with family or friends, you or your host register within 24 hours of arrival, online through NIA channels or at the local police station.
3. Missing it can bring a warning or a fine; register again after each move to a private home.

steps.title: Extend the stay at the exit-entry office
conditions: Only if you need to stay longer than your visa allows
steps.howTo:
1. Apply at the exit-entry administration of the local public security bureau (公安局出入境管理, gōng'ānjú chūrùjìng guǎnlǐ) where you are staying.
2. The Exit and Entry Administration Law asks for the application at least 7 days before the stay runs out, and the total extension cannot exceed the original stay.
3. Leaving Hainan for the rest of China on visa-free entry also needs a visa from Hainan's exit-entry office before the stay ends.
4. The date here assumes a 30-day stay; move it to at least 7 days before your real last day.

steps.title: Register on eTravel before flying home
steps.howTo:
1. eTravel is the Philippine government's free online travel declaration; arriving travellers, Filipinos included, register before landing, usually within 72 hours of the flight; check the current window.
2. Use etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app only; look-alike sites charge fees.
3. Show the QR code on arrival in the Philippines.

steps.title: Leave China before the permitted stay ends
prepare: Copies of the visa and boarding passes
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the last day of your visa stay or extension; overstaying brings fines or detention and can affect later visas.
2. Keep the visa and boarding passes; later applications ask about past trips.
3. Until the trip has a Back home date, the date here assumes a 30-day stay; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting the Philippines · Chinese passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a short visit to the Philippines on a Chinese passport, from the eVisa or 9(a) temporary visitor visa to eTravel, arrival, extensions at the Bureau of Immigration and leaving on time.
conditions: You hold a passport of the People's Republic of China (mainland ordinary passport)
You are visiting the Philippines for tourism or to see family or friends
Not for work, study or long stays; those use other visas
The date is the day you arrive in the Philippines

sources.title: Visa (Updated), including eVisa for Chinese nationals, 26 November 2025 — Philippine Consulate General in Shanghai
Philippine visa policy and 9(a) requirements — eVisaPH, Department of Foreign Affairs
Philippine e-Visa FAQs — eVisaPH, Department of Foreign Affairs
Philippines visa application centre in China — VFS Global
Philippine Embassy in Beijing — Department of Foreign Affairs
eTravel — Philippine Travel Information System
Temporary Visitor (9A) visa waiver and extensions beyond 59 days — Bureau of Immigration
Tourist visa extension online — Bureau of Immigration e-services
Waiver of Exclusion Ground — Bureau of Immigration e-services

steps.title: Check whether you need a visa for the Philippines
prepare: Passport valid 6 months beyond the day you leave the Philippines
Purpose of the trip and how long you plan to stay
Where you live now: mainland China or another country
steps.howTo:
1. China is not on the Philippines' list of countries allowed a 30-day visa-free stay under Executive Order No. 408, as posted by the consulate in Shanghai in November 2025, so a mainland Chinese passport holder generally needs a visa.
2. Visa-free entry for Chinese nationals holding certain other countries' visas or residence has been offered and suspended at different times; check current with the embassy or consulate before relying on it.
3. The passport has to be machine readable and valid at least 6 months beyond the intended stay.
4. Not immigration advice; the DFA and Bureau of Immigration are the reference.

steps.title: Pick the route: eVisa, 9(a) sticker visa or tour group
prepare: Length of stay: more than 14 days, or a chance you will want to extend, points to a sticker visa
Airport of arrival: the eVisa is only for Manila (NAIA) or Mactan-Cebu
Whether you are joining a tour from an accredited Chinese travel agency
steps.howTo:
1. Since November 1, 2025, Chinese nationals living in China can apply for a Philippine eVisa through VFS Global; it allows a stay of up to 14 days, cannot be extended or converted, and is for arrivals at NAIA or Mactan-Cebu airports.
2. The 9(a) temporary visitor visa, subclass 9(a-2) tourism or leisure, covers visits to family, relatives or friends; in China it is a sticker visa filed at the Philippine visa application centre (VFS), in person or by mail.
3. Tour groups go through Chinese travel agencies accredited with the embassy or consulate; the agency files the group visa.
4. Other visa types, and visas you plan to convert in the Philippines, are handled by the consulate directly.

steps.title: Gather a child's papers
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Birth medical certificate (出生医学证明) or notarial certificate of kinship (亲属关系公证书), with an English translation
Letter of permission from a parent or guardian, if the child is not travelling with one
For a child under 15 travelling without a parent, a waiver of exclusion ground (WEG) from the Bureau of Immigration (check current)
steps.howTo:
1. The DFA's 9(a) requirements add a letter of permission from a parent or guardian for minors not travelling with a parent or guardian.
2. The Bureau of Immigration handles the waiver of exclusion ground for young foreign children arriving without a parent; check the current age limit and fee on its site.
3. Each child has their own passport and application.

steps.title: Ask your host in the Philippines for an invitation letter
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends, or a sponsor is paying for the trip
prepare: Notarized invitation letter from the person in the Philippines, with a copy of their valid Philippine ID
Sponsor's letter of support with proof of the sponsor's finances, if they are paying
Proof of relationship, e.g. a notarial certificate of kinship or marriage certificate
Host's address where you will stay
steps.howTo:
1. The Shanghai consulate's 9(a) checklist asks for an original notarized invitation letter from a Philippine-based company or person, with the signer's valid Philippine ID.
2. A sponsor who pays for the trip adds a letter of support with proof of their finances, which the DFA accepts as proof of financial capacity.
3. Have the host send originals early; courier from the Philippines can take a week or more.

steps.title: Gather your own documents
prepare: Visa application form (printed for a sticker visa; online for the eVisa)
Passport original and copy, and Chinese ID card (居民身份证) original and copy
Employment certificate (在职证明) or business licence copy, as ties to home
Bank statements for the last 3 to 6 months, or property certificates
Flight reservation in and out (not a paid ticket yet) and hotel booking
steps.howTo:
1. The DFA minimum for tourism: flight reservation in and out, proof of financial capacity (bank statements for the last 6 months, employment certificate with pay, business income, or a sponsor), proof of ties to home (job, property), itinerary and lodging.
2. The Shanghai consulate asks you not to buy the ticket until the visa is issued; a reservation is enough.
3. Translate Chinese documents into English where the checklist asks.

steps.title: Apply in China: eVisa online or sticker visa at VFS
conditions: Only if you live in mainland China
prepare: Which Philippine post covers where you live: the Beijing embassy or a consulate (Shanghai covers Shanghai, Anhui, Hubei, Jiangsu and Zhejiang)
An account on the VFS Global Philippines site for China
Check the current visa and service fees
steps.howTo:
1. eVisa: register on the VFS Global Philippines page for China, fill in the form, upload documents and pay; the fee is not refunded if refused, and an unpaid application lapses after 48 hours.
2. The DFA says eVisas take about 7 to 12 working days for single entry and 15 to 21 for multiple entry; the officer can call you for an interview.
3. Sticker 9(a) visa: submit at the Philippine visa application centre in person or by mail; the consulate can ask for a personal appearance and interview.
4. Apply early enough to leave time for an interview; the 14 days here are an estimate.

steps.title: Apply from the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally outside mainland China, e.g. in Canada
prepare: Proof of legal residence (PR card, residence permit or long-term visa)
The Philippine embassy or consulate covering your address
Whether that post takes eVisa applications for Chinese nationals (check current)
steps.howTo:
1. The eVisa system lets a foreign national apply through the Philippine post for their country of origin or legal residence; the China eVisa channel described by the consulates is for Chinese nationals living in China.
2. Living elsewhere, apply to the Philippine embassy or consulate for where you live, with proof of legal residence there; check its page for Chinese applicants.
3. If you may want to extend or convert your stay, ask for a regular sticker visa; the DFA says eVisas cannot be converted or extended.

steps.title: Get the visa and check its details
prepare: Entries, validity and length of stay
Port of entry named on an eVisa
steps.howTo:
1. eVisas arrive by email and in your eVisa account; a sticker visa comes back in the passport.
2. The eVisa is tied to that passport; if the passport is lost, a new eVisa application is needed.
3. Book the flight once the visa is issued.

steps.title: Register on eTravel within 72 hours before arrival
prepare: A phone to save the QR code
steps.howTo:
1. All inbound travellers fill in eTravel at etravel.gov.ph or in the eGovPH app; it is free.
2. Register no earlier than 72 hours before arrival; airlines can ask for the QR code at boarding.
3. Beware of paid look-alike sites.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: meet the immigration officer
steps.howTo:
1. The DFA notes a visa does not mean automatic admission; the Bureau of Immigration officer decides at the port of entry.
2. eVisa holders arrive at NAIA or Mactan-Cebu only.
3. Note the period of stay stamped in the passport; the rest of this plan uses it.

steps.title: Extend your stay with the Bureau of Immigration
conditions: Only if you hold a sticker visa (not an eVisa) and want to stay past the date you were given
prepare: Application form (CGAF) from the BI website
Return ticket and proof of funds
steps.howTo:
1. eVisas cannot be extended, so this is for sticker visa holders.
2. Apply before your stay ends at the BI main office, an authorised immigration office, or online through the BI tourist visa extension e-service.
3. Stays beyond 59 days bring extra charges, such as an ACR I-Card for tourists; the BI publishes the fee tables.
4. Overstaying brings fines per month; extend before the stamped date.
5. The date here is an estimate; move it to before your stamped date.

steps.title: Leave on time and keep the records
prepare: The last day of your authorised stay
Copies of the visa and extension receipts
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the last day stamped in the passport or given in an extension.
2. Staying 6 months or more can bring an emigration clearance certificate at departure; check current with the BI.
3. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 14 days here match the eVisa stay; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting Japan · Chinese passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a short visit to Japan on a Chinese passport, from the tourist or family-visit visa through a designated agency or a consulate abroad to Visit Japan Web, arrival and leaving on time.
conditions: You hold a passport of the People's Republic of China (mainland ordinary passport)
You are visiting Japan for tourism or to see family or friends, for up to 90 days
Not for work, study or long stays; those use other visas
The date is the day you arrive in Japan

sources.title: Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay) — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
Chinese nationals travelling to Japan for a short stay (中国国籍の方が短期滞在を目的として日本へ渡航する場合) — MOFA
Group and individual tourist visas for Chinese nationals (中国団体観光・個人観光査証) — MOFA
Single-entry short-stay visa: procedure for Chinese nationals in China, April 2025 (PDF) — MOFA
Single-entry short-stay visa: Chinese nationals living outside China, April 2025 (PDF) — MOFA
Multiple-entry short-stay visa for Chinese nationals: business and cultural figures (PDF) — MOFA
Visa application form (English, PDF) — MOFA
Letter of guarantor (身元保証書, PDF) — MOFA
Letter of invitation (招へい理由書, PDF) — MOFA
Itinerary (滞在予定表, PDF) — MOFA
The JAPAN eVISA system (electronic visa) — MOFA
Japanese embassies and consulates — MOFA
Embassy of Japan in China: visas (签证) — Embassy of Japan
Visit Japan Web — Digital Agency
Extension of period of stay — Immigration Services Agency of Japan

steps.title: Check whether you need a visa for Japan
prepare: Purpose of the trip and how long you plan to stay
Where you live now: mainland China or another country
steps.howTo:
1. Japan's visa exemption list (MOFA, updated September 2025) covers 74 countries and regions, including Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports, but not the mainland Chinese passport.
2. So a mainland Chinese passport holder needs a short-stay visa (短期滞在査証) for tourism or family visits; check the MOFA list again before booking, since it changes.
3. The visa itself is valid 3 months from issue and cannot be extended; the stay (15, 30 or 90 days) is decided at landing.
4. Short-stay status does not allow paid work in Japan.
5. Not immigration advice; MOFA and the Japanese embassy or consulate are the reference.

steps.title: Pick the visa type: tourist, family visit or multiple entry
prepare: Whether you are joining a tour, travelling on your own, or staying with family or friends in Japan
Your income and past trips to Japan, for the multiple-entry options
Whether you live in mainland China or legally in a third country
steps.howTo:
1. Tourism, living in China: apply through a travel agency in China that handles Japan visas; group tours (団体観光) allow a stay of up to 15 days with a guide, individual tourist visas (個人観光) 15 or 30 days.
2. Individual tourist visas come as single entry for people with a certain level of income and their family, or multiple entry (3 years, 30 days per stay, or 5 years, 90 days per stay for high earners) under income and travel-history tiers; the tiers were changing in 2025 to 2026, so check current rules with the agency.
3. Visiting relatives or friends (including a tourist trip where you sleep at their home): a short-stay visa based on documents from the person inviting you (招へい人) and a guarantor (身元保証人) in Japan; relatives here means a spouse and blood or in-law relatives within three degrees.
4. Chinese nationals living in China can get a tourist eVISA (15 or 30 days, single entry) through an accredited agency; an eVISA is shown online at the airport, as a "visa issuance notice", not as a screenshot or printout.
5. Living legally outside China: apply to the Japanese embassy or consulate for your place of residence, not in China (see the third-country step).

steps.title: Gather a child's papers
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Birth medical certificate (出生医学证明) or notarial certificate of kinship (亲属关系公证书) to show the parents
The child's own passport and photo
A consent letter signed by the parent who is not travelling, if the child travels with one parent or neither (check current with the agency or consulate)
Parents' employment and bank papers, since a child's finances are shown through them
steps.howTo:
1. Each child applies with their own passport and application form; a parent signs for a young child.
2. MOFA's family-visit list accepts a notarial certificate of kinship or the birth medical certificate as proof of relationship; these do not expire.
3. A consent letter from the absent parent is commonly asked for by agencies and airlines; confirm with the agency or consulate.
4. For a family group, the agency can file the applications together with one list of applicants (申請人名簿).

steps.title: Ask your host in Japan for the invitation and guarantor papers
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends in Japan, or staying at their home
prepare: Letter of invitation (招へい理由書) and itinerary (滞在予定表), filled in by the host, addressed to the embassy or consulate you apply to
Letter of guarantor (身元保証書): the guarantor covers your stay, return fare and compliance with the law
Host's and guarantor's residence record for the whole household with relationships (住民票)
Guarantor's employment certificate and latest income certificate (課税証明書) or tax certificate (納税証明書 その2)
Copy of the residence card (在留カード), both sides, if the host or guarantor is not Japanese
Proof of the reason for the trip if any, e.g. a wedding booking or medical note
steps.howTo:
1. The host (招へい人) and guarantor (身元保証人) prepare these in Japan and send them to you, not to MOFA or the embassy; copies are accepted, but the consulate can ask for originals.
2. Documents need to be issued within 3 months of the application.
3. A foreign guarantor generally holds a status such as permanent resident, spouse of a Japanese national or an employment status with a period of stay of 3 years or more, and is not a dependant.
4. If host and guarantor are the same person, the host's residence record, employment and residence-card copies are not repeated.
5. A guarantor with no job (e.g. a pensioner) adds a short letter explaining why there is no employment certificate.

steps.title: Gather your own documents
prepare: Visa application form, signed, with a photo 45 x 35 mm taken within 6 months
Copy of the household register (户口簿)
Residence permit (居住证) or residence certificate, if your hukou is outside the consulate's area
Employment certificate (在职证明) with position, salary and dates, or student certificate
Bank statements or deposit certificate (存款证明), and income or tax records for the multiple-entry tiers
Flight booking and hotel bookings or itinerary, for tourist visas
steps.howTo:
1. For a family visit from China, MOFA lists: application form, photo, passport, household register copy, residence permit if applicable, and proof of the relationship with the person in Japan.
2. Tourist visa papers are set by the travel agency; ask it for its current list.
3. Living outside China: add proof of legal residence in that country (residence permit, PR card or visa), a flight booking and proof of funds (bank balance or income certificate).
4. Keep documents issued within the last 3 months.

steps.title: Apply through a designated agency in China
conditions: Only if you live in mainland China
prepare: Which Japanese mission covers where you live: Beijing embassy, or the consulates in Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenyang, Chongqing, Qingdao or the Dalian office
A travel agency or application agency (代理申请机构) designated by that mission
Check the current visa and agency fees
steps.howTo:
1. Applications from China go in, as a rule, through an agency designated by the embassy or consulate for your place of residence; you do not walk in to the embassy.
2. Tourist visas: the agency books the trip or itinerary, prepares the Japanese guarantor papers and files the application; eVISA tourist applications also go through accredited agencies.
3. Family visits: hand the agency your documents plus the host and guarantor papers from Japan.
4. MOFA says checks take about 1 week once filed when nothing is missing, plus agency and courier time; allow longer, and apply early.
5. The consulate can ask for more papers or an interview; submitting everything does not mean a visa will be issued.

steps.title: Apply from the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally outside mainland China, e.g. in Canada
prepare: Proof of legal residence (PR card, residence permit or long-term visa) valid for the whole trip
The Japanese embassy or consulate covering your address, from the MOFA list
Whether your country of residence is on the JAPAN eVISA list
steps.howTo:
1. MOFA's procedure for Chinese nationals living outside China: apply to the Japanese embassy or consulate for your place of residence, or its visa agency; applications cannot be made inside Japan.
2. Residents of Australia, Brazil, Cambodia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Taiwan, the United Kingdom and the United States (list as of May 15, 2026) can apply online for a single-entry tourist eVISA on the JAPAN eVISA website, arriving by air or on the listed ferries.
3. Family visits and multiple-entry visas still go to the embassy or consulate as a paper application with a visa sticker.
4. The document list is shorter for residents of North America, Western Europe, Australia, New Zealand and some Asian places; check the mission's page.
5. MOFA estimates about 1 week after all papers are in; the mission can ask for an interview.

steps.title: Collect the visa and check its details
prepare: Name and passport number on the visa
Single or multiple entry, and the stay allowed
steps.howTo:
1. A sticker visa comes back in the passport; an eVISA arrives as a visa issuance notice in your eVISA account.
2. The visa is valid 3 months for entry and cannot be extended, so enter within that window.
3. The consulate does not give reasons for a refusal.
4. With a multiple-entry visa, check the first-trip conditions, e.g. an agency-arranged first trip.

steps.title: Book flights and travel medical insurance
prepare: Trip dates within the stay the visa allows
steps.howTo:
1. Book after the visa is issued so a refusal or delay does not cost the fare.
2. Japanese public health insurance does not cover short-term visitors; travel medical insurance is worth having, though not a visa condition.
3. eVISA holders enter by air, or by the scheduled ferries named by MOFA.

steps.title: Register on Visit Japan Web before you fly
prepare: Flight number and address in Japan
A phone with the QR codes saved
steps.howTo:
1. Visit Japan Web is the Digital Agency site for entering immigration and customs details online before arrival; it gives QR codes to show at the airport.
2. It is optional; paper cards on the plane still work.
3. Register each traveller, including children, in one account if you like.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: landing examination
prepare: Address and phone number of your hotel or host
eVISA holders: the visa issuance notice open online, not a screenshot
steps.howTo:
1. The immigration officer takes fingerprints and a face photo, checks the visa and decides the period of stay (15, 30 or 90 days); holding a visa does not mean entry is assured.
2. The landing sticker in the passport shows the status (Temporary Visitor) and the last day of the stay.
3. Note that date; the rest of this plan uses it.

steps.title: Ask the immigration bureau for more time
conditions: Only if something like illness or an accident keeps you in Japan past the date you were given
prepare: Reason and proof, e.g. a doctor's letter
Return ticket and proof of funds
steps.howTo:
1. Extensions of a period of stay are filed at the regional immigration bureau (出入国在留管理局) for where you are staying, before the stay ends.
2. For Temporary Visitor status they are the exception, for reasons such as illness or accidents (check current); a wish to stay longer is not usually enough.
3. The Immigration Services Agency lists the fee as a revenue stamp (6,000 yen, or 5,500 yen online, check current).
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to before the last day on your landing sticker.

steps.title: Leave on time and keep the records
prepare: The last day on the landing sticker
Copies of the visa and boarding passes
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the last day of your period of stay; overstaying can lead to removal and a ban on returning.
2. Keep the visa, stamps and boarding passes; multiple-entry tiers and later applications look at past trips to Japan.
3. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 30 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting Japan · Philippine passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a Philippine passport holder visiting Japan for tourism or family, from the temporary visitor visa through the Japan Visa Application Centre, an accredited agency or a consulate abroad to leaving the Philippines, Visit Japan Web, arrival and coming home.
conditions: You hold a Philippine passport
You are visiting Japan for tourism or to see family or friends, for up to 90 days
Not for work, study or long stays; those use other visas
The date is the day you arrive in Japan
This is a planning aid, not immigration advice; MOFA, the Japanese embassy and the Philippine agency pages are the reference

sources.title: Visa — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
Nationals of the Philippines who wish to come to Japan for a short-term stay — MOFA
Checklist for single-entry short-term stay visa, Philippine nationals applying in the Philippines, April 2025 (PDF) — MOFA
Multiple-entry visa for nationals of Indonesia, the Philippines and Viet Nam (PDF) — MOFA
Visa application form (English, PDF) — MOFA
Letter of guarantor (身元保証書, PDF) — MOFA
Letter of invitation, single entry (PDF) — MOFA
Travel itinerary (PDF) — MOFA
Documents for Filipino parents of Japanese-Filipino children — MOFA
The JAPAN eVISA system (electronic visa) — MOFA
Visa / Consular Services — Embassy of Japan in the Philippines
General information on visa application — Embassy of Japan in the Philippines
Japan Visa Application Centre in the Philippines — VFS Global
Visit Japan Web — Digital Agency
Extension of period of stay — Immigration Services Agency of Japan
Philippine passport appointments — Department of Foreign Affairs
Travel tax — TIEZA
Reduced travel tax — TIEZA
Bureau of Immigration — Philippines
Commission on Filipinos Overseas
Travel clearance for minors — DSWD
eTravel — Philippine travel information system

steps.title: Check which Japanese visa fits the trip
prepare: Purpose of the trip and number of days
Where you live now: the Philippines or another country
Past visits to Japan and G7 countries in the last 3 years
steps.howTo:
1. MOFA lists the Philippines among the nationalities that need a visa for a short-term stay (up to 90 days for tourism, business or visiting relatives or friends, with no paid work).
2. The Embassy of Japan says the temporary visitor visa for Philippine nationals is free of charge (gratis); the visa centre or agency charges its own handling fee.
3. Single entry is the usual visa. A multiple-entry visa, up to 30 days per stay, is open to Filipinos with an ICAO-standard passport who visited Japan in the last 3 years and can pay for the trip, who visited Japan and a G7 country in that time, who have ample finances, or who are the spouse or child of the last group; the visa may still be issued as single entry.
4. JAPAN eVISA (MOFA, May 15, 2026): Filipinos living in the Philippines can get one only on a packaged tour through a designated travel agency, with a 15-day stay; residents of listed countries such as Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States apply online there.
5. MOFA's lists change; check them again before booking.

steps.title: Renew the Philippine passport if it runs short
conditions: Only if your passport expires during or soon after the trip, or has no blank page
steps.howTo:
1. The visa goes on a valid passport; a multiple-entry visa needs a machine-readable or e-passport to the ICAO standard.
2. Book a renewal on the DFA online appointment system; renew before applying so the visa is not on a passport about to lapse.

steps.title: Gather your own documents
prepare: PSA birth certificate; if it is illegible, also the local civil registrar copy
Income certificate or income tax return, or a bank balance certificate or statement
Itinerary in Japan on the MOFA form (tourism)
Certificate of employment and approved leave, for the departure check later
steps.howTo:
1. The MOFA checklist for Filipinos applying in the Philippines lists passport, one application form, one photo, PSA birth certificate (and marriage certificate if married) and proof you can pay for the trip.
2. For a late-registered birth, it also asks for a baptismal certificate, an elementary or high school record and a yearbook.
3. Documents must be issued within the last 3 months.
4. Flight and hotel bookings are not needed at application; the itinerary lists dates, where you stay and what you plan to do.

steps.title: Get the invitation and guarantor papers from Japan
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends in Japan
prepare: Relationship proof: PSA birth or marriage certificates, or the Japanese family register (Koseki tohon); for friends, photos, e-mails or call history
A document showing the reason, e.g. a wedding or graduation invitation or a medical certificate
Host's itinerary for you and a list of applicants if more than one
If the host is a foreign resident: copy of both sides of the residence card, full Juminhyo and passport copy
If the host pays: the guarantor's letter and an income or tax certificate, or a bank balance certificate
steps.howTo:
1. The host in Japan prepares these and sends them to you, not to the embassy.
2. The invitation letter is addressed to the Ambassador of Japan in the Philippines and describes the planned activities in detail; just 'tourism' or 'visiting relatives' is not accepted.
3. The guarantor's letter (身元保証書, mimoto hoshōsho) is for whoever in Japan covers your costs; MOFA says a withholding tax slip is not accepted as proof of their funds.
4. Copies of documents issued in Japan are accepted, issued within the last 3 months; seals on these forms are no longer needed.

steps.title: Prepare a child's application
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Each child's own application form and photo
Parents' marriage certificate and proof of the parents' funds
A parent's written consent if the child travels without both parents (check the current checklist)
steps.howTo:
1. Each child needs their own visa; family members travelling together on the same schedule usually apply together.
2. The PSA birth certificate shows the parents and links the child to the funds and invitation.
3. A Filipino parent travelling with a Japanese-Filipino child uses the separate MOFA list for JFC families.
4. The Philippine departure side for minors is in the DSWD step below.

steps.title: Apply through the Japan Visa Application Centre or an accredited agency
conditions: Only if you are applying from the Philippines
prepare: Book on the VFS Global Japan site, or go through a travel agency the embassy has accredited
Handling fee for the centre or agency (the visa itself is gratis)
The 8-digit acceptance number on your receipt
steps.howTo:
1. Since April 7, 2025, the embassy takes ordinary applications through its Japan Visa Application Centre run by VFS Global, with centres in Parañaque, Makati, Quezon City, Cebu and Davao; accredited travel agencies also lodge applications there.
2. Only special cases, such as government invitees or humanitarian cases, apply directly at the embassy or the consulates in Cebu and Davao.
3. Processing takes at least 5 working days after the embassy accepts the file; the embassy may ask for more documents or an interview and does not release passports early for a flight date.
4. After a refusal, the same purpose can be reapplied for only after 6 months, and reasons are not given.

steps.title: Join a packaged tour that includes the eVISA
