conditions: Only if you live in the Philippines and join a packaged tour from a designated travel agency
prepare: Tour booking with the designated agency
steps.howTo:
1. MOFA lets Filipinos living in the Philippines get a tourism eVISA through designated travel agencies for packaged tours; the stay is 15 days.
2. The agency applies; an interview at the embassy may still be requested.
3. At the airport the visa issuance notice is shown online; a PDF, screenshot or printout is not accepted.
4. eVISA is for air or scheduled sea travel only.

steps.title: Apply from the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally outside the Philippines, e.g. working in Canada or the Gulf
prepare: Proof of legal residence there (residence card or visa)
The Japanese embassy or consulate that covers where you live, and its own checklist
steps.howTo:
1. MOFA says visas are applied for at the Japanese mission with jurisdiction over your place of residence, or through its accredited agency, visa centre or online system.
2. As of May 15, 2026, residents of Australia, Brazil, Cambodia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Taiwan, the United Kingdom and the United States can apply for a single-entry tourism eVISA online at JAPAN eVISA; Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Macau, Mongolia, Korea, Singapore and the UAE go through accredited agencies.
3. The Philippine checklist above is for applications in the Philippines; the documents abroad may differ, so use that mission's list.
4. Family visits and multiple-entry visas still go to the mission as a paper application.

steps.title: Collect the passport and check the visa
prepare: Check name, passport number, number of entries, validity and stay
steps.howTo:
1. The passport comes back through the centre or agency, with the visa if issued.
2. Check the visa right away; a single-entry visa has an expiry date to enter by (check the date printed on it).
3. Book flights once the visa is issued, so a refusal or delay does not cost the fare.

steps.title: Get a DSWD travel clearance for a child
conditions: Only if a Filipino child under 18 is leaving without a parent, or with someone other than a parent
prepare: Details of the adult travelling with the child
steps.howTo:
1. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) issues travel clearances for Filipino minors travelling abroad alone or with an adult who is not a parent.
2. A child travelling with a parent generally does not need one; check current exemptions on the DSWD site.
3. Apply online or at a DSWD field office; check current processing time and validity, and apply earlier if you can.

steps.title: Check whether a CFO certificate applies
conditions: Only if you are going to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), or emigrating, rather than just visiting
prepare: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship
steps.howTo:
1. The Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO) runs guidance and counselling for Filipinos leaving to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), and registration for emigrants; the Bureau of Immigration checks the CFO certificate at departure.
2. A short visit on a temporary visitor visa is generally not an emigrant departure, but visiting a Japanese partner can prompt questions at the counter; check with the CFO which case yours is.
3. Moving to Japan as a spouse uses a Certificate of Eligibility and is outside this plan.

steps.title: Pay the Philippine travel tax or check the exemption
prepare: Proof of exemption or reduced rate, if any
steps.howTo:
1. Filipinos and some residents leaving the Philippines pay travel tax to TIEZA: PHP 1,620 economy or PHP 2,700 first class at the full rate when this plan was reviewed.
2. Many airline tickets bought in the Philippines include it; check the fare breakdown.
3. Children over 2 and under 12 pay the reduced rate, infants up to 2 are exempt, and overseas Filipino workers and some permanent residents abroad are exempt; check TIEZA.
4. If not included, pay online on the TIEZA site or at the airport counter before check-in.

steps.title: Pack papers for the Bureau of Immigration departure check
prepare: Hotel booking or host address in Japan
Proof of work, approved leave, business or school
Copies of the invitation letter, guarantor's letter and relationship proof if visiting family or friends
steps.howTo:
1. At departure, a Bureau of Immigration (BI) officer checks the passport, visa, boarding pass and return ticket, following inter-agency (IACAT) departure guidelines meant to stop trafficking and illegal recruitment.
2. Some travellers are sent to secondary inspection and asked for supporting papers; being refused departure is called offloading.
3. Keep the papers in the carry-on, not the checked bag.
4. Check the current IACAT guidelines on the BI site before the trip.

steps.title: Leave the Philippines
prepare: Arrive at the airport early for immigration lines
Check any eTravel or e-Gate registration the BI currently asks departing travellers for
steps.howTo:
1. Check in, then go through BI departure; answer questions about the trip plainly.
2. If referred to secondary inspection, show the papers from the previous step.
3. The date here is the day before arrival; move it to the real flight.

steps.title: Register on Visit Japan Web before you fly
prepare: Flight number and address in Japan
A phone with the QR codes saved
steps.howTo:
1. The Embassy of Japan points travellers to Visit Japan Web, the Digital Agency site for entering immigration and customs details before arrival; it gives QR codes to show at the airport.
2. It is optional; paper cards on the plane still work.
3. eVISA holders also keep the visa issuance notice open online for the airport.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: landing examination
prepare: Address and phone number of your hotel or host
Invitation letter copy, if visiting family
steps.howTo:
1. The immigration officer takes fingerprints and a face photo, checks the visa and decides the period of stay; holding a visa does not mean entry is assured.
2. The landing sticker shows the status (Temporary Visitor) and the last day of the stay; eVISA tour stays are 15 days.
3. Short-term visitors carry their passport while in Japan.
4. Note the last day; the rest of this plan uses it.

steps.title: Ask the immigration bureau for more time
conditions: Only if something like illness or an accident keeps you in Japan past the date you were given
prepare: Reason and proof, e.g. a doctor's letter
Return ticket and proof of funds
steps.howTo:
1. Extensions of a period of stay are filed at the regional immigration bureau (出入国在留管理局) for where you are staying, before the stay ends.
2. For Temporary Visitor status they are the exception, for reasons such as illness or accidents (check current); a wish to stay longer is not usually enough.
3. Changing to a long-stay status from inside Japan is generally not how it works; long stays start with a Certificate of Eligibility.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to before the last day on your landing sticker.

steps.title: Register on eTravel before flying home
steps.howTo:
1. eTravel is the Philippine government's free online travel declaration; arriving travellers, Filipinos included, register before landing, usually within 72 hours of the flight; check the current window.
2. Use etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app only; look-alike sites charge fees.
3. Show the QR code on arrival in the Philippines.

steps.title: Leave Japan on time and keep the records
prepare: The last day on the landing sticker
Copies of the visa and boarding passes
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the last day of your period of stay; overstaying can lead to removal and a ban on returning.
2. Keep the visa, landing stickers and boarding passes; a multiple-entry visa later looks at trips to Japan in the last 3 years.
3. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 30 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting the United Kingdom · Chinese passport

conditions: You travel on a passport of the People's Republic of China
The visit is for tourism, visiting family or friends, or business visitor activities
Not for study over 6 months, work or moving to the UK
The date is the day you arrive in the UK

steps.title: Confirm the Standard Visitor visa is needed
prepare: Purpose and length of the trip
Whether the route changes planes in the UK
Any earlier UK visas or refusals
steps.howTo:
1. Answer the GOV.UK "Check if you need a UK visa" questions for a Chinese passport; for a visit it points to the Standard Visitor visa.
2. The UK electronic travel authorisation (ETA) is for visa-free nationalities; a Chinese passport holder with a visitor visa does not use it. Check current.
3. Changing planes in the UK may need a transit visa unless an exemption applies, such as holding certain valid visas for other countries; check the transit page for your route.
4. A visit is usually up to 6 months per trip, whatever the length of the visa.

steps.title: Choose 6 months or a 2, 5 or 10-year visa
prepare: How often you expect to visit
steps.howTo:
1. The standard visa covers one visit period of up to 6 months; GOV.UK listed its fee at £135 when this plan was reviewed.
2. A long-term Standard Visitor visa lasts 2, 5 or 10 years, still up to 6 months per visit; GOV.UK listed £506, £903 and £1,128. Check current before paying.
3. A long-term visa is more likely to be granted after earlier UK trips that followed the rules; if refused, the fee is not refunded.
4. Fees change most years; the GOV.UK page is the reference.

steps.title: Gather passport, funds and ties papers
prepare: Passport valid for the whole stay, with a blank page
Bank statements, deposit or property certificates
Employment letter with approved leave, business licence (营业执照), or retirement certificate (退休证)
Rough itinerary and where you will stay
Certified English translations of Chinese documents
steps.howTo:
1. GOV.UK asks visitors to show they will leave at the end of the visit and can pay for the trip and the return.
2. The Home Office guide to supporting documents lists the kinds of evidence usually given: finances, job, accommodation, travel plans.
3. Anything not in English or Welsh needs a certified translation.
4. Only the papers that match your situation are needed; more pages do not help by themselves.

steps.title: Ask your host for an invitation letter and status proof
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends in the UK
documents: Copy of host's UK status document
prepare: Host's full name, address, phone and relationship to you
Copy of the host's British passport, or visa or eVisa share code
Where you will stay, and proof of it if at the host's home
Host's bank statements or payslips, if the host is paying
steps.howTo:
1. A letter from the host explaining the relationship, the dates and where you will stay helps the caseworker understand the trip.
2. Add a copy of the host's UK status and, if staying with them, proof of their address.
3. If the host is paying, include evidence of their means; the caseworker checks that support is realistic.
4. The host sends scans or originals to upload or bring.

steps.title: Prepare a child's birth certificate and parents' consent
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Both parents' names, addresses and ID copies
Signed consent from the parent or parents not travelling
Details of the adult the child travels with and where the child stays
steps.howTo:
1. Each child needs their own application and visa.
2. For a child under 18, GOV.UK asks for the parent or guardian details, where the child will stay, and consent when travelling with someone else.
3. Bring the birth certificate to show the relationship.
4. Children also attend the biometrics appointment; check current rules for young children on the centre's site.

steps.title: Apply online on GOV.UK and pay the fee

steps.howTo:
1. Apply online on GOV.UK in English; the earliest is 3 months before travel.
2. The form asks about the purpose, funds, job, family and travel history; answers are checked against earlier applications.
3. Pay the fee online; priority services, where offered, cost extra.
4. After paying, the form hands over to the visa application centre booking site for the biometrics appointment.

steps.title: Give biometrics at a UK visa application centre in China
conditions: Only if you are applying in mainland China
prepare: Printed or uploaded supporting documents, as the centre instructs
steps.howTo:
1. UK visa application centres in mainland China are run by a commercial partner (VFS Global when last checked; check current on the GOV.UK centre finder), with centres in several large cities.
2. Fingerprints and a photo are taken; documents are uploaded before or scanned at the centre.
3. Optional paid services, such as document scanning or passport courier, are not needed for the decision.
4. The passport may be kept or returned, depending on the centre; ask at the appointment.

steps.title: Give biometrics in the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally outside China and apply there
documents: Residence permit or visa for that country
prepare: Proof of legal status there: permit, PR card or long-stay visa
Proof of ties there: job, study, lease
steps.howTo:
1. The online form is the same from any country outside the UK; you choose the centre in the country you apply from.
2. Applying where you live legally, with your residence permit, lets the caseworker weigh your ties there; applying from a country you are only visiting can raise questions. Check current guidance for that country.
3. Centres and operators differ by country; use the GOV.UK centre finder.

steps.title: Wait for the decision and collect the passport
prepare: Check the GOV.UK processing times page
Watch the email used in the application
steps.howTo:
1. GOV.UK says a decision usually comes within 3 weeks after the biometrics appointment; it can take longer if more checks are needed.
2. If approved, a visa vignette is put in the passport; check the name, dates and number of entries.
3. The 21 days here is an estimate; move it to the real appointment.

steps.title: Book flights and travel medical insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Book after the visa is in the passport, so a refusal or delay does not cost the fare.
2. Visitors generally pay for NHS hospital care; travel medical insurance is not a visa requirement but is widely bought.
3. Arrive on or after the visa start date.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit

Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: UK border control
prepare: Return ticket and proof of funds in carry-on
steps.howTo:
1. A Border Force officer may ask about the purpose and length of the trip.
2. A visit is up to 6 months per entry, even on a 2, 5 or 10-year visa.
3. Visitors cannot work, claim public funds, or live in the UK through frequent or back-to-back visits.

steps.title: Apply to extend the stay from inside the UK
conditions: Only if you were given less than 6 months and need to stay longer
steps.howTo:
1. GOV.UK allows an extension only if the permission given was under 6 months, and only up to 6 months in total.
2. It is applied for from inside the UK before the current permission ends; biometrics are taken again.
3. GOV.UK listed the fee at £1,172 when this plan was reviewed; check current.
4. Stays beyond 6 months as a visitor are limited to special cases such as private medical treatment; the GOV.UK page lists them.

steps.title: Leave on time and keep the records
prepare: Copies of the visa and boarding passes
steps.howTo:
1. Leave within 6 months of entry, or by the end of any extension.
2. Overstaying makes later UK visas harder to get.
3. Keep boarding passes; the next application asks about earlier trips.
4. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 180 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting the United Kingdom · Philippine passport

2. The UK electronic travel authorisation (ETA) is for visa-free nationalities, so it does not replace the visa on a Philippine passport.
3. A Standard Visitor can usually stay up to 6 months per visit; work and study longer than the visitor rules allow need other visas.
4. Frequent visitors can apply for a long-term Standard Visitor visa valid for 2, 5 or 10 years, still up to 6 months per visit.
5. Coming to marry or join a partner, or passing through the UK, has other routes; check the GOV.UK visa checker for those.

steps.title: Renew the Philippine passport if it runs short
conditions: Only if your passport expires before the end of the trip, or soon after, or has no blank page
steps.howTo:
1. GOV.UK asks for a passport valid for the whole stay, with a blank page for the visa.
2. A long-term visa cannot outlast the passport, so renew first if you want a 2, 5 or 10-year visa.
3. Book a renewal on the DFA online appointment system.

steps.title: Gather proof of ties and funds
prepare: Certificate of employment with position, salary and approved leave dates
Recent bank statements showing funds for the trip
Business registration (DTI or SEC) if self-employed
Property titles or other ties to the Philippines
Travel history for the last 10 years and old passports
steps.howTo:
1. The decision weighs whether you will leave at the end of the visit, can pay for the trip, and are not living in the UK through repeated visits.
2. Documents not in English or Welsh need a certified translation.
3. Upload or bring copies as the online checklist says; originals may be asked for.

steps.title: Get an invitation letter and your host's status proof

documents: Copy of host's UK passport or visa, or eVisa share code details
prepare: Host name, UK address, phone and immigration status
Your relationship, with PSA birth or marriage certificates if family
Dates, where you will stay and who pays
Host's proof of accommodation and bank statements if they support the trip
steps.howTo:
1. An invitation letter is not a set requirement, but it supports the stated purpose of the visit.
2. The host signs a letter with their details and status, your relationship, the dates, where you will stay and who pays.
3. If the host pays or houses you, add their bank statements and proof they can accommodate you, such as a tenancy or ownership record.

steps.title: Prepare a child's application papers
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Parents' or guardian's written consent for the child to travel to the UK, with full contact details
Details of who will care for the child in the UK: name, date of birth, address and relationship
Consent for the child to stay with that person
steps.howTo:
1. Each child has their own application and visa.
2. GOV.UK asks for a parent or guardian's written consent and contact details, and proof of suitable care and accommodation in the UK.
3. Children can travel without an adult if the consent and care arrangements are in place.
4. The PSA birth certificate shows who the parents are; the Philippine departure side is in the DSWD step below.

steps.title: Apply online and pay the visa fee
prepare: Check the current fee: GBP 135 for up to 6 months when this plan was reviewed
Long-term visas: GBP 506 for 2 years, GBP 903 for 5 years, GBP 1,128 for 10 years when this plan was reviewed
Answers on work, finances, criminal history and 10 years of travel
steps.howTo:
1. The earliest you can apply is 3 months before you travel; the date here is about 12 weeks ahead.
2. Apply on GOV.UK; it books the biometrics appointment through the visa application centre provider.
3. Pay the fee online; priority services cost extra where offered.
4. A long-term visa costs more up front; check current rules on what happens if a shorter visa is issued instead.

steps.title: Give biometrics at VFS in Manila or Cebu

Check current VFS centre locations and optional services

1. UK visa application centres in the Philippines are run by VFS Global; check current locations, which have included Manila and Cebu.
2. Fingerprints and a photo are taken at the appointment.
3. GOV.UK says the passport is returned the same day; check current practice at your centre.

The nearest UK visa application centre there

3. Processing times and priority options differ by country; check the GOV.UK processing times page.

steps.title: Arrival: UK Border Force
prepare: Return ticket, proof of funds and invitation letter in carry-on
steps.howTo:
1. A Border Force officer checks the visa and may ask about the visit; carry the key supporting papers.
2. Visa holders generally use the staffed desks; check current eGate eligibility for your passport.

steps.title: Check whether the stay can be extended
conditions: Only if you need to stay longer than planned, while still in the UK
