2. Keep boarding passes; later UK applications ask about travel history, and a clean record helps long-term visa applications.
3. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 30 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting the Schengen area · Chinese passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a short visit to the Schengen area on a Chinese passport, from choosing the right consulate and booking the visa centre to insurance, the decision, the Entry/Exit System and the 90/180-day limit.
conditions: You hold a passport of the People's Republic of China (mainland ordinary passport)
You are visiting one or more Schengen countries for tourism or to see family or friends, for up to 90 days in any 180
Not for work, study or stays over 90 days; those are national visas
The date is the day you arrive in the Schengen area

sources.title: Applying for a Schengen visa — European Commission, Migration and Home Affairs
Visa policy — European Commission, Migration and Home Affairs
Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, Annex I: countries whose nationals need a visa — EUR-Lex
Visa Code, Regulation (EC) No 810/2009, consolidated — EUR-Lex
Short-stay calculator — European Commission
Entry/Exit System (EES) — European Commission, Migration and Home Affairs
EES and ETIAS for travellers — European Union

steps.title: Check the visa rule for a Chinese passport
prepare: Passport valid at least 3 months after you leave the Schengen area, issued within the last 10 years, with 2 blank pages
Countries you plan to visit and nights in each
Any transit through a Schengen airport on the way
steps.howTo:
1. China is on Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, so a mainland Chinese passport holder needs a short-stay (type C) Schengen visa; Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports are visa-exempt.
2. A Schengen visa covers all 29 Schengen countries for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
3. China is not on the EU-wide airport transit visa list, but single countries can add their own; check current if you connect through a Schengen airport to a non-Schengen country.
4. Countries outside Schengen, such as Ireland, Cyprus or the United Kingdom, need their own visa.
5. Not immigration advice; the consulate of your main destination is the reference.

steps.title: Work out which country you apply to
prepare: Day-by-day plan with nights in each country
Where you live now: mainland China or another country
steps.howTo:
1. One country: apply to that country.
2. Several countries: apply to the one where you spend the longest time.
3. Equal stays: apply to the country you enter first.
4. As a rule, apply at that country's consulate (or its visa centre) covering the place where you legally live; in China, each consulate covers set provinces.
5. Keep the plan consistent: travelling mostly elsewhere than the country that issued the visa can cause questions at the border or on the next application.

steps.title: Gather a child's papers
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Birth medical certificate (出生医学证明) or notarial certificate of kinship (亲属关系公证书), translated if the consulate asks
Application form signed by a parent or guardian
Notarized consent from the parent(s) not travelling, with a copy of their ID (check the consulate's checklist)
steps.howTo:
1. Each child has their own application; a person with parental authority signs for a minor.
2. Children under 12 do not give fingerprints.
3. The visa fee is lower for children aged 6 to under 12 (45 euros) and waived under 6.
4. Consulates commonly ask for consent from a parent who is not travelling; follow the checklist of the consulate you apply to.

steps.title: Ask your host for an invitation and proof of their status
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends, or staying at their home
prepare: Invitation letter with the host's address, your dates and relationship
Copy of the host's passport or residence permit
A formal undertaking of accommodation or costs where the country uses one, e.g. Verpflichtungserklärung (Germany) or attestation d'accueil (France), made by the host at a local office
Proof of the host's finances if they cover your costs
Proof of relationship, e.g. notarial certificate of kinship
steps.howTo:
1. The Visa Code asks for proof of accommodation, or of sufficient means to cover it; an invitation from a host is one way.
2. Some countries use an official form issued to the host by their town hall or foreigners' office; the host starts it weeks ahead.
3. Send originals by courier if the consulate asks for them.

steps.title: Buy travel medical insurance of at least 30,000 euros
prepare: Trip dates, plus a few days of margin
Every Schengen country you will visit
steps.howTo:
1. The Visa Code asks for travel medical insurance valid across the whole Schengen area for the full stay, covering emergency care, hospital treatment and repatriation, including for death, with at least 30,000 euros of cover.
2. For a multiple-entry visa, the first trip is covered at application and later trips need cover too.
3. Many consulates in China list accepted insurers; buy a policy that can be refunded if the visa is refused.

steps.title: Gather your own documents
prepare: Application form (online or paper, per country), and an ICAO-standard photo
Household register (户口簿) copy, and residence permit (居住证) if your hukou is outside the consulate's area
Employment certificate (在职证明) with approved leave, or business licence, or student and retirement papers
Flight reservation and hotel bookings or the host invitation
Previous passports with past Schengen visas
steps.howTo:
1. EU list: passport, form, photo, travel medical insurance, and papers on the purpose of the trip, money and accommodation for the stay, and your intention to return.
2. Each consulate publishes its own checklist and translation rules; follow the one for your main destination.
3. Many consulates ask for flight reservations, not paid tickets.

steps.title: Book the visa centre appointment
prepare: The visa centre the consulate uses (VFS Global, TLScontact or BLS International, depending on the country)
Earliest and latest filing dates for your trip
Check the current visa fee and service fee
steps.howTo:
1. Applications go in no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before the trip; in busy seasons, appointments can be weeks out.
2. Book online with the visa centre named on the consulate website; do not use paid slot resellers.
3. The EU visa fee is 90 euros for adults; the visa centre adds its own service fee.

steps.title: Lodge the application and give fingerprints in China
conditions: Only if you live in mainland China
prepare: Originals and copies of every document on the checklist
steps.howTo:
1. Go in person to the visa centre in the consulate district that covers your residence; the consulate's district rules decide which city.
2. Fingerprints are taken at the first application and reused for 59 months if they are in the Visa Information System.
3. Some consulates also interview applicants.
4. The passport stays with the consulate while it decides.

steps.title: Lodge the application from the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally outside mainland China, e.g. in Canada
prepare: Proof of legal residence (PR card, residence permit or long-term visa), usually valid for some months beyond your return (check the consulate)
Your main destination's consulate or visa centre covering where you live
steps.howTo:
1. The EU rule is to apply at the consulate with territorial responsibility for the country where you legally live, so a Chinese citizen living in Canada applies in Canada, not in China.
2. A consulate can accept an application from someone legally present but not resident if there is a good reason; this is at its discretion.
3. Add proof of your status and job in the country of residence; the rest of the list is the same.

steps.title: Wait for the decision and check the visa sticker
prepare: Valid from and to dates, number of entries and duration of stay (days)
steps.howTo:
1. The normal decision time is 15 days, extendable to 45 days if more checks are needed; the 45 days here is a planning estimate.
2. Multiple-entry visas: under the Visa Code cascade, a traveller who has lawfully used 3 visas in the last 2 years is to be considered for a 1-year multiple-entry visa, then 2 years, then up to 5 years; whether a China-specific cascade applies is check current.
3. A refusal gives the reasons and how to appeal.

steps.title: Book flights once the visa is issued
prepare: Enter first in the country you applied to, if that was the plan
steps.howTo:
1. Book after the visa is issued, so a refusal or delay does not cost the fare.
2. Match the route to the itinerary you filed.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: register in the Entry/Exit System
prepare: Return ticket, hotel bookings or invitation, and proof of funds in your carry-on
steps.howTo:
1. The Entry/Exit System (EES) started on October 12, 2025 and has been fully running since April 10, 2026; it records your passport, fingerprints, face image and each entry and exit, and replaces passport stamps.
2. The border guard can still ask about purpose, money, accommodation and return.
3. ETIAS is for visa-exempt travellers, so it does not apply to a Chinese visa holder.

steps.title: Ask for an extension only in exceptional cases
conditions: Only if something like illness, force majeure or a serious personal reason keeps you in the Schengen area past your visa
prepare: Proof of the reason, e.g. a doctor's letter or cancelled flight
Proof of funds and insurance for the extra days
steps.howTo:
1. Schengen visas are generally not extended; the Visa Code allows it only for force majeure, humanitarian or serious personal reasons, or professional reasons in some cases.
2. Apply before the visa runs out to the immigration authority of the country where you are.
3. The date here is an estimate; move it to before your visa ends.

steps.title: Leave within 90 days in any 180
prepare: Days used in the last 180, from the EU short-stay calculator
The end date on the visa sticker
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the earlier of the visa end date and the day you reach 90 days in the last 180.
2. EES records the exit and flags overstays automatically; an overstay can lead to fines, an entry ban and refusals later.
3. Keep boarding passes and hotel receipts; the next application asks about earlier Schengen visas.
4. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 90 days here is the maximum; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Visiting the Schengen area · Philippine passport
summary: Paperwork plan for a Philippine passport holder visiting the Schengen area for tourism or family on a short-stay (C) visa, from choosing the consulate of the main destination and €30,000 insurance to VFS or TLS in Manila or abroad, leaving the Philippines, the EES border check, the 90/180 rule and coming home.
conditions: You hold a Philippine passport
You are visiting one or more Schengen countries for tourism or to see family or friends, up to 90 days in any 180
Not for work, study or moving to Europe; those use national long-stay visas
The date is the day you arrive in the Schengen area
This is a planning aid, not immigration advice; the EU and the main destination's consulate pages are the reference

sources.title: Applying for a Schengen visa — European Commission, Migration and Home Affairs
Short-stay calculator — European Commission
Visa Code, Regulation (EC) No 810/2009, consolidated — EUR-Lex
Entry/Exit System (EES) and ETIAS — Travel to Europe, European Union
Philippine passport appointments — Department of Foreign Affairs
Travel tax — TIEZA
Reduced travel tax — TIEZA
Bureau of Immigration — Philippines
Commission on Filipinos Overseas
Travel clearance for minors — DSWD
eTravel — Philippine travel information system

steps.title: Check the visa and the Schengen rules
prepare: Countries you will visit and nights in each
Past Schengen visas and how you used them
steps.howTo:
1. Philippine citizens are on the EU list of nationalities that need a short-stay (type C) Schengen visa.
2. It covers up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries, for tourism, visiting family or friends, or business; it can be single or multiple entry.
3. ETIAS is for visa-exempt nationalities, so it does not apply to a Philippine passport; it is not running yet anyway.
4. Ireland and Cyprus are EU members outside Schengen and issue their own visas.
5. Not immigration advice; the EU site and the consulate of your main destination are the reference.

steps.title: Renew the Philippine passport if it runs short
conditions: Only if your passport would expire less than 3 months after you leave the Schengen area, is over 10 years old, or has too few blank pages
steps.howTo:
1. The EU asks for a passport valid at least 3 months after the planned departure from the Schengen area; the Visa Code also asks that it was issued within the last 10 years and has at least 2 blank pages.
2. For a multiple-entry visa, the 3 months count from the last planned departure.
3. Book a renewal on the DFA online appointment system.

steps.title: Work out which country's consulate handles the application
steps.howTo:
1. One country: apply to its consulate.
2. Several countries: apply to the one where you spend the longest time; if the stays are equal, to the country you enter first.
3. As a rule, you apply at that country's consulate responsible for the country where you legally live.
4. Each consulate has its own checklist and appointment channel; read it before gathering papers.

steps.title: Gather proof of purpose, funds and ties
prepare: Recent bank statements and income tax return (BIR Form 2316 or 1701)
Certificate of employment with approved leave, or business registration (DTI or SEC) if self-employed
Round-trip flight reservation and hotel bookings or host address
PSA birth and marriage certificates if the consulate asks
steps.howTo:
1. The EU lists the passport, application form, ICAO photo, travel medical insurance and papers showing the purpose, funds, accommodation and your intention to return home.
2. Consulates may ask for more; the local checklist decides.
3. Many consulates prefer flight reservations rather than paid tickets until the visa is issued; check yours.

steps.title: Buy travel medical insurance with €30,000 cover
prepare: Check cover for emergency care, hospital and repatriation
steps.howTo:
1. The Visa Code asks for travel medical insurance with at least €30,000 cover, valid in all Schengen countries for the whole stay, including emergency care, hospitalisation and repatriation (including after death).
2. For a multiple-entry visa, the first trip's cover is usually enough at application, with a signature that later trips will be covered too; check the consulate's rule.
3. Pick a policy that refunds or can be moved if the visa is refused or dates change.

steps.title: Get an invitation and your host's papers
conditions: Only if visiting family or friends
documents: Copy of host's passport or residence permit
prepare: Host's name, address, phone and status in that country
Relationship proof, e.g. PSA birth or marriage certificates
If the host pays or houses you: their proof of funds and of the home
Any official host form the country uses (check current)
steps.howTo:
1. The host writes an invitation with your details, the dates, where you will stay, your relationship and who pays, and adds a copy of their ID or residence permit.
2. Some countries have an official form done at a local office, for example France's attestation d'accueil or Germany's Verpflichtungserklärung, which can stand in for your own proof of funds.
3. Start early; those forms take an appointment with the host's town hall or foreigners' office.

steps.title: Prepare a child's application
conditions: Only if a child under 18 is travelling
prepare: Both parents' signatures on the form, or a guardianship document
Notarised consent from a parent who is not travelling
Copies of both parents' passports or IDs
steps.howTo:
1. Each child needs their own application.
2. The EU fee is €45 for children aged 6 to 12; the Visa Code waives it for children under 6.
3. Consulates usually ask for both parents' consent and the PSA birth certificate; check the checklist.
4. The Philippine departure side for minors is in the DSWD step below.

steps.title: Book and lodge the application in the Philippines
conditions: Only if you are applying from the Philippines
prepare: Visa fee: €90 for adults when this plan was reviewed, plus the service provider fee
Appointment with the provider the consulate uses (for example VFS Global or TLScontact)
Originals and copies as the checklist says
steps.howTo:
1. Apply no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before the trip; with Manila appointment waits, earlier is safer.
2. Most Schengen embassies in Manila take applications through an external provider such as VFS Global or TLScontact; the embassy site names which one and where (some also have centres outside Metro Manila).
3. Fingerprints are taken in person; if you gave them for a Schengen visa in the last 59 months, they may be reused.
4. You may be asked to an interview at the embassy.

steps.title: Apply from the country where you live
conditions: Only if you live legally outside the Philippines, e.g. working in Canada, Singapore or the Gulf
prepare: Residence permit valid well beyond the trip (check the local rule)
Proof of work or study there
steps.howTo:
1. The EU rule is to apply at the main destination's consulate responsible for the country where you legally live.
2. Bring proof of that residence; the consulate weighs your ties there as well as to the Philippines.
3. Applying while only visiting a third country is possible only if that consulate accepts a justified reason; check first.
4. Fees are the same in euros, charged in local currency.

steps.title: Collect the passport and check the visa sticker
prepare: Check the dates, number of entries, duration of stay and territorial validity
steps.howTo:
1. The EU says a decision normally takes 15 days, up to 45 if more checks are needed.
2. Check the sticker: valid from and until, entries (1, 2 or MULT), days allowed and 'Schengen States'.
3. Frequent travellers with past visas used lawfully can get multiple-entry visas of longer validity under the Visa Code's cascade; check current.
4. A refusal gives the reasons and the way to appeal.
5. Book flights once the visa is issued.

steps.title: Get a DSWD travel clearance for a child
conditions: Only if a Filipino child under 18 is leaving without a parent, or with someone other than a parent
prepare: Details of the adult travelling with the child
steps.howTo:
1. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) issues travel clearances for Filipino minors travelling abroad alone or with an adult who is not a parent.
2. A child travelling with a parent generally does not need one; check current exemptions on the DSWD site.
3. Apply online or at a DSWD field office; check current processing time and validity, and apply earlier if you can.

steps.title: Check whether a CFO certificate applies
conditions: Only if you are going to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), or emigrating, rather than just visiting
prepare: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship
steps.howTo:
1. The Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO) runs guidance and counselling for Filipinos leaving to join a foreign spouse, partner or fiancé(e), and registration for emigrants; the Bureau of Immigration checks the CFO certificate at departure.
2. A short Schengen visit is generally not an emigrant departure, but visiting a European partner can prompt questions at the counter; check with the CFO which case yours is.
3. Moving to Europe on a family or long-stay visa is outside this plan.

steps.title: Pay the Philippine travel tax or check the exemption
prepare: Proof of exemption or reduced rate, if any
steps.howTo:
1. Filipinos and some residents leaving the Philippines pay travel tax to TIEZA: PHP 1,620 economy or PHP 2,700 first class at the full rate when this plan was reviewed.
2. Many airline tickets bought in the Philippines include it; check the fare breakdown.
3. Children over 2 and under 12 pay the reduced rate, infants up to 2 are exempt, and overseas Filipino workers and some permanent residents abroad are exempt; check TIEZA.
4. If not included, pay online on the TIEZA site or at the airport counter before check-in.

steps.title: Pack papers for the Bureau of Immigration departure check
prepare: Proof of work, approved leave, business or school
Invitation letter and relationship proof if visiting family or friends
steps.howTo:
1. At departure, a Bureau of Immigration (BI) officer checks the passport, visa, boarding pass and return ticket, following inter-agency (IACAT) departure guidelines meant to stop trafficking and illegal recruitment.
2. Some travellers are sent to secondary inspection and asked for supporting papers; being refused departure is called offloading.
3. Keep the papers in the carry-on, not the checked bag.
4. Check the current IACAT guidelines on the BI site before the trip.

steps.title: Leave the Philippines
prepare: Arrive at the airport early for immigration lines
Check any eTravel or e-Gate registration the BI currently asks departing travellers for
steps.howTo:
1. Check in, then go through BI departure; answer questions about the trip plainly.
2. If referred to secondary inspection, show the papers from the previous step.
3. The date here is the day before arrival; move it to the real flight.

steps.title: Get a business invitation and an employer letter
documents: Invitation letter from the company you visit
prepare: Who you meet, where, and on which dates
Who pays for travel and the stay
Your role, salary and approved leave or travel dates
steps.howTo:
1. A business visitor attends meetings, conferences or negotiations; paid work for a local company usually needs a work visa instead.
2. Ask the host company for a letter naming you, the purpose, the dates and who covers costs.
3. Ask your employer for a letter confirming your job, salary and the trip's purpose.
4. Carry both on the flight too; the border officer may ask.

steps.title: Check travel medical insurance covers the whole trip
prepare: Cover dates from departure to the return flight, with a margin for delays
Policy number and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number, on paper too
Whether a credit card or employer plan already covers travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Public health cover from home usually pays little or nothing abroad; check what yours does.
2. Hospital care for visitors is billed at full price in many countries, the US especially.
3. If the return date moves, extend the policy to match.
4. Where a visa sets a minimum cover, the visa steps in this plan say so.

steps.title: Get ready for the border check on arrival
prepare: Address where you'll stay, and your host's name and phone
Proof of funds: bank card, a recent statement
Papers for the trip's purpose: invitation, hotel booking or business letter
Paper copies in the carry-on, not only on the phone
steps.howTo:
1. A visa or visa-free status lets you ask to enter; the border officer decides admission and how long you may stay.
2. Expect questions on purpose, length of stay, where you stay and who pays; answers that match the visa application are the easiest to check.
3. Bags can be inspected, and in some countries phones and laptops too.
4. Declare food, plants, medicine and cash over the country's limit as the customs form asks.

steps.title: Arrival: border check and EES registration
prepare: Proof of funds and invitation letter in the carry-on
steps.howTo:
1. The Entry/Exit System (EES) records non-EU short-stay travellers at the external border with fingerprints and a face photo, in place of passport stamps (started October 2025; check current).
2. The border guard may ask about the purpose, funds, accommodation and return; a visa does not assure entry.
3. Entering first through the main destination is usual but the visa is valid across Schengen; keep the itinerary close to what you declared.
4. Use the EU short-stay calculator to track days against the 90/180 limit.

steps.title: Ask the local authorities about an extension
conditions: Only if something like illness, a flight cancellation or a serious family reason keeps you past your visa
prepare: Proof of the reason, e.g. a doctor's letter
Proof of funds and insurance for the extra days
steps.howTo:
1. Schengen visas are generally not extended; the Visa Code allows it only for force majeure, humanitarian or serious personal reasons.
2. Apply to the immigration authorities of the country where you are, before the visa ends.
3. Switching to a long-stay visa from inside is generally not possible; those are applied for from home.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to before the last day allowed.

steps.title: Register on eTravel before flying home
steps.howTo:
1. eTravel is the Philippine government's free online travel declaration; arriving travellers, Filipinos included, register before landing, usually within 72 hours of the flight; check the current window.
2. Use etravel.gov.ph or the eGovPH app only; look-alike sites charge fees.
3. Show the QR code on arrival in the Philippines.

steps.title: Leave the Schengen area on time and keep the records
prepare: Copies of the visa and boarding passes
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the visa end date and within 90 days in any 180; EES records the exit, and overstays show up on later applications.
2. Keep the visa and boarding passes; lawful use of past visas helps later multiple-entry applications.
3. Until the trip has a Back home date, the 30 days here is an estimate; setting one moves this step to it.

title: Travelling abroad from Canada
summary: Paperwork plan for a trip abroad while living in Canada: passport and PR card validity, the destination's entry rules, a child's consent letter, insurance, provincial health coverage while away, and customs on the way back.
conditions: You live in Canada and are travelling abroad for a visit, then coming back
The date is the day you leave Canada
Health coverage steps describe British Columbia and Ontario; other provinces have their own rules

sources.title: Travel advice and advisories — Travel.gc.ca
Canadian passports — Canada.ca
Permanent resident travel document — Canada.ca
Understand PR status — Canada.ca
Recommended consent letter for children travelling abroad — Travel.gc.ca
Travel insurance — Travel.gc.ca
Registration of Canadians Abroad — Travel.gc.ca
Medical Services Plan eligibility — Province of British Columbia
Apply for OHIP and get a health card — Ontario.ca
Guaranteed Income Supplement — Canada.ca
Personal exemptions for residents returning to Canada — CBSA
Crossing the border with $10,000 or more — CBSA

steps.title: Check the passport is valid well past the return date
steps.howTo:
1. Many countries ask for a passport valid 6 months beyond the stay, and some for blank pages; the destination's own rules decide.
2. A Canadian passport renewal takes a few weeks by standard service; urgent and express service cost more.
3. Children's passports last at most 5 years.
4. Travellers on a foreign passport renew with that country's embassy or consulate, which can take longer.

steps.title: Check the PR card is valid on the return date
prepare: Days spent in Canada in the last 5 years
conditions: Only if you are a permanent resident, not yet a citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Airlines and other commercial carriers ask for a valid PR card or a permanent resident travel document (PRTD) before boarding for Canada.
2. A card with less than 9 months left can be renewed from Canada before leaving.
3. Without a valid card, the PRTD is applied for from abroad.
4. The 730-days-in-5-years residency obligation is checked when renewing or applying for a PRTD.

steps.title: Get the destination's visa, eTA or ESTA
prepare: Travel.gc.ca advice page for the country
steps.howTo:
1. Entry rules depend on the passport held, not on living in Canada; Travel.gc.ca lists them for Canadian passports.
2. Examples: the United States uses ESTA for visa-waiver passports, the UK an ETA, and the EU is bringing in ETIAS; check current.
3. Transit stops can have their own rules.
4. Use official sites; look-alike sites charge extra fees.

steps.title: Write a consent letter for a child travelling without both parents
documents: Custody or guardianship papers, if any
prepare: Names and contact details of the parents not travelling
conditions: Only if a child under 18 travels alone, with one parent, or with another adult
steps.howTo:
1. Canada recommends a consent letter signed by each parent or guardian not travelling; border officers can ask for one.
2. Travel.gc.ca has a template; having it witnessed or notarized adds weight.
3. The destination country can have stricter rules.

steps.title: Buy travel medical insurance
prepare: Workplace or credit card coverage, to compare
steps.howTo:
1. Provincial health plans pay only a small part of emergency costs abroad, often at home-province rates.
2. Policies usually exclude unstable pre-existing conditions; the stability period is in the wording.
3. Some workplace plans and credit cards include coverage with day limits.

steps.title: Check provincial health coverage stays in place while away
prepare: Days outside the province this year and in the last 12 months
conditions: Only if the trip is long, or you spend much of the year outside your province
steps.howTo:
1. British Columbia: MSP expects residents to be in B.C. at least 6 months in a calendar year; citizens and permanent residents away on vacation can be absent up to 7 months in a year. Longer absences, such as work or study abroad, can sometimes be approved by Health Insurance BC in advance; check current.
2. Ontario: OHIP expects 153 days in Ontario in any 12-month period; after more than 212 days away in 12 months, re-applying may be needed. Longer approved absences exist for work, study or missionary work; check current.
3. Other provinces set their own limits.

steps.title: Tell Service Canada about a long stay abroad while on GIS
conditions: Only if you receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement or Allowance and will be away more than 6 months
steps.howTo:
1. GIS and the Allowance stop after 6 months outside Canada, counted from the month after leaving; they restart after coming back and applying again.
2. OAS itself can keep being paid abroad in many cases.
3. Service Canada is the reference for the exact rules.

steps.title: Register the trip with Registration of Canadians Abroad
conditions: Only if you are a Canadian citizen
steps.howTo:
1. The free service lets the Government of Canada reach travellers in an emergency abroad.
2. Travel.gc.ca advisories for the destination are worth a last look before leaving.

steps.title: Log the dates you leave and return to Canada
conditions: Only if you are a permanent resident, or plan to apply for citizenship
steps.howTo:
1. The citizenship physical presence calculator and the PR residency obligation both count days in Canada.
2. Keeping each departure and return date as it happens is easier than rebuilding them later.
3. This repeats every trip.

steps.title: Declare goods and cash when coming back
prepare: Value of goods bought or received abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Residents returning after 24 hours or more have a personal exemption of CAN$200; after 48 hours, CAN$800, with limits on alcohol and tobacco; check current.
2. Goods over the exemption are declared and taxed; food, plants and animals have their own rules.
3. Cash or monetary instruments of CAN$10,000 or more are reported to the CBSA.
4. This date is a placeholder; move it to the return date.

title: Travelling to China · visa and arrival
summary: Paperwork plan for a trip to mainland China on a foreign passport, from visa-free entry or a visa to the arrival card, accommodation registration, payments and leaving on time.
conditions: You are travelling to mainland China on a foreign passport, e.g. Canadian
You are visiting, not moving to China for work or study
The date is the day you leave for China

sources.title: Notice on Visa-free Policy for Canada and the UK — Chinese Embassy in Canada
FAQs on Visa-free Entry into China — Chinese Embassy in Canada
List of Countries Covered by Unilateral Visa Exemption Policies — National Immigration Administration
Visa-Free Transit Policies — National Immigration Administration
Visa Requirements and Procedures for Chinese Visa Application — Chinese Embassy in Canada
Notice on the Launch of China Online Visa Application System — Chinese Embassy in Canada
Notice on Fingerprints Collection Exemptions for Chinese Visa Applications — Chinese Embassy in Canada
Consular Jurisdiction and Contact Information — Chinese Embassy in Canada
Ottawa Chinese Visa Application Service Center
Beware of Fraudulent Websites for Arrival Card Filling — National Immigration Administration
Online Arrival Card Filling — National Immigration Administration
Policy Interpretation of the Nationwide Online Accommodation Registration for Foreigners — National Immigration Administration
Online channels for Accommodation Registration for Foreigners — National Immigration Administration
Exit and Entry Administration Law of the PRC — National Immigration Administration
Regulations on the Administration of Foreigners Entry and Exit — National Immigration Administration
Guide to Payment Services in China — Chinese Embassy in Canada

steps.title: Check whether you can enter visa-free
prepare: Purpose of the trip and number of days
Onward ticket to a third country, for visa-free transit
steps.howTo:
1. China's unilateral visa exemption (免签) covers ordinary Canadian passports from February 17, 2026 to December 31, 2026, for business, tourism, family or friends visits, exchange and transit.
2. It allows up to 30 days per entry, counted from the day after arrival, through any port open to foreigners; multiple entries are allowed.
3. For a trip after December 31, 2026, check the embassy or NIA list to see whether it was extended.
4. The 240-hour visa-free transit (过境免签) covers Canada too: up to 10 days in the permitted areas, entering through one of 65 listed ports in 24 provinces, with a confirmed onward ticket to a third country or region.
5. Neither covers work, study or news reporting; those need a visa.
6. If visa-free fits your trip, mark the visa steps "Not for me". Not immigration advice; the embassy and NIA pages are the reference.

steps.title: Check passport validity and blank pages
steps.howTo:
1. The embassy asks for a passport with at least 6 months of validity left and blank visa pages.
2. If it falls short, renew it before applying for a visa or booking; renewals take weeks.

steps.title: Check the travel document for a child with a Chinese parent
conditions: Only for a child born in Canada to a Chinese-citizen parent
prepare: Parents' passports and status in Canada at the child's birth
steps.howTo:
1. Such a child may be treated as a Chinese citizen and travel on a Chinese travel document (旅行证, lǚxíngzhèng) rather than a visa on a Canadian passport.
2. Which one applies depends on the parents' status when the child was born.
3. See the "Born in Canada to a Chinese parent" plan before choosing.

steps.title: Choose the visa type and gather the documents
conditions: Only if you need a visa: the trip is longer, the purpose is not covered, or visa-free has ended
prepare: L (tourism): round-trip booking and hotel reservations, or an invitation
Q2 (visiting relatives who are Chinese citizens): the relative's invitation letter and a copy of their Chinese ID card
M (business): an invitation from the trade partner or trade fair
steps.howTo:
1. L is for tourism, Q2 for short visits to relatives who are Chinese citizens or foreigners with permanent residence in China (up to 180 days), M for business.
2. A Q2 invitation letter gives your details, the visit (purpose, dates, places, relationship, who pays) and the inviter's details, with a copy of the inviter's Chinese ID card.
3. For Q2, the embassy also lists proof of the family relationship: a birth or marriage certificate, or a kinship certificate from the public security bureau or a notary.
4. Check whether your centre's checklist also asks for the relative's household register (户口本, hùkǒu běn).

steps.title: Fill in the online form and book the visa centre
conditions: Only if you need a visa
prepare: Find the Chinese Visa Application Service Center for your consular district
Scans of the documents to upload
steps.howTo:
1. Since September 30, 2025, applicants in Canada fill in the form and upload documents on the China Online Visa Application system (COVA), then go to the Chinese Visa Application Service Center.
2. Each centre serves a consular district; the embassy lists which one covers where you live.
3. Print and sign the form and its confirmation page.

steps.title: Submit, give fingerprints if asked, and collect the visa
conditions: Only if you need a visa
steps.howTo:
1. From December 17, 2025 to December 31, 2026, short-term visa applicants staying 180 days or less are exempt from fingerprints; D, J1, Q1, S1, X1 and Z applicants still give them.
2. The embassy lists regular processing as 3 working days, with express and rush for extra fees; the centre may take longer or ask for more documents or an interview.
3. The 10 days here is a planning estimate that leaves room for mail and requests.

steps.title: Set up mobile payments with a foreign card
prepare: A Visa, Mastercard or UnionPay card
steps.howTo:
1. Alipay and Weixin Pay (WeChat Pay) accept foreign phone numbers and let you add Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay, JCB, Diners Club and Discover cards.
2. Set them up at home and make a small test payment.
3. Foreign cards work where their logo is shown; UnionPay works at all merchant terminals on the mainland.
4. The embassy's Guide to Payment Services in China walks through each option.

steps.title: Fill in the arrival card online
steps.howTo:
1. Since November 20, 2025, foreigners can submit the arrival card (入境卡, rùjìng kǎ) before travelling on the NIA website, the "NIA 12367" app, or WeChat and Alipay mini-programs.
2. It is free; NIA warns of fake sites charging fees, so use only the official channels.
3. Kiosks and paper cards are still available at the port.

steps.title: Enter China and note your stay limit
prepare: Address and phone of where you stay
steps.howTo:
1. The border officer checks your passport, visa or visa-free eligibility, and arrival card.
2. Visa-free days count from the day after arrival; on a visa, the stay is the duration printed on it.
3. Write down the last day you can stay; the rest of this plan uses it.

steps.title: Register where you stay within 24 hours
steps.howTo:
1. Accommodation registration (住宿登记, zhùsù dēngjì): hotels register guests for you.
2. Staying with family or friends, you or your host register within 24 hours of arrival, online through the NIA website, the "NIA 12367" app, or WeChat and Alipay mini-programs, or in person at the local police station.
3. Online registration counts the same as registering in person; missing it can bring a warning or a fine.
4. Register again each time you move to a new home that is not a hotel.

steps.title: Get a local SIM card
conditions: Only if you want a Chinese phone number
steps.howTo:
1. Mobile numbers in China are registered in the user's real name, so carriers ask for your passport.
2. Buy at a carrier store rather than a street stall.
3. A local number makes app sign-ups and payments easier.

steps.title: Extend the stay at the exit-entry office
conditions: Only if you need to stay longer than your visa or visa-free period
steps.howTo:
1. Apply at the exit-entry administration of the local public security bureau (公安局出入境管理, gōng'ānjú chūrùjìng guǎnlǐ) where you are staying.
2. The Exit and Entry Administration Law asks for the application at least 7 days before the stay runs out, and the total extension cannot exceed the original stay.
3. Visa-free travellers can also ask this office for a stay permit.
4. The date here assumes a 30-day stay; move it to at least 7 days before your real last day.

steps.title: Change to a residence permit or a new purpose
conditions: Only if you plan to live in China, e.g. family reunion with a Chinese spouse or parent
steps.howTo:
1. Holders of a Q1 (family reunion) or similar visa apply for a residence permit at the local exit-entry administration within 30 days of entry.
2. The office decides within 15 days.
3. A change of purpose can also be requested at that office after entry.
4. For moving to China, see the "Relocating to China · Canadian with Chinese family" plan.

steps.title: Leave before the permitted stay ends
prepare: Keep the boarding pass and visa copies
steps.howTo:
1. Leave by the last day of your visa-free period, visa stay or extension.
2. For 240-hour transit, leave for a third country within 10 days on the booked onward ticket.
3. The date here assumes a 30-day visa-free stay; move it to your real last day.

title: Travelling abroad from China
summary: Paperwork plan for a mainland resident going abroad or to Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan: passport or travel permit and endorsement, the destination's visa, foreign currency, insurance, leaving and coming back through customs.
conditions: You live in mainland China and hold a Chinese passport or travel permit
You are travelling for a visit, holiday or business, not moving abroad
The date is the day you leave

sources.title: National Immigration Administration
National Immigration Administration: Photo guide for exit-entry documents (出入境证件相片照相指引)
Exit and Entry Administration Law of the PRC — National Immigration Administration
China Consular Service Network (中国领事服务网) — Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Notice on further facilitating personal current account foreign exchange business — State Administration of Foreign Exchange
State Administration of Foreign Exchange
General Administration of Customs

steps.title: Check or apply for the passport (普通护照)
prepare: Photo meeting the exit-entry photo rules, or taken at the office
conditions: Only if you are going to a foreign country
steps.howTo:
1. Mainland residents can apply for an ordinary passport at any exit-entry administration office in the country, or book through the NIA 12367 app.
2. Many countries ask for at least 6 months of validity left at entry and blank visa pages.
3. Some groups, such as certain public employees, go through their employer first.
4. The 14 days is an estimate; check current processing times locally.

steps.title: Get the destination's visa or confirm visa-free entry
prepare: Bank statements, employment letter or invitation, as the destination asks
conditions: Only if you are going to a foreign country
steps.howTo:
1. Entry rules are set by the destination, not China; its embassy or official visa site is the reference.
2. The China Consular Service Network lists which countries let Chinese passport holders in visa-free or with a visa on arrival.
3. Some countries want an online authorisation before travel even without a visa.
4. Processing times vary widely; the 30 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Get the Hong Kong and Macao permit and endorsement (港澳通行证 / 签注)
documents: Exit-Entry Permit for Travelling to and from Hong Kong and Macao (往来港澳通行证)
prepare: Photo meeting the exit-entry photo rules
conditions: Only if you are going to Hong Kong or Macao
steps.howTo:
1. Mainland residents travel to Hong Kong and Macao on the permit, not a passport; each trip type needs an endorsement (签注), such as tourism, business or family visit.
2. The permit for adults is valid for 10 years; endorsements are valid for a set time and number of trips.
3. Endorsements can often be added again at self-service machines in exit-entry offices.
4. Check current endorsement types for your hukou city.

steps.title: Get the Taiwan permit and endorsement (往来台湾通行证 / 签注)
documents: Travel Permit to and from Taiwan (往来台湾通行证)
prepare: Photo meeting the exit-entry photo rules
Purpose of the trip and supporting papers
conditions: Only if you are going to Taiwan
steps.howTo:
1. Mainland residents travel to Taiwan on this permit with an endorsement for the trip type.
2. An entry permit from the Taiwan side is also needed.
3. Which trip types are open changes over time; check current rules with the exit-entry office before booking.

steps.title: Buy travel insurance
prepare: Medical cover amount the visa asks for, if any
steps.howTo:
1. Basic medical insurance in China generally does not pay for treatment abroad.
2. Some visas, such as Schengen visas, ask for proof of travel medical insurance with a minimum cover.
3. Check what it pays for medical care, evacuation, delays and lost baggage. Not financial advice.

steps.title: Arrange foreign currency and cards (购汇)
prepare: Bank card that works abroad, e.g. UnionPay or Visa or Mastercard
Some cash in the local currency
steps.howTo:
1. Individuals can buy foreign currency at banks within a yearly convenience quota (年度便利化额度), currently US$50,000 a person; check current with the bank or SAFE.
2. The quota is for current items such as travel and study; it does not cover things like buying property or securities abroad.
3. Tell the bank about the trip so cards are not blocked, and check fees for spending abroad.
4. Carrying cash out above set limits needs a customs declaration; check current limits.

steps.title: Save consular contacts and register the trip
prepare: Embassy or consulate contacts at the destination
conditions: Optional
steps.howTo:
1. The 中国领事 (China Consular) app has voluntary registration of Chinese citizens abroad and travel alerts for each country.
2. The embassy or consulate at the destination helps with lost passports and emergencies.
3. Check the app for current travel reminders before leaving.

steps.title: Leave through the border check
prepare: Customs declaration, if carrying cash or goods above the limits
steps.howTo:
1. Adults with a passport or permit and a recorded fingerprint can usually use the self-service e-channels (自助通道).
2. The border officer or e-channel checks the document and, for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, the endorsement.
3. Keep the boarding pass until you are back.

steps.title: Come back through customs with goods bought abroad
prepare: List and value of goods bought abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Residents coming back have a duty-free allowance for personal goods bought abroad, plus a separate one for arrival duty-free shops; check current figures with customs.
2. Goods above the allowance, or cash above the set limit, go through the red declaration channel; otherwise the green channel.
3. Some items, such as certain foods, plants and meat, are restricted.
4. The date assumes a one-week trip; move it to your return day.

title: Born in Canada to a Chinese parent
summary: Documents for a child born in Canada with at least one Chinese-citizen parent: the Canadian passport, the child's position under China's Nationality Law, the document for a first trip to China, and what each path involves at 18.
conditions: For a child born in Canada
At least one parent is a Chinese citizen

sources.title: Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China (National Immigration Administration)
Consulate General in Toronto: passport and travel document application guide (申办护照旅行证须知)
Chinese Embassy in Canada: passport and travel document application guide (申办须知)
Consulate General in Toronto: passport and travel document FAQ
Consulate General in Toronto: China visa application guide
Chinese Embassy in Canada: visa introduction and Q&A
Chinese Embassy in Canada: online Chinese visa application
Chinese Embassy in Canada: FAQ on the unilateral visa-free policy
NIA: Instructions on Application for Naturalization as a Chinese National
NIA: Instructions on Application for Renunciation of Chinese Nationality
How to apply for a child passport in Canada
Get proof of citizenship (citizenship certificate)
Apply for a citizenship certificate
Give up (renounce) Canadian citizenship
Renounce Canadian citizenship: who can apply

steps.title: Ask the Chinese embassy or a consulate how China treats the child's nationality
documents: Consulate's answer on the child's nationality position
prepare: Both parents' passports held at the time of the birth
Both parents' Canadian status documents at the time of the birth (PR card, citizenship certificate, work or study permit)
Any other countries' residence documents the parents held then
steps.howTo:
1. China's Nationality Law (中华人民共和国国籍法), Article 5: a person born abroad with at least one Chinese-national parent has Chinese nationality; but if a Chinese-national parent has settled abroad (定居国外) and the child acquires a foreign nationality at birth, the child does not have Chinese nationality.
2. A child born in Canada is a Canadian citizen at birth, so the question is whether the Chinese parent had settled abroad at the time of the birth.
3. The consulates ask for both parents' passports and their residence documents in the birth country at the time of the birth; the parents' status then (for example Canadian permanent residence or citizenship, or a temporary permit) is what they review.
4. China does not recognise dual nationality for Chinese nationals (Article 3).
5. Confirm the child's status with the Chinese Embassy in Ottawa or the consulate for your area (Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary or Montreal); this plan does not decide it.

steps.title: Keep the family's status records from the time of the birth
documents: Copies of the parents' status documents at the birth
prepare: Copies of both parents' passports valid at the birth
Copies of both parents' Canadian status documents valid at the birth
Original birth certificate listing both parents
Any written reply from the embassy or consulate
steps.howTo:
1. Chinese consulates ask for the passports and residence documents both parents held when the child was born, not the current ones.
2. The same papers come up for a travel document, a visa application for a child with a Chinese parent, and any later nationality application.
3. Parents' documents get renewed or replaced over the years; keep copies of the ones valid on the birth date.

steps.title: Apply for the child's Canadian passport
prepare: Long-form (parental) birth certificate from the province of birth
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
steps.howTo:
1. Wait for the provincial birth certificate; the long-form certificate from the province of birth, or a citizenship certificate, is accepted as proof of citizenship.
2. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail.
3. A child passport is valid for up to 5 years and can't be renewed.
4. The child passport is left unsigned; a parent's signature makes it invalid.
5. The date here is a planning estimate; move it to 2 months before travel.

steps.title: Apply for a Chinese travel document (旅行证) for a first trip to China
prepare: China Consular (中国领事) app account
Child's digital photo and two paper photos (33 x 48 mm)
Both parents' passports held at the birth
Both parents' residence documents at the birth
conditions: Only if the embassy or consulate treats the child as a Chinese national
steps.howTo:
1. The consulates issue a travel document to a child born in Canada with a de facto nationality conflict (事实上存在国籍冲突), applied for through the China Consular app while the child is in Canada.
2. The consulates quote Article 5 of the Nationality Law on this page: the travel document is for a child the law treats as Chinese.
3. The travel document and a Chinese visa in the Canadian passport are alternatives: a child applies for one or the other, depending on how the consulate treats the child.
4. The Toronto consulate quotes about 4 business days and the Embassy about 10 business days from complete materials; the date here is a planning estimate, so move it to 2 months before travel.
5. A child already holding a valid Chinese passport uses that instead.
6. Confirm the child's status with the Chinese embassy or a consulate in Canada before applying.

steps.title: Apply for a Chinese visa in the Canadian passport for a first trip to China
prepare: Invitation letter and the relative's Chinese ID copy, for a family visit (Q2) or family reunion (Q1)
Birth certificate, as proof of the relationship
Parents' status documents at the birth
conditions: Only if the embassy or consulate treats the child as a foreign national
steps.howTo:
1. Ordinary visas are applied for through a Chinese Visa Application Service Center in Canada, with online forms at visaforchina.cn; standard processing is about 4 business days.
2. Q2 is for a short family visit of up to 180 days; Q1 is for family reunion residence of more than 180 days.
3. For a Q1 visa for fosterage (寄养) of a child with a Chinese-citizen parent, the Toronto consulate lists proof that the Chinese parent had settled abroad at the birth; this ties back to Article 5 of the Nationality Law.
4. A visa-free policy for Canadian ordinary passports, announced to run until 31 December 2026, covers visits of up to 30 days; check whether it is still in force and whether it applies to the child.
5. Confirm the child's status with the Chinese embassy or a consulate in Canada before applying.
6. The date here is a planning estimate; move it to 1 month before travel.

steps.title: Apply for a Canadian citizenship certificate as extra proof
conditions: Only if you want proof of Canadian citizenship besides the provincial birth certificate
steps.howTo:
1. A citizenship certificate is IRCC's proof of Canadian citizenship; for a child born in Canada, the provincial birth certificate is already accepted as proof for a passport.
2. A parent at birth can apply for a child under 18.
3. IRCC publishes current processing times; the 6 months here is a planning estimate.

steps.title: At 18: what each nationality path involves
prepare: Any Chinese travel document or passport issued so far
The parents' status records from the birth
steps.howTo:
1. This is information only; which path, if any, is the person's own decision.
2. China does not recognise dual nationality for Chinese nationals (Nationality Law, Article 3).
3. Keeping Canadian citizenship only: a Chinese national who has settled abroad and acquired a foreign nationality of their own free will loses Chinese nationality automatically (Article 9); a Chinese national settled abroad can also apply to renounce it (Article 10), through a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad.
4. Taking Chinese nationality: a foreign national with Chinese-national close relatives can apply to be naturalized (Article 7) and does not keep the foreign nationality once approved (Article 8); the application includes a written declaration giving up the foreign nationality.
5. Giving up Canadian citizenship: IRCC accepts renunciation from someone at least 18 who is, or will become, a citizen of another country and does not live in Canada.
6. Before 18, parents or other legal representatives can file nationality applications for a child (Article 14).
7. Confirm the person's status with the Chinese embassy or a consulate in Canada.

title: Adult paperwork · renewals and yearly tax · British Columbia
summary: The recurring paperwork of adult life in British Columbia from 19 to 65: the yearly return and credits, savings room, ID renewals, health cover and legal papers.
conditions: An adult living in British Columbia, from 19 to 65
Some steps are only for Canadian citizens, renters, home owners or people without workplace benefits

sources.title: Important dates for individuals — Canada Revenue Agency
Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB) — Canada Revenue Agency
Renter's tax credit — Province of British Columbia
Home owner grant — Province of British Columbia
Before you contribute to a TFSA — Canada.ca
Opening your FHSAs — Canada.ca
How contributions affect your RRSP deduction limit — Canada.ca
Apply for a new adult passport — Canada.ca
Renew or replace a BC Services Card — Province of British Columbia
Fair PharmaCare plan — Province of British Columbia
Health Connect Registry — HealthLink BC
Canadian Dental Care Plan: Do you qualify — Canada.ca
Incapacity planning — Province of British Columbia

steps.title: File the yearly tax return
prepare: Receipts for tuition, rent, medical and donations
steps.howTo:
1. The return is due April 30 each year; with self-employment income (yours or a spouse’s), filing is due June 15, but any balance is still due April 30.
2. Filing even with little or no income keeps benefits such as the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB) and, for parents, the Canada Child Benefit coming.
3. With a spouse or common-law partner, both file every year; benefits are worked out from family income.
4. The B.C. Family Benefit comes automatically with the Canada Child Benefit; there is no separate application.
5. This repeats every year; the date here is an estimate for the first return after 19.

steps.title: Claim the B.C. renter's tax credit
conditions: Only if you rented a home in B.C. for at least 6 months of the year
steps.howTo:
1. The credit is claimed on form BC479 with the tax return.
2. It is for people 19 or older, a parent, or living with a spouse on December 31, who rented an eligible unit in B.C. for at least 6 one-month periods.
3. The maximum is $400; it shrinks above an income threshold and is refundable (check current amounts).
4. This repeats every year with the return.

steps.title: Check TFSA, FHSA and RRSP room
steps.howTo:
1. TFSA room builds from the year you turn 18 and carries forward; CRA My Account shows it, but recent contributions may not be counted yet.
2. An FHSA is for first-time home buyers: up to $8,000 a year and $40,000 in total (check current); ask the issuer about the minimum age to open one in B.C., where the age of majority is 19.
3. RRSP room comes from earned income and is on the notice of assessment; contributions for a tax year are due 60 days after the year ends.
4. Not financial advice; this repeats every year.

steps.title: Make a will, enduring power of attorney and representation agreement
prepare: Who should decide on money and on care
Beneficiaries on TFSA, RRSP, pension and insurance
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. an enduring power of attorney covers financial affairs, and a representation agreement covers health and personal care.
2. An advance directive gives or refuses consent to health care directly.
3. The standard provincial forms are optional.
4. Review after marriage, separation, a child or buying a home.
5. Not legal advice; age 19 here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Register for Fair PharmaCare
conditions: Only if you are enrolled in MSP and not registered yet
prepare: Net income from the tax return of 2 years ago
steps.howTo:
1. Fair PharmaCare is open to anyone enrolled in MSP; the deductible depends on family net income, not age.
2. Register online, by phone with Health Insurance BC, or on paper.
3. Return the CRA consent form within 30 days, or the temporary coverage ends.
4. Coverage continues while income can be checked with the CRA each year, so keep filing taxes.

steps.title: Join the Health Connect Registry
conditions: Only if you have no family doctor or nurse practitioner
steps.howTo:
1. The Health Connect Registry matches people with a family doctor or nurse practitioner in their area.
2. Register online or by calling 8-1-1.
3. Keep the contact details current while waiting.

steps.title: Check the Canadian Dental Care Plan
conditions: Only if you have no dental insurance and adjusted family net income is under $90,000
steps.howTo:
1. The plan is for Canadian residents for tax purposes with no access to private dental insurance, including health spending accounts.
2. Adjusted family net income is under $90,000, and the tax returns for the previous year are filed.
3. Government dental programs do not count as private insurance.
4. Check again whenever workplace benefits start or stop.

steps.title: Renew the adult passport
conditions: Only for Canadian citizens with a passport
prepare: Expiry date of the current passport
Travel plans in the next 6 months
steps.howTo:
1. Adult passports are valid for 5 or 10 years.
2. Many countries want 6 months of validity left past the return date.
3. The last child passport usually runs out around 20; move this date to your own expiry.
4. This repeats every 5 or 10 years.

steps.title: Renew the driver's licence and BC Services Card
documents: BC Driver's Licence and Services Card
steps.howTo:
1. The licence and the BC Services Card can be one combined card, renewed at an ICBC driver licensing office; renewals are usually every 5 years (check the expiry on the card).
2. Renewing the BC Services Card also renews MSP enrolment.
3. Without a licence, the photo BC Services Card is renewed on its own before it expires.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the expiry on your card. This repeats at each expiry.

steps.title: Claim the home owner grant
conditions: Only if you own and live in your home in B.C.
steps.howTo:
1. The grant lowers property tax on a principal residence and is claimed every year.
2. Claim after the property tax notice arrives and before the tax due date.
3. Apply online, by phone or at Service BC; check the current assessed value limit.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to your next property tax notice.

title: Adult paperwork · renewals and yearly tax · China
summary: Paperwork plan for adult life in mainland China from 22 to 60: ID card, driving licence, passport and permit renewals, the yearly income tax reconciliation and deductions, social insurance record checks, residents' medical insurance and the private pension. Recurring items show once, at their first date.
conditions: You are a Chinese citizen living in mainland China, aged 22 to 60
Renewal dates depend on when each document was issued; the dates here assume common ages, so move them to the expiry dates on your own cards

Resident Identity Card Law of the PRC (2011 amendment, fingerprints) — National People's Congress
Motor Vehicle Driving Licence Application and Use Provisions (MPS Order 162) — gov.cn
Traffic Safety Integrated Service Platform (交管12123) — Ministry of Public Security
National Immigration Administration

State Taxation Administration
