National Healthcare Security Administration

steps.title: Confirm next year's special additional deductions (专项附加扣除)
documents: Deduction declaration in the individual income tax app
prepare: Children's education or infant care details
conditions: Only if a deduction applies to you
steps.howTo:
1. Each December the individual income tax app (个人所得税) asks for the next year's deductions to be confirmed; unconfirmed ones may stop being applied from January.
2. Deductions cover children's education, infant care under 3, continuing education, serious illness medical costs, mortgage interest or rent, and elderly support.
3. Check each item still fits: a move, a new child, a paid-off mortgage or a parent turning 60 changes them.
4. This repeats every December; the date here is only the first one, so move it to December.

steps.title: Do the annual income tax reconciliation (年度汇算)
prepare: Income from all employers and other sources in the year
Class I bank card for refunds
conditions: Only if you had income taxed in China the year before
steps.howTo:
1. The reconciliation for a tax year runs from March 1 to June 30 of the following year, in the individual income tax app.
2. It settles a refund or extra tax across wages, labour fees, author fees and royalties.
3. The tax authority sets who is required to file; early in the window the app may ask for a booking.
4. This repeats every year; the date here is only the first one, so move it into the March to June window.

steps.title: Check your social insurance record (社保缴费记录)
prepare: Electronic social security card or the 掌上12333 app
A list of employers and cities you worked in
steps.howTo:
1. Look up contribution months on the National Social Insurance Public Service Platform, the 掌上12333 app or the local platform.
2. Compare them with payslips; missing months, a wrong contribution base (缴费基数) or a gap between jobs are easier to fix within the year.
3. Months of unbroken contributions often count for home purchase eligibility, hukou points and school places in big cities.
4. This repeats yearly; the date here is only the first one.

steps.title: Pay the yearly residents' medical insurance (城乡居民医保)
prepare: Where your hukou or residence permit is
conditions: Only if you are not covered by employee medical insurance, e.g. not employed or between jobs
steps.howTo:
1. Urban and rural residents' basic medical insurance is paid once a year for the next calendar year, usually in a window set locally, often from autumn to the end of the year.
2. Pay through the tax app, a bank app, WeChat or Alipay, or the local medical insurance office.
3. Paying late can bring a waiting period before cover starts; check the local rule.
4. This repeats yearly; the date here is only the first one, so move it to the local window.

steps.title: Pay into the private pension account (个人养老金)
prepare: A bank that offers private pension accounts
How much to put in this year
conditions: Only if you pay into the employee or residents' basic pension and choose to take part
steps.howTo:
1. The private pension (个人养老金) is voluntary; the account is opened through the national platform or a bank app.
2. Contributions up to 12,000 yuan a year are deductible from income tax; payments by December 31 count for that tax year, so claim them in the reconciliation or with the employer.
3. The money is locked until retirement or another allowed reason; withdrawals are taxed at a low flat rate (check current).
4. This repeats yearly; the date here is only the first one. Not financial advice.

steps.title: Decide on the city's supplementary health cover (惠民保)
conditions: Optional; only if your city runs such a scheme
steps.howTo:
1. Many cities back a low-cost commercial plan (城市定制型商业医疗保险, often called 惠民保) that pays some costs basic medical insurance does not.
2. Enrolment is usually open once a year, often with no health questions; the deductible and what it pays vary by city.
3. It is private insurance, not social insurance. Not financial advice.
4. This repeats yearly; move the date to the city's window.

steps.title: Renew the driving licence at 6 years (机动车驾驶证换证)
prepare: Health check the vehicle office asks for
conditions: Only if you hold a driving licence; the date assumes it was first issued at about 18
steps.howTo:
1. Under MPS Order 162, a first licence is valid for 6 years; renewal is applied for within 90 days before it expires.
2. A driver who never reached 12 points in any scoring cycle usually moves to a 10-year licence, then to a long-term one; otherwise the next one is 6 years again.
3. Many places accept the renewal and health check online through 交管12123, including outside the issuing area.
4. Move this date to 90 days before the expiry on your licence.

steps.title: Renew the driving licence at 10 years
prepare: Health check the vehicle office asks for
conditions: Only if you hold a driving licence and moved to a 10-year one
steps.howTo:
1. At the end of the 10-year licence, a driver without a 12-point cycle usually moves to a long-term licence (长期).
2. Apply within 90 days before expiry, online or at the vehicle management office.
3. Move this date to 90 days before the expiry on your licence.

steps.title: Renew the resident ID card at 26 (居民身份证换领)
prepare: ID photo taken at the office or an approved studio
conditions: Only if your card was issued between 16 and 25, so valid for 10 years
steps.howTo:
1. Cards issued from 16 to 25 are valid for 10 years; from 26 to 45, 20 years; from 46, long-term.
2. A new card can be applied for up to 3 months before the old one expires, at the police station where the hukou is, and in many cities anywhere in the country (异地换领).
3. Fingerprints are recorded again; a temporary ID card can be issued while waiting.
4. The date assumes a card issued at 16; move it to your card's expiry.

steps.title: Renew the passport and the Hong Kong and Macao permit (护照 / 港澳通行证)
documents: Exit-Entry Permit for Travelling to and from Hong Kong and Macao (往来港澳通行证)
prepare: Photo meeting the exit-entry photo rules
conditions: Only if you hold a passport or travel permit
steps.howTo:
1. Adult passports and Hong Kong and Macao permits are valid for 10 years.
2. Mainland residents can apply at any exit-entry administration office in the country, not only where the hukou is.
3. Many countries ask for 6 months of validity left at entry, so renew well before expiry.
4. This repeats every 10 years; the date assumes documents first issued at 18, so move it to about 6 months before your own expiry.

steps.title: Renew the resident ID card at 46 for a long-term card
prepare: ID photo taken at the office or an approved studio
conditions: Only if your 20-year card expires at about 46
steps.howTo:
1. A card issued from 46 is long-term (长期) and does not need renewing for age.
2. Apply up to 3 months before the old one expires.
3. The date assumes a card issued at 26; move it to your card's expiry.

title: Adult paperwork · renewals and yearly tax · Ontario
summary: The recurring paperwork of adult life in Ontario from 18 to 65: the yearly return and credits, savings room, ID renewals, health cover and legal papers.
conditions: An adult living in Ontario, from 18 to 65
Some steps are only for Canadian citizens, renters, home owners or people without workplace benefits

sources.title: Important dates for individuals — Canada Revenue Agency
Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB) — Canada Revenue Agency
Ontario Trillium Benefit — Ontario.ca
Before you contribute to a TFSA — Canada.ca
Opening your FHSAs — Canada.ca
How contributions affect your RRSP deduction limit — Canada.ca
Apply for a new adult passport — Canada.ca
Renew a driver's licence — Ontario.ca
Health card renewal — Ontario.ca
Learn about OHIP+ — Ontario.ca
Get help with high prescription drug costs — Ontario.ca
Find a family doctor or nurse practitioner — Ontario.ca
Canadian Dental Care Plan: Do you qualify — Canada.ca
Make a power of attorney — Ontario.ca

steps.title: File the yearly tax return
prepare: Receipts for tuition, rent, property tax, medical and donations
steps.howTo:
1. The return is due April 30 each year; with self-employment income (yours or a spouse’s), filing is due June 15, but any balance is still due April 30.
2. Filing even with little or no income keeps benefits such as the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB) and, for parents, the Canada Child Benefit coming.
3. With a spouse or common-law partner, both file every year; benefits are worked out from family income.
4. The Ontario Child Benefit comes with the Canada Child Benefit; there is no separate application.
5. This repeats every year; the date here is an estimate for the first return after 18.

steps.title: Apply for the Ontario Trillium Benefit (ON-BEN)
conditions: Only if you paid rent or property tax in Ontario, or may get the Ontario sales tax credit
documents: ON-BEN Application Form, in the tax return package
prepare: Rent paid or property tax paid for the year
Address and landlord or roll number details
steps.howTo:
1. The Ontario Trillium Benefit combines the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit, the Northern Ontario Energy Credit and the Ontario Sales Tax Credit.
2. It is applied for with the ON-BEN form in the tax return, by April 30.
3. The sales tax credit is for people 19 or older, or younger with a spouse or child; other age and household rules apply to each part (check current).
4. Amounts over $500 can be paid monthly from July or as one payment the next June.
5. This repeats every year with the return.

steps.title: Check TFSA, FHSA and RRSP room
steps.howTo:
1. TFSA room builds from the year you turn 18 and carries forward; CRA My Account shows it, but recent contributions may not be counted yet.
2. An FHSA is for first-time home buyers 18 or older: up to $8,000 a year and $40,000 in total (check current).
3. RRSP room comes from earned income and is on the notice of assessment; contributions for a tax year are due 60 days after the year ends.
4. Not financial advice; this repeats every year.

steps.title: Make a will and powers of attorney for property and personal care
documents: Continuing power of attorney for property
Power of attorney for personal care
prepare: Who should decide on money and on care
Beneficiaries on TFSA, RRSP, pension and insurance
steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario a power of attorney for property covers money and property (from 18), and a power of attorney for personal care covers health and care decisions (from 16).
2. Both can be made for free with the Ontario kit or online tool, or with a lawyer.
3. Review after marriage, separation, a child or buying a home.
4. Not legal advice; age 18 here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Check drug cover when OHIP+ ends at 25
conditions: Only if you have no private drug plan
prepare: Household income from the last tax return
steps.howTo:
1. OHIP+ covers eligible prescriptions for people 24 and under with OHIP and no private plan.
2. It stops on the 25th birthday, or once a private plan starts.
3. The Trillium Drug Program helps with high drug costs compared with household income, including for people with a private plan.
4. Check a workplace or student plan first.

steps.title: Register with Health Care Connect
conditions: Only if you have no family doctor or nurse practitioner
prepare: Mailing address matching the health card
steps.howTo:
1. Health Care Connect assigns a Care Connector to look for a family doctor, nurse practitioner or team taking new patients nearby.
2. Register online or by calling 811; people who used it before re-register by phone.
3. Keep the health card current while waiting.

steps.title: Check the Canadian Dental Care Plan
conditions: Only if you have no dental insurance and adjusted family net income is under $90,000
steps.howTo:
1. The plan is for Canadian residents for tax purposes with no access to private dental insurance, including health spending accounts.
2. Adjusted family net income is under $90,000, and the tax returns for the previous year are filed.
3. Government dental programs do not count as private insurance.
4. Check again whenever workplace benefits start or stop.

steps.title: Renew the adult passport
conditions: Only for Canadian citizens with a passport
prepare: Expiry date of the current passport
Travel plans in the next 6 months
steps.howTo:
1. Adult passports are valid for 5 or 10 years.
2. Many countries want 6 months of validity left past the return date.
3. The last child passport usually runs out around 20; move this date to your own expiry.
4. This repeats every 5 or 10 years.

steps.title: Renew the driver's licence
conditions: Only if you have an Ontario driver's licence
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario licences are renewed every 5 years, online if eligible or at a ServiceOntario centre.
2. Free reminders by email, text or phone can be set up.
3. The date here is an estimate; move it to the expiry on your licence. This repeats every 5 years.

steps.title: Renew the photo health card
prepare: Driver's licence or Ontario Photo Card, for online renewal
steps.howTo:
1. Photo health cards are renewed every 5 years; a reminder comes by mail.
2. Online renewal works within 180 days before or after expiry, with an up-to-date photo on file and a licence or Ontario Photo Card.
3. A red and white card is replaced in person at ServiceOntario.
4. The new card arrives in about 4 to 6 weeks, at no cost. This repeats every 5 years.

title: Getting married · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for a wedding in British Columbia, from booking an officiant and the marriage licence to the certificate, name updates, taxes and wills.
conditions: You are marrying in British Columbia
Both of you are 19 or older; at 16 to 18, written consent from parents or guardians is needed
Neither of you is still married to someone else

sources.title: Marriage — Province of British Columbia
Marriage licences — Province of British Columbia
Search for a marriage licence issuer — B.C. Ministry of Health
Marriage commissioners — Province of British Columbia
Marriage Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 282
Marriage registration — Province of British Columbia
Marriage certificates — Province of British Columbia
Change your name after marriage or divorce — Province of British Columbia
Legal change of name application — Province of British Columbia
MSP: Changing or correcting a name — Province of British Columbia
BC Services Card: Change your personal information — Province of British Columbia
Change your name, address or gender — ICBC
Update your Social Insurance Number record — Canada.ca
Changing the name on your passport — Canada.ca
Change your marital status with the CRA — Canada.ca
Wills, Estates and Succession Act, S.B.C. 2009, c. 13
Wills, Estates and Succession Act Questions and Answers — Province of British Columbia
Incapacity planning — Province of British Columbia
Sponsor your spouse, partner or child — Canada.ca
Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Who can apply — Canada.ca
Death of a TFSA holder (successor holder) — Canada.ca

steps.title: Book an officiant and the ceremony
prepare: For a religious ceremony, check the religious representative is registered in B.C.
For a civil ceremony, search the provincial list of marriage commissioners
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. a marriage is performed by a religious representative registered with the Vital Statistics Agency, or by a marriage commissioner.
2. Marriage commissioners offer non-religious ceremonies; the province has an online search to find one in your area.
3. Commissioners charge a set fee plus travel costs; check the current fees on the marriage commissioners page.
4. The 6 months here is an estimate; popular dates can go sooner.

steps.title: Buy the marriage licence
prepare: Primary ID for both of you, e.g. birth certificate, citizenship card or permanent resident card
Proof the divorce order has taken effect, if either of you was married before
Written consent from parents or guardians, if either of you is 16 to 18
Check the current fee with the issuer
steps.howTo:
1. Licences are sold by marriage licence issuers, many of them private businesses such as insurance agencies, plus some Service BC offices; use the provincial search to find one.
2. Only one of you needs to go in person, with primary ID for both.
3. The issuer prints the licence on the spot; there is no waiting period.
4. The licence is valid for 3 months from the day it is issued, so buy it within 3 months before the wedding.
5. If recently divorced, wait until the divorce order takes effect before buying.

steps.title: Confirm two witnesses
prepare: Tell them to be there in person
steps.howTo:
1. The Marriage Act calls for at least 2 witnesses at the ceremony, besides the officiant.
2. After the ceremony the couple, both witnesses and the officiant sign the Marriage Licence and Registration of Marriage.

steps.title: Hold the ceremony and sign the licence
steps.howTo:
1. You, your spouse, the two witnesses and the officiant sign the Marriage Licence and Registration of Marriage after the ceremony.
2. A keepsake certificate from the officiant is not the legal, government-issued marriage certificate.

steps.title: Officiant sends the registration to Vital Statistics
prepare: Confirm with the officiant that it was sent
steps.howTo:
1. Within 48 hours of the wedding, the officiant submits the registration to the B.C. Vital Statistics Agency.
2. A marriage certificate can only be issued once the registration is processed.

steps.title: Receive the marriage certificate
prepare: Check the mailing address you gave when buying the licence
Decide whether you need extra copies
steps.howTo:
1. One official certificate comes by mail about 3 weeks after the wedding, to the address given on the licence application; it is included in the licence fee.
2. Either spouse can order more from Vital Statistics online, by mail or at Service BC once the marriage is registered.
3. Standard orders print within 5 business days plus mail; courier orders print the next business day.
4. The date here is an estimate; most name and record updates ask for this certificate.

steps.title: Decide which last name to use
conditions: Only if either of you wants to use a new last name
prepare: The exact last name you will use, as shown on the marriage certificate
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. either spouse can assume the other's last name, or both names joined with a hyphen or a space, without a legal change of name.
2. Assuming a name does not change the name on your birth record.
3. For another name, part of a name, or a change to first or middle names, apply for a legal change of name under the Name Act: 19 or older, living in B.C. at least 3 months, with a fingerprint-based criminal record check.
4. A legal change of name takes about 24 weeks to process.

steps.title: Update your name with MSP
conditions: Only if you changed your last name
prepare: Marriage certificate showing the new last name
steps.howTo:
1. Update MSP first, so the name matches when ICBC opens your file.
2. Use the online MSP Account Change Request or call Health Insurance BC; there is no fee.
3. If your spouse is already on your MSP account, no document may be needed; otherwise send the marriage certificate.
4. Allow 21 business days; the 30 days here is an estimate. A confirmation letter comes by mail.

steps.title: Get a new BC Services Card and driver's licence or BCID
conditions: Only if you changed your last name
prepare: Marriage certificate linking the old and new last names
steps.howTo:
1. Once the MSP letter arrives, visit an ICBC driver licensing office to order the new card.
2. Bring documents that link your last name at birth to the new one.
3. A BC Services Card combined with a driver's licence is updated in one visit.
4. The 14 days is an estimate, including mail time for the new card.

steps.title: Update the name on your SIN record
conditions: Only if you changed your last name
prepare: Document linking the old and new names
steps.howTo:
1. Service Canada asks you to update your SIN record when your name changes.
2. Update online or by mail; there is no fee.
3. Online confirmation takes about 5 business days; by mail about 20 business days.

steps.title: Apply for a passport in the new name
conditions: Only if you changed your last name and hold a Canadian passport
prepare: ID showing the new last name
Check the current fee and processing time
steps.howTo:
1. A new last name after marriage means applying for a new passport, not amending the old one.
2. Include ID in the new name and the marriage certificate showing the previous and current last name.
3. The 30 days is an estimate; check current processing times before booking travel.

steps.title: Tell the CRA you are married
steps.howTo:
1. The deadline is the end of the month after the month you married; e.g. married in March, tell the CRA by the end of April.
2. Update in CRA My Account or by phone (processed straight away), or mail form RC65 (4 to 6 weeks).
3. The date here is a safe estimate; move it to the real deadline.

steps.title: Add your spouse to workplace health and dental benefits
conditions: Only if either of you has health or dental benefits through work
steps.howTo:
1. Group plans usually treat marriage as a life event that lets you add a spouse outside the yearly enrolment period.
2. The window is set by each plan and is often 31 days from the wedding; after it, late enrolment may need health evidence or wait for the next enrolment period.
3. If both of you have plans, each plan's coordination of benefits rules decide which pays first.
4. Update life insurance and pension beneficiaries in the same session.

steps.title: Check the Canada Child Benefit and credits
conditions: Only if either of you has children or gets CRA benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Benefit and credit payments, including the Canada Child Benefit, are based on adjusted family net income, which now includes your spouse.
2. The CRA recalculates from the month after your marital status changed.
3. Check the new amounts in CRA My Account; a drop is normal if family income rose.

steps.title: Review wills, incapacity documents and beneficiaries
prepare: Beneficiaries on RRSPs, TFSAs, pensions and life insurance
Successor holder on a TFSA or FHSA
Who should decide for you if you cannot
steps.howTo:
1. Since March 31, 2014, marriage no longer revokes a will in B.C. under the Wills, Estates and Succession Act, so an old will stays in force until you change it.
2. A will revoked by marriage before that date is not revived.
3. If married spouses later separate in a way that gives rise to a family property interest, gifts to the spouse in a will are revoked as if the spouse died first.
4. For finances, B.C. uses an enduring power of attorney; for health and personal care, a representation agreement. The standard provincial forms are optional.
5. On a TFSA, a spouse can be named successor holder, so the account carries on in their name; the FHSA has the same option, and RRSPs and RRIFs take a beneficiary. Designations are made with the financial institution; check the plan documents.
6. Not legal advice; see a lawyer if your affairs are complicated.

steps.title: Look into sponsoring your spouse
conditions: Only if your spouse isn't a Canadian citizen or permanent resident
prepare: Check the current IRCC guide and fees
steps.howTo:
1. The sponsor must be 18 or older, a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or registered under the Indian Act, and usually live in Canada.
2. Your spouse applies for permanent residence and both applications go in together through the IRCC PR portal.
3. Processing times vary; check IRCC for current times.

title: Getting married · China
summary: Paperwork plan for registering a marriage in mainland China, from the optional health check and booking to the certificate, marriage leave, hukou, insurance, tax and housing fund.
conditions: You are registering the marriage in mainland China
The man is 22 or older and the woman is 20 or older (Civil Code, Article 1047)
Neither of you is married to someone else, and you are not close blood relatives
The steps below are for two mainland residents; with a foreign, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan partner, other documents and offices apply

sources.title: Marriage Registration Regulations (婚姻登记条例), State Council Decree No. 804 — gov.cn
New Marriage Registration Regulations: no hukou book, nationwide registration from May 10, 2025 — Xinhui District Government
Marriage registration "全国通办" policy Q&A (Ministry of Civil Affairs officials) — Luohu District Civil Affairs Bureau, Shenzhen
Nationwide marriage registration: the reform, five months on — Guangdong Department of Civil Affairs
Civil Code of the PRC (中华人民共和国民法典) — National People's Congress
Civil Code, Book Five: Marriage and Family — Suixi County Government

Reply on extending marriage leave (national 1980 notice, 1 to 3 days) — Wuhan Health Commission
Shanxi Population and Family Planning Regulations, Article 25 — Shanxi Health Commission
Decision amending the Sichuan Population and Family Planning Regulations — Sichuan Provincial People's Congress
Reply on pre-marital health checks (voluntary since 2003, free in many provinces) — National Health Commission
Employee medical insurance personal accounts can be used for close relatives — gov.cn
Interim Measures for Individual Income Tax Special Additional Deductions (国发〔2018〕41号) — State Taxation Administration
State Council decision amending the Housing Provident Fund Regulations (住房公积金管理条例, State Council Order No. 844, effective September 20, 2026; check current) — gov.cn

steps.title: Consider the pre-marital health check
conditions: Only if you choose to have it; it is voluntary
prepare: ID card for both of you
Ask the local maternal and child health centre whether the check is free where you live
steps.howTo:
1. The pre-marital health check (婚前医学检查) has been voluntary since the 2003 registration rules; the registration office does not ask for the report.
2. Many provinces offer it free, often at a centre next to or inside the registration office.
3. Some provinces add marriage leave for it: e.g. Sichuan adds 5 days if the check is done before registration.
4. The 45 days here is an estimate, to leave time for any follow-up.

steps.title: Plan marriage leave with your employer
conditions: Only if either of you is employed
prepare: Your province's current marriage leave rule
Dates you want off, around the registration and any wedding
steps.howTo:
1. The national rule is still a 1980 notice: 1 to 3 days of paid marriage leave (婚假), plus travel days if the two of you work in different places.
2. Provinces set longer leave in their population and family planning regulations, and many have extended it. Examples: Shanxi 30 days; Sichuan 20 days, plus 5 with a pre-marital check, from late 2025.
3. The leave follows the rule where you work; check your province's current text, as several changed in 2024 and 2025.
4. Leave counts from registration, not the wedding party; agree the dates with your employer in writing.

steps.title: Book the registration appointment
prepare: Pick any marriage registration office (婚姻登记处) in mainland China
A first and second choice of date
steps.howTo:
1. Since May 10, 2025, two mainland residents can register at any registration office in the country (全国通办), not just where one of you has hukou.
2. Offices may offer online appointments (预约) and a certificate ceremony; many book through the local civil affairs app or mini-program.
3. Popular dates fill early; the 14 days here is an estimate, so book sooner for a special date.

steps.title: Get joint photos for the certificate
prepare: Ask the office its photo size, background and number of copies
steps.howTo:
1. The certificate carries a joint photo of the two of you; offices usually ask for recent 2-inch half-length joint photos.
2. Many offices have a photo booth on site; check before you go.
3. The size and count are set by each office, not the regulations; treat these as typical, not fixed.

steps.title: Register the marriage at the civil affairs office
prepare: Original ID card for each of you
Both of you there in person
steps.howTo:
1. Both of you go in person and apply together for marriage registration (结婚登记).
2. Each of you shows your resident ID card and signs a declaration that you have no spouse and are not direct blood relatives or collateral relatives within three generations.
3. The hukou book (户口簿) is no longer needed since May 10, 2025.
4. The office checks your identity and marital status online; if you meet the conditions, it registers you on the spot and issues the marriage certificate (结婚证) the same day, one for each of you.
5. Registration is free of charge.

steps.title: Share medical insurance with your spouse
conditions: Only if either of you has employee medical insurance
prepare: Check your spouse is enrolled in basic medical insurance
The national medical insurance app, or your local one
steps.howTo:
1. Employee medical insurance does not add a spouse as a dependant; each person is insured on their own.
2. Through family sharing (家庭共济), the insured person's personal account can pay a spouse's resident medical insurance premiums and their eligible medical costs.
3. The spouse must be enrolled in basic medical insurance themselves; set up the authorisation in the medical insurance app or at the local office.
4. Sharing works within the same area and, in many provinces, across cities in the province; check your local rules.

steps.title: Update your income tax deductions
conditions: Only if either of you claims housing loan interest, rent or major medical deductions
prepare: The 个人所得税 app for both of you
Loan contracts for any first homes bought before marriage
steps.howTo:
1. Special additional deductions (专项附加扣除) are updated in the 个人所得税 app, through your employer or at the annual reconciliation (年度汇算).
2. Housing loan interest: a couple may agree which one of you claims it. If each of you bought a first home with a loan before marriage, after marriage you choose one home at 100% claimed by its buyer, or each claims 50% for your own home.
3. The choice cannot be changed within a tax year.
4. Housing rent: if you mainly work in the same city, only one of you can claim it.
5. Major medical costs can be claimed by the patient or their spouse.

steps.title: Move your hukou to join your spouse
conditions: Only if one of you wants to move hukou to the other's
prepare: Ask the police station (派出所) where the hukou would go about its rules
Hukou book of the household you are joining
steps.howTo:
1. Marriage does not change your hukou; moving it to join a spouse (投靠配偶) is optional.
2. The conditions are set by the city receiving the hukou and differ widely; some cities set extra conditions.
3. Apply at the receiving police station or its online service; the 30 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Plan the housing provident fund for a joint home
conditions: Only if you plan to buy, build or repay a loan on a home together
prepare: Ask the local housing provident fund centre (公积金中心) about spouse withdrawals and joint loans
steps.howTo:
1. The national regulations let a contributor withdraw the fund (住房公积金) to buy, build or repair a home, repay a home loan, pay rent and more, and apply for a provident fund loan.
2. Whether a spouse can withdraw for a home in the other's name, and how both balances count toward a joint loan, is set by each city's fund centre.
3. Centres decide on a withdrawal within 3 days and a loan within 10 days of accepting the application (as amended from September 20, 2026; check current).
4. Not financial advice; the date here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Learn how inheritance works for spouses
prepare: What each of you owns, and whether it is joint or separate property
steps.howTo:
1. Without a will, the Civil Code puts the spouse in the first order of heirs, together with children and parents (Article 1127).
2. Property acquired during the marriage, such as wages and investment income, is generally joint property of the couple unless you agree otherwise.
3. A will (遗嘱) can change who inherits; the Civil Code allows handwritten, witnessed, printed, audio or video, and notarised wills.
4. For information only, not legal advice; see a lawyer or notary for your situation.

steps.title: Consider a written property agreement (婚前 / 婚内财产约定)
conditions: Only if you want to set your own property arrangement
prepare: List of each person's property and debts
A notary office (公证处), if you want it notarised
steps.howTo:
1. Under Article 1065 of the Civil Code, a couple can agree in writing that property is separate, joint or partly joint; without it, most property acquired during the marriage is joint.
2. It can be signed before or during the marriage; notarising is optional but common.
3. For information only, not legal advice.

title: Getting married · Ontario
summary: Paperwork plan for a wedding in Ontario, from booking an officiant and the marriage licence to the certificate, name updates, taxes and wills.
conditions: You are marrying in Ontario
Both of you are 18 or older; at 16 or 17, written consent from both parents or a court order is needed
Neither of you is still married to someone else

sources.title: Getting married — Ontario.ca
Marriage Officiant's Guide to Performing Marriage Ceremonies in Ontario (ON00459E)
Marriage Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. M.3
Get a copy of an Ontario marriage certificate — Ontario.ca
Change your last name — Ontario.ca
Change your name — Ontario.ca
Update your Social Insurance Number record — Canada.ca
Changing the name on your passport — Canada.ca
Change your marital status with the CRA — Canada.ca
Succession Law Reform Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. S.26
Make a power of attorney — Ontario.ca
Sponsor your spouse, partner or child — Canada.ca
Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Who can apply — Canada.ca
Death of a TFSA holder (successor holder) — Canada.ca

steps.title: Book an officiant and the ceremony
prepare: Check the officiant is registered to marry in Ontario
For a civil ceremony, ask the local city hall or town hall
steps.howTo:
1. Only registered or civil marriage officiants can perform a marriage in Ontario.
2. Registered officiants act for a religious body, or a band, First Nation, Métis or Inuit organization or community.
3. Civil marriages are performed by municipal clerks or their delegates, judges, associate judges, justices of the peace and Members of Provincial Parliament.
4. Ontario.ca lets you check whether an officiant is registered.
5. The 6 months here is an estimate; popular dates and city hall slots can go sooner.

steps.title: Get the marriage licence
prepare: Both of you complete the application
ID for each of you, e.g. birth certificate or passport
Proof of divorce, if either of you was married before
Check the current fee with the municipality
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online through ServiceOntario (select municipalities) or on paper at a municipal office that issues licences.
2. Each person completes the application and provides government-issued ID; at least one of you attends in person to swear it is true and to pick up the licence.
3. The licence is valid for 3 months from the date it was issued, so the wedding must fall inside that window.
4. A licence from another province is not valid in Ontario.
5. A divorce outside Canada needs extra documents that can take up to 4 weeks to validate; start earlier.
6. In limited cases, banns can replace a licence; ask the officiant.

steps.title: Confirm two witnesses
prepare: Tell them to be there in person
steps.howTo:
1. The Marriage Act requires at least two witnesses at the ceremony.
2. They must be physically present, understand what they are witnessing, and sign the licence and the register.
3. With the couple and officiant that is at least five people.

steps.title: Hold the ceremony and sign the licence
prepare: Ask the officiant for a record of solemnization
steps.howTo:
1. You, your spouse, the two witnesses and the officiant sign the licence immediately after the ceremony.
2. The officiant must give a record of solemnization at the time of the marriage if either of you asks.

steps.title: Officiant sends the licence for registration
prepare: Confirm with the officiant that it was sent
steps.howTo:
1. The officiant must forward the signed licence to the Office of the Registrar General within two days after the ceremony.
2. The marriage certificate can only be issued once the marriage is registered.

steps.title: Order the marriage certificate
prepare: Both full names and dates of birth
Date and city or town of the marriage
Pick marriage certificate or certified copy of the registration
steps.howTo:
1. Either spouse can order online from ServiceOntario at any time after the ceremony.
2. It can take up to 8 weeks after the marriage is registered to process.
3. Regular online service then takes 15 business days plus mail; premium service is 5 business days by courier.
4. The date here is an estimate; most name and record updates ask for this certificate.

steps.title: Decide whether to change your last name
conditions: Only if either of you wants a new last name
prepare: The full last name as it appears on the marriage certificate
steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario you can assume your spouse's last name on government documents without a legal name change; it does not change your Ontario birth registration.
2. Use the full last name as shown on the marriage certificate, including any hyphen.
3. For only part of a hyphenated name, or another name, apply for a legal change of name: 16 or older and 12 months living in Ontario.
4. Legal name changes can take up to 24 weeks.

steps.title: Update the health card and driver's licence
conditions: Only if you changed your last name
prepare: Driver's licence or Ontario Photo Card
steps.howTo:
1. Assuming a spouse's last name on these cards is free at a ServiceOntario centre.
2. Updated cards arrive by mail in 6 to 8 weeks.

steps.title: Update the name on your SIN record
conditions: Only if you changed your last name
prepare: Document linking the old and new names
steps.howTo:
1. Service Canada asks you to update your SIN record when your legal name changes.
2. Update online or by mail; there is no fee.
3. Online confirmation takes about 5 business days; by mail about 20 business days.

steps.title: Apply for a passport in the new name
conditions: Only if you changed your last name and hold a Canadian passport
prepare: ID showing the new last name
Check the current fee and processing time
steps.howTo:
1. A new last name after marriage means applying for a new passport, not amending the old one.
2. Include ID in the new name and the marriage certificate showing the previous and current last name.
3. The 30 days is an estimate; check current processing times before booking travel.

steps.title: Tell the CRA you are married
steps.howTo:
1. The deadline is the end of the month after the month you married; e.g. married in March, tell the CRA by the end of April.
2. Update in CRA My Account or by phone (processed straight away), or mail form RC65 (4 to 6 weeks).
3. The date here is a safe estimate; move it to the real deadline.

steps.title: Add your spouse to workplace health and dental benefits
conditions: Only if either of you has health or dental benefits through work
steps.howTo:
1. Group plans usually treat marriage as a life event that lets you add a spouse outside the yearly enrolment period.
2. The window is set by each plan and is often 31 days from the wedding; after it, late enrolment may need health evidence or wait for the next enrolment period.
3. If both of you have plans, each plan's coordination of benefits rules decide which pays first.
4. Update life insurance and pension beneficiaries in the same session.

steps.title: Check the Canada Child Benefit and credits
conditions: Only if either of you gets the Canada Child Benefit or other CRA benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Benefit and credit payments, including the Canada Child Benefit, are based on adjusted family net income, which now includes your spouse.
2. The CRA recalculates from the month after your marital status changed.
3. Check the new amounts in CRA My Account; a drop is normal if family income rose.

steps.title: Review wills, powers of attorney and beneficiaries
documents: Power of attorney for personal care
prepare: Beneficiaries on RRSPs, TFSAs, pensions and life insurance
Successor holder on a TFSA or FHSA
Who should decide for you if you cannot
steps.howTo:
1. Since January 1, 2022, marriage no longer revokes an existing will in Ontario, so an old will stays in force until you change it.
2. Without an attorney for property, a spouse cannot automatically step in on finances.
3. You can make a power of attorney yourself for free or with a lawyer.
4. On a TFSA, a spouse can be named successor holder, so the account carries on in their name; the FHSA has the same option, and RRSPs and RRIFs take a beneficiary. Designations are made with the financial institution; check the plan documents.
5. Not legal advice; see a lawyer if your affairs are complicated.

steps.title: Look into sponsoring your spouse
conditions: Only if your spouse isn't a Canadian citizen or permanent resident
prepare: Check the current IRCC guide and fees
steps.howTo:
1. The sponsor must be 18 or older, a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or registered under the Indian Act, and usually live in Canada.
2. Your spouse applies for permanent residence and both applications go in together through the IRCC PR portal.
3. Processing times vary; check IRCC for current times.

title: Moving in together · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for an unmarried couple moving in together in British Columbia: addresses, a cohabitation agreement, benefits and beneficiaries, wills, the 1- and 2-year marks for tax and family law, and sponsorship.
conditions: You and your partner live together in British Columbia in a relationship like a marriage, without being married
The event date is the day you started living together

sources.title: Update your marital status with the CRA — Canada.ca
Marital status — Canada.ca
Family Law Act, S.B.C. 2011, c. 25
Wills, Estates and Succession Act, S.B.C. 2009, c. 13
Change your name or address — ICBC
Incapacity planning — Province of British Columbia
Sponsor your spouse, partner or children — Canada.ca

steps.title: Sort out the lease or title for the shared home
steps.howTo:
1. Renting: check whether the tenancy agreement limits occupants; adding the partner as a co-tenant gives them their own rights, while an occupant has fewer.
2. Owned by one partner: the other has no title unless it is added; family law may still give a share later.
3. Keep copies; a joint lease is also proof of living together.

steps.title: Update your address
conditions: Only if you moved
steps.howTo:
1. A new address for a BC driver's licence goes to ICBC within 10 days.
2. Update MSP and the BC Services Card, the CRA, banks and employers.
3. Canada Post mail forwarding covers the gap.

steps.title: Consider a cohabitation agreement
prepare: List of what each partner owns and owes now
Plans for the home, money and children
steps.howTo:
1. A written agreement can set out how property, debts and support are handled if you separate, instead of the Family Law Act defaults.
2. It is signed by both and witnessed; each partner getting independent legal advice makes it harder to set aside.
3. It can be updated, or becomes a marriage agreement if you later marry.
4. Not legal advice; a family lawyer can help.

steps.title: Add your partner to workplace benefits
conditions: Only if either of you has a workplace health, dental or life insurance plan
prepare: Proof of living together, if the plan asks
steps.howTo:
1. Plans set their own rules for when a common-law partner counts; some from the day you move in, others after 12 months.
2. Changes are often only accepted within a set window (commonly 31 days) of a life event; check the plan booklet.
3. If both have plans, coordinating them can cover more.

steps.title: Update beneficiaries on accounts and insurance
prepare: RRSP, TFSA, FHSA, pension and life insurance account list
steps.howTo:
1. In British Columbia beneficiaries can be named directly on RRSPs, TFSAs, FHSAs and life insurance.
2. A spouse or common-law partner can be named successor holder on a TFSA or FHSA, keeping it tax-free.
3. Designations made before you moved in stay in force until changed.

steps.title: Make or update wills and incapacity documents
prepare: Who should decide for you if you cannot
steps.howTo:
1. Under WESA, a partner counts as a spouse after living in a marriage-like relationship for at least 2 years; before that, a partner inherits nothing without a will.
2. A will can be registered with the BC Wills Registry through Vital Statistics.
3. An enduring power of attorney and a representation agreement let a partner act on money and health decisions.
4. Not legal advice; a lawyer or notary can help.

steps.title: Tell the CRA you are common-law
steps.howTo:
1. For tax, a partner becomes common-law after 12 continuous months living together, or sooner if you have a child together.
2. Report the change by the end of the month after the month it happened, in CRA My Account, by phone, or on form RC65.
3. The Canada Child Benefit and the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit are recalculated on family net income from the next month; both partners file a return each year to keep them.

steps.title: Look into sponsoring your partner
conditions: Only if your partner isn't a Canadian citizen or permanent resident
prepare: Joint lease or title, shared bills, same address on ID
Check the current IRCC guide and fees
steps.howTo:
1. IRCC treats a partner as common-law after 12 continuous months living together.
2. The sponsor is 18 or older, a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or registered under the Indian Act.
3. Both applications go in together through the IRCC PR portal; check current processing times.

steps.title: Know what changes at 2 years together
steps.howTo:
1. Under the BC Family Law Act, partners in a marriage-like relationship for 2 years are spouses: family property and debt are shared equally on separation, and spousal support can be claimed.
2. With a child together, spousal support can be claimed sooner.
3. Claims for property division are made within 2 years of separating.
4. Not legal advice; the dates here are prompts.

title: Moving in together · Ontario
summary: Paperwork plan for an unmarried couple moving in together in Ontario: addresses, a cohabitation agreement, benefits and beneficiaries, wills, the 1- and 3-year marks for tax and family law, and sponsorship.
conditions: You and your partner live together in Ontario in a relationship like a marriage, without being married
The event date is the day you started living together

steps.title: Update your address

steps.howTo:
1. A new address for an Ontario driver's licence and vehicle permit goes to ServiceOntario within 6 days; one online change also covers the health card.
2. Update the CRA, banks and employers.
3. Canada Post mail forwarding covers the gap.

steps.title: Consider a cohabitation agreement
prepare: List of what each partner owns and owes now
Plans for the home, money and children
steps.howTo:
1. The Ontario Family Law Act lets unmarried partners make a written cohabitation agreement on property, support and other matters; it becomes a marriage contract if you marry.
2. It is in writing, signed by both and witnessed; each partner getting independent legal advice makes it harder to set aside.
3. Without one, unmarried partners have no equalization of property on separation.
4. Not legal advice; a family lawyer can help.

steps.title: Add your partner to workplace benefits
conditions: Only if either of you has a workplace health, dental or life insurance plan
prepare: Proof of living together, if the plan asks

1. Plans set their own rules for when a common-law partner counts; some from the day you move in, others after 12 months.
2. Changes are often only accepted within a set window (commonly 31 days) of a life event; check the plan booklet.
3. If both have plans, coordinating them can cover more.

steps.title: Update beneficiaries on accounts and insurance

steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario beneficiaries can be named directly on RRSPs, TFSAs, FHSAs and life insurance.
2. A spouse or common-law partner can be named successor holder on a TFSA or FHSA, keeping it tax-free.
3. Designations made before you moved in stay in force until changed.

steps.title: Make or update wills and powers of attorney
documents: Continuing power of attorney for property
Power of attorney for personal care
prepare: Who should decide for you if you cannot
steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario a common-law partner inherits nothing when someone dies without a will, however long you lived together; a court claim for dependant support is the only route.
2. A will is the way to leave a partner the home or other property.
3. Powers of attorney for property and personal care let a partner act on money and health decisions; free kits are on Ontario.ca.
4. Not legal advice; a lawyer can help.

steps.title: Tell the CRA you are common-law
steps.howTo:
1. For tax, a partner becomes common-law after 12 continuous months living together, or sooner if you have a child together.
2. Report the change by the end of the month after the month it happened, in CRA My Account, by phone, or on form RC65.

prepare: Joint lease or title, shared bills, same address on ID
Check the current IRCC guide and fees

1. IRCC treats a partner as common-law after 12 continuous months living together.
2. The sponsor is 18 or older, a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or registered under the Indian Act.
3. Both applications go in together through the IRCC PR portal; check current processing times.

steps.title: Know what changes at 3 years together
steps.howTo:

2. Property is not divided by equalization for unmarried partners at any length; claims go through trust law in court.
3. Not legal advice; the dates here are prompts.

title: Expecting a baby · British Columbia
summary: Care, leave, benefits and preparation plan for a pregnancy in British Columbia, counted back from the due date.
conditions: For a pregnancy with a due date, living in British Columbia
Leave steps apply to employees covered by the BC Employment Standards Act
EI steps apply to people who pay into Employment Insurance

sources.title: Coverage wait period for the Medical Services Plan (MSP)

steps.title: Check your MSP coverage is active
prepare: Date you arrived in BC, if new
conditions: Only if you are new to BC or unsure your MSP coverage is active
steps.howTo:
1. New and returning BC residents wait the rest of the month they arrive plus two months before MSP coverage starts; apply as soon as you arrive.
2. Midwifery care and prenatal genetic screening are free with MSP coverage.
3. This date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Book prenatal care with a family doctor, OB or midwife
prepare: First day of the last period, for the due date
List of medications and health history
Choose a midwife, family doctor or obstetrician
steps.howTo:
1. Midwifery care is covered by MSP for BC residents and needs no referral; contact a midwife as soon as you know you are pregnant, as spaces can be limited.
2. Midwives are the primary care provider through pregnancy, birth and about 6 weeks after.
3. Without a family doctor or nurse practitioner, join the Health Connect Registry online or by calling 8-1-1.
4. Register the pregnancy with your local health authority to connect with public health nurses, and ask for the Baby's Best Chance handbook.
5. This date (about 8 weeks pregnant) is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Decide on prenatal genetic screening with your provider
prepare: Questions about SIPS, IPS, Quad and NIPT
Lab requisition from your provider if you choose to screen
conditions: Only if you choose to screen; screening is optional
steps.howTo:
1. Perinatal Services BC offers screening free to pregnant people with MSP coverage.
2. SIPS is two blood tests: the first from 9 weeks to the end of the 13th week, the second from 14 weeks to the end of the 20th week. IPS adds a nuchal translucency ultrasound.
3. Quad is one blood test from 14 weeks to the end of the 20th week, for those who start prenatal care later.
4. NIPT can be done after 10 weeks; MSP covers it only in certain situations.
5. This due date is the end of the first SIPS window; talk to your provider before it.

steps.title: Tell the employer and plan the leave dates
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by BC employment standards
steps.howTo:
1. BC maternity (pregnancy) leave is up to 17 consecutive weeks, unpaid, with no minimum length of employment.
2. It can start no earlier than 13 weeks before the expected birth date and no later than the birth, and lasts at least 6 weeks after the birth.
3. Parental leave for the birth parent is up to 61 weeks and starts right after maternity leave unless the employer agrees otherwise; about 78 weeks in total.
4. When to tell the employer is your choice; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Update your will and name a guardian for the child
prepare: Who would care for the child
Who would manage money for the child
steps.howTo:
1. Under the BC Family Law Act, a guardian can appoint, in a will, a person to become the child's guardian on their death.
2. Review beneficiaries on insurance and registered accounts at the same time.
3. Timing is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Choose standard or extended EI parental benefits
prepare: How the weeks will be shared
conditions: Only if you're eligible for EI (600 insured hours)
steps.howTo:
1. Maternity benefits: up to 15 weeks for the person who gave birth.
2. Standard parental: up to 40 weeks shared, at most 35 per parent, at 55% of earnings up to a cap, taken within 52 weeks of the birth.
3. Extended parental: up to 69 weeks shared, at most 61 per parent, at 33% of earnings up to a cap, taken within 78 weeks.
4. Sharing parents pick the same option, and it can't be changed once payments start.

steps.title: Take prenatal classes
prepare: Ask your provider or public health nurse which classes run locally
steps.howTo:
1. Providers and public health nurses can point to prenatal classes and pregnancy programs in your community.
2. Perinatal Services BC runs a free online Pregnancy & Parent Learning Centre.
3. Timing in the second and third trimester is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Confirm where you'll give birth and the hospital pre-registration
steps.howTo:
1. Midwives attend births in hospital or out of hospital, such as at home.
2. For a hospital birth, your doctor or midwife usually pre-registers you; BC Women's Hospital, for example, asks for this before 32 weeks.
3. This date (32 weeks) is a planning estimate; ask your provider what your hospital needs.

steps.title: Buy a rear-facing infant car seat with the National Safety Mark
steps.howTo:
1. The National Safety Mark shows a seat meets Canadian safety standards.
2. Infants ride rear-facing until they reach the seat's weight or height limit.
3. If a seat is second-hand: it has the mark, was never in a collision, has no recalls, and all parts work.
4. The expiry date is on a label on the seat or in the manual.

steps.title: Give written notice of maternity leave
prepare: Medical or nurse practitioner certificate if the employer asks
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by BC employment standards
steps.howTo:
1. The Employment Standards Act asks for a written request at least 4 weeks before the leave starts; the employer may ask for a medical or nurse practitioner certificate.
2. The due date here is 4 weeks before a leave assumed to start 2 weeks before the due date; move it with the real leave date.

steps.title: Pack the hospital bag
prepare: Clothes for you and the baby
conditions: Only if planning a hospital birth
steps.howTo:
1. Think about what you will need for a hospital birth and pack the bag.
2. Timing is a planning estimate; babies can arrive early.

steps.title: Choose the baby's name
steps.howTo:
1. A birth in BC is registered with the Vital Statistics Agency within 30 days of the birth.
2. The child needs a given name and a surname; the surname can be either parent's, a combination, or different, but no more than two surnames combined.
3. Each parent listed certifies the online registration and is present when it is completed.

steps.title: Other parent: give notice of parental leave
prepare: Weeks of EI parental benefits to claim
conditions: Only if the other parent is an employee planning parental leave
steps.howTo:
1. A parent who did not take maternity leave gets up to 62 consecutive weeks of parental leave.
2. It can start any time within 78 weeks of the birth.
3. A written request is given at least 4 weeks before the leave starts; this date assumes leave from the birth, so move it with the real start.

steps.title: Install the car seat and register it for recalls
steps.howTo:
1. Install following both manuals.
2. Register with the manufacturer by card or online, so they can contact you about recalls.

steps.title: Start maternity leave
prepare: Confirm the employer will issue the Record of Employment
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by BC employment standards
steps.howTo:
1. BC maternity leave can start as early as 13 weeks before the due date; EI maternity benefits as early as 12 weeks before.
2. Two weeks before the due date is a planning estimate; move it to your real last day.

steps.title: Apply for EI maternity and parental benefits
conditions: Only if you're eligible for EI (600 insured hours in the 52 weeks before the claim)
Only if your weekly earnings drop by more than 40%
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online as soon as possible after you stop working; applying more than 4 weeks after the last day of work may lose benefits.
2. Don't wait for the Record of Employment; documents can follow.
3. A sharing parent submits their own application.
