steps.title: Register the pregnancy and get the Maternal and Child Health Handbook (建档 / 母子健康手册)
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: First day of the last period, for the due date
Your local community health service centre (社区卫生服务中心) or township health centre
steps.howTo:
1. Under the national basic public health service, the community or township health centre where you live sets up the Maternal and Child Health Handbook before 13 weeks, together with the first prenatal check.
2. The first check covers a health assessment, blood and urine tests, blood type, liver and kidney function and hepatitis B; many areas add syphilis, HIV and blood sugar.
3. Provinces and cities run this differently, some fully online; a big city such as Beijing or Shanghai is an example where the local service may differ. Ask your health centre.
4. This date (12 weeks) is a planning estimate.

steps.title: First prenatal check (产检) and early ultrasound
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Fasting for blood tests, if asked
steps.howTo:
1. The national service asks for at least 5 prenatal checks: one before 13 weeks, one at 16 to 20 weeks, one at 21 to 24 weeks, one at 28 to 36 weeks and one at 37 to 40 weeks.
2. The 2018 clinical guideline of the Chinese Medical Association suggests checks at 6 to 13+6, 14 to 19+6, 20 to 24, 25 to 28, 29 to 32, 33 to 36 and 37 to 41 weeks, 7 to 11 checks in all, more with risk factors.
3. An ultrasound at 6 to 8 weeks confirms the pregnancy and the weeks.
4. Hospitals set their own booking; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Check your maternity insurance (生育保险) contributions
documents: Social security card (社会保障卡) or medical insurance e-voucher (医保电子凭证)
prepare: Your contribution record from the local medical insurance app or office
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by maternity insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Maternity insurance pays birth medical costs and the maternity allowance (生育津贴) for insured employees.
2. The city where you are insured sets how long you have to have contributed before the birth; check your record early so a gap can be fixed.
3. Rules differ by province and city; ask the local medical insurance bureau (医疗保障局).
4. This date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Early screening: NT scan (颈项透明层) at 11 to 13+6 weeks
prepare: Book the scan at a hospital that offers NT
Ask about early serum screening (10 to 13+6 weeks)
conditions: Only if you choose early screening
steps.howTo:
1. The 2018 guideline lists the nuchal translucency (NT) ultrasound at 11 to 13+6 weeks, and early serum screening at 10 to 13+6 weeks, as optional items.
2. Hospitals often book NT slots weeks ahead.
3. The due date here is the end of the NT window; book before it.

steps.title: Choose the delivery hospital (分娩医院) and set up your record there
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Level of the hospital and its neonatal care
Maternity insurance designated hospital (定点医院)
steps.howTo:
1. Many families have the later prenatal checks at the hospital where they will give birth.
2. Check the hospital is a designated hospital for your maternity insurance, so birth costs can be settled directly.
3. In a big city, for example Beijing or Shanghai, popular hospitals can fill up early; ask when they take new records.
4. This date (16 weeks) is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Second-trimester screening: serum screening (唐氏筛查) or NIPT (无创产前检测)
prepare: Questions about serum screening, NIPT and diagnosis
Your age on the due date
conditions: Only if you choose to screen; screening is optional
steps.howTo:
1. Second-trimester serum screening for Down syndrome and other chromosome conditions is done at 15 to 20 weeks, best at 16 to 18 weeks.
2. NIPT screens for trisomy 21, 18 and 13 at 12 to 22+6 weeks, under the NHC technical standard.
3. A high-risk or positive result leads to diagnosis at a prenatal diagnosis centre.
4. The due date here is the end of the serum screening window (20 weeks).

steps.title: Tell the employer and plan maternity leave (产假)
conditions: Only if you are an employee
steps.howTo:
1. The Special Provisions on Labour Protection for Female Employees give 98 days of maternity leave, of which up to 15 can be taken before the birth.
2. A difficult birth adds 15 days; each extra baby in a multiple birth adds 15 days.
3. Provinces add their own leave. Example: Beijing adds 60 days, 158 in total, and the employer may agree to 1 to 3 more months.
4. When to tell the employer is your choice; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Glucose tolerance test (OGTT) for gestational diabetes at 24 to 28 weeks
steps.howTo:
1. The 2018 guideline lists screening for gestational diabetes at 24 to 28 weeks as a standard check, usually a 75 g OGTT.
2. The fetal anomaly ultrasound (胎儿系统超声筛查) comes just before, at 20 to 24 weeks.
3. The due date here is the end of the window (28 weeks).

steps.title: Partner: plan paternity leave (陪产假)
prepare: Planned dates around the due date
conditions: Only if the partner is an employee
steps.howTo:
1. There is no national paternity leave; each province sets it.
2. Example: Beijing gives the father 15 days, and more if the mother gives up some of her extra leave.
3. Check your province's regulations and your employer's policy; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Pack the hospital bag (待产包)
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Clothes for you and the baby
Marriage certificate (结婚证) and household register (户口簿)
steps.howTo:
1. Pack the documents the hospital asks for at admission along with clothes and toiletries.
2. Example from Hubei: the hospital checks the mother's ID card at admission and issues the birth medical certificate against it, so bring the original.
3. Timing is a planning estimate; babies can arrive early.

steps.title: Choose the baby's name
steps.howTo:
1. The name goes on the birth medical certificate (出生医学证明) and then the household register, so decide it before the hospital issues the certificate.
2. Example rules from Hubei: characters come from the Table of General Standard Chinese Characters (通用规范汉字表), rare characters are not used, and the baby generally takes a parent's surname.
3. Your province may have its own rules; ask the hospital.

steps.title: From 37 weeks: weekly checks and fetal monitoring (胎心监护)
prepare: Signs of labour and when to go in
steps.howTo:
1. The 2018 guideline lists weekly non-stress tests (NST) and an ultrasound from 37 weeks.
2. At 41 weeks the guideline suggests admission and induction.
3. Follow your hospital's schedule; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Gather the documents needed after the birth
prepare: Which parent's household the baby will join
Bank card for insurance and subsidy payments
steps.howTo:
1. After the birth come the birth medical certificate (出生医学证明), household registration (户口登记) within one month, the vaccination certificate, medical insurance and the social security card.
2. Many provinces run these together as the newborn birth "one thing" service (新生儿出生一件事), online or at one window.
3. Example from Hubei: the mother applies for the birth medical certificate within 1 month with both parents' ID cards and the marriage certificate.
4. Check your province's list; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Start maternity leave
prepare: Confirm with HR how the maternity allowance will be paid
conditions: Only if you are an employee
steps.howTo:
1. Up to 15 of the 98 national days can be taken before the birth.
2. Fifteen days before the due date is a planning estimate; move it to your real last day.

steps.title: Claim the maternity allowance (生育津贴) and birth medical costs
documents: Birth medical certificate (出生医学证明)
prepare: ID card or social security card
conditions: Only if you are covered by maternity insurance
steps.howTo:
1. For insured employees the maternity allowance is paid from the maternity insurance fund at the employer's average monthly wage for the previous year; without insurance the employer pays the pre-leave wage.
2. Birth costs at a designated hospital are often settled directly; otherwise claim them with the invoices, itemised bill and discharge record.
3. Depending on the city, the employer or you apply, and some provinces include it in the birth "one thing" service.
4. Timing is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Check maternity cover as a flexible worker (灵活就业人员生育保险)
conditions: Only if you are self-employed or a flexible worker paying employee medical insurance yourself
prepare: The local medical insurance bureau's rule for flexible workers
steps.howTo:
1. Maternity insurance has mostly covered employees; a growing number of provinces let flexible workers who pay employee medical insurance join it or get birth medical costs covered.
2. Whether an allowance is paid, and how long you have to have paid in, is local; check current rules with the local medical insurance bureau (医疗保障局).
3. This date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Do the birth registration (生育登记)
prepare: The provincial government service app or platform
steps.howTo:
1. Birth registration (生育登记) is a free service record, done online in most provinces, for first, second and third children alike.
2. Some provinces ask for it before paying the maternity allowance or other birth benefits; others do not.
3. Ask the local health commission or community office what it is used for where you live.

steps.title: Note the workplace protections during pregnancy
conditions: Only if you are an employee
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Special Provisions on Labour Protection for Female Employees, time for prenatal checks during work hours counts as working time.
2. The employer cannot cut wages, dismiss or end the contract because of pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding.
3. From 7 months pregnant, no overtime or night shifts, and rest time in the working day.
4. Provinces may add more; this is information, not legal advice.

title: Expecting a baby · Ontario
summary: Care, leave, benefits and preparation plan for a pregnancy in Ontario, counted back from the due date.
conditions: For a pregnancy with a due date, living in Ontario
Leave steps apply to employees covered by the Ontario Employment Standards Act
EI steps apply to people who pay into Employment Insurance

sources.title: Midwifery in Ontario
Find a family doctor or nurse practitioner (Health Care Connect)
Healthy Babies Healthy Children program
Prenatal Screening Ontario: Enhanced First Trimester Screening (eFTS)
Your guide to the Employment Standards Act: Pregnancy and parental leave
EI maternity and parental benefits: What these benefits offer
EI maternity and parental benefits: Eligibility
EI maternity and parental benefits: Apply
Your Guide to a Healthy Pregnancy
Transport Canada: Choosing a child car seat or booster seat
Transport Canada: Expiry dates on child car seats and booster seats
Register the birth of a new baby (Ontario)
Estate planning and wills (Ontario)

steps.title: Book prenatal care with a family doctor, OB or midwife
prepare: First day of the last period, for the due date
List of medications and health history
Choose a midwife, family doctor or obstetrician
steps.howTo:
1. Midwifery care is free to Ontario residents and needs no referral; call a midwife as early in pregnancy as possible, as spaces fill.
2. Midwives are the primary care provider through pregnancy, birth and 6 weeks after.
3. Without a family doctor or nurse practitioner, register with Health Care Connect by phone.
4. Ask about the free Healthy Babies Healthy Children program.
5. This date (about 8 weeks pregnant) is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Decide on prenatal screening with your provider
prepare: Book the ultrasound and blood test if chosen
conditions: Only if you choose to screen; screening is optional
steps.howTo:
1. Enhanced First Trimester Screening (eFTS) is done between 11 weeks 2 days and 13 weeks 3 days of pregnancy: an ultrasound, then a blood test.
2. NIPT can be done after 9 or 10 weeks, depending on the lab; it is publicly funded only in certain situations.
3. This due date is the end of the eFTS window; talk to your provider before it.

steps.title: Tell the employer and plan the leave dates
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by Ontario employment standards
steps.howTo:
1. Pregnancy leave needs at least 13 weeks of employment before the due date.
2. Pregnancy leave is up to 17 weeks, unpaid, and can start as early as 17 weeks before the due date.
3. Parental leave is up to 61 weeks after pregnancy leave, or up to 63 weeks for other parents, and must start within 78 weeks of the birth.
4. When to tell the employer is your choice; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Update your will and name a guardian for the child
prepare: Who would care for the child
Who would manage money for the child
steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario, a will can appoint one or more people to have decision-making responsibility (custody) for children who are not yet adults.
2. Review beneficiaries on insurance and registered accounts at the same time.
3. Timing is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Choose standard or extended EI parental benefits
prepare: How the weeks will be shared
conditions: Only if you're eligible for EI (600 insured hours)
steps.howTo:
1. Maternity benefits: up to 15 weeks for the person who gave birth.
2. Standard parental: up to 40 weeks shared, at most 35 per parent, at 55% of earnings up to a cap, taken within 52 weeks of the birth.
3. Extended parental: up to 69 weeks shared, at most 61 per parent, at 33% of earnings up to a cap, taken within 78 weeks.
4. Sharing parents must pick the same option, and it can't be changed once payments start.

steps.title: Take prenatal classes
prepare: Ask your provider or public health unit which classes run locally
steps.howTo:
1. Local public health units, which run Healthy Babies Healthy Children, offer prenatal education.
2. Timing in the second and third trimester is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Buy a rear-facing infant car seat with the National Safety Mark
steps.howTo:
1. The National Safety Mark shows a seat meets Canadian safety standards.
2. Infants ride rear-facing until they reach the seat's weight or height limit.
3. If a seat is second-hand: it has the mark, was never in a collision, has no recalls, and all parts work.
4. The expiry date is on a label on the seat or in the manual.

steps.title: Pack the hospital bag
prepare: Clothes for you and the baby
conditions: Only if planning a hospital or birth centre birth
steps.howTo:
1. Think about what you will need for a hospital birth and pack the bag.
2. Timing is a planning estimate; babies can arrive early.

steps.title: Choose the baby's name
steps.howTo:
1. The birth is registered online within 30 days of the birth.
2. A surname different from the parents', or a single name for cultural reasons, can be registered online; all parents must be present to agree.

steps.title: Give written notice of pregnancy leave
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by Ontario employment standards
steps.howTo:
1. The Employment Standards Act requires at least 2 weeks' written notice before pregnancy leave starts.
2. The due date here is 2 weeks before a leave assumed to start 2 weeks before the due date; move it with the real leave date.

steps.title: Other parent: give notice of parental leave
prepare: Weeks of EI parental benefits to claim
conditions: Only if the other parent is an employee planning parental leave
steps.howTo:
1. Parents who did not take pregnancy leave get up to 63 weeks of parental leave.
2. Parental leave must start within 78 weeks of the birth.
3. Check the Employment Standards guide for the written notice rules; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Install the car seat and register it for recalls
steps.howTo:
1. Install following both manuals.
2. Register with the manufacturer by card or online, so they can contact you about recalls.

steps.title: Start pregnancy leave
prepare: Confirm the employer will issue the Record of Employment
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by Ontario employment standards
steps.howTo:
1. Pregnancy leave can start as early as 17 weeks before the due date; EI maternity benefits as early as 12 weeks before.
2. Two weeks before the due date is a planning estimate; move it to your real last day.

steps.title: Apply for EI maternity and parental benefits
conditions: Only if you're eligible for EI (600 insured hours in the 52 weeks before the claim)
Only if your weekly earnings drop by more than 40%
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online as soon as possible after you stop working; applying more than 4 weeks after the last day of work may lose benefits.
2. Don't wait for the Record of Employment; documents can follow.
3. A sharing parent submits their own application.

title: Newborn · first year · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork, health and money plan for a baby born in British Columbia, from birth registration to the 18-month vaccines, plus the BC education grant from age 6.
conditions: For a baby born in British Columbia
For parents living in British Columbia

sources.title: Birth registration (British Columbia)
BC online birth registration: FAQ
BC Vital Statistics: Electronic Certificate Ordering System
Enrolling your newborn in the Medical Services Plan (MSP)
MSP: Adding or removing spouse or children
Birth Registration and Canada Child Benefits - British Columbia (RC4476)
Canada child benefit: How to apply
Apply for a Social Insurance Number
HealthLink BC: Health Connect Registry
Midwives Association of BC: Frequently asked questions
HealthLink BC: Immunization schedules for children
Vancouver Coastal Health: Immunization for infants and toddlers
How to apply for a child passport in Canada
Documents to submit when applying for a child's passport
Canada Education Savings Grant (CESG)
Canada Learning Bond (CRA)
Canada Learning Bond brochure for those under 18 years old
BC Employment Standards: Leaves of absence
EI maternity and parental benefits: What these benefits offer
Canadian Dental Association: Your child's first visit
Child disability benefit — Canada.ca
Disability tax credit (DTC) — Canada.ca
Registered disability savings plan (RDSP) — Canada.ca

steps.title: Register the birth online with BC Vital Statistics
prepare: All parents to be listed present to certify
Tick MSP, Canada Child Benefits and Social Insurance Number
steps.howTo:
1. A birth in BC is registered with the Vital Statistics Agency within 30 days; a fee may be charged after that.
2. Online registration is not available for a child over 1 year old, more than two parents, or surrogacy; call Vital Statistics instead.
3. Each parent listed certifies the online registration separately and is present when it is completed.
4. At the same time you can apply, at no fee, for the baby's MSP coverage, Canada Child Benefits and Social Insurance Number.

steps.title: Order the baby's birth certificate
prepare: Choose the parental certificate, which lists the parents
Credit or debit card for the fee
steps.howTo:
1. Certificates can be ordered at the end of the online registration, or later through the Electronic Certificate Ordering System.
2. Certificates are issued once both the registration and the hospital's Notice of Live Birth are received; registration and certificate take about 4 to 6 weeks in total.
3. The parental birth certificate is the one needed for a passport; if the name is too long, you receive an individual certificate and a birth extract instead.

steps.title: Add the baby to the workplace health and dental plan
prepare: Baby's full name and birth date
Which parent's plan is primary, if both have one
conditions: Only if a parent has health or dental benefits through work
steps.howTo:
1. A birth is a life event that lets a dependant be added outside open enrolment, usually within a set window, often around 31 days; the benefits booklet has the real limit.
2. Adding the baby late can mean waiting for the next open enrolment or giving proof of good health.
3. With two plans, children are usually claimed first on the plan of the parent whose birthday comes first in the year.

steps.title: Line up a family doctor or NP for the baby's checkups
prepare: Join the Health Connect Registry if you have no doctor
steps.howTo:
1. Midwives care for parent and baby until about 6 weeks after the birth; care then passes to a family doctor or nurse practitioner.
2. The Health Connect Registry matches people with a family doctor or nurse practitioner; register online or call 8-1-1 to add family members.
3. The checkup schedule is set by the provider; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Apply for the Canada Child Benefit
conditions: Only if you didn't apply through the BC birth registration
steps.howTo:
1. The BC online birth registration can apply for Canada child benefits when the mother consents; she is a citizen or permanent resident and primarily cares for the child.
2. Otherwise apply through CRA My Account or Form RC66 as soon as the child is born and living with you.
3. Applying for a child who started living with you more than 11 months ago needs extra documents.

steps.title: Confirm the baby's MSP enrolment and BC Services Card
prepare: Baby Enrolment form (HLTH 115) if not done through birth registration
steps.howTo:
1. When the mother has MSP coverage, ticking MSP in the online birth registration enrols the baby through Health Insurance BC.
2. A hospital-assigned Personal Health Number does not replace enrolment.
3. A BC Services Card in the baby's name arrives within about 4 to 5 weeks.
4. Otherwise send the Baby Enrolment form (HLTH 115) within 60 days of the birth; a parent enrolling the baby on a different MSP account contacts Health Insurance BC.

steps.title: Get the baby's Social Insurance Number
conditions: Only if you didn't apply through the BC birth registration
steps.howTo:
1. Through the birth registration, the SIN is delivered within about 5 business days.
2. Otherwise apply to Service Canada online, by mail or in person with the birth certificate; there is no fee.
3. The SIN is needed to open an RESP and claim education grants.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 2 months
prepare: Book with the public health unit or your doctor or NP
steps.howTo:
1. Follow the BC routine immunization schedule; at 2 months it lists DTaP-HB-IPV-Hib, pneumococcal conjugate, meningococcal C conjugate and rotavirus.
2. Routine vaccines are free, from public health units or a family doctor or nurse practitioner.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Apply for the baby's passport
prepare: Parental birth certificate, as proof of parentage
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the baby will travel outside Canada
steps.howTo:
1. Wait for the parental birth certificate.
2. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail.
3. A child passport is valid for up to 5 years and can't be renewed.
4. The date here is a planning estimate; move it to 2 months before travel.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 4 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow the BC routine immunization schedule; at 4 months it lists DTaP-HB-IPV-Hib, pneumococcal conjugate and rotavirus.
2. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Open an RESP for the Canada Education Savings Grant
prepare: Compare RESP providers, including ones offering the BC grant
steps.howTo:
1. The baby's SIN is needed to open the RESP.
2. The basic CESG adds 20% of yearly contributions, up to a yearly and a lifetime limit, whatever the family income.
3. Middle- and lower-income families can get an additional grant.
4. Grants apply to contributions until the end of the year the child turns 17.
5. Timing is a planning estimate; unused grant room carries forward.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 6 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow the BC routine immunization schedule; at 6 months it lists DTaP-HB-IPV-Hib, plus hepatitis A for Indigenous children.
2. The schedule also lists a yearly flu vaccine from 6 months, with a second dose 4 weeks later the first time; COVID-19 vaccine is free from 6 months.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Request the Canada Learning Bond
prepare: Ask the RESP provider to apply
conditions: Only if the family is low-income and the child is eligible for the Canada Child Benefit
steps.howTo:
1. The CLB is for children from low-income families born in 2004 or later.
2. No contribution to the RESP is needed.
3. It is retroactive: yearly amounts build up until the year the child turns 15.
4. It can be claimed for past eligible years even if no RESP was open then.

steps.title: Confirm the return-to-work date with the employer
conditions: Only if a parent is on maternity or parental leave
steps.howTo:
1. Under BC employment standards, the employer contacts the employee to arrange the return to work.
2. Standard EI parental benefits are taken within 52 weeks of the birth; extended within 78 weeks.
3. The one-year return is a planning estimate; move it for extended leave.

steps.title: Parental leave ends: return to work
conditions: Only if a parent is on maternity or parental leave
steps.howTo:
1. BC parental leave is up to 61 weeks after maternity leave, or 62 weeks for the other parent; about 78 weeks at most with maternity leave.
2. When leave ends, the employee comes back to their job or one like it.
3. One year is a planning estimate for standard benefits; move this to your real date.

steps.title: Apply for the disability tax credit, Child Disability Benefit and RDSP
prepare: Medical practitioner to fill in the medical part of T2201
conditions: Only if the child has a severe and prolonged impairment
steps.howTo:
1. The disability tax credit is applied for with Form T2201, part filled in by a medical practitioner, or through the CRA digital application.
2. Once the child is approved for the DTC and gets the Canada Child Benefit, the Child Disability Benefit is added to the CCB payments automatically.
3. DTC eligibility also opens a registered disability savings plan (RDSP): the Canada Disability Savings Grant matches contributions, and the Canada Disability Savings Bond is paid for lower-income families without contributions.
4. CRA processing takes several weeks; the dates here are estimates. Move this step to when a diagnosis is made.

steps.title: First dental visit
prepare: Find a dentist who sees babies
Note when the first tooth came in
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Dental Association recommends a first dental assessment within 6 months of the first tooth or by one year of age.
2. Move this earlier if the first tooth came early.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 12 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow the BC routine immunization schedule; at 12 months it lists pneumococcal conjugate, meningococcal C conjugate, MMR and chickenpox (varicella).
2. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 18 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow the BC routine immunization schedule; at 18 months it lists DTaP-IPV-Hib, plus hepatitis A for Indigenous children.
2. The next routine vaccines are at 4 to 6 years, at school entry.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

title: Newborn · first year · China
summary: Paperwork, insurance, vaccines and health checks for a baby born in mainland China, from the birth medical certificate to the 18-month vaccines.
conditions: For a baby born in mainland China to parents who are Chinese citizens
Provinces and cities add to or change the national rules

steps.title: Birth vaccines: hepatitis B dose 1 and BCG (卡介苗)
prepare: Keep the hospital's vaccination slip for the vaccination certificate
steps.howTo:
1. The National Immunization Program schedule gives hepatitis B dose 1 and BCG at birth, usually in the birth hospital.
2. If either is missed, the newborn home visit reminds you to catch up.
3. National program vaccines are free.

steps.title: Newborn home visit (新生儿家庭访视)
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Newborn screening (新生儿疾病筛查) result, if back
steps.howTo:
1. Under the national basic public health service, a health worker from the community or township health centre visits within 1 week of discharge, with the postnatal visit for the mother.
2. They weigh and examine the baby and check vaccines and newborn screening.
3. The centre learns of the birth from the hospital; call them if nobody comes.
4. This date assumes discharge a few days after the birth.

steps.title: Get the birth medical certificate (出生医学证明)
documents: Birth medical certificate (出生医学证明)
steps.howTo:
1. The birth hospital issues the certificate; it is the base for household registration, insurance and the passport.
2. Check every character of the baby's and parents' names and the dates before you sign; correcting it later goes back through the hospital.
3. Example from Hubei: the mother applies within 1 month of the birth, or within 3 months at the county office; she brings both parents' ID cards and the marriage certificate.
4. Many provinces take this online through the birth "one thing" service (新生儿出生一件事).

steps.title: Get the vaccination certificate (预防接种证)
prepare: Find the vaccination clinic (接种门诊) for where you live
steps.howTo:
1. The vaccination certificate records every dose and is checked at nursery, kindergarten and school entry.
2. It is part of the birth "one thing" service; some provinces issue an electronic certificate, for example Hubei through its CDC account.
3. Bring it to every vaccine visit.

steps.title: Register the birth in the household register (户口登记)
documents: Household register (户口簿) with the baby added
prepare: Parents' ID cards and household register
Which parent's household the baby joins
steps.howTo:
1. The Household Registration Regulations ask for the birth to be registered within one month, where the baby will normally live.
2. The baby can join either the father's or the mother's household.
3. Many provinces take this through the birth "one thing" service, online or at one window; otherwise go to the local police station (派出所).
4. Cities set their own hukou rules; check with the local police station, for example in Beijing or Shanghai.

steps.title: One-month check (满月健康管理) and hepatitis B dose 2
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Book with the community health centre
steps.howTo:
1. The national service gives a check at 28 to 30 days, together with hepatitis B dose 2 at 1 month.
2. Weight, length and head size are measured.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Apply for the childcare subsidy (育儿补贴)
prepare: Bank card or the baby's social security card for payment
steps.howTo:
1. Since 1 January 2025 a national childcare subsidy (育儿补贴) of 3,600 yuan a year is paid for each child under 3, until the third birthday, for first, second and third children alike.
2. Children born before 2025 who were still under 3 get a pro-rated amount for their months under 3 from 2025 on.
3. One parent or guardian applies where the baby's hukou is registered, mainly online through the national subsidy system, the provincial government service platform, Alipay or WeChat; offline at the township or street office.
4. It is exempt from income tax; provinces set when it is paid, and some pay more than the national base.
5. Timing is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Vaccines at 2 months: polio (IPV) dose 1 and DTaP (百白破) dose 1
steps.howTo:
1. Since 2025 the national DTaP schedule starts at 2 months (2, 4, 6 and 18 months and 6 years); the 2026 schedule keeps this.
2. Inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) dose 1 is at 2 months.
3. Clinics may offer optional paid vaccines too; ask what is in the national program.
4. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Maternity leave ends: return to work
conditions: Only if the mother is an employee on maternity leave
steps.howTo:
1. National maternity leave is 98 days, up to 15 before the birth, so about 83 days after it; a difficult birth or twins add 15 days each.
2. Provinces add leave. Example: Beijing adds 60 days, so leave ends about 143 days after the birth.
3. Until the baby is 1, the employer gives 1 hour a day for breastfeeding and no overtime or night shifts.
4. Move this to your real date.

steps.title: Enrol the baby in resident basic medical insurance (城乡居民医保)
prepare: Birth medical certificate or household register
Payment channel, often the tax app
steps.howTo:
1. The NHSA asks for newborns to be enrolled and paid within 90 days of birth; then costs from the day of birth are covered.
2. Newborns have no waiting period.
3. The birth certificate alone is enough in many places, and the birth "one thing" service enrols the baby together with the other steps.
4. Contributions and any free first year are set locally.

steps.title: 3-month check and polio (IPV) dose 2
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Book the health check and the vaccine together if the centre allows
steps.howTo:
1. The national child health service has a check at 3 months: growth, development and feeding advice.
2. The immunization schedule gives IPV dose 2 at 3 months.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Plan parental leave (育儿假)
conditions: Only if a parent is an employee
steps.howTo:
1. There is no national parental leave; each province sets it.
2. Example: Beijing gives each parent 5 working days a year until the child turns 3, counted by the child's birthday year.
3. Check your province's regulations and your employer; timing is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Apply for the baby's social security card (社会保障卡)
steps.howTo:
1. The card is used for medical insurance and can receive the childcare subsidy.
2. It is part of the birth "one thing" service in many provinces.
3. Example from Hubei: the card is ready about 30 working days after applying.

steps.title: Apply for the baby's passport (护照)
prepare: Household register and birth medical certificate
Photo taken to the exit-entry photo guide
conditions: Only if the baby will travel abroad
steps.howTo:
1. Passports are issued by the exit-entry administration (出入境管理机构) of the National Immigration Administration.
2. A parent or guardian applies with the baby and their own ID; bring the household register and birth medical certificate.
3. Photos follow the NIA photo guide; many offices take them on site.
4. The date here is a planning estimate; move it to 2 months before travel.

steps.title: Vaccines at 4 months: polio (bOPV) dose 3 and DTaP dose 2
steps.howTo:
1. The schedule gives oral polio vaccine (bOPV) dose 3 and DTaP dose 2 at 4 months.
2. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: 6-month check and vaccines: hepatitis B dose 3, DTaP dose 3, meningococcal A dose 1
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Book the health check and vaccines
steps.howTo:
1. The national child health service has a check at 6 months, with a hearing screen, and a blood test once between 6 and 8 months.
2. The immunization schedule gives hepatitis B dose 3, DTaP dose 3 and meningococcal A (MPSV-A) dose 1 at 6 months.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: 8-month check and vaccines: MMR (麻腮风) dose 1 and Japanese encephalitis (乙脑)
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Book the health check and vaccines
steps.howTo:
1. The national child health service has a check at 8 months.
2. The schedule gives MMR dose 1 and Japanese encephalitis vaccine at 8 months: live vaccine dose 1, or inactivated doses 1 and 2, 7 to 10 days apart.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Vaccines at 9 months: meningococcal A dose 2
steps.howTo:
1. The schedule gives meningococcal A (MPSV-A) dose 2 at 9 months.
2. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: 12-month health check
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Book with the community health centre
Notes on walking, words and teeth
steps.howTo:
1. The national child health service has a check at 12 months, with a hearing screen.
2. Later checks are at 18, 24, 30 and 36 months.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: 18-month check and vaccines: DTaP dose 4, MMR dose 2, hepatitis A
documents: Maternal and Child Health Handbook (母子健康手册)
prepare: Book the health check and vaccines
steps.howTo:
1. The schedule gives DTaP dose 4, MMR dose 2 and hepatitis A (live, one dose; or inactivated dose 1) at 18 months, with a health check and blood test.
2. Next come Japanese encephalitis, and hepatitis A dose 2 if inactivated, at 2 years.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Claim the infant care tax deduction (3岁以下婴幼儿照护专项附加扣除)
conditions: Only if a parent pays individual income tax
prepare: Birth medical certificate or household register
steps.howTo:
1. From the month of birth until the month before the third birthday, parents can deduct 2,000 yuan a month per child (the amount since January 2023).
2. One parent claims 100%, or each claims 50%; the split cannot change within a tax year.
3. Declare it in the 个人所得税 app through the employer, or at the annual reconciliation; months missed in the year can be claimed there.

steps.title: Consider a resident ID card for the baby (居民身份证)
conditions: Only if you want one; under 16 it is optional
prepare: Photo taken at the police station
steps.howTo:
1. Children under 16 can get an ID card if a guardian applies at the police station where the hukou is registered; it is valid for 5 years.
2. It is handy for flights, trains, hotels and some online services; the household register works for most of these too.
3. Timing is only a prompt.

steps.title: Pay next year's resident medical insurance for the baby
conditions: Only if the baby is in resident basic medical insurance (城乡居民医保)
prepare: The payment channel, often the 个人所得税 app, WeChat or Alipay
steps.howTo:
1. Resident medical insurance is paid once a year for the next calendar year, usually in a window from September to December; the local medical insurance bureau sets it.
2. Missing the window can bring a waiting period before costs are covered.
3. It repeats every year; move this date to the local window.

title: Newborn · first year · Ontario
summary: Paperwork, health and money plan for a baby born in Ontario, from birth registration to the first birthday and the 18-month visit.
conditions: For a baby born in Ontario
For parents living in Ontario

Apply for OHIP and get a health card

Find a family doctor or nurse practitioner (Health Care Connect)
Midwifery in Ontario

Registered disability savings plan (RDSP) — Canada.ca

steps.title: Register the baby for OHIP
prepare: Keep the bottom part of the form with the health number
steps.howTo:
1. Hospitals with birthing facilities and registered midwives hand out the Ontario Health Coverage Infant Registration form; it is not online.
2. They send the top part; the bottom part shows the baby's health number.
3. The health card is mailed within 8 weeks.
4. Born elsewhere or without a midwife: apply in person at ServiceOntario.

steps.title: Register the birth with the 5-in-1 newborn bundle
prepare: All parents present to certify the birth
Tick birth certificate, SIN, child benefits and Education Savings Referral
steps.howTo:
1. A birth in Ontario must be registered within 30 days.
2. The online bundle registers the birth and applies for a birth certificate, the baby's SIN, Canada child benefits and an Education Savings Referral in one go.
3. Registration is free within 12 months of the birth.
4. Ask for the long-form birth certificate listing parents if a passport is planned.

steps.title: Add the baby to the workplace health and dental plan
prepare: Baby's full name and birth date
Which parent's plan is primary, if both have one
conditions: Only if a parent has health or dental benefits through work
steps.howTo:
1. A birth is a life event that lets a dependant be added outside open enrolment, usually within a set window, often around 31 days; the benefits booklet has the real limit.
2. Adding the baby late can mean waiting for the next open enrolment or giving proof of good health.
3. With two plans, children are usually claimed first on the plan of the parent whose birthday comes first in the year.

steps.title: Line up a family doctor or NP for the baby's checkups
prepare: Register with Health Care Connect if you have no doctor
steps.howTo:
1. Midwives care for parent and baby for 6 weeks after birth; ongoing well-baby checkups are then with a family doctor, nurse practitioner or paediatrician.
2. Health Care Connect finds a family doctor or nurse practitioner accepting patients; the whole family can register.
3. The free Healthy Babies Healthy Children program runs through the local public health unit.
4. The checkup schedule is set by the provider; this date is a planning estimate.

steps.title: Apply for the Canada Child Benefit
conditions: Only if you didn't apply through the birth registration bundle
steps.howTo:
1. Apply as soon as the child is born and living with you.
2. The bundle's Automated Benefits Application usually covers this; otherwise apply through CRA My Account.
3. Applying for a child who started living with you more than 11 months ago needs extra documents.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 2 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow Ontario's routine immunization schedule; at 2 months it lists DTaP-IPV-Hib, pneumococcal conjugate and rotavirus.
2. Ask the doctor or nurse any questions.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Apply for the baby's passport
prepare: Long-form birth certificate listing parents, as proof of parentage
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the baby will travel outside Canada
steps.howTo:
1. Wait for the birth certificate from the registration.
2. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail.
3. A child passport is valid for up to 5 years and can't be renewed.
4. The date here is a planning estimate; move it to 2 months before travel.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 4 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow Ontario's routine immunization schedule; at 4 months it lists DTaP-IPV-Hib, pneumococcal conjugate and rotavirus.
2. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Open an RESP for the Canada Education Savings Grant
steps.howTo:
1. The baby's SIN comes from the registration bundle and is needed to open the RESP.
2. The basic CESG adds 20% of yearly contributions, up to a yearly and a lifetime limit, whatever the family income.
3. Middle- and lower-income families can get an additional grant.
4. Grants apply to contributions until the end of the year the child turns 17.
5. Timing is a planning estimate; unused grant room carries forward.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 6 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow Ontario's routine immunization schedule; at 6 months it lists DTaP-IPV-Hib.
2. The schedule also recommends yearly flu and COVID-19 vaccines each fall from 6 months.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Request the Canada Learning Bond
prepare: Ask the RESP provider to apply
conditions: Only if the family is low-income and the child is eligible for the Canada Child Benefit
steps.howTo:
1. The CLB is for children from low-income families born in 2004 or later.
2. No contribution to the RESP is needed.
3. It is retroactive: yearly amounts build up until the year the child turns 15.
4. The caregiver can request it until the day before the child turns 18.

steps.title: Confirm the return-to-work date with the employer
conditions: Only if a parent is on pregnancy or parental leave
steps.howTo:
1. Returning before the leave ends needs at least 4 weeks' written notice.
2. Standard EI parental benefits are taken within 52 weeks of the birth; extended within 78 weeks.
3. The one-year return is a planning estimate; move it for extended leave.

steps.title: Parental leave ends: return to work
conditions: Only if a parent is on pregnancy or parental leave
steps.howTo:
1. Parental leave is up to 61 weeks after pregnancy leave, or 63 weeks otherwise.
2. One year is a planning estimate for standard benefits; move this to your real date.

steps.title: Apply for the disability tax credit, Child Disability Benefit and RDSP
prepare: Medical practitioner to fill in the medical part of T2201
conditions: Only if the child has a severe and prolonged impairment
steps.howTo:
1. The disability tax credit is applied for with Form T2201, part filled in by a medical practitioner, or through the CRA digital application.
2. Once the child is approved for the DTC and gets the Canada Child Benefit, the Child Disability Benefit is added to the CCB payments automatically.
3. DTC eligibility also opens a registered disability savings plan (RDSP): the Canada Disability Savings Grant matches contributions, and the Canada Disability Savings Bond is paid for lower-income families without contributions.
4. CRA processing takes several weeks; the dates here are estimates. Move this step to when a diagnosis is made.

steps.title: First dental visit
prepare: Find a dentist who sees babies
Note when the first tooth came in
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Dental Association recommends a first dental assessment within 6 months of the first tooth or by one year of age.
2. Move this earlier if the first tooth came early.

steps.title: Routine vaccines at 1 year
steps.howTo:
1. Follow Ontario's routine immunization schedule; at 1 year it lists pneumococcal conjugate, meningococcal conjugate and MMR.
2. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Routine vaccine at 15 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow Ontario's routine immunization schedule; at 15 months it lists varicella (chickenpox).
2. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Routine vaccine at 18 months
steps.howTo:
1. Follow Ontario's routine immunization schedule; at 18 months it lists DTaP-IPV-Hib.
2. Book it with the enhanced 18-month well-baby visit if you can.

steps.title: Enhanced 18-month well-baby visit
steps.howTo:
1. Book with the primary care provider when the child is 18 months old.
2. A short survey gives a snapshot of development to start the discussion.
3. The provider may point to free community resources such as EarlyON centres.

title: Early years · ages 1–4 · British Columbia
summary: Child care, fee help, early learning drop-ins, health coverage and vaccines for a child from 1 to 4 in British Columbia. Child care waitlists are kept by each provider.
conditions: Your child is between 1 and 4
You live in British Columbia

Speech and language therapy, children — HealthLink BC

steps.title: Join licensed child care waitlists
prepare: Shortlist of centres near home or work
steps.howTo:
1. Search licensed facilities on the province's child care map by city, distance, program type and hours.
2. There is no provincial waitlist; each operator keeps and manages its own, so contact each one.
3. If nobody has space, your local Child Care Resource and Referral Centre or the Child Care Service Centre (1-888-338-6622) can help.
4. Facilities are licensed and inspected by the local health authority; inspection reports are on its website.

steps.title: Ask about $10 a Day ChildCareBC centres
conditions: Only if a $10 a Day ChildCareBC centre near you has, or may have, space
prepare: Province's list of $10 a Day centres by school region
steps.howTo:
1. $10 a Day ChildCareBC centres charge a capped low fee for full-time care.
2. Parents don't apply to the province; contact each centre about its space and waitlist.
3. Access depends on each centre's licensed capacity and waitlist; there is no priority list.
4. If your current centre joins the program, your space converts without re-enrolling.

steps.title: Confirm the centre passes on the Child Care Fee Reduction
conditions: Only if you use licensed child care
prepare: Ask the provider whether it takes part in the Child Care Fee Reduction Initiative (CCFRI)
steps.howTo:
1. Participating licensed providers cut monthly fees for children 12 and under; it is not income-tested.
2. Parents don't apply; the reduction shows as a lower monthly fee.
3. Part-time care gets a pro-rated reduction.
4. Check participants on the child care map or the fee reduction estimator; a provider still applying won't show, so ask it directly.

steps.title: Apply for the Affordable Child Care Benefit
conditions: Only if your family income is under the province's limit, or higher with large deductions
Only if you work, study, look for work or have another qualifying reason for care
steps.howTo:
1. A monthly benefit toward child care fees; income, family size and type of care set the amount.
2. A parent is a BC resident and a citizen, permanent resident, Convention refugee or protected person.
3. Parental leave is not a qualifying reason.
4. New applicants fill in the Child Care Arrangement form with the provider and send it with the application.
5. Apply through My Family Services, or by mail or fax with form CF2900, before the end of the month care starts.
6. Renew every year, or sooner if your reason for care changes.

steps.title: Find a StrongStart BC centre and try a drop-in
prepare: Nearest programs on the StrongStart BC map
Hours from the school or school district
steps.howTo:
1. StrongStart BC runs free, play-based early learning drop-ins for children 0 to 5 with a parent or caregiver.
2. Most are in schools and run during the school year.
3. On the first visit you fill in a registration form and show the child's ID, e.g. birth certificate or passport.
4. Registering gives the child a Personal Education Number (PEN), the start of their BC school record.

steps.title: Sign up for children's dental and vision coverage
conditions: Only if your child has no private dental insurance or your family income is low
prepare: Any government dental coverage you already have
steps.howTo:
1. BC Healthy Kids: basic dental, prescription glasses and hearing help for children under 19 in families eligible for MSP supplementary benefits, which have an income limit.
2. Apply for supplementary benefits with Health Insurance BC (HIBC); it asks for 12 months in Canada as a citizen or permanent resident.
3. File taxes every year so HIBC can reassess; show the child's BC Services Card at the dentist or optometrist and confirm coverage first.
4. Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP): for families with no private dental coverage and adjusted family net income under the federal limit, with tax returns filed.
5. For CDCP, list the child as a dependant on your own application.

steps.title: Get the 12-month vaccines
prepare: Book with public health, your doctor or nurse practitioner
steps.howTo:
1. At 12 months: pneumococcal conjugate, meningococcal C conjugate, MMR and chickenpox (varicella).
2. Routine vaccines are free.
3. Keep the record; school will ask for it.

steps.title: Get the 18-month vaccines
prepare: Book with public health, your doctor or nurse practitioner
steps.howTo:
1. At 18 months: DTaP-IPV-Hib (diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib).
2. Indigenous children are also offered hepatitis A.
3. Update the record after each visit.

steps.title: Check speech and language; self-refer if unsure
prepare: Notes on words and sentences your child uses
Local public health unit's phone number
steps.howTo:
1. Public health speech-language services see preschool children with speech or language delays.
2. Parents can self-refer; no doctor's referral is needed (Fraser Health and Island Health, for example).
3. In Fraser Health, call your local health unit, which refers you to the nearest preschool speech service; it serves ages 5 and under.
4. Don't wait for Kindergarten; re-check at 3 and 4.

steps.title: Book an MSP-covered eye exam
prepare: Any family history of eye problems
steps.howTo:
1. MSP covers an annual eye exam for children 0 to 18.
2. Book with an optometrist and bring the child's BC Services Card.
3. Healthy Kids covers prescription glasses once a year for eligible families.
4. The date here is an estimate at age 3; book again every year.

steps.title: Get the 4-to-6-year school-entry boosters
prepare: Book with public health, your doctor, nurse practitioner or a pharmacist
steps.howTo:
1. At 4 to 6 years: Tdap-IPV and MMRV.
2. Pharmacists can give routine vaccines from age 4; in some areas nurses run Kindergarten clinics at school.
3. A child who had lab-confirmed chickenpox after age 1 gets MMR instead of MMRV.
4. The date here is set at age 4; many families book before Kindergarten starts.

steps.title: Make sure the immunization record is in the provincial registry
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Vaccination Status Reporting Regulation, public health collects immunization records for students from Kindergarten to Grade 12.
2. Check the record in Health Gateway; if doses are missing, upload the record on the Provincial Immunization Registry page, or bring it to a public health unit or clinic.
3. Online updates take about 10 to 14 days.
4. A child with no record on file is noted as unimmunized and may be asked to stay home during an outbreak.

title: Early years · ages 1–5 · China
summary: Childcare, kindergarten places, the free final kindergarten year, routine vaccines and free child health checks for a child from 1 to 5 in mainland China. Each city or district sets its own kindergarten dates and papers.
conditions: Your child is between 1 and 5
You live in mainland China

国家托育机构备案信息系统 (national childcare filing system)

National Healthcare Security Administration

steps.title: Check a childcare provider is filed (托育机构备案)
conditions: Only if you plan to use childcare before age 3
prepare: Shortlist of providers near home or work
steps.howTo:
1. Childcare for children under 3 is run by childcare providers (托育机构), and some kindergartens also run toddler classes.
2. A provider first registers as a public institution, a social-service organisation (with civil affairs) or a business (with market regulation), depending on its type.
3. It then files (备案) with the county-level health commission (卫生健康部门), which checks it against the national standards.
4. Filing is done in the national childcare filing system; health departments publish provider details for the public to check.
5. Ask the provider for its filing receipt (备案回执), or check your district health commission's published list.

steps.title: Get the 18-month vaccines
prepare: Appointment at your vaccination clinic (接种单位), usually the community health centre (社区卫生服务中心)
steps.howTo:
1. Under the national immunization programme (国家免疫规划, 2026 schedule), 18 months brings: DTaP (百白破) dose 4, MMR (麻腮风) dose 2, and hepatitis A (甲肝) — the single live dose, or dose 1 of the inactivated vaccine.
2. National programme vaccines are free.
3. Keep the vaccination certificate safe; kindergarten and school will check it.

steps.title: Book the 18-month child health check
documents: Child health record (儿童保健手册)
prepare: Community health centre or township health centre (乡镇卫生院)
steps.howTo:
1. Free child health checks (0–6岁儿童健康管理) under the national basic public health services run at 18, 24, 30 and 36 months, then once a year at 4, 5 and 6.
2. At 18 months: growth, development and teeth, plus a blood test.
3. Checks are meant to line up with vaccine visits, so ask to do both on the same day.

steps.title: Get the 2-year vaccines
steps.howTo:
1. At 2 years: Japanese encephalitis (乙脑) — dose 2 of the live vaccine, or the 2-year dose of the inactivated vaccine.
2. If your child had the inactivated hepatitis A vaccine at 18 months, dose 2 is due now.
3. The clinic knows which products your child had; check the certificate after each visit.

steps.title: Book the 2-year and 30-month child health checks
documents: Child health record (儿童保健手册)
steps.howTo:
1. At 24 months: growth, development, teeth and a hearing screen.
2. Another free check is due at 30 months, with a blood test.
3. Ask about speech or development worries at either visit.

steps.title: Shortlist kindergartens: public or affordable private (公办 / 普惠性民办幼儿园)
prepare: Your district education bureau's admissions notice
steps.howTo:
1. Kindergarten (幼儿园) is for children from 3 until primary school, under the Preschool Education Law (学前教育法, in force since 1 June 2025).
2. Public kindergartens (公办) and affordable private ones (普惠性民办, with government-set fees) are the lower-cost options; other private kindergartens set their own fees.
3. The law asks local governments to help children attend near where parents live or work; admission is test-free.
4. Each city or district sets the rules: in Fengtai, Beijing (example, 2026) families list 2 to 5 kindergartens of at least 2 types on the city platform; Shanghai (example) holds kindergarten open days in April.

steps.title: Gather kindergarten registration papers
documents: Property certificate (房产证) or rental and residence papers
prepare: Residence permit (居住证) or residence registration, if the hukou is elsewhere
steps.howTo:
1. Districts publish their own lists; these papers are the usual ones.
2. Children with a local hukou usually use the household register and home address.
3. Children without a local hukou usually need a local residence permit; Shanghai (example) accepts a Shanghai residence permit (居住证) or residence registration certificate (居住登记凭证) for the child and guardian.
4. Check how your district orders admissions before choosing kindergartens.

steps.title: Get the 3-year vaccine
steps.howTo:
1. At 3 years: meningococcal A and C polysaccharide vaccine (A群C群流脑多糖疫苗), dose 1.
2. Do this before kindergarten starts, so the certificate is complete for the entry check.

steps.title: Book the 3-year child health check
documents: Child health record (儿童保健手册)
steps.howTo:
1. At 36 months: growth, development, teeth and a hearing screen.
2. From 3 to 6 the free check is yearly; children in kindergarten may have it there.

steps.title: Register for kindergarten (幼儿园报名)
prepare: Account on your city's kindergarten admissions platform
steps.howTo:
1. Children usually start in the September after they turn 3, with a cut-off such as 31 August; the city sets it.
2. Registration is usually in spring or early summer before the September start.
3. Shanghai (example, 2026): children born 1 Sept 2022 to 31 Aug 2023; online sign-up 22–29 April, registration and document checks 7–29 May, offers by 1 July.
4. Beijing (example, 2026): district portals on the admissions platform opened from 1 June, mostly with sign-up in June and document checks in July.
5. The law allows a health check at entry but no test or interview.
6. The due date here is a planning estimate at age 3; set it to your district's window.

steps.title: Hand in the vaccination certificate for the entry check (入托入学查验预防接种证)
prepare: Copy or photo of the certificate
steps.howTo:
1. Under the national check rules (2021), every childcare provider, kindergarten and primary school checks the certificate of each new or transferring child.
2. The kindergarten asks for it at registration and finishes the check within 30 days of the start of term.
3. If doses are missing, the clinic gives catch-up doses (补种) and notes them on the certificate; the kindergarten checks again by the end of December.
4. A lost certificate can be re-issued (补证) by the vaccination clinic.
5. The due date here is a planning estimate, about a month after a September start.

steps.title: Get the 4-year polio vaccine
steps.howTo:
1. At 4 years: oral polio vaccine (bOPV, 脊灰), dose 4.
2. The national schedule has no routine dose at 5; the next visit is at 6, in the school-years plan.

steps.title: Book the 4-year child health check
documents: Child health record (儿童保健手册)
prepare: Community health centre, or ask whether the kindergarten hosts it
steps.howTo:
1. At 4: growth, development, teeth, a vision screen and a blood test.
2. Children in kindergarten may be checked there; ask the kindergarten's health staff.

steps.title: Book the 5-year child health check
documents: Child health record (儿童保健手册)
prepare: Community health centre, or ask whether the kindergarten hosts it
steps.howTo:
1. At 5: growth, development, teeth, a vision screen and a blood test.
2. The last free yearly check is at 6.

steps.title: Check the free final kindergarten year (免费学前教育)
conditions: Only if your child is in the final kindergarten year (大班) at a public or approved private kindergarten
prepare: This term's fee notice from the kindergarten
steps.howTo:
1. From autumn term 2025, childcare and education fees (保育教育费) for the final year before primary school (学前一年, the 大班) are waived at public kindergartens.
2. At private kindergartens approved by the education department, fees are cut by the same amount as at a similar local public kindergarten; the private kindergarten may still charge the difference.
3. Meals, boarding and other charges (伙食费、住宿费、杂费) are not covered.
4. The kindergarten and the education system handle it; there is no family application in the national rules.
5. Tibet, Xinjiang and some other areas keep their own existing free-preschool policies.
6. The due date here is a planning estimate at the start of the final year; check the fee notice then.

steps.title: Pay the yearly resident medical insurance (城乡居民医保)
conditions: Only if the child is in resident basic medical insurance
prepare: The payment channel, often the 个人所得税 app, WeChat or Alipay
steps.howTo:
1. Resident medical insurance is paid once a year for the next calendar year, usually in a window from September to December; the local medical insurance bureau sets it.
2. Missing the window can bring a waiting period before costs are covered.
3. It repeats every year; move this date to the local window.

steps.title: Switch from the infant care to the children's education deduction (子女教育)
conditions: Only if a parent claims the infant care deduction
prepare: Kindergarten or school details, if any
steps.howTo:
1. The infant care deduction ends the month before the third birthday; the children's education deduction (子女教育专项附加扣除) starts from the month the child turns 3.
2. Both are 2,000 yuan a month per child (since January 2023), split 100% or 50/50 between parents.
3. Update the declaration in the 个人所得税 app; it runs through preschool, school and university.

title: Early years · ages 1–4 · Ontario
summary: Child care, family programs, health coverage and check-ups for a child from 1 to 4 in Ontario. Child care is run locally; details vary by municipality.
conditions: Your child is between 1 and 4
You live in Ontario

sources.title: Find and pay for child care — Ontario.ca
Find child care near you — Ontario child care finder
TELCCS waitlist registration — City of Toronto (example)
Canada-Ontario early years and child care agreement — Ontario.ca
Child care subsidies — Ontario.ca
Child care fee subsidy — City of Toronto (example)
Find an EarlyON child and family centre — Ontario.ca
Ontario's routine immunization schedule — Ontario.ca
Vaccines for children at school — Ontario.ca
Enhanced 18-month well-baby visit — Ontario.ca
Preschool speech and language program — Ontario.ca
Canadian Dental Care Plan: Who qualifies — Canada.ca
Canadian Dental Care Plan: How to apply — Canada.ca
Get dental care (Healthy Smiles Ontario) — Ontario.ca
What OHIP covers — Ontario.ca

steps.title: Join licensed child care waitlists
prepare: Shortlist of centres near home or work
steps.howTo:
1. Search licensed centres and home child care with Ontario's child care finder.
2. There is no single provincial waitlist; join each centre's own list, or your city's where it runs one (Toronto does for its own centres).
3. Waits can be long; many families join during pregnancy, so join now if you haven't.
4. Check a caregiver's safety record through the link on the Ontario child care page.

steps.title: Confirm the centre charges CWELCC reduced fees
conditions: Only if you use a licensed centre or home child care agency enrolled in CWELCC
prepare: Ask each centre whether it is enrolled in CWELCC
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) system, enrolled licensees cut fees for children under 6.
2. A child who turns 6 in a licensed preschool, kindergarten or family age group stays eligible until June 30.
3. Parents don't apply; the reduction comes through an enrolled provider.
4. The province sets a daily fee cap that changes over time; check the current cap on Ontario.ca.

steps.title: Apply for a child care fee subsidy
conditions: Only if you need help with fees; the amount depends on family income
prepare: Adjusted family net income from your tax return
Your municipality's or DSSAB's subsidy office
steps.howTo:
1. Apply to your local municipal service manager (CMSM), District Social Services Administration Board (DSSAB) or First Nation, not the province.
2. What you pay is set on a sliding scale from adjusted family net income on your tax return.
3. Children under 13 qualify, or up to 18 with special needs.
4. Some cities keep a subsidy waitlist (Toronto does); apply early.
5. It can be used for licensed care, recreation programs, camps and school-board before- and after-school programs.

steps.title: Find an EarlyON centre and try a drop-in
prepare: Nearest centres on the Ontario map
steps.howTo:
1. EarlyON Child and Family Centres run free programs for children from birth to 6 and their parents or caregivers.
2. Activities include reading, storytelling, sing-alongs and games, with advice from early childhood professionals.
3. Many run in libraries, schools, parks and community centres.

steps.title: Sign up for children's dental coverage
conditions: Only if your child has no private dental insurance or your family income is low
prepare: Child's SIN, if they have one
Any government dental coverage you already have
steps.howTo:
1. Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP): for families with no access to private dental insurance and adjusted family net income under the federal limit; tax returns must be filed.
2. For CDCP, list the child as a dependant on your own application.
3. Healthy Smiles Ontario (HSO): free for children 17 and under in low-income households; income limits are updated yearly.
4. Children on Ontario Works or ODSP are enrolled in HSO automatically; others apply online or by mail, and a card arrives by post.

steps.title: Get the 12- and 15-month vaccines
prepare: Book with your doctor or nurse practitioner
steps.howTo:
1. At 12 months: pneumococcal conjugate, meningococcal conjugate and MMR.
2. At 15 months: chickenpox (varicella).
3. Keep the record; you will report it to public health before school.

steps.title: Book the enhanced 18-month well-baby visit
prepare: Questions about development, sleep or behaviour
steps.howTo:
1. Your doctor or nurse practitioner spends extra time on development and can refer you to local services.
2. The 18-month vaccine is DTaP-IPV-Hib.
3. Fill in the free Looksee Checklist beforehand and bring it.

steps.title: Check speech and language; self-refer if unsure
prepare: Looksee Checklist for your child's age
Notes on words and sentences your child uses
steps.howTo:
1. Compare your child with the Looksee Checklist or your local program's milestone sheet.
2. If anything worries you, register with the local Preschool Speech and Language program; no doctor's referral is needed.
3. The program serves children from birth until they start school, so don't wait for Kindergarten.
4. Re-check at 3 and 4.

steps.title: Book an OHIP-covered eye exam
prepare: Any family history of eye problems
steps.howTo:
1. OHIP covers 1 major eye exam every 12 months, plus any minor assessments needed, for people 19 and under.
2. Book with an optometrist and bring the child's health card.
3. Book again every year.

steps.title: Get the 4-year vaccines and report them to public health
prepare: Local public health unit's ICON page
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario's schedule gives Tdap-IPV and MMRV at 4 years; the school vaccine page calls these the 4-to-6-year boosters.
2. They are needed to attend school unless there is a valid exemption.
3. Doctors don't report doses to public health; parents do, e.g. through Immunization Connect Ontario (ICON).

title: School years · K to Grade 7 · British Columbia
summary: Registration, records, assessments, school vaccines and the move to secondary for a child at a British Columbia public elementary school. Many dates are set by each school district.
conditions: Your child will attend a public school in British Columbia
From Kindergarten to the end of Grade 7

sources.title: British Columbia Training and Education Savings Grant
Full day Kindergarten — Province of British Columbia
School Act, Part 2 (students and parents) — BC Laws
Priority Kindergarten registration — Vancouver School Board (example)
Kindergarten registration FAQs — Vancouver School Board (example)
Kindergarten District Choice Programs — Vancouver School Board (example)
French Immersion — Burnaby Schools (example)
Vaccination Status Reporting Regulation — HealthLink BC
Submit or update your immunization records — Province of British Columbia
Immunization schedules for children — HealthLink BC
Grade 6 immunizations in B.C. (HealthLinkBC File #50f)
Grade 9 immunizations in B.C. — HealthLink BC
Foundation Skills Assessment (FSA) — Province of British Columbia
Mini School Programs — Vancouver School Board (example)
Middle School Program — Coquitlam School District 43 (example)
How to apply for a child passport in Canada — Canada.ca

steps.title: Apply for the BC Training and Education Savings Grant
conditions: Only if the child has an RESP (the newborn plan opens one)
Only if the child and the applying parent or guardian live in BC when applying
steps.howTo:
1. Apply through the RESP provider between the child's 6th birthday and the day before they turn 9.
2. No contribution to the RESP is needed.
3. Not every provider takes part; check the list of participating promoters.
4. The due date is the 6th birthday, the start of the window.

steps.title: Find the catchment school with the district's school locator
steps.howTo:
1. Each school district runs its own locator by home address.
2. Registration is with the district and catchment school, not the province.
3. A school outside your catchment is a separate cross-boundary request; in Vancouver it runs in February, after catchment registration.

steps.title: Gather proof of age, identity and address
prepare: Child's birth certificate or immigration or citizenship documents
Property tax statement, purchase agreement or rental agreement
Plus a recent bill showing your name and address
steps.howTo:
1. Vancouver, for example, asks for proof of address, the child's original birth certificate or immigration documents, the parent's ID and immunization records if available.
2. Each district publishes the documents it accepts; some schools ask for more proof of address.
3. In Vancouver, children born outside Canada register through the Newcomer Welcome Centre instead.

steps.title: Check the immunization record is on file with public health
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Vaccination Status Reporting Regulation, public health collects immunization records for students from Kindergarten to Grade 12.
2. The regulation asks for the record; it doesn't make vaccination a condition of attending school.
3. Without a record on file, the child is noted as unimmunized and public health may follow up.
4. During an outbreak of a vaccine-preventable disease, an unimmunized child may be asked to stay home, possibly for several weeks.
5. Upload the record on the Provincial Immunization Registry page, or bring it to a public health unit or clinic; online updates take about 10 to 14 days.

steps.title: Register for Kindergarten
prepare: Status documents, if not a citizen or permanent resident
steps.howTo:
1. A child who turns 5 by December 31 can start Kindergarten that September; it is full day and there is no Junior Kindergarten.
2. Registration usually begins in January or February for September; Vancouver's priority window runs November 1 to January 31, with an online form and then an appointment at the catchment school.
3. The date here is an estimate at about age 4½; set it to your district's window.
4. Parents may defer Kindergarten by a year; the child is registered for school or homeschooling by the year they turn 6.

steps.title: Apply for Early French Immersion
conditions: Only if you want French Immersion
prepare: District's French Immersion information session date
steps.howTo:
1. Most districts ask you to register at the English catchment school first, then apply to French Immersion separately.
2. Places are often decided by lottery, not first come, first served.
3. Vancouver: online Kindergarten choice window in January (January 6 to February 3, 2026), up to 3 schools, random computer draw.
4. Burnaby: applications during February all get equal priority; the lottery is in early March, and Late French Immersion starts in Grade 6.
5. The date here is an estimate; set it to your district's window.

steps.title: Every September: back-to-school admin
prepare: Before- and after-school care and transport
New vaccine doses added to the immunization registry
steps.howTo:
1. Repeat every September from Kindergarten to Grade 7; this step is dated at the start of Kindergarten, about age 5.
2. Districts send their own forms; return them in the first weeks.
3. Keep the immunization record in the provincial registry current after new doses.

steps.title: Grade 4 Foundation Skills Assessment
steps.howTo:
1. The FSA checks reading, writing and numeracy for all BC students in Grades 4 and 7.
2. It runs in the fall, in parts spread over days or weeks, none longer than an hour; the 2026 window is September 28 to November 6.
3. Grade 4 starts in September of the year the child turns 9; the date here is an estimate at about age 9¼.
4. The school shares the student report and writing booklet with parents once scoring is done.

steps.title: Talk through the Grade 6 school vaccine
steps.howTo:
1. Public health offers HPV vaccine to all Grade 6 students at school, as one dose.
2. Hepatitis B is not a routine Grade 6 vaccine in BC; students missing earlier childhood doses may be offered catch-up.
3. Under BC's mature minor rule, a child under 19 who understands the benefits and risks can consent or refuse; parents and children are encouraged to discuss it.
4. Grade 6 starts in September of the year the child turns 11; the date here is an estimate.
5. In Grade 9, school clinics offer meningococcal quadrivalent and Tdap vaccines.

steps.title: Grade 7 Foundation Skills Assessment
steps.howTo:
1. The same reading, writing and numeracy assessment as Grade 4, in the fall of Grade 7.
2. Grade 7 starts in September of the year the child turns 12; the date here is an estimate at about age 12¼.
3. The student report and writing booklet come home once scoring is done.

steps.title: Apply to secondary specialty programs
conditions: Only if you want a specialty or choice program, e.g. a mini school, arts or sports academy
prepare: Portfolio, test or interview, if asked
steps.howTo:
1. Programs, entry rules and dates are district-specific.
2. Vancouver mini schools start in Grade 8; apply in Grade 7 through the District Registry (November 16 to December 17, 2026) and to each program separately.
3. Each program sets its own requirements; start early.
4. The date here is an estimate for late fall of Grade 7.

steps.title: Get ready for the move to secondary school
prepare: Catchment secondary from the district locator
Talk with the Grade 7 teacher or counsellor
Electives your child is interested in
steps.howTo:
1. Elementary is usually Kindergarten to Grade 7, with secondary from Grade 8.
2. Some districts run middle schools instead; Coquitlam, for example, has Grades 6 to 8, so the move comes at Grade 6 and again at Grade 9.
3. Transition events and course selection are district- and school-specific; ask the elementary school.
4. The date here is an estimate for the winter of Grade 7.

steps.title: Apply for a new child passport (around age 5)
prepare: Expiry date of the current child passport
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the child has, or needs, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. A child passport, for under 16, is valid for up to 5 years and cannot be renewed; each one is a new application.
2. This date assumes a first passport in the baby's first months; move it to about 2 months before the current one expires, or before travel.
3. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail; check current times.
4. Many countries ask for a passport valid 6 months past the return date.

steps.title: Apply for a new child passport (around age 10)
prepare: Expiry date of the current child passport
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the child has, or needs, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. A child passport, for under 16, is valid for up to 5 years and cannot be renewed; each one is a new application.
2. This date assumes a first passport in the baby's first months; move it to about 2 months before the current one expires, or before travel.
3. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail; check current times.
4. Many countries ask for a passport valid 6 months past the return date.

title: School years · primary · China
summary: Primary school enrollment, catchment allocation, private school lotteries, student status, school-entry vaccines and the move to middle school for a child in mainland China. Each city or district sets its own dates and papers.
conditions: Your child will attend primary school in mainland China
From enrollment to the move to middle school

sources.title: 中华人民共和国义务教育法 (Compulsory Education Law) — Ministry of Education
教育部办公厅关于进一步做好普通中小学招生入学工作的通知 (2022 enrollment notice) — Ministry of Education
