市教委关于2026年上海市义务教育阶段学校招生入学工作的实施意见 (Shanghai enrollment 2026) — Shanghai Municipal Government (example)

steps.title: Check the rules for children without a local hukou (随迁子女) and get a residence permit (居住证)
conditions: Only if your child's hukou (户口) is not in the city where you live
documents: Social insurance record (社保缴费记录)
prepare: Your city's enrollment rules for children without a local hukou
Months of social insurance paid in this city
steps.howTo:
1. The Compulsory Education Law says children living where parents work or live, away from their hukou, get equal access to compulsory education there; each province sets the details.
2. National policy uses the residence permit as the main basis, and the MOE's 2026 notice asks cities to cut extra papers, with some areas moving to residence-permit-only entry.
3. A residence permit generally follows at least half a year of living in the city with a stable job, home or studies.
4. Shanghai (example, 2026): the child holds a valid Shanghai residence permit or residence registration, and one parent holds a residence permit with 6 months of city social insurance within a year, or 3 years of registered flexible employment.
5. Beijing (example, 2026): parents bring proof of work and home in Beijing, the whole family's household register and a Beijing residence permit to the local street office for an eligibility check.
6. Some cities use points (积分) instead; start early, since social insurance months take time to build.

steps.title: Find your catchment primary school (划片 / 学区)
prepare: Home address as on the property or rental papers
Your district education bureau's catchment map
steps.howTo:
1. Compulsory education is test-free and near home (免试就近入学): each public school has a catchment area (划片) set by the county or district education bureau.
2. A single-school catchment (单校划片) maps an address to one school; a multi-school catchment (多校划片) covers several schools and places children among them.
3. Beijing (example) mainly uses registration with both single- and multi-school catchments.
4. Catchment maps, entry conditions and places are published by the district each spring; many districts give priority by hukou and home ownership or length of residence at the address.

steps.title: Gather enrollment papers
documents: Property certificate (房产证) or rental contract
prepare: Residence permit (居住证) and social insurance record, if the hukou is elsewhere
steps.howTo:
1. Each district publishes what it accepts; these are the usual papers.
2. Local-hukou children usually use the household register plus the home's property certificate; renters follow district rules.
3. Non-hukou children usually add the residence permit and parents' social insurance or work papers.
4. The MOE says only necessary papers may be asked for, and cities are sharing hukou, property and social insurance data to cut paperwork.

steps.title: Take part in enrollment information collection (入学信息采集)
documents: Property certificate (房产证) or residence permit (居住证)
prepare: Account on your city's compulsory-education enrollment platform
steps.howTo:
1. Children who turn 6 start primary school that September; the law allows a delay to 7 where conditions are lacking.
2. Cities use a cut-off date, often 31 August: Beijing (2026) took children born by 31 Aug 2020; Shanghai (2026) took those born 1 Sept 2019 to 31 Aug 2020.
3. Collection is usually in spring: in Shanghai (2026), 13–26 April through the kindergarten or the district; in Beijing, on the city enrollment platform, then the printed form goes to the school.
4. The vaccination certificate is not a precondition for registration; schools ask for it after the start of term.
5. The due date here is a planning estimate at age 6; set it to your district's window.

steps.title: Apply to a private primary school and its lottery (民办摇号)
conditions: Only if you want a private (民办) primary school
documents: Enrollment information form from the collection step
prepare: Private schools approved in your district or city
steps.howTo:
1. Private and public schools enroll at the same time (公民同招), and private schools take pupils mainly from their approving area.
2. When applicants exceed places, a computer lottery (电脑随机录取) decides, under supervision.
3. Shanghai (example, 2026): private primary sign-up 7–9 May, lottery 20–21 May, recorded and notarised.
4. A child not placed by lottery falls back to the public catchment allocation.

steps.title: Get the school place and register at the school (入学登记)
documents: Property certificate (房产证) or residence permit (居住证)
prepare: Notice from the district or school
steps.howTo:
1. The district assigns a public school by catchment (划片), or confirms the private place.
2. Shanghai (example, 2026): public primary sign-up 7–11 May; results from 22 May by text and the enrollment platform.
3. Schools may not select by tests, interviews, certificates or competition results.
4. If the place is wrong or missing, call the district's enrollment hotline.

steps.title: Get the 6-year vaccines
prepare: Appointment at your vaccination clinic (接种单位)
steps.howTo:
1. At 6 (2026 national schedule): DTaP (百白破) dose 5, which since 1 January 2025 replaces the old DT (白破) dose, and meningococcal A and C polysaccharide vaccine dose 2.
2. Children who had the inactivated Japanese encephalitis (乙脑) vaccine also get their 6-year dose.
3. Book the free 6-year child health check (vision, teeth, blood test) at the same time.

steps.title: Hand in the vaccination certificate for the school-entry check (入学查验预防接种证)
prepare: Copy or photo of the certificate
steps.howTo:
1. Every primary school checks the certificate of each new, transferring or joining pupil.
2. The check is done within 30 days of the start of term.
3. If doses are missing, the clinic gives catch-up doses (补种) and notes them; the school checks again by the end of December.
4. A lost certificate can be re-issued (补证) by the vaccination clinic.
5. The due date here is a planning estimate, about a month after a September start.

steps.title: Confirm the student status record (学籍)
prepare: Child's ID number as on the household register
steps.howTo:
1. The school registers each pupil in the national student status system (全国中小学生学籍信息管理系统).
2. The rule is one pupil, one record, and the record follows the pupil (一人一籍、籍随人走) on transfer.
3. Being registered at one school while attending another (人籍分离) is not allowed.
4. Shanghai (example) links new pupils into its system by 31 August.
5. Check the name, date of birth and ID number with the class teacher; the middle-school allocation uses this record.

steps.title: Yearly September start: school notices and forms
prepare: School notices for the new year
steps.howTo:
1. Each September, read the school's start-of-year notices and update contact and health details.
2. If you move and change schools (转学), the student status transfers with the pupil, and the new school checks the vaccination certificate again.
3. The date here is set at age 7; repeat each September.

steps.title: Check the middle-school allocation rules (小升初)
prepare: Whether to apply to return to the hukou district
steps.howTo:
1. Middle school is also test-free and near home: in a single-school catchment each middle school takes all pupils from its linked primary schools (对口直升).
2. In a multi-school catchment, families list choices; oversubscribed schools place pupils by random allocation (随机派位).
3. The allocation runs on the national student status record.
4. Timing is usually spring of Grade 6; in Shanghai (example, 2026) Grade 5 pupils check their details in April, as primary there has 5 grades.
5. Beijing (example): a pupil can apply to go to middle school in the hukou district or where the family actually lives, through the primary school.
6. The due date here is a planning estimate, about age 12; set it to your district's notice.

steps.title: Apply to a private middle school and its lottery (民办摇号)
conditions: Only if you want a private (民办) middle school
prepare: Private middle schools in your approving area
steps.howTo:
1. Private middle schools enroll at the same time as public ones, and use a computer lottery when oversubscribed.
2. They may not test, interview or use certificates to select pupils.
3. Shanghai (example, 2026): private middle school sign-up 12–14 May.

steps.title: Take part in catchment allocation to middle school (对口 / 派位)
prepare: Account on your city's enrollment platform
Ordered list of choices, if your area uses them
steps.howTo:
1. The district places pupils by linked primary (对口) or random allocation (派位) inside the catchment.
2. Beijing (example) places pupils by listed choices and random allocation (志愿派位); a middle school with fewer applicants than places takes them directly.
3. Results come from the district; a pupil with a private place does not enter this allocation.

title: School years · JK to Grade 8 · Ontario
summary: Registration, records, assessments, school vaccines and the move to high school for a child at an Ontario public elementary school. Many dates are set by each school board.
conditions: Your child will attend a publicly funded school in Ontario
From Junior Kindergarten to the end of Grade 8

steps.title: Find the designated school with the board's school locator
prepare: Public or Catholic board, English or French
steps.howTo:
1. Each school board runs its own locator by home address.
2. Registration is with the board and school, not the province.

steps.title: Gather proof of age and address
prepare: Lease, property tax bill or similar
Plus a utility bill, bank statement or insurance policy
steps.howTo:
1. Boards usually ask for one proof of age and two proofs of address (the Ottawa-Carleton board, for example).
2. Each board publishes the documents it accepts; check its list.
3. Families with temporary status are often asked to contact the board's admissions office first.

steps.title: Report immunizations to the local public health unit
prepare: Yellow immunization card or doctor's printout
Local public health unit's ICON page
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Immunization of School Pupils Act (ISPA), pupils need diphtheria, tetanus, polio, measles, mumps, rubella, meningococcal, whooping cough and chickenpox vaccines, or a valid exemption.
2. Parents report doses to public health, e.g. through Immunization Connect Ontario (ICON); doctors don't do it for you.
3. If records are missing, public health sends a notice and then a suspension order; a pupil can be suspended for up to 20 school days (Toronto Public Health).
4. Medical and non-medical exemptions have their own forms and process.

steps.title: Register for Junior Kindergarten
prepare: Status documents, if not a citizen or permanent resident
steps.howTo:
1. A child can start Junior Kindergarten in September of the year they turn 4, i.e. turning 4 by December 31.
2. Registration usually opens in the winter before, often January (York Region, for example); the date here is an estimate at about age 3½.
3. Kindergarten is a free 2-year program; school is compulsory from September of the year the child turns 6.

steps.title: Check French Immersion entry points and apply
conditions: Only if you want French Immersion
prepare: Board's French Immersion information session date
steps.howTo:
1. Entry grades and deadlines are set by each board, and a missed window can mean waiting for a later entry point.
2. York Region: entry at Grade 1, with registration in January–February alongside Kindergarten registration.
3. Toronto: apply online in November of the JK year for entry in Senior Kindergarten, the only Early French Immersion entry; Toronto also has a later Middle French Immersion entry.
4. The date here is an estimate; set it to your board's window.

steps.title: Every September: back-to-school admin
prepare: Before- and after-school care and transport
New vaccine doses reported to public health
steps.howTo:
1. Repeat every September from JK to Grade 8; this step is dated at the start of JK.
2. Boards send their own forms; return them in the first weeks.
3. Report any new vaccine doses to public health so ISPA records stay current.

steps.title: Grade 3 EQAO assessment
steps.howTo:
1. EQAO tests the reading, writing and math expected by the end of Grade 3.
2. Schools pick dates within EQAO's spring window (May 4 – June 8 in 2027); the date here is an estimate at about age 8¾.
3. Results don't count toward report card marks.
4. The Individual Student Report comes home from school by the end of the following September.

steps.title: Grade 6 EQAO assessment
steps.howTo:
1. EQAO tests the reading, writing and math expected by the end of Grade 6.
2. Schools pick dates within EQAO's spring window; the date here is an estimate at about age 11¾.
3. Results don't count toward report card marks; the Individual Student Report comes home the following fall.

steps.title: Consent to the Grade 7 school vaccines
steps.howTo:
1. Public health runs school clinics in Grade 7 for meningococcal conjugate (ACYW), hepatitis B and HPV.
2. Meningococcal is required under ISPA; hepatitis B and HPV are recommended, not required.
3. Return the consent form before the clinic; Toronto asks for it even if you decline.
4. Hepatitis B and HPV can take more than one dose, months apart; the health unit sets the schedule.
5. Missed doses stay free to catch up at public health or your doctor while still in school (Grades 7–12 in Toronto).
6. Grade 7 starts in September of the year the child turns 12; the date here is an estimate.

steps.title: Attend high school open houses
prepare: Designated high school from the board locator
steps.howTo:
1. Open houses and information nights run from November to January in Toronto, for example.
2. Grade 8 starts in September of the year the child turns 13; the date here is an estimate for November of Grade 8.

steps.title: Apply to specialized high school programs
conditions: Only if you want a specialized program, e.g. arts, math, science or technology
prepare: Portfolio, video or audition, if asked
steps.howTo:
1. Programs, entry rules and dates are board-specific.
2. Toronto, for example, opens a 3-week online window in November of Grade 8.
3. Some programs ask for more than a form; start early.

steps.title: Choose Grade 9 courses
prepare: Talk with the Grade 8 teacher or guidance counsellor
Electives your child is interested in
steps.howTo:
1. Grade 9 course types are de-streamed, academic and open; core subjects are de-streamed, so there is no applied/academic choice for them.
2. Course selection for students under 18 needs a parent's approval.
3. Windows are board-specific; Toronto, for example, runs it online in February of Grade 8; the date here is an estimate.

steps.title: Apply for a new child passport (around age 5)
prepare: Expiry date of the current child passport
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the child has, or needs, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. A child passport, for under 16, is valid for up to 5 years and cannot be renewed; each one is a new application.
2. This date assumes a first passport in the baby's first months; move it to about 2 months before the current one expires, or before travel.
3. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail; check current times.
4. Many countries ask for a passport valid 6 months past the return date.

steps.title: Apply for a new child passport (around age 10)
prepare: Expiry date of the current child passport
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the child has, or needs, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. A child passport, for under 16, is valid for up to 5 years and cannot be renewed; each one is a new application.
2. This date assumes a first passport in the baby's first months; move it to about 2 months before the current one expires, or before travel.
3. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail; check current times.
4. Many countries ask for a passport valid 6 months past the return date.

title: High school · Grades 8–12 · British Columbia
summary: Dogwood requirements, graduation assessments and post-secondary applications for a teen going through a BC public secondary school. Dates assume Grade 8 starts around age 13.
conditions: For a young person attending secondary school in British Columbia, Grades 8 to 12
Working towards the BC Certificate of Graduation (Dogwood Diploma)

Certificates of Graduation — Gov.bc.ca
Graduation Requirements policy — Gov.bc.ca

Career-Life Connections — B.C. Curriculum
Graduation assessment information for parents and students — Gov.bc.ca
Apply — EducationPlannerBC
Complete the application — UBC Undergraduate Admissions

How to apply — StudentAid BC
Pay for education using the Registered Education Savings Plan — Canada.ca

steps.title: Choose Grade 8 courses with the Grade 7 teacher
prepare: Questions for the secondary school counsellor
steps.howTo:
1. Most BC districts run secondary school from Grade 8 to 12; some start it at Grade 9 after a middle school, so check the district.
2. Course selection usually happens in the winter or spring of Grade 7; schools set their own dates.
3. Most students start Grade 8 in September of the year they turn 13, so move this step to the real date.

steps.title: Start Grade 8
steps.howTo: 1. The school year starts in September, the year the student turns 13 in most cases.

steps.title: Choose Grade 10 courses and map out the 80 credits
steps.howTo:
1. The Dogwood needs at least 80 credits from Grades 10 to 12: 52 from required courses and at least 28 elective credits.
2. Required: Language Arts 10, 11 and 12; Math 10 and 11 or 12; Science 10 and 11 or 12; Social Studies 10 and 11 or 12; Physical and Health Education 10; an Arts Education or Applied Design, Skills and Technologies course; Career-Life Education; and Career-Life Connections.
3. At least 16 credits must be at Grade 12 level, including a Language Arts 12 course and Career-Life Connections.
4. The 3 graduation assessments and 4 Indigenous-focused credits are also needed.
5. Course selection is usually in the winter of Grade 9; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Write the Grade 10 Numeracy Assessment
steps.howTo:
1. Writing it is a graduation requirement; it tests maths learned across subjects up to Grade 10.
2. It is usually written in Grade 10; the school picks the session, so this due date is an estimate.
3. It can be rewritten; the best result counts and goes on the transcript.

steps.title: Write the Grade 10 Literacy Assessment
steps.howTo:
1. Writing it is a graduation requirement.
2. It is usually written in Grade 10; the school picks the session, so this due date is an estimate.
3. It can be rewritten; the best result counts and goes on the transcript.

steps.title: Complete Career-Life Education
prepare: Ideas for university, college, trades or work
steps.howTo:
1. Career-Life Education is a required 4-credit course.
2. Many schools run it in Grade 10; this due date assumes the end of Grade 10, so move it to match the school.

steps.title: Choose Grade 11 courses to keep post-secondary options open
prepare: Programs of interest and their admission requirements
steps.howTo:
1. Post-secondary programs list specific Grade 11 and 12 courses, such as a particular Math or Science, as admission requirements.
2. Some Grade 12 courses need a Grade 11 course first, so plan both years together.
3. Course selection is usually in the winter of Grade 10; schools set their own dates.

steps.title: Choose Grade 12 courses to meet program requirements
prepare: Admission requirements for each program on the shortlist
steps.howTo:
1. Check each program's required Grade 12 courses and minimum marks on the institution's site or EducationPlannerBC.
2. Count at least 16 Grade 12 credits, including Language Arts 12 and Career-Life Connections.
3. Course selection is usually in the winter of Grade 11.

steps.title: Earn the 4 Indigenous-focused credits
prepare: List of Indigenous-focused courses the school offers
steps.howTo:
1. Since 2023/24, every Dogwood student completes at least 4 credits of Indigenous-focused coursework; the 80-credit total stays the same.
2. Options include provincial Indigenous-focused courses, First Nations language courses, approved local courses and some external credentials.
3. Ask the school which of its courses also count towards another requirement.
4. This due date assumes the end of Grade 11 and is an estimate.

steps.title: Apply for scholarships and awards
steps.howTo:
1. District/Authority Scholarships are provincial awards chosen by local committees for excellence in areas such as fine arts, athletics, trades, languages or community service; ask the school how to apply.
2. Recipients hear in spring, are confirmed in September and get a tuition voucher in November; it has 5 years to be redeemed.
3. Many post-secondary schools also have entrance awards with their own forms.
4. Deadlines vary widely; this date is an estimate for spring of Grade 12.

steps.title: Apply to BC post-secondary through EducationPlannerBC
prepare: Personal Education Number (PEN) from the school
conditions: Only if they plan to go to a public college or university in BC
steps.howTo:
1. Most BC public post-secondary institutions take applications through EducationPlannerBC.
2. Each institution sets its own deadlines; UBC's application opens in early October and closes January 15 for September entry.
3. This due date assumes mid-January of Grade 12 and is an estimate; check each program.

steps.title: Send the transcript to chosen schools through StudentTranscripts Service
conditions: Only if they applied to post-secondary
steps.howTo:
1. Grade 12 students pick institutions in the StudentTranscripts Service between November and June of their graduation year.
2. Choosing "Send Updates" lets the institution request updated marks until the date entered.
3. This date is an estimate; some institutions ask for it with the application.

steps.title: Write the Grade 12 Literacy Assessment
steps.howTo:
1. Writing it is a graduation requirement.
2. It is usually written in Grade 12; the school picks the session, so this due date is an estimate.
3. It can be rewritten; the best result counts.

steps.title: Complete Career-Life Connections and the capstone
steps.howTo:
1. Career-Life Connections is a required 4-credit course and counts as a Grade 12 credit.
2. It includes at least 30 hours of career-life exploration, such as work, volunteering, fieldwork or a passion project.
3. It ends with a capstone project the student designs and presents.
4. Schools spread it over Grades 11 and 12 differently; this date assumes spring of Grade 12.

steps.title: Apply for StudentAid BC
conditions: Only if they need student financial aid for college or university
steps.howTo:
1. Applications for the next program year usually open in June.
2. There is no need to wait for an offer; funding is released once the school confirms enrolment.
3. Parents usually add their part through the Supporting Users Portal.
4. Applying about 2 months before classes is an estimate that leaves time for funding to arrive.

steps.title: Graduate with the Dogwood Diploma
steps.howTo:
1. The Dogwood is awarded once the 80 credits, required courses, Indigenous-focused credits and 3 graduation assessments are all done.
2. Most students finish in June of Grade 12; move this step to the real date.

steps.title: Keep a copy of the transcript and Dogwood
steps.howTo:
1. The transcript lists Grade 10 to 12 courses and assessment results.
2. Later copies are ordered through the StudentTranscripts Service with a BCeID.

steps.title: Request Educational Assistance Payments from the RESP
conditions: Only if they have an RESP
Only if they enrol in a qualifying post-secondary program
steps.howTo:
1. The subscriber contacts the RESP promoter to request an EAP.
2. The promoter needs official proof of enrolment.
3. Full-time programs in Canada must run at least 3 weeks in a row with at least 10 hours a week.
4. EAPs are taxable income for the student and can be paid up to 6 months after enrolment ends.

title: Secondary school · 中考 and 高考 · China
summary: Junior middle school, the 中考, senior high school, the gaokao and university enrolment in mainland China. Exams and admissions are run by each province or city; dates assume junior middle school starts in September of the year they turn 12.
conditions: For a young person going through junior and senior secondary school in mainland China
Exam subjects, dates and admission rules are set by the province or city where they study

steps.title: Enrol in junior middle school (初中)
documents: Enrolment notice from the school or district
steps.howTo:
1. Junior middle school is the last part of 9 years of compulsory education (义务教育); public schools admit without an entrance exam, near where the child lives.
2. The local education bureau sets the enrolment dates, the documents and which school serves which address.
3. Children start school at 6; how the 9 years split between primary and junior middle school varies by place, so check locally.
4. This date assumes junior middle school starts in September of the year they turn 12 and is an estimate.

steps.title: Start junior middle school (Grade 7, 初一)
prepare: Name of the class teacher (班主任)
steps.howTo:
1. The school year starts in September.
2. The student status record (学籍) follows the student and is checked later for exam registration.

steps.title: Keep the comprehensive quality evaluation record (综合素质评价)
steps.howTo:
1. The record covers moral character, academic achievement, physical and mental health, arts, and social practice.
2. Senior high schools use it as a basis or reference for admission; each place sets how.
3. Sports and arts talents are recorded here rather than earning extra exam points.

steps.title: Check the conditions for sitting the 中考 without a local hukou (随迁子女)
prepare: Parents' proof of stable work and home (including a lease)
Years of schooling in the city
conditions: Only if their household registration (户口) is outside the city where they go to school
steps.howTo:
1. Each province sets the conditions for children of migrant workers to sit exams where they live.
2. The national guideline lists the factors: the parents' stable job, stable home (renting counts) and years of social insurance, and the child's years of continuous schooling there.
3. Those who don't qualify return to the hukou province for the exam; some cities offer a borrowed exam seat (借考).
4. Check the education bureau's rules early in Grade 9 at the latest; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Register for the 中考 (中考报名)
prepare: Resident ID card or household register
steps.howTo:
1. Registration usually goes through the school; the city or province sets the dates.
2. This date assumes the winter of Grade 9 and is an estimate.

steps.title: Take the PE test counted in the 中考 (体育考试)
prepare: Event choices, if the city offers them
steps.howTo:
1. National policy puts PE among the subjects counted for senior high school admission.
2. The events, points and dates are set locally.
3. This date assumes spring of Grade 9 and is an estimate.

steps.title: Sit the junior secondary academic proficiency tests (初中学业水平考试)
steps.howTo:
1. The tests cover the subjects in the national curriculum; the results are the basis for junior middle school graduation.
2. Some subjects may be tested before Grade 9; the province decides.
3. This date assumes the end of Grade 9 and is an estimate.

steps.title: Sit the senior high school entrance exam (中考)
prepare: Resident ID card or other ID the exam office names
steps.howTo:
1. In most places the 中考 is the admission part of the proficiency tests: besides Chinese, maths and a foreign language, the province picks which other subjects count.
2. In many places the two are one sitting.
3. The city or province sets the dates, often near the end of Grade 9; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Choose and submit senior high school choices (志愿填报)
prepare: Past admission scores of target schools
steps.howTo:
1. Graduates go on to either a general senior high school (普通高中) or a secondary vocational school (中等职业学校); both admit through the 中考.
2. Each place plans how many places go to general and vocational schools, and part of the places at top schools are set aside for each junior middle school (名额分配).
3. Some cities collect choices before the exam, some after the scores; follow the local timetable.
4. This date is an estimate.

steps.title: Receive the admission result and enrol in senior high school
prepare: Documents the school lists for enrolment
steps.howTo: 1. Admission results and enrolment dates are published by the city; this date assumes July and is an estimate.

steps.title: Start senior high school (Grade 10, 高一)
documents: Senior high school student status (学籍)
steps.howTo:
1. Senior high school (高中) is usually 3 years, from Grade 10 to Grade 12.
2. The school year starts in September.

steps.title: Choose gaokao elective subjects (选科): 3+1+2 or 3+3
prepare: Subject requirements of target universities and majors
steps.howTo:
1. Under the "new gaokao" the score is Chinese, maths and a foreign language from the national exam, plus elective subjects from the senior secondary proficiency tests; there is no arts/science split.
2. 3+3 (the first reform provinces, such as Shanghai and Zhejiang): any 3 of politics, history, geography, physics, chemistry and biology.
3. 3+1+2 (most other reform provinces): physics or history first, then 2 of chemistry, biology, politics and geography.
4. By 2022, 29 provinces had started the reform; the last batch was set to sit its first new gaokao in 2025. Check the province's current plan.
5. Universities publish the subjects each major needs; check them before choosing.
6. Schools usually ask for the choice during Grade 10 or early Grade 11; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Sit the senior secondary academic proficiency tests (高中学业水平考试)
steps.howTo:
1. The tests cover every subject in the national curriculum and are a key basis for graduation and admission.
2. The province runs them and sets when each subject is sat.
3. Where offered, a subject can be sat twice.
4. This date assumes the end of Grade 11 and is an estimate.

steps.title: Check gaokao eligibility where they live without a local hukou (异地高考)
prepare: Parents' proof of stable work and home
Years of high school study and student status (学籍) in the province
conditions: Only if their household registration (户口) is in a different province from their high school
steps.howTo:
1. Each province sets whether and how non-hukou students can sit the gaokao there, based on the parents' work, home and social insurance and the student's years of schooling.
2. Those who don't qualify go back to the hukou province to register and sit the exam.
3. Provinces check hukou and student status closely to prevent "gaokao migration".
4. Check by Grade 11; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Register for the gaokao (高考报名)
prepare: Valid resident ID card (居民身份证)
Household register and student status details
steps.howTo:
1. Registration is run by the provincial examinations authority, usually online in October or November of the year before the exam.
2. Examples for the 2026 exam: Hunan ran it from October 16 to 31, 2025, with no late registration.
3. The ID card has to be valid; Hunan asked candidates with an expired card to renew it before the check.
4. Arts and sports candidates have extra registration steps.
5. This date assumes November of Grade 12 and is an estimate.

steps.title: Sit the gaokao (普通高考) in early June
prepare: ID named by the provincial exam office
steps.howTo:
1. The national exam is held on June 7 and 8; in some provinces other subjects run on June 9 and 10.
2. Phones, smart watches and other devices that send or receive data count as cheating if taken into the room.
3. Move this step to June 7 of the exam year.

steps.title: Check results and submit university choices (志愿填报)
prepare: Past admission ranks of target universities
Each university's admission rules (招生章程)
steps.howTo:
1. Each province publishes the results date and the official way to check scores, usually in the second half of June.
2. Choices are submitted online in the province's system within the window it sets.
3. The province decides the matching model: parallel choices (平行志愿, by score rank) or sequential choices.
4. The Sunshine Gaokao platform (gaokao.chsi.com.cn) lists universities, plans and admission rules.
5. This date is an estimate; follow the provincial window.

steps.title: Track admission and receive the admission letter (录取通知书)
steps.howTo:
1. Admission runs online by province, usually from early July to the end of August.
2. Universities usually post admission letters about a week after each batch closes.
3. If the result shows online but no letter arrives, call the university's admissions line.
4. This date is an estimate.

steps.title: Apply for a national student loan (国家助学贷款)
prepare: Resident ID cards of student and parent
conditions: Only if the family needs help with tuition and accommodation
steps.howTo:
1. The student-origin credit loan (生源地信用助学贷款) is applied for at the student aid office of the county where the student's hukou is, before entering university.
2. Student and parent or guardian sign as co-borrowers; no collateral is needed.
3. Example: in 2025 Shenzhen asked new students to fill in the form in the China Development Bank loan system and then sign in person with the admission letter, ID and household register.
4. Amounts and windows change each year; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Gather the university enrolment documents
steps.howTo:
1. The admission letter pack lists what the university wants at registration.
2. Follow the pack for the student file (档案) and any hukou transfer.

steps.title: Register at university
steps.howTo: 1. Universities set their own registration dates, usually early to mid-September; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: HPV vaccine for girls at 13 (national immunization program)
conditions: Only for girls
prepare: Ask the school or community vaccination clinic for the schedule
steps.howTo:
1. The 2026 national immunization schedule adds the bivalent HPV vaccine for girls aged 13, 2 doses, free.
2. Local rollout and whether it is given at school or at the clinic differ; check with the local clinic.
3. Move this to the appointment date.

steps.title: Join student medical insurance at university
conditions: Only if they start university
prepare: The university's enrolment notice for medical insurance
steps.howTo:
1. University students usually join resident medical insurance through the university, in the city where it is.
2. They can instead stay insured where the hukou is; avoid paying twice, and ask how cross-region care works either way.
3. It is paid yearly, usually in the autumn term.

title: High school · Grades 9–12 · Ontario
summary: Diploma requirements, key tests and post-secondary applications for a teen going through an Ontario public high school. Dates assume Grade 9 starts around age 14.
conditions: For a young person attending high school in Ontario, Grades 9 to 12
Working towards the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD)

steps.title: Choose Grade 9 courses with the Grade 8 teacher
steps.howTo:
1. Course selection for Grade 9 usually happens in the winter of Grade 8; schools set their own dates.
2. Most students start Grade 9 in September of the year they turn 14, so move this step to the real date.
3. For students who started Grade 9 in 2024 or later, 1 technological education credit is compulsory in Grade 9 or 10.

steps.title: Start a log of community involvement hours
prepare: Supervisor name and contact for each activity
steps.howTo:
1. The diploma needs at least 40 hours of community involvement (volunteering).
2. Hours can be collected from the summer before Grade 9.
3. Each board publishes its own form and list of eligible activities; get supervisors to sign as you go.

steps.title: Start Grade 9
steps.howTo: 1. The school year starts in September, the year the student turns 14 in most cases.

steps.title: Map out the 30 credits and 2 online credits
steps.howTo:
1. The OSSD needs 30 credits: 17 compulsory and 13 optional for students who started Grade 9 in 2024 or later; 18 and 12 for earlier starters.
2. At least 2 credits must be online learning credits; opting out is possible, and the student can opt out themselves at 18.
3. Other requirements: 40 community hours and the literacy requirement.

steps.title: Write the Ontario Secondary School Literacy Test
steps.howTo:
1. Students usually write the OSSLT in Grade 10, their second year of high school.
2. The school sets the date; this due date is an estimate.
3. Passing it meets the diploma literacy requirement.

steps.title: Take the literacy course (OSSLC) instead
conditions: Only if they have had two chances at the OSSLT and were unsuccessful at least once
steps.howTo:
1. The Ontario Secondary School Literacy Course meets the literacy requirement for students eligible under the EQAO rule.
2. Ask the school about other ways to meet the requirement too.

steps.title: Complete Grade 10 Career Studies
prepare: Ideas for university, college, apprenticeship or work
steps.howTo:
1. Career Studies (GLC2O) is a compulsory half-credit course taken in Grade 10.
2. Schools run it in either semester; this due date assumes the end of Grade 10.

steps.title: Pass the financial literacy modules in Career Studies
conditions: Only if they started Grade 9 in 2025–26 or later
steps.howTo:
1. Students need at least 70% on the financial literacy modules in Grade 10 Career Studies.
2. There are 2 attempts.
3. The requirement is in place from the 2026–27 school year.

steps.title: Choose Grade 11 courses to keep post-secondary options open
prepare: Programs of interest and their admission prerequisites
steps.howTo:
1. Grades 11 and 12 courses have types: university (U), university/college (M), college (C), workplace (E) and open (O).
2. University and college programs list specific Grade 12 U or M courses as prerequisites, which need Grade 11 courses first.
3. Course selection is usually in the winter of Grade 10; schools set their own dates.

steps.title: Choose Grade 12 courses to meet program prerequisites
prepare: Prerequisite list for each program on the shortlist
steps.howTo:
1. Check each program's required Grade 12 courses and minimum marks.
2. Course selection is usually in the winter of Grade 11.

steps.title: Apply for scholarships and awards
steps.howTo:
1. Ask the guidance office for the school's award list.
2. Many universities and colleges consider applicants for entrance awards automatically; others need a separate form.
3. Deadlines vary widely; this date is an estimate for spring of Grade 12.

steps.title: Apply to Ontario universities through OUAC
conditions: Only if they plan to go to university in Ontario
steps.howTo:
1. High school students apply through the OUAC 101 application; the school provides access details.
2. Applications in by mid-January (January 15 for fall 2027) get equal consideration; check the current OUAC deadline.
3. Some programs need supplementary forms or portfolios with their own deadlines.
4. The school sends marks to OUAC; the student does not.

steps.title: Apply to Ontario colleges on ontariocolleges.ca
conditions: Only if they plan to go to college in Ontario
steps.howTo:
1. Applications for the next academic year open in the fall.
2. Apply and pay by February 1 for equal consideration; after that, colleges consider applicants first-come, first-served.
3. Colleges may send offers from November 1; the confirm-by date is May 1.

steps.title: Apply for OSAP
conditions: Only if they need student financial aid for college or university
steps.howTo:
1. The application for the next school year opens in spring at ontario.ca/osap.
2. Processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks once documents are in.
3. Applying at least 2 months before classes is an estimate that lets funding arrive for the first week.

steps.title: Finish and hand in the 40 community involvement hours
steps.howTo:
1. At least 40 hours are needed to graduate.
2. Hand forms in as hours are done rather than all at the end; the school records them.

steps.title: Graduate with the OSSD
steps.howTo:
1. The Minister grants the diploma on the principal's recommendation once all requirements are met.
2. Most students finish in June of Grade 12; move this step to the real date.

steps.title: Keep a copy of the Ontario Student Transcript
steps.howTo:
1. The OST is the official record of all courses and diploma requirements.
2. For a copy later, contact the school or school board.

steps.title: Request Educational Assistance Payments from the RESP
conditions: Only if they have an RESP
Only if they enrol in a qualifying post-secondary program
steps.howTo:
1. The subscriber contacts the RESP promoter to request an EAP.
2. The promoter needs official proof of enrolment.
3. Full-time programs in Canada must run at least 3 weeks in a row with at least 10 hours a week.
4. EAPs are taxable income for the student and can be paid up to 6 months after enrolment ends.

title: Growing up · ages 14–19 · British Columbia
summary: IDs, first job, driving, voting and first accounts from 14 to 19. Federal rules apply across Canada; provincial rules are British Columbia's, where adulthood starts at 19.
conditions: For a young person living in British Columbia, from 14 to 19
Some steps are only for Canadian citizens or residents

steps.title: Check which jobs they can legally do
prepare: Type of workplace and tasks for each job idea
steps.howTo:
1. At 14 and 15: "light work" such as cashier, server of food, lifeguard, tutor, stocking shelves or dishwashing, with a parent's written consent.
2. Other jobs at 14 or 15 also need a permit from the Employment Standards Branch.
3. From 16: no parental consent needed, but construction and silviculture stay off-limits until 16.
4. Under 18: no logging, tree falling, chainsaw work or power line work.

steps.title: Sign the written consent for a first job at 14 or 15
prepare: Job offer with duties and hours
Proof of age for the employer
conditions: Only if they take a job before turning 16
steps.howTo:
1. The employer keeps the parent's written consent and proof of age on file.
2. At 14 and 15 they cannot work during school hours, more than 4 hours on a school day, more than 7 hours on a non-school day, or more than 20 hours in a week with 5 school days.

steps.title: Join the Register of Future Electors
conditions: Only if they are a Canadian citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Canadian citizens aged 14 to 17 living in Canada can sign up with Elections Canada.
2. At 18 they are registered to vote in the next federal election.

steps.title: Apply for a Social Insurance Number
prepare: Primary identity document: birth certificate, citizenship certificate or PR card
Secondary document with name and date of birth, such as a passport
steps.howTo:
1. Anyone 12 or older can apply for their own SIN; a parent can apply for a minor.
2. Apply online, by mail or at a Service Canada office. There is no fee.
3. No card is issued; the number is shown in My Service Canada Account.

steps.title: Get a BCID card as photo ID
prepare: Original ID with legal name and date of birth, such as a birth certificate
A parent or guardian to consent
conditions: Only if they don't have a driver's licence
steps.howTo:
1. Anyone 12 or older can apply at an ICBC driver licensing office.
2. Under 19, a parent or guardian consents to the application.
3. The card is valid for about 5 years, ending on the birthday nearest 5 years from issue.

steps.title: File a first income tax return
conditions: Only once they have earned income, e.g. from a first job
steps.howTo:
1. Returns are due April 30 of the following year; this date assumes income the year they turn 15, so move it to match.
2. Filing gets back tax withheld from pay and records earned income for future RRSP deduction room.
3. Filing every year also sets up the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB, formerly the GST/HST credit), which students can get once they turn 19.

steps.title: Join Elections BC's List of Future Voters
conditions: Only if they are a Canadian citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Canadian citizens who are 16 or 17 and live in BC can sign up online with Elections BC.
2. At 18 they are added to the Provincial Voters List automatically.

steps.title: Get the L learner's licence
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo:
1. The L is available on or after the 16th birthday.
2. Pass a vision screening and a knowledge test: 40 of 50 questions right.
3. Under 19, a parent or guardian signs consent.
4. The L is valid for 2 years; renewing it means passing the knowledge test again.

steps.title: Take an ICBC-approved driver training course
conditions: Only if they want a shorter novice stage
steps.howTo:
1. Finishing an approved course during the L stage, within 365 days of starting it, can cut the 24-month N stage to 18 months.
2. The shorter stage applies only while they stay free of violations and at-fault crashes.

steps.title: Pass the road test for the N novice licence
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo: 1. The road test is allowed after at least 12 months of practice on the L with a qualified supervisor.

steps.title: Check registration and vote
conditions: Only if they are a Canadian citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Canadian citizens 18 or older can vote in federal elections and, once they have lived in BC for 6 months, in BC provincial elections.
2. Check or update federal registration with Elections Canada and provincial registration with Elections BC online.
3. Updating a driver's licence, BCID or BC Services Card address also updates Elections BC.

steps.title: Upgrade to a full Class 5 licence
prepare: Driving record with no prohibitions or suspensions
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo:
1. Drivers under 25 need at least 24 months of safe driving on the N, or 18 months after approved training.
2. From October 19, 2026, a Driving Record Assessment replaces the second road test, followed by a 12-month restriction period.
3. Speeding or phone convictions in that time, or any prohibition or suspension, block the upgrade.
4. This date assumes 24 months; move it 6 months earlier after approved training.

steps.title: Get a photo BC Services Card
documents: Photo BC Services Card or combined driver's licence
prepare: ID documents the letter asks for
conditions: Only if they are enrolled in MSP
steps.howTo:
1. Under 19, MSP issues a non-photo BC Services Card and enrolment doesn't need renewing.
2. Around 18 and a half, Health Insurance BC sends a letter to renew enrolment; the photo card is then issued at an ICBC driver licensing office.
3. Drivers can combine the BC Services Card with their driver's licence.

steps.title: Turn 19: the age of majority in BC
prepare: Talk through contracts, consent and money now in their own name
steps.howTo:
1. In British Columbia a person becomes an adult at 19, a year later than federal ages such as voting at 18.
2. Some contracts, such as a TFSA or a credit card, wait until then.

steps.title: Turn 19: legal age for alcohol and cannabis
prepare: Talk about safe use and never driving impaired
steps.howTo: 1. In BC, 19 is the minimum age to buy, possess or consume non-medical cannabis, the same as for liquor.

steps.title: Get a credit card in their own name
prepare: One document with name and address and one with name and date of birth
Compare no-cost or low-cost student accounts
steps.howTo:
1. Banks need two ID documents from a reliable source, or one plus someone vouching.
2. The primary cardholder of a credit card must be of the age of majority in their province, which is 19 in BC.
3. Purchases as an authorized user on a parent's card don't build their own credit history.

steps.title: Open a TFSA
conditions: Only if they are a resident of Canada
steps.howTo:
1. TFSA room starts building the year they turn 18, if they are a resident of Canada with a valid SIN.
2. In provinces where contracts need age 19, like BC, the account opens at 19 and the room from 18 carries over.
3. Unused room carries forward, so opening later loses nothing.

steps.title: Consider opening an FHSA
conditions: Only if they are a resident of Canada
Only if they are a first-time home buyer
steps.howTo:
1. The FHSA opens at 18, or at 19 where that is the legal age to enter a contract, as in BC.
2. They must not have lived in a home they owned in the current year or the 4 years before.
3. FHSA room only starts once the account is opened, so opening early starts the clock even with no deposit.

steps.title: Apply for the last child passport, around age 15
prepare: Expiry date of the current child passport
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the child has, or needs, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. A child passport, for under 16, is valid for up to 5 years and cannot be renewed; each one is a new application.
2. This date assumes a first passport in the baby's first months; move it to about 2 months before the current one expires, or before travel.
3. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail; check current times.
4. From 16 the application is for an adult passport instead; see the next passport step.
5. Many countries ask for a passport valid 6 months past the return date.

steps.title: Apply for a first adult passport
prepare: Expiry date of the last child passport
conditions: Only if they have, or need, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. From 16, a passport is applied for as an adult, by the young person themselves, with a choice of 5 or 10 years of validity.
2. A child passport issued before 16 stays valid to its expiry, then the first adult passport is a new application, not a renewal.
3. This date assumes a child passport issued at about 15; move it to about 2 months before that one expires, or earlier for travel.
4. Check the current document list, guarantor rules and fees on canada.ca.

title: Growing up · ages 16–22 · China
summary: ID card, adulthood at 18, military service registration, driving, first job, tax and the legal marriage age in mainland China. National rules; local offices set the details.
conditions: For a Chinese citizen living in mainland China, from 16 to 22
Some steps apply only to men, drivers or people with a job

sources.title: Resident Identity Card Law of the PRC (2003 text) — gov.cn
Resident Identity Card Law of the PRC (2011 amendment, fingerprints) — National People's Congress

steps.title: Apply for the resident ID card (居民身份证) at 16
prepare: ID card application form (居民身份证申领登记表)
Old card, if they had one as a child
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Resident ID Card Law, Chinese citizens living in China apply for a card from 16; under 16 it is optional and a guardian applies.
2. The law gives 3 months from the 16th birthday to apply to the police (公安机关) where the hukou is registered.
3. Fingerprints are recorded when applying.
4. Cards issued under 16 are valid for 5 years; from 16 to 25, 10 years; from 26 to 45, 20 years; from 46, long-term.
5. The card is later needed for gaokao registration, bank accounts, phone numbers and driving tests.

steps.title: Turn 18: full civil capacity (完全民事行为能力人)
prepare: Talk through contracts, money and responsibility now in their own name
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Civil Code, a person of 18 or over is an adult with full civil capacity and can enter civil legal acts alone.
2. A 16- or 17-year-old whose main income is their own labour is treated as having full civil capacity too.

steps.title: Check voter registration (选民登记) for local elections
prepare: Where they live or work now
conditions: Only when a direct local people's congress election is held where they live
steps.howTo:
1. Citizens of 18 or over have the right to vote and to stand for election.
2. Deputies to county and township people's congresses are elected directly by voters.
3. Registration is by electoral district and stays valid; before each election the list adds people who have turned 18 since the last one.
4. After moving, ask the local election office where they are registered.

steps.title: Open a bank account in their own name (Class I, Ⅰ类户)
documents: Bank card for a Class I account
prepare: Mobile number in their own name
steps.howTo:
1. Personal accounts come in 3 classes: Class I is opened at a bank counter with an in-person identity check and has full functions.
2. Class II and III accounts can be opened online with limited functions and are linked to a Class I account.
3. One person can hold only one Class I account at each bank.
4. Salary, social insurance, housing provident fund and large transfers go through a Class I account.

steps.title: Get a mobile number in their own name
steps.howTo:
1. Operators ask for a valid ID and register the user's real identity when a number is set up.
2. A number in their own name is used for bank, tax and government app logins.
3. For a number already registered to a parent, ask the operator how to move it.

steps.title: Complete the initial military service registration (兵役登记)
documents: Military service registration certificate (兵役登记证)
prepare: Account on the National Conscription Office site (全国征兵网)
conditions: Only for men
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Military Service Law, men who turn 18 by December 31 do the initial registration that year, as the local military service office arranges.
2. It can be done online or in person at a registration point.
3. The National Conscription Office lists the window as January 1 to October 31; this date assumes the 18th birthday, so move it to fall inside the window of the year they turn 18.
4. Registering is not enlisting; those who want to serve apply separately online.
5. The initial registration is for men; the law lets the army take women into service according to its needs.

steps.title: Join a driving school and pass the theory test (科目一)
prepare: Health check the vehicle office asks for
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo:
1. The small car licence (小型汽车, C1, or automatic, C2) is open from 18.
2. The theory test (科目一) on traffic law is marked out of 100; 90 passes.
3. The vehicle office issues the learner permit within a day of passing; it is valid for 3 years.
4. All subjects have to be passed while the permit is valid, or passed subjects are void.

steps.title: Pass the site test (科目二) and road test (科目三)
prepare: Practice hours with the driving school
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo:
1. For a C1 small car, the site test can be booked 10 days after getting the learner permit and the road test 30 days after (20 days for C2).
2. The site test passes at 80 of 100 for small cars; the road test at 90.
3. Each sitting allows one retake; after failing both, rebook after 10 days.
4. Each of the two tests can be booked at most 5 times while the permit is valid; failing the 5th time voids the other passed subjects.
5. This date is an estimate.

steps.title: Pass the safe driving knowledge test (科目四) and get the licence (机动车驾驶证)
prepare: Practice questions on safe and civil driving
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo:
1. Officially this is the second part of subject 3 (安全文明驾驶常识), commonly called 科目四; it can be sat the same day both driving tests are passed.
2. It is marked out of 100; 90 passes. Failing it keeps the road test pass.
3. The licence can also be held in electronic form on 交管12123.

steps.title: Drive out the 12-month probation period (实习期)
prepare: Put the probation sign on the back of the car
conditions: Only if they drive
steps.howTo:
1. The first 12 months after a first car licence are the probation period, with the standard probation sign on the back of the car.
2. During it: no buses, passenger transport, emergency vehicles or dangerous goods, and no towing a trailer.
3. On an expressway, a driver who has held a covering licence for 3 years or more rides along.
4. Reaching 12 points during probation cancels the licence class.

steps.title: Note the legal marriage age (法定婚龄)
steps.howTo: 1. Under Article 1047 of the Civil Code, men can marry from 22 and women from 20.

steps.title: Check social insurance is set up with the first job (社会保险)
conditions: Only once they start a job with an employer
Only if no Starting a job or After graduation plan is tracking this
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Social Insurance Law, the employer applies for the employee's social insurance registration within 30 days of the start date.
2. Self-employed people and flexible workers can register themselves.
3. This date assumes a first job at about 21; move it to the real start date.
4. The Starting a job · China and After graduation · China plans cover this in more detail; mark this one "Not for me" if one of those is on the board.

steps.title: Check the housing provident fund account is opened (住房公积金)
conditions: Only once they start a job with an employer
Only if no Starting a job or After graduation plan is tracking this
steps.howTo:
1. Under the provident fund regulations, an employer registers a new employee with the housing provident fund centre within 30 days of hiring and opens or transfers their account.
2. This date assumes a first job at about 21; move it to the real start date.
3. The Starting a job · China and After graduation · China plans cover this in more detail; mark this one "Not for me" if one of those is on the board.

steps.title: Register on the individual income tax app (个人所得税)
prepare: Mobile number in their own name
Class I bank card for refunds
conditions: Only once they have earned income, e.g. from a job
Only if no Starting a job or After graduation plan is tracking this
steps.howTo:
1. Employers withhold tax from pay; the app shows income and tax reported under their ID.
2. This date assumes a first job at about 21; move it to the real start date.
3. The Starting a job · China and After graduation · China plans cover this in more detail; mark this one "Not for me" if one of those is on the board.

steps.title: Do the annual income tax reconciliation (年度汇算)
prepare: Special additional deductions (专项附加扣除), if any
conditions: Only once they have earned income, e.g. from a job
Only if no Starting a job or After graduation plan is tracking this
steps.howTo:
1. The reconciliation for a tax year runs from March 1 to June 30 of the following year, in the app.
2. It settles a refund or extra tax; the tax authority sets who is required to file.
3. Early in the window, the app may ask for a booking.
4. This date assumes income the year they turn 21; move it to June 30 of the year after.
5. The Starting a job · China and After graduation · China plans cover this in more detail; mark this one "Not for me" if one of those is on the board.

steps.title: Apply for a first passport and Mainland travel permit for Hong Kong and Macao (护照 / 港澳通行证)
conditions: Only if they plan to travel abroad, or to Hong Kong or Macao
documents: Mainland travel permit for Hong Kong and Macao (往来港澳通行证)
prepare: Photo to the exit-entry photo standard, or taken on site
steps.howTo:
1. Passports and Hong Kong and Macao permits are issued by exit-entry offices (出入境管理) of public security; many cities accept applications from people whose hukou is elsewhere.
2. An adult passport is valid for 10 years; the Hong Kong and Macao permit also needs an endorsement (签注) for each kind of trip.
3. Under 16 a guardian applies, and the passport is valid for 5 years.
4. Processing time is set locally; age 18 here is only a prompt.

title: Growing up · ages 14–19 · Ontario
summary: IDs, first job, driving, voting and first accounts from 14 to 19. Federal rules apply across Canada; provincial rules are Ontario's.
conditions: For a young person living in Ontario, from 14 to 19
Some steps are only for Canadian citizens or residents

Register to vote — Elections Canada

steps.title: Check which jobs they can legally do
prepare: Type of workplace for each job idea
steps.howTo:
1. From 14: offices, stores, arenas and restaurant serving areas.
2. From 15: factories, restaurant kitchens, repair shops, garages, warehouses and laundries.
3. From 16: construction, logging and most surface mining.
4. From 18: underground mines, window cleaning and a few others.
5. Under 16s cannot work during school hours.

steps.title: Join the Register of Future Electors
conditions: Only if they are a Canadian citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Canadian citizens aged 14 to 17 living in Canada can sign up with Elections Canada.
2. At 18 they are registered to vote in the next federal election.

steps.title: Apply for a Social Insurance Number
prepare: Primary identity document: birth certificate, citizenship certificate or PR card
Secondary document with name and date of birth, such as a passport
steps.howTo:
1. Anyone 12 or older can apply for their own SIN; a parent can apply for a minor.
2. Apply online, by mail or at a Service Canada office. There is no fee.
3. No card is issued; the number is shown in My Service Canada Account.

steps.title: File a first income tax return
conditions: Only once they have earned income, e.g. from a first job
steps.howTo:
1. Returns are due April 30 of the following year; this date assumes income the year they turn 15, so move it to match.
2. Filing gets back tax withheld from pay and records earned income for future RRSP deduction room.
3. Filing every year also sets up the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB, formerly the GST/HST credit), which students can get once they turn 19.

steps.title: Renew the health card in person with a photo
prepare: Proof of Ontario residency and identity
conditions: Only if they have an Ontario health card
steps.howTo:
1. Anyone turning 16 must renew their Ontario health card in person at ServiceOntario.
2. A photo and signature are taken then.

steps.title: Get the G1 learner's licence
prepare: Original ID with legal name and date of birth
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo:
1. The minimum age is 16.
2. Pass a vision test and a knowledge test at a DriveTest centre.
3. The whole graduated licensing process must be finished within 5 years or it starts over.

steps.title: Get an Ontario Photo Card as ID
prepare: Original ID with legal name and date of birth, such as a birth certificate
conditions: Only if they don't have a driver's licence
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario residents 16 or older without a driver's licence can apply in person at ServiceOntario.
2. The card is valid for 5 years.

steps.title: Take a government-approved beginner driver education course
conditions: Only if they want to take the G2 road test sooner
steps.howTo: 1. Finishing an approved course lets them take the first road test after 8 months with a G1 instead of 12.

steps.title: Pass the G2 road test
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo:
1. The first road test is allowed after 12 months with a G1, or after 8 months with approved driver education.
2. This date assumes 12 months; move it 4 months earlier after driver education.

steps.title: Pass the G road test for a full licence
conditions: Only if they want to drive
steps.howTo: 1. The G test is allowed after 12 months with a G2.

steps.title: Turn 18: the age of majority in Ontario
prepare: Talk through contracts, consent and money now in their own name
steps.howTo: 1. In Ontario a person stops being a minor and becomes an adult at 18.

steps.title: Open a bank account and credit card in their own name
prepare: One document with name and address and one with name and date of birth
Compare no-cost or low-cost student accounts
steps.howTo:
1. Banks need two ID documents from a reliable source, or one plus someone vouching.
2. The primary cardholder of a credit card must be of the age of majority in their province.
3. Purchases as an authorized user on a parent's card don't build their own credit history.

steps.title: Check registration and vote
conditions: Only if they are a Canadian citizen
steps.howTo:
1. Canadian citizens 18 or older can vote in federal elections.
2. Check or update registration with Elections Canada's online service; the tax return can also update it.

steps.title: Open a TFSA
conditions: Only if they are a resident of Canada
steps.howTo:
1. Residents of Canada with a valid SIN start building TFSA room the year they turn 18.
2. Unused room carries forward, so opening later loses nothing.

steps.title: Consider opening an FHSA
conditions: Only if they are a resident of Canada
Only if they are a first-time home buyer
steps.howTo:
1. They must be 18 or older and a resident of Canada.
2. They must not have lived in a home they owned in the current year or the 4 years before.
3. FHSA room only starts once the account is opened, so opening early starts the clock even with no deposit.

steps.title: Turn 19: legal age for alcohol and cannabis
prepare: Talk about safe use and never driving impaired
steps.howTo: 1. In Ontario, 19 is the minimum age to buy, use or possess recreational cannabis, the same as for alcohol and tobacco.

steps.title: Apply for the last child passport, around age 15
prepare: Expiry date of the current child passport
Guarantor who has known you 2 years and knows the child
conditions: Only if the child has, or needs, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. A child passport, for under 16, is valid for up to 5 years and cannot be renewed; each one is a new application.
2. This date assumes a first passport in the baby's first months; move it to about 2 months before the current one expires, or before travel.
3. Standard processing is 10 to 20 business days plus mail; check current times.
4. From 16 the application is for an adult passport instead; see the next passport step.
5. Many countries ask for a passport valid 6 months past the return date.

steps.title: Apply for a first adult passport
prepare: Expiry date of the last child passport
conditions: Only if they have, or need, a Canadian passport
steps.howTo:
1. From 16, a passport is applied for as an adult, by the young person themselves, with a choice of 5 or 10 years of validity.
2. A child passport issued before 16 stays valid to its expiry, then the first adult passport is a new application, not a renewal.
3. This date assumes a child passport issued at about 15; move it to about 2 months before that one expires, or earlier for travel.
4. Check the current document list, guarantor rules and fees on canada.ca.

title: After graduation · Canada
summary: Paperwork around finishing college or university in Canada: graduation and transcripts, student loan repayment, health coverage, tax credits, and the Post-Graduation Work Permit for international graduates. Dates count from convocation.
conditions: You are finishing a program at a Canadian college, polytechnic or university
Loan, RESP and permit steps apply only to those who have them
This is a planning aid, not financial or immigration advice; the government pages and your school are the reference

sources.title: Repaying your student loan — Canada.ca

Repayment Assistance Plan — Canada.ca
National Student Loans Service Centre (NSLSC)

Post-graduation work permit: How to apply — Canada.ca

steps.title: Apply to graduate
prepare: Degree audit or program check from the registrar
Name exactly as it should appear on the parchment
Outstanding fees or library fines cleared
steps.howTo:
1. Most schools ask students to apply to graduate through the student portal, a few months before convocation.
2. The registrar checks the program requirements; holds for unpaid fees can block the parchment and transcripts.
3. Deadlines are set by each school; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Take a language test for the PGWP
documents: Language test results (IELTS, CELPIP, TEF, TCF or PTE Core)
prepare: Book a test date with an approved test provider
conditions: Only if you studied on a study permit and plan to apply for a PGWP
steps.howTo:
1. PGWP applications include results from an approved language test.
2. IRCC lists the levels: CLB or NCLC 7 in all four skills for a university degree, CLB or NCLC 5 for a college or other program.
3. Results are valid for 2 years from the test date and must be valid when the application is submitted.
4. Check the current rules on the PGWP eligibility page.

steps.title: Check the study permit expiry and status after studies
prepare: Expected date final marks are released
conditions: Only if you studied on a study permit
steps.howTo:
1. A study permit usually stops being valid 90 days after the program is completed, or on its expiry date if that comes first.
2. Applying for a PGWP while the study permit is still valid keeps the right to stay under maintained status until IRCC decides.
3. If the study permit expires first, a visitor record or leaving Canada are the options IRCC lists.

steps.title: Get the completion letter and final transcript
steps.howTo:
1. Once final marks are in, the registrar issues an official completion letter and a final transcript showing the credential was granted.
2. The date on the completion confirmation starts the 180-day PGWP window.
3. Employers and other schools often ask for official transcripts sent directly by the registrar.
4. Release dates depend on the school; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Receive the degree parchment
prepare: Mailing address if the parchment is mailed
steps.howTo:
1. The parchment is handed out at convocation or mailed afterwards.
2. Keep it flat and safe; replacements are slow and cost a fee.
3. Certified copies are often used instead of the original for applications.

steps.title: Order official transcripts and copies
prepare: List of employers, schools or licensing bodies that ask for them
steps.howTo:
1. Registrars send official transcripts on paper or electronically, often straight to the recipient.
2. Professional licensing bodies and graduate schools usually ask for transcripts sent directly by the school.
3. A few spare sealed copies can save time later.

steps.title: Confirm the student loan account at the NSLSC
prepare: Last day of studies as the school reported it
Current mailing address, email and phone
conditions: Only if you have Canada Student Loans or provincial student loans
steps.howTo:
1. Loans enter a 6-month non-repayment period after the final term ends or studies drop to part-time.
2. In B.C., Ontario and most provinces, the federal and provincial parts are managed together at the NSLSC; Alberta, Nova Scotia and P.E.I. loans are repaid separately, and Quebec, Nunavut and the Northwest Territories are handled by the province or territory.
3. The federal part has been interest-free since April 2023; a provincial part may still build interest, so check the terms in the account.
4. A repayment schedule arrives within the 6 months.

steps.title: Replace the student health and dental plan
prepare: End date of the student plan coverage
Employer benefits start date, if any
Provincial health insurance status (MSP in B.C., OHIP in Ontario)
steps.howTo:
1. Student health and dental plans usually run to the end of the term or policy year the fee was paid for; the school's plan office has the exact end date.
2. Some student plans offer a short graduate extension or a conversion plan without medical questions, applied for within a set time.
3. Provincial coverage (MSP, OHIP and others) covers doctor and hospital care, not usually dental or most drugs.
4. International graduates: eligibility for provincial coverage on a work permit differs by province; check with the province.
5. The date is an estimate for a spring convocation.

steps.title: Take any last RESP education payments
documents: Proof of enrolment for the last term
conditions: Only if you are the beneficiary of an RESP with money left in it
steps.howTo:
1. Educational assistance payments (EAPs) can still be paid for up to 6 months after enrolment in a qualifying program ends.
2. EAPs are taxable income for the student, who often pays little or no tax on them.
3. After that window, the grant portion goes back to the government and the options change; the RESP provider explains them.
4. The due date counts roughly from the last day of studies; move it to match.

steps.title: Apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)
prepare: Official completion letter and final transcript
conditions: Only if you studied on a study permit at an eligible institution
steps.howTo:
1. The PGWP is applied for online within 180 days of the confirmation that the program was completed.
2. The study permit has to have been valid at some point in those 180 days.
3. Applying while the study permit is still valid gives maintained status, and graduates who met the off-campus work conditions can work full-time while waiting.
4. Field-of-study requirements apply to some college programs for students who applied for their study permit on or after 1 November 2024.
5. The due date is an estimate; count 180 days from the date on the completion letter.

steps.title: Make the first student loan payment
conditions: Only if you have Canada Student Loans or provincial student loans
steps.howTo:
1. Payments start in the 7th month after studies end, on the date in the repayment schedule.
2. Payments can be made through the NSLSC account; loans repaid to a province separately follow that province's schedule.
3. The due date is an estimate; set it to the date in the schedule.

steps.title: Apply for the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP)
conditions: Only if the monthly student loan payment is hard to afford
steps.howTo:
1. RAP sets an affordable payment based on family income and size; below set income levels the payment can be zero for 6 months.
2. The loan has to be in repayment and the borrower living in Canada.
3. RAP is applied for online through the NSLSC or on paper, and renewed every 6 months.
4. Provincial loans managed separately have their own repayment help.

steps.title: Claim tuition amounts on the tax return
prepare: T2202 from the school's student portal (issued by the end of February)
Unused tuition amounts from the last notice of assessment
Student loan interest paid in the year, if any
steps.howTo:
1. Tuition fees on the T2202 are claimed on Schedule 11.
2. Unused tuition amounts carry forward with no time limit and are used once there is tax to reduce; the notice of assessment shows the balance.
3. Up to $5,000 of the current year's federal amount can be transferred to a parent, grandparent or spouse instead.
4. Interest paid on government student loans can be claimed on line 31900 or carried forward up to 5 years.
5. Provinces set their own tuition credits; some, such as Ontario, ended new provincial tuition credits but still let earlier amounts carry forward.
6. The return is due by 30 April; this date is an estimate for a spring convocation.

steps.title: Update the SIN record with the new permit
conditions: Only if you have a SIN starting with 9 and received a PGWP
steps.howTo:
1. A SIN starting with 9 expires on the same date as the permit it was issued with.
2. After a new permit is issued, the SIN record is updated online, by mail or at a Service Canada office.
3. Employers ask for the updated expiry date.

steps.title: Check the timing for the Canadian Experience Class
documents: Record of skilled work hours in Canada
prepare: Start date of full-time skilled work
conditions: Only if you hold a PGWP and plan to apply for permanent residence
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Experience Class counts at least 1 year, or 1,560 hours, of skilled paid work in Canada (TEER 0 to 3) in the 3 years before applying.
2. Work done while a full-time student, including co-op terms, does not count.
3. A PGWP cannot be extended, so its expiry date sets the time available.
4. The Express Entry steps are in the Skilled migration · CA plan.

title: After graduation · China
summary: Graduation (毕业) paperwork for a graduate of a university in mainland China: the employment agreement, destination registration, certificates and CHSI records, the personal file, household registration and student loan repayment. Dates count from the graduation date.
conditions: For a graduate of a regular higher education institution (普通高校) in mainland China
Archive, household registration and loan rules are set by the school, the province and the receiving city; check them locally

sources.title: Notice on further improving employment for college graduates and young people (国办发〔2022〕13号) — gov.cn
National graduate destination registration system (全国高校毕业生毕业去向登记系统) — NCSS
National university graduate employment service platform (国家大学生就业服务平台) — NCSS
Higher education qualification check (学历查询) — CHSI
Student-origin credit student loan guide (Shenzhen example, 2025) — Shenzhen Education Bureau

National Social Insurance Public Service Platform (国家社会保险公共服务平台)
