Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
National Healthcare Security Administration

steps.title: Sign the employment agreement (三方协议 / 就业协议书)
prepare: Blank agreement from the school's career centre, or its online version
Terms on archive and household registration handling, if the employer offers them
conditions: Only if you accepted a job offer before graduation
steps.howTo:
1. The agreement is signed by the student, the employer and the school; it records the job before the labour contract (劳动合同) is signed.
2. Many schools now handle it online; the career centre explains the steps and how to cancel (解约) if plans change.
3. The labour contract signed after starting work is the document that governs the job itself.
4. Timing depends on the hiring season; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Confirm the student loan before leaving school (毕业确认)
documents: Graduation confirmation in the student loan system
prepare: Login for the loan system (e.g. China Development Bank's 学生在线服务系统)
Current phone number and a contact person
conditions: Only if you have a national student loan (国家助学贷款)
steps.howTo:
1. Before leaving school, graduates with a national student loan confirm their graduation details and repayment plan in the lender's online system; the school's student aid office sets the deadline.
2. Up-to-date contact details keep repayment notices from being missed.
3. Interest is paid by the government while the student is in school.

steps.title: Register the graduation destination (毕业去向登记)
prepare: Employment agreement or labour contract, if employed
Admission letter, if going on to further study
Address for the personal file (档案) and household registration
steps.howTo:
1. From 2023 the employment report certificate (就业报到证) is no longer issued, and the reissue and redirection (改派) procedures for it ended.
2. Graduates instead register where they are going through the school, recorded in the national destination registration system (dj.ncss.cn).
3. The diploma and the labour contract (or employment agreement) now serve for hiring, household registration and archive transfer.
4. The school sets the deadline; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Complete leaving procedures (离校手续)
documents: Leaving clearance form or online record
prepare: Library books returned and fees paid
steps.howTo:
1. Schools run a clearance process before handing over certificates, often online.
2. Unpaid fees can hold back the certificates.
3. Dates are set by the school.

steps.title: Collect the graduation and degree certificates (毕业证 / 学位证)
prepare: Authorisation letter if someone collects them for you
steps.howTo:
1. The graduation certificate records the completed programme (学历); the degree certificate records the degree (学位), which has its own requirements.
2. Lost originals are not reissued; the school can issue a certificate of proof (证明书) instead.
3. Scan both and keep the originals safe.

steps.title: Transfer Party membership records (党组织关系转接)
prepare: Name of the receiving Party organisation
Contact at the school's Party branch
conditions: Only if you are a Party member or probationary member
steps.howTo:
1. The school's Party branch transfers the membership records to the employer's organisation or the local one where you live, usually online.
2. The branch sets the timing, usually around graduation; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Check the records on CHSI (学信网)
documents: Online verification report for the qualification (学历证书电子注册备案表)
Online verification report for the degree
prepare: CHSI account (学信档案) linked to the resident ID card
steps.howTo:
1. CHSI (chsi.com.cn), run for the Ministry of Education, records the qualification once the school registers the certificate electronically.
2. The online registration record and verification reports are downloaded from the 学信档案 account, in Chinese or with an English translation, and verified online for free while valid.
3. Degree records can also be checked there.
4. Employers and overseas credential checks often ask for these reports.
5. Registration takes some weeks after graduation; this date is an estimate.

steps.title: Have the personal file transferred (档案转递)
documents: Archive transfer tracking number or receipt
prepare: Receiving agency's acceptance terms, if any
steps.howTo:
1. The school sends the personal file (档案) by confidential mail (机要) or another official channel; graduates do not usually carry it themselves.
2. Under the 2022 State Council notice, it goes to the employer for Party and government organs, state-owned enterprises and public institutions, or directed-placement students; otherwise to the public employment and talent service agency (公共就业人才服务机构) where the graduate works or is registered.
3. Graduates without a job often can leave it at the school for a period; the school sets the terms.
4. This date is an estimate.

steps.title: Confirm the personal file arrived (报到)
prepare: Resident ID card and graduation certificate
steps.howTo:
1. The receiving employer or talent service agency confirms receipt; many cities let you check online or through a government app.
2. Without the old report certificate, registering with the agency (报到) uses the graduation certificate and the labour contract.
3. A file that stays lost is hard to rebuild, so the check is worth doing early.

steps.title: Move the collective household registration (集体户口迁出)
documents: Migration certificate (户口迁移证) or cross-province move record
prepare: Labour contract, if settling where you work
Acceptance for settlement (准迁证) from the new place, if needed
conditions: Only if your household registration (户口) moved to the school's collective household
steps.howTo:
1. Students who moved their hukou to the school are on its collective household (集体户口) and move out after graduation.
2. Graduates can settle where they work, or return to their home registration, using the graduation certificate and the labour contract or employment agreement.
3. Many places let graduates without a job keep the hukou at the school for a limited time; the school and local police set the deadline.
4. Cross-province moves can often be handled in one trip at the new place.
5. This date is an estimate.

steps.title: Start social insurance with the first employer (社保)
conditions: Only if you start a job with an employer
steps.howTo:
1. The employer registers new staff for social insurance (pension, medical, unemployment, work injury and maternity).
2. Contributions can be checked on the national social insurance platform or a local app.
3. The job plan covers the first-job steps in more detail.
4. This date is an estimate based on a start soon after graduation.

steps.title: Open the housing provident fund account (公积金)
conditions: Only if you start a job with an employer
steps.howTo:
1. Employers open or transfer a housing provident fund account (住房公积金) for new staff and pay contributions matched by the employee.
2. The fund can later be used for buying a home or rent, under local rules.
3. Contributions can be checked with the local housing fund centre.

steps.title: Pay the first student loan interest
prepare: Bank card or account linked for repayment
Amount due from the loan system
conditions: Only if you have a national student loan (国家助学贷款)
steps.howTo:
1. After graduation the government stops paying the interest, and the graduate pays it.
2. The grace period (还本宽限期) is up to 5 years, during which only interest is paid.
3. The lender sets the repayment date each year; check it in the loan system, since this date is an estimate.
4. Missed payments are reported to the credit reference system (征信).

steps.title: Start repaying the student loan principal
prepare: Repayment schedule from the loan system
conditions: Only if you have a national student loan (国家助学贷款)
steps.howTo:
1. Principal repayments begin after the grace period ends; early repayment is allowed.
2. The loan term is the length of study plus 15 years, up to 22 years.
3. The due date assumes the full 5-year grace period; set it to the date in the repayment plan.

steps.title: Check the one-off job-search subsidy (一次性求职创业补贴)
conditions: Only if you are from a low-income family, hold a student loan, have a disability or meet another listed group
prepare: Proof of the family situation or disability
steps.howTo:
1. Final-year students in listed groups can get a one-off job-search subsidy; the amount and groups are set by each province.
2. Applications usually go through the school in the autumn or early in the final year.
3. Ask the school employment office for the local window.

steps.title: Check graduate hukou settlement and talent subsidies in the job city (应届生落户 / 人才补贴)
conditions: Only if you plan to work in a city other than your hukou city
steps.howTo:
1. Many cities let new graduates settle their hukou (落户) and pay rent, living or housing subsidies (人才补贴) within a set time after graduating.
2. Conditions often include degree, age, a local job and local social insurance; some count "new graduate" (应届生) status for up to 2 years.
3. Check the city's human resources bureau before accepting an offer; the hukou step later covers the move itself.

steps.title: Move from student medical insurance to employee or resident insurance
prepare: When the student insurance ends, often the end of the year you graduate
steps.howTo:
1. Student medical insurance through the university usually covers you until the end of its insurance year.
2. A job brings employee medical insurance through the employer; without one, enrol in resident medical insurance (城乡居民医保) where your hukou or residence permit is, or pay as a flexible worker.
3. Enrolling late can bring a waiting period before costs are covered; the waiting period is set locally.

steps.title: Register as unemployed if no job yet (失业登记)
conditions: Only if you have no job after graduating
steps.howTo:
1. Graduates without a job can register as unemployed with the public employment service where their hukou or residence is, often online.
2. It opens job referrals, training, internships (就业见习) and some subsidies; it is separate from unemployment insurance benefits.
3. The registration is cancelled once you find work.

title: Starting a job · Canada

conditions: You are starting a job as an employee in Canada, your first or a new one
Employment standards are provincial; British Columbia and Ontario are described, other provinces have their own
Some steps apply only to work permit holders or to someone leaving another job

steps.title: Get a new permit before working for a new employer
documents: New work permit or IRCC work authorization
prepare: New employer's LMIA or offer of employment number
conditions: Only if you hold an employer-specific (closed) work permit and are changing employers
steps.howTo:
1. An employer-specific permit covers only the employer named on it; working for another employer needs a new permit or an authorization from IRCC first.
2. The new employer may need an LMIA, or an offer of employment submitted in the IRCC Employer Portal for LMIA-exempt jobs.
3. IRCC's "changing jobs or employers" page describes when you can request authorization to work while the application is processed; check current.
4. The 90 days here is an estimate; move it to match the planned start date.

steps.title: Check the job fits your work permit
prepare: Employer name, job title and location on the permit, if it names them
conditions: Only if you work in Canada on a work permit
steps.howTo:
1. An employer-specific work permit names the employer and usually the job and location; a different employer means a new permit first.
2. An open work permit covers most employers, with some exceptions listed on the permit.
3. The permit expiry sets how long the job can run on it.
4. IRCC is the reference; this is not immigration advice.

steps.title: Check your SIN expiry matches the permit
conditions: Only if your SIN starts with 9 (temporary residents)
steps.howTo:
1. A SIN starting with 9 carries the same expiry date as the work permit.
2. After a permit renewal, Service Canada updates the SIN expiry; an employer can ask to see the new date.
3. Renewing the permit before it expires keeps maintained status while waiting.

steps.title: Read the offer letter or employment contract
documents: Signed offer letter or employment contract
steps.howTo:
1. The offer or contract sets pay, hours, duties, probation and benefits start dates.
2. A contract can give more than provincial employment standards, not less.
3. Keep a signed copy; it is the reference later for probation, benefits and notice.

steps.title: Cover health and dental between jobs
prepare: Last day of the old plan's coverage
conditions: Only if you are leaving a job with health or dental benefits, or the new job has none
steps.howTo:
1. Group coverage usually ends on the last day of work or the end of that month; new plans often have a waiting period.
2. Some insurers offer a conversion or individual plan within a short window after group coverage ends, often around 30 to 60 days; check the booklet.
3. The Canadian Dental Care Plan is for people with no access to dental insurance, adjusted family net income under $90,000, tax returns filed and Canadian tax residency; check current.
4. Provincial health cover (MSP, OHIP) continues regardless of the job.

steps.title: Give your Social Insurance Number to the employer
steps.howTo:
1. Under the SIN Code of Practice, a new employee gives the SIN to the employer no later than 3 days after starting.
2. Without a SIN yet, work can begin: apply within those 3 days and give the number within 3 days of receiving it.
3. Applying is free, online, in person at Service Canada, or by mail.

steps.title: Fill in the TD1 federal and provincial forms
documents: TD1 for your province or territory
prepare: Credits you can claim: tuition, disability, dependants
Other jobs held at the same time
steps.howTo:
1. The federal TD1 and the provincial TD1 (TD1BC in British Columbia, TD1ON in Ontario) tell the employer how much tax to withhold.
2. Without them, the employer withholds using the basic personal amount only.
3. Someone with two jobs usually claims the credits at one of them only.
4. A new form is filed when credits change; Quebec has its own provincial form.

steps.title: Set up direct deposit for pay
documents: Void cheque or direct deposit form
steps.howTo:
1. Employers usually ask for a void cheque or the bank's direct deposit form.
2. Most banks produce the form in online banking.

steps.title: Note probation and your province's employment standards
steps.howTo:
1. Minimum wage, overtime, vacation, leaves and termination notice come from the province's employment standards law; federally regulated jobs (banks, airlines, telecoms) follow the Canada Labour Code.
2. British Columbia (Employment Standards Act): after 3 consecutive months of work, the employer owes written notice or compensation for length of service on ending the job, with exceptions such as just cause.
3. Ontario (Employment Standards Act, 2000): after 3 months of continuous employment, notice or termination pay applies, with exceptions.
4. A probation clause in the contract does not remove these minimums.
5. Other provinces publish their own rules; the province's employment standards site is the reference.

steps.title: Check the Record of Employment from the previous job
conditions: Only if you left another job
steps.howTo:
1. The previous employer issues an ROE whenever earnings stop; electronic ROEs are due within 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period in which the job ended.
2. ROEs can be viewed and printed in My Service Canada Account.
3. It matters for any EI claim; errors are fixed by asking the previous employer for an amended ROE.

steps.title: Check your first pay stub
prepare: CRA Payroll Deductions Online Calculator, to compare
steps.howTo:
1. Deductions usually shown: CPP contributions, EI premiums and income tax (federal and provincial); Quebec shows QPP and QPIP instead.
2. CPP stops for the year once earnings pass the yearly maximum, plus a second tier (CPP2) above it; EI stops at its own maximum.
3. Benefit premiums, pension or RRSP contributions and union dues may also appear.
4. Errors are easiest to fix with payroll early in the year.

steps.title: Decide what to do with the old employer's pension and group RRSP
documents: Termination statement from the pension plan
prepare: Commuted value and deferred pension figures
conditions: Only if you left another job with a pension plan or group RRSP
steps.howTo:
1. A registered pension plan usually sends a statement of options after you leave, with a deadline to choose.
2. Common options: leave it as a deferred pension, transfer the commuted value to a locked-in account (LIRA, or LIRA-like account under provincial pension law), or move it to the new employer's plan if that plan accepts it.
3. Part of a commuted value above the tax-free transfer limit may be paid out in cash and taxed.
4. A group RRSP can move by direct transfer to a personal RRSP without tax withheld; a cash withdrawal is taxed.
5. Not financial advice; the plan administrator is the reference.

steps.title: Enrol in group benefits within the enrolment window
conditions: Only if the employer offers health, dental or insurance benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Many plans have a waiting period, then an enrolment window, often 30 to 90 days after starting.
2. Enrolling late can mean proof of good health or waiting for the next open enrolment, depending on the insurer.
3. Coverage can be coordinated with a spouse's plan.
4. The date here is an estimate; the benefits booklet has the real window.

steps.title: Join the workplace pension or group RRSP match
documents: Pension or group RRSP enrolment confirmation
prepare: Contribution rate for the full employer match
conditions: Only if the employer offers a pension plan or group RRSP
steps.howTo:
1. Employers may match contributions up to a set percentage; some plans enrol automatically, others wait for the employee.
2. Eligibility may start after a waiting period, often around 3 months.
3. Pension contributions reduce next year's RRSP room through a pension adjustment on the T4.
4. The date here is an estimate.

steps.title: Mark the end of probation
prepare: Probation end date from the contract
steps.howTo:
1. Many contracts set a 3-month probation; some benefits and pension plans start after it.
2. A review meeting is common near the end.
3. The date here assumes 3 months; move it to the contract's date.

steps.title: Collect your T4 slip
prepare: CRA My Account, where T4s also appear
steps.howTo:
1. Employers issue T4 slips for the calendar year by the end of February of the next year.
2. Each employer in the year issues its own T4.
3. If one has not arrived by early April, the CRA suggests contacting the employer.
4. This date assumes a mid-year start; move it to the end of February after the first year of work.

steps.title: File the income tax return
prepare: All T4 slips for the year
steps.howTo:
1. For most people the return is due April 30 of the year after.
2. Filing online with certified software gets a notice of assessment within about 2 weeks.
3. Filing also keeps benefits such as the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (formerly the GST/HST credit) coming.
4. This date assumes a mid-year start; move it to April 30.

steps.title: Note RRSP and TFSA contribution room in CRA My Account
steps.howTo:
1. The notice of assessment and CRA My Account show the RRSP deduction limit for the year: 18% of last year's earned income up to a yearly maximum, minus any pension adjustment, plus unused room.
2. TFSA room grows each year from age 18 while resident in Canada; My Account shows it, though recent-year contributions may not be counted yet.
3. RRSP contributions more than $2,000 over the limit, and any TFSA excess, are taxed 1% a month until removed.
4. With a first job, RRSP room starts building from this year's earnings and shows on the next notice of assessment.

title: Starting a job · China
summary: Paperwork plan for starting a job in mainland China, first or later: entry health check, the written labour contract and probation, social insurance, housing provident fund, income tax, personnel file and hukou. National rules; local offices set the details.
conditions: You are starting a job as an employee in mainland China, your first or a new one
Some steps apply only to a first job, to someone leaving another job, or to moving a personnel file or hukou

sources.title: Decision amending the Labour Contract Law of the PRC (2012) — gov.cn
Social Insurance Law of the PRC — State Taxation Administration law library
Regulations on the Management of Housing Provident Fund — gov.cn
Interim Measures for Special Additional Deductions of Individual Income Tax (2018) — gov.cn
When to do the annual individual income tax reconciliation — Shanxi Tax Service, State Taxation Administration
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
State Taxation Administration
Opinion on promoting the personal pension (国办发〔2022〕7号) — gov.cn

steps.title: Do the pre-employment health check (入职体检)
prepare: The hospital and item list the employer names
Fasting on the morning of the blood test
conditions: Only if the employer asks for one
steps.howTo:
1. Many employers ask for a check at a named hospital before or just after the start date; some jobs, such as food handling, have their own health certificate rules.
2. Under a 2010 notice from the human resources, education and health ministries, hepatitis B tests are not part of routine entry checks.
3. The report usually goes to HR; keep a copy.

steps.title: Get the leaving certificate from the previous employer (离职证明)
documents: Certificate of termination of the labour contract (解除或者终止劳动合同的证明)
prepare: Handover done with the previous employer
conditions: Only if you left another job
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Contract Law, the previous employer issues a certificate when the contract ends, and moves the personnel file and social insurance within 15 days.
2. New employers often ask for it to confirm there is no overlapping contract.

steps.title: Check the new employer on the individual income tax app (个人所得税)
prepare: Mobile number in your own name
Class I bank card for refunds
steps.howTo:
1. The employer withholds tax from pay each month and reports it under your ID.
2. The app lists each employer that reports you (任职受雇信息); an unknown employer can be disputed there.
3. For a first job, register with the ID card and face check.

steps.title: Declare special additional deductions (专项附加扣除)
prepare: Children's education or infant care details
conditions: Only if a deduction applies to you
steps.howTo:
1. Deductions cover children's education, infant care under 3, continuing education, serious illness medical costs, mortgage interest or rent, and elderly support.
2. In the app, choose whether the employer applies them each month or they are claimed in the annual reconciliation.
3. With a new employer, the declaration is pointed at the new one.
4. Declarations are confirmed again each year, usually in December.

steps.title: Sign the written labour contract (劳动合同) within one month
documents: Signed labour contract, your own copy
prepare: Agreed pay, job, place of work and hours
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Contract Law, a written contract is signed within one month of the start date.
2. If an employer goes more than a month without one, the law has it pay double wages each month, for up to a year.
3. After a full year without a written contract, the law treats it as an open-ended contract.
4. Each side keeps a signed copy.

steps.title: Check the probation period (试用期) against the contract length
prepare: Probation length and pay in the contract
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Contract Law: a contract of 3 months to under 1 year allows up to 1 month of probation; 1 to under 3 years, up to 2 months; 3 years or more, or open-ended, up to 6 months.
2. Contracts under 3 months, or for a set task, have no probation.
3. One employer can set probation only once for the same person, and it counts inside the contract term.
4. Probation pay is at least 80% of the agreed wage or the lowest wage for the same job there, and not below the local minimum wage.

steps.title: Check social insurance is registered (社会保险, five insurances)
prepare: National social insurance public service platform or the local app
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Social Insurance Law, the employer applies for the employee's registration within 30 days of the start date.
2. The five insurances are pension, medical (maternity is merged into it in most places), unemployment and work injury.
3. Contribution months show in the electronic social security card or the local platform.
4. For a first job, a social security card is issued if there is none yet.

steps.title: Check the housing provident fund account (住房公积金)
steps.howTo:
1. Under the provident fund regulations, the employer registers a new employee with the local fund centre within 30 days of hiring and opens or transfers the account.
2. Employer and employee each pay a share of wages, at rates the city sets.
3. The balance shows in the local fund centre app or the national provident fund app.

steps.title: Check the first payslip
steps.howTo:
1. Deductions usually shown: pension, medical and unemployment insurance, housing provident fund, and withheld income tax.
2. The income tax app shows the same withholding under the employer.
3. The first month is sometimes partial or paid a month late.

steps.title: Transfer social insurance and provident fund from another city
conditions: Only if your previous job was in another city
steps.howTo:
1. Basic pension and medical insurance can be transferred across provinces online through the national social insurance public service platform.
2. Provident fund accounts can be transferred between cities through the national provident fund app.
3. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Move your personnel file (档案) to the employer or a talent centre
prepare: Where the file sits now: school, previous employer or talent centre
conditions: Only if you have a personnel file, e.g. after university or a state employer
steps.howTo:
1. State bodies and some large employers keep files themselves; most private employers do not, and files go to a public talent exchange centre (人才交流中心) or employment service centre.
2. For a first job after graduating, the school sends the file as arranged with the graduate and the receiving office.
3. Files move between offices, not through your hands; a sealed file opened by the holder may be refused.
4. The file matters for professional titles, civil service and pension records.

steps.title: Settle the hukou in the job's city (户口)
conditions: Only if you want to move your hukou to the city of the job
steps.howTo:
1. Each city sets its own settlement rules, often by degree, age, job or months of social insurance paid.
2. Many cities open settlement to new graduates within a set time after graduating.
3. The local public security bureau or talent service centre handles it.
4. The date and time taken are estimates.

steps.title: Mark the end of probation
prepare: Probation end date from the contract
steps.howTo:
1. Pay moves to the full agreed wage after probation.
2. The date here assumes 3 months; move it to the contract's date.

steps.title: Do the annual income tax reconciliation (汇算清缴)
prepare: Income from all employers in the year
steps.howTo:
1. The reconciliation for a tax year runs from March 1 to June 30 of the following year, in the app.
2. It settles a refund or extra tax; changing jobs mid-year often leaves withholding off, since each employer counted only its own months.
3. The tax authority sets who is required to file; early in the window the app may ask for a booking.
4. This date assumes a mid-year start; move it to June 30 of the year after.

steps.title: Check for a social insurance gap between jobs (社保断缴)
conditions: Only if you left another job
prepare: Last month the previous employer paid
First month the new employer pays
steps.howTo:
1. A month with no contribution can break the continuous months some city rules count: home purchase eligibility, hukou points and school places.
2. A medical insurance gap can bring a waiting period before costs are covered again.
3. If there is a gap, some people pay as a flexible worker (灵活就业) for the months between; check the local rule.

steps.title: Check the contribution base against real pay (缴费基数)
documents: Social insurance and provident fund records
prepare: The social insurance app or local platform
steps.howTo:
1. Social insurance and the provident fund are paid on a contribution base (缴费基数), usually last year's average monthly wage, within the local floor and ceiling.
2. A base set lower than real pay means lower pension, unemployment and provident fund amounts later.
3. The base shows in the social insurance and fund centre apps; ask HR if it looks wrong.
4. Bases are reset each year, often in July; this repeats yearly.

steps.title: Consider opening a personal pension account (个人养老金)
prepare: Social security card or resident ID card
A bank that offers personal pension accounts
steps.howTo:
1. Anyone in the basic pension can open one personal pension account (个人养老金) through a bank or the national platform; the scheme has run nationwide since December 2024.
2. Contributions of up to 12,000 yuan a year are deducted from taxable income; payouts are taxed at 3%.
3. The money is locked until retirement age, disability or settling abroad.
4. Contributions count for the calendar year, so pay by December 31; this repeats yearly. Not financial advice.

steps.title: Check the enterprise or occupational annuity (企业年金 / 职业年金)
conditions: Only if the employer offers an annuity
prepare: Ask HR for the plan rules and your share
steps.howTo:
1. Some employers run an enterprise annuity (企业年金); public institutions pay an occupational annuity (职业年金).
2. Employer and employee both pay in; rules on vesting when leaving are in the plan.
3. The account moves with you to a new employer that has a plan, and pays out at retirement.

steps.title: Note paid annual leave (带薪年休假)
prepare: Your total years of work, with all employers
steps.howTo:
1. Employees who have worked continuously for over a year get paid annual leave: 5 days with 1 to under 10 years of total work, 10 days with 10 to under 20, 15 days with 20 or more.
2. Years with all employers count; a new employer may pro-rate the first year.
3. Leave not taken at the employer's request is paid at 300% of the daily wage.

title: Job ended · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for the weeks and months after a job ends in British Columbia: final pay, EI, notice pay, benefits, pension and next year’s taxes.
conditions: Your job in British Columbia ended: laid off, let go, or you quit
For provincially regulated work; banks, airlines, telecoms and other federally regulated employers follow the Canada Labour Code instead
This is a planning aid, not legal advice; the Employment Standards Branch and Service Canada are the reference

sources.title: Quitting or getting fired — Province of British Columbia
Employment standards complaint process — Province of British Columbia
EI regular benefits: Apply — Canada.ca
EI reporting — Canada.ca
Record of Employment guide — Canada.ca
Canadian Dental Care Plan: Do you qualify — Canada.ca
Fair PharmaCare plan — Province of British Columbia
Work permit types — Canada.ca

steps.title: Check the final pay and vacation pay
prepare: Hours worked since the last pay
steps.howTo:
1. Under the B.C. Employment Standards Act, final wages are due within 48 hours after the last day worked if the employer ended the job, or within 6 days if you quit.
2. Final pay includes wages earned and any vacation pay owing.
3. Keep the last pay stubs; they help with EI and any complaint later.

steps.title: Apply for EI regular benefits
conditions: Only if you worked enough insurable hours; check current EI rules for your region
prepare: Last day of work and reason it ended
Employer names and dates for the past 52 weeks
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online as soon as possible after the last day of work; applying more than 4 weeks later can mean losing benefits.
2. There is no need to wait for the Record of Employment; Service Canada gets electronic ones from the employer.
3. A new claim has a 1-week unpaid waiting period.
4. Declare any severance, notice pay or vacation pay; Service Canada decides whether it changes when payments start.
5. The online form takes about an hour; a partly filled form is saved for 72 hours.

steps.title: Check the Record of Employment
steps.howTo:
1. Electronic ROEs are usually due 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period with the last day worked; paper ones within 5 days of the interruption.
2. View and print electronic ROEs in My Service Canada Account.
3. Check the reason for separation, dates and insurable hours; ask the employer to amend errors, or tell Service Canada.

steps.title: Send the first EI report, then every 2 weeks
conditions: Only if you applied for EI
prepare: 4-digit access code from the benefit statement
Days and hours worked and earnings before deductions
Any training, travel or days not available for work
steps.howTo:
1. Service Canada mails a benefit statement with a 4-digit access code.
2. A report is completed every 2 weeks to keep benefits coming.
3. Report work and earnings for each week, even if paid later, and any other money received.
4. This repeats every 2 weeks while on EI; the date here is an estimate for the first one.

steps.title: Check notice or compensation for length of service
conditions: Only if the employer ended the job and you worked there more than 3 months
steps.howTo:
1. B.C. employers give written working notice, pay instead of notice, or a mix.
2. The minimum is: 1 week after 3 months; 2 weeks after 1 year; 3 weeks after 3 years, plus 1 week for each extra year, up to 8 weeks.
3. There is no notice pay for 3 months or less, or when the employee quits.
4. Group terminations and temporary layoffs have their own rules.
5. A contract or the courts may give more than the Act; not legal advice.

steps.title: Replace workplace health and dental cover
conditions: Only if you had workplace health, drug or dental benefits
steps.howTo:
1. MSP is not tied to the job; basic medical cover carries on.
2. Many group plans let you convert life or health cover to an individual plan within a short window, often around 31 days; check the booklet or insurer.
3. For drugs, Fair PharmaCare covers MSP enrollees based on family net income; register if not already.
4. With no dental insurance and adjusted family net income under $90,000, the Canadian Dental Care Plan may apply; taxes have to be filed.
5. A spouse’s plan may be able to add you.

steps.title: Check your status on an employer-specific permit
conditions: Only if you hold an employer-specific (closed) work permit
prepare: Any new job offer and whether it needs an LMIA
steps.howTo:
1. A closed permit only allows work for the employer named on it; a new employer usually means a new permit or authorization before starting.
2. Staying in Canada without work may mean changing to visitor status before the permit expires.
3. Check current IRCC rules and processing times; not immigration advice.

steps.title: Register for job search help
steps.howTo:
1. WorkBC centres offer free job search help, training and, for some people, funding.
2. Job Bank lists jobs across Canada and can send alerts.
3. Keep a record of job searches; Service Canada may ask for it while on EI.

steps.title: Decide what to do with the pension and group RRSP
conditions: Only if you were in a workplace pension plan or group RRSP
prepare: Details of an RRSP or LIRA to transfer to
steps.howTo:
1. The plan administrator sends a statement of options after the job ends.
2. A vested pension can usually be left as a deferred pension, or its commuted value moved to a locked-in account (LIRA) or a new employer’s plan.
3. A group RRSP can usually be moved to a personal RRSP without tax by direct transfer.
4. B.C.-registered plans are overseen by the BC Financial Services Authority.
5. Not financial advice; the statement lists the deadline to choose.

steps.title: File an employment standards complaint if pay is missing
conditions: Only if final pay, vacation pay or notice pay was not paid
prepare: What is owed and for which dates
steps.howTo:
1. File with the Employment Standards Branch within 6 months of the last day of work.
2. Issues from the last year of employment are reviewed.
3. The Solution Explorer online helps check the rules first.
4. The date here leaves a margin before the 6-month limit.

steps.title: Report severance and EI on the next tax return
steps.howTo:
1. EI benefits are taxable and come on a T4E slip.
2. Severance and payments for loss of employment are usually treated as a retiring allowance; part of it may be moved to an RRSP for years of service before 1996 (check current CRA rules).
3. Lump sums have tax withheld at set rates, which may not match the tax owed.
4. With high net income for the year, part of the EI may have to be repaid on the return.
5. File by April 30; the date here is an estimate.

title: Job ended · China
summary: Paperwork plan for when a job in mainland China ends: the leaving certificate, final pay and severance, labour arbitration time limits, unemployment registration and benefit, keeping social insurance unbroken, the housing provident fund and income tax.
conditions: A job as an employee in mainland China has ended, by layoff, dismissal, contract expiry or resignation
Some steps apply only when the employer ended the contract, to someone without a new job yet, or to a dispute

sources.title: Decision amending the Labour Contract Law of the PRC (2012) — gov.cn
Social Insurance Law of the PRC — State Taxation Administration law library
Housing Provident Fund Regulations, consolidated text — Ministry of Justice regulations database
National social insurance public service platform
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
State Taxation Administration

steps.title: Get the leaving certificate and file transfer (离职证明)
documents: Certificate of termination of the labour contract (解除或者终止劳动合同的证明)
prepare: Any written notice of termination from the employer
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Contract Law, the employer issues a certificate when the contract ends, and moves the personnel file (档案) and social insurance within 15 days.
2. The certificate usually states the contract term, the end date, the job and years of service.
3. It is needed for unemployment registration and by most new employers.
4. If the employer delays, the local labour inspection office (劳动保障监察) takes complaints.

steps.title: Check the final pay and unused annual leave
prepare: Days of annual leave taken this year
steps.howTo:
1. Wages up to the last day are paid in full when the contract ends, usually on the next payday.
2. Under the paid annual leave rules, unused leave for the part of the year worked is paid at 300% of the daily wage (the normal day's pay plus 200%).
3. Keep the final payslip; it is useful evidence in any later dispute.

steps.title: Check severance pay (经济补偿)
prepare: Average monthly wage over the last 12 months
conditions: Only if the employer ended the contract, did not renew it, or the law otherwise gives severance
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Contract Law, severance is one month's wage per full year of service (N); 6 months to under a year counts as a year, under 6 months as half a month.
2. Where the monthly wage is over three times the local average, the wage used is capped at three times the average and the years at 12.
3. Where the employer ends the contract without 30 days' written notice in the cases that allow it, one extra month is paid in lieu (N+1).
4. An unlawful dismissal can lead to double severance (2N) instead.
5. A resignation on your own initiative usually brings no severance, unless the employer broke the law first, e.g. unpaid wages or no social insurance.
6. A mutual agreement to end the contract is put in writing; read the amounts before signing.

steps.title: Check how severance is taxed
documents: Individual income tax app record of the payment
conditions: Only if severance was paid
steps.howTo:
1. One-off compensation for ending a labour contract is tax-free up to three times the local average annual wage; the part above is taxed on its own, not added to the year's wages.
2. This treatment has been extended by later notices; check current.
3. The employer withholds; the payment then shows in the individual income tax app.

steps.title: Check any non-compete agreement (竞业限制)
prepare: Scope, region and length of the restriction
conditions: Only if you signed a non-compete
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Contract Law, a non-compete lasts at most 2 years after leaving and applies to senior staff, technical staff and others with confidentiality duties.
2. The employer pays monthly compensation during the restriction.
3. Keep records of the payments received.

steps.title: Note the time limit for labour arbitration (劳动仲裁)
conditions: Only if there is a dispute with the employer
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Dispute Mediation and Arbitration Law, the time limit is one year from the day the right was known to be infringed.
2. Applications go to the labour dispute arbitration commission where the job was or where the employer is registered; it charges no fee.
3. Arbitration usually comes before any court case for labour disputes.
4. The 30 days here is a placeholder, not the deadline.

steps.title: Register as unemployed (失业登记)
conditions: Only if you have no new job yet
steps.howTo:
1. Registration is with the public employment service, at the place of residence or hukou, or online through the national social insurance public service platform, 掌上12333 or the local app.
2. It opens free job-search services and training, and is a condition of unemployment benefit.
3. Registering promptly keeps the benefit months from slipping.

steps.title: Apply for unemployment benefit (失业保险金)
conditions: Only if you paid unemployment insurance for at least a year and did not leave of your own will
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Social Insurance Law, the conditions are: at least one year of contributions, leaving not by your own choice, and unemployment registration with a wish to find work.
2. Benefit lasts up to 12 months for 1 to under 5 years of contributions, 18 months for 5 to under 10, and 24 months for 10 or more.
3. The monthly amount is set by the province, below the local minimum wage.
4. While drawing it, employee medical insurance continues, paid from the unemployment fund.
5. It stops on a new job, moving abroad, reaching pension age, or refusing suitable work or training without reason.
6. Apply online through the national platform or 掌上12333, or at the local office.

steps.title: Keep social insurance unbroken (避免社保断缴)
conditions: Only if no new job starts soon
steps.howTo:
1. When the employer stops paying, contributions can continue as a flexible worker (灵活就业): basic pension and medical insurance, paid by you, at a base chosen within the local range, usually 60% to 300% of the local average wage.
2. Many cities now let flexible workers join where they work without a local hukou; check current.
3. A break in medical insurance can bring a waiting period before benefits restart, set locally.
4. Home purchase eligibility, hukou points and school places in some cities count unbroken months of social insurance.
5. The record shows in the electronic social security card or on the national platform.

steps.title: Check where your personnel file (档案) went
prepare: Name of the previous employer or talent centre that held it
conditions: Only if you have a personnel file
steps.howTo:
1. Files held by the employer are moved within 15 days of the contract ending, usually to a public talent exchange or employment service centre.
2. Files move between offices, not through your hands.
3. The file matters for professional titles, civil service applications and pension records.

steps.title: Check the housing provident fund account (住房公积金封存)
prepare: National provident fund app or local fund centre app
steps.howTo:
1. Under the provident fund regulations, the employer asks the fund centre to transfer or seal (封存) the account within 30 days of the job ending.
2. A sealed account keeps its balance and interest; the next employer transfers it on.
3. Withdrawal is limited to the listed reasons, such as rent, buying a home, loan repayment or retirement; some cities also allow withdrawal after a spell of unemployment, set locally, so check current.
4. A provident fund mortgage keeps running; check with the lender how repayments continue without monthly contributions.

steps.title: Do the annual income tax reconciliation (汇算清缴)
prepare: Income from all employers in the year
steps.howTo:
1. The reconciliation for a tax year runs from March 1 to June 30 of the following year, in the individual income tax app.
2. A job ending mid-year often leaves too much tax withheld, since each employer counted only its own months; a refund can follow.
3. The tax authority sets who is required to file.
4. This date assumes a mid-year ending; move it to June 30 of the year after.

title: Job ended · Ontario

steps.title: Check the final pay and vacation pay
prepare: Hours worked since the last pay
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Ontario Employment Standards Act, termination pay is due 7 days after the job ends or on the next regular pay day, whichever is later; final wages follow the same timing.
2. Final pay includes wages earned and any vacation pay owing.
3. Keep the last pay stubs; they help with EI and any claim later.

steps.title: Apply for EI regular benefits
conditions: Only if you worked enough insurable hours; check current EI rules for your region
prepare: Last day of work and reason it ended
Employer names and dates for the past 52 weeks
steps.howTo:
1. Apply online as soon as possible after the last day of work; applying more than 4 weeks later can mean losing benefits.
2. There is no need to wait for the Record of Employment; Service Canada gets electronic ones from the employer.
3. A new claim has a 1-week unpaid waiting period.
4. Declare any severance, termination pay or vacation pay; Service Canada decides whether it changes when payments start.
5. The online form takes about an hour; a partly filled form is saved for 72 hours.

steps.title: Check the Record of Employment
steps.howTo:
1. Electronic ROEs are usually due 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period with the last day worked; paper ones within 5 days of the interruption.
2. View and print electronic ROEs in My Service Canada Account.
3. Check the reason for separation, dates and insurable hours; ask the employer to amend errors, or tell Service Canada.

steps.title: Send the first EI report, then every 2 weeks
conditions: Only if you applied for EI
prepare: 4-digit access code from the benefit statement
Days and hours worked and earnings before deductions
Any training, travel or days not available for work
steps.howTo:
1. Service Canada mails a benefit statement with a 4-digit access code.
2. A report is completed every 2 weeks to keep benefits coming.
3. Report work and earnings for each week, even if paid later, and any other money received.
4. This repeats every 2 weeks while on EI; the date here is an estimate for the first one.

steps.title: Check termination pay and severance pay
conditions: Only if the employer ended the job and you worked there at least 3 months
prepare: Whether the employer's payroll is $2.5 million or more
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario employers give written notice, termination pay instead, or a mix: 1 week under 1 year, 2 weeks for 1 to 3 years, then 1 more week per year, up to 8 weeks at 8 years.
2. Benefit plan contributions continue through the statutory notice period.
3. Severance pay is separate: after 5 or more years, where the employer has a payroll of $2.5 million or more or ended 50 or more jobs in 6 months because of a closure; 1 week per year of service, up to 26 weeks.
4. Some cases are exempt, such as wilful misconduct or temporary layoff.
5. A contract or the courts may give more than the Act; not legal advice.

steps.title: Replace workplace health and dental cover
conditions: Only if you had workplace health, drug or dental benefits
prepare: Date the group cover ends, after any statutory notice period
steps.howTo:
1. OHIP is not tied to the job; basic medical cover carries on.
2. Many group plans let you convert life or health cover to an individual plan within a short window, often around 31 days; check the booklet or insurer.
3. For drugs, OHIP+ covers people 24 and under with no private plan; from 25 the Trillium Drug Program helps with high drug costs.
4. With no dental insurance and adjusted family net income under $90,000, the Canadian Dental Care Plan may apply; taxes have to be filed.
5. A spouse’s plan may be able to add you.

steps.title: Check your status on an employer-specific permit
conditions: Only if you hold an employer-specific (closed) work permit
prepare: Any new job offer and whether it needs an LMIA
steps.howTo:
1. A closed permit only allows work for the employer named on it; a new employer usually means a new permit or authorization before starting.
2. Staying in Canada without work may mean changing to visitor status before the permit expires.
3. Check current IRCC rules and processing times; not immigration advice.

steps.title: Register for job search help
steps.howTo:
1. Employment Ontario offers free job search help, training and, for some people, funding.
2. Job Bank lists jobs across Canada and can send alerts.
3. Keep a record of job searches; Service Canada may ask for it while on EI.

steps.title: Decide what to do with the pension and group RRSP
conditions: Only if you were in a workplace pension plan or group RRSP
prepare: Details of an RRSP or LIRA to transfer to
steps.howTo:
1. The plan administrator sends a statement of options after the job ends.
2. A vested pension can usually be left as a deferred pension, or its commuted value moved to a locked-in account (LIRA) or a new employer’s plan.
3. A group RRSP can usually be moved to a personal RRSP without tax by direct transfer.
4. Ontario-registered plans are overseen by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA).
5. Not financial advice; the statement lists the deadline to choose.

steps.title: File an employment standards claim if pay is missing
conditions: Only if final pay, vacation pay, termination or severance pay was not paid
prepare: What is owed and for which dates
My Ontario account for the online claim
steps.howTo:
1. A claim is generally filed within 2 years of the alleged ESA violation.
2. File online through the e-claim system or the claimant portal, or send the PDF form by fax or mail.
3. The Employment Standards Information Centre answers questions: 1-800-531-5551.
4. Filing sooner keeps records fresh; the date here leaves a margin before the 2-year limit.

steps.title: Report severance and EI on the next tax return
steps.howTo:
1. EI benefits are taxable and come on a T4E slip.
2. Severance and payments for loss of employment are usually treated as a retiring allowance; part of it may be moved to an RRSP for years of service before 1996 (check current CRA rules).
3. Lump sums have tax withheld at set rates, which may not match the tax owed.
4. With high net income for the year, part of the EI may have to be repaid on the return.
5. File by April 30; the date here is an estimate.

title: Self-employed or starting a business · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for a sole proprietorship or partnership in British Columbia, from the business name and CRA accounts to sales taxes, workers, EI special benefits and the first self-employed tax return.
conditions: You are starting to work for yourself in British Columbia, as a sole proprietor or in a partnership; the event date is when you start trading
Incorporating a company follows different steps and filings

sources.title: Register a proprietorship or partnership — Province of British Columbia
BC Registries and Online Services
Business number registration — Canada.ca
When to register for and start charging the GST/HST — Canada.ca
PST registration — Province of British Columbia
BizPaL business permits and licences
Register for coverage — WorkSafeBC
Open or manage a payroll account — Canada.ca
EI special benefits for self-employed people — Canada.ca
Sole proprietorships and partnerships — Canada.ca
Paying your income tax by instalments — Canada.ca

steps.title: Request and reserve a business name
conditions: Only if you trade under a name other than your own
prepare: A short description of the business
Check the current fee ($30 at review)
steps.howTo:
1. Submit a name request online through BC Registries; priority service costs more and is faster.
2. An approved name is held for 56 days; after that a new request is needed.
3. Trading under your own name alone does not need registration, but registering protects the name.

steps.title: Register the proprietorship or partnership with BC Registries
conditions: Only if you trade under a name other than your own
prepare: Check the current fee ($40 at review)
steps.howTo:
1. Register online through the BC Business Registry, or at a Service BC office, before the name request expires.
2. Registration with the province is separate from a local business licence.
3. Keep the statement of registration; banks ask for it to open a business account.

steps.title: Get a CRA business number and program accounts
conditions: Only if you will register for GST, open a payroll account, or import or export
steps.howTo:
1. Register online with Business Registration Online, by phone or by mail; BC Registries can also request one when you register.
2. The business number is 9 digits; each program account (RT for GST, RP for payroll) is added to it.
3. A sole proprietor with no GST, payroll or trade accounts may not need one.

steps.title: Register to collect BC PST
conditions: Only if you sell or lease taxable goods, software or taxable services in British Columbia
prepare: What you sell and to whom
Business number, if you have one
steps.howTo:
1. Register with the province before you start selling taxable goods or services.
2. Small sellers with low yearly sales may be exempt; check the current small seller threshold.
3. Returns are filed on the schedule the province assigns (monthly, quarterly or yearly).

steps.title: Set up a business bank account and bookkeeping
steps.howTo:
1. Keeping business money separate makes the T2125 and any GST return easier.
2. The CRA generally asks for records and receipts to be kept for 6 years after the tax year they relate to.
3. Track home office and vehicle use from the start; only the business share is deductible.

steps.title: Get a municipal business licence
prepare: Zoning or home-based business rules for your city
steps.howTo:
1. Most BC municipalities license businesses operating within their boundaries, including many home-based ones.
2. BizPaL lists the permits and licences for your type of business and location.
3. Licences are usually renewed every year.

steps.title: Register with WorkSafeBC
conditions: Only if you hire workers, or want optional personal coverage for yourself
prepare: Type of work and expected payroll
steps.howTo:
1. Employers in BC register before workers start.
2. Sole proprietors and partners are not covered automatically; optional personal protection can be bought.
3. Premiums are reported and paid on the schedule WorkSafeBC sets.

steps.title: Open a payroll account before the first payday
conditions: Only if you hire employees
prepare: Each employee's SIN and TD1 forms
steps.howTo:
1. Add an RP program account to the business number before the first payday.
2. Deduct CPP, EI and income tax from each pay; most new employers remit by the 15th of the next month.
3. File T4 slips and the summary by the end of February each year.

steps.title: Decide whether to opt in to EI special benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Self-employed people can opt in to EI maternity, parental, sickness and caregiving benefits; regular EI is not included.
2. Claims can be made 12 months after registering, and need a minimum of self-employed earnings in the previous calendar year; check current amounts.
3. Once a benefit is paid, premiums continue for as long as you stay self-employed.

steps.title: Watch the $30,000 small supplier limit and register for GST
conditions: Only if taxable sales pass $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters, or you choose to register earlier
prepare: Business number, if you have one
steps.howTo:
1. Check total taxable sales every quarter; the limit counts the last four calendar quarters together.
2. Passing $30,000 in a single quarter means registering within 29 days, with GST charged from the sale that went over.
3. In British Columbia GST is 5%, charged alongside PST where PST applies.
4. Registering early lets you claim input tax credits on business costs.

steps.title: File the first self-employed tax return (T2125)
prepare: Income and expense records for the year
steps.howTo:
1. Report business income and expenses on form T2125 with your T1 return.
2. Self-employed people pay both the employee and employer shares of CPP (Schedule 8).
3. The return is due June 15, but any balance owing is due April 30; interest runs from April 30.
4. This date is an estimate; move it to the year after your first business year. It repeats every year.

steps.title: Pay tax instalments
conditions: Only if net tax owing is more than $3,000 this year and in either of the two previous years
steps.howTo:
1. Instalments are due March 15, June 15, September 15 and December 15.
2. The CRA mails reminders with suggested amounts; paying those avoids instalment interest.
3. This is the first one after tax is owed; they repeat every quarter.

title: Self-employed or starting a business · China
summary: Paperwork plan for working for yourself in mainland China, as a flexible worker, an individual business (个体工商户) or a small company: the business licence, tax, social insurance paid on your own account, the provident fund, staff, and the yearly report and tax filing.
conditions: You are starting to work for yourself or opening a business in mainland China
Some steps apply only to a registered business, a company, or one that hires staff

sources.title: State Administration for Market Regulation
National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (国家企业信用信息公示系统)
State Taxation Administration
Social Insurance Law of the PRC — State Taxation Administration law library
National social insurance public service platform
Housing Provident Fund Regulations, consolidated text — Ministry of Justice regulations database
Decision amending the Labour Contract Law of the PRC (2012) — gov.cn
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security

steps.title: Choose the form: flexible work, individual business or company
steps.howTo:
1. Flexible work (灵活就业) with no registration suits freelance and gig work; some small, occasional activities are exempt from registration, and tax is then withheld by the payer or paid through the tax app.
2. An individual business (个体工商户) is registered by one person or a family; the owner answers for debts with personal assets.
3. A limited company (有限责任公司) is a separate legal person; under the Company Law as revised from July 2024, subscribed capital is paid in within 5 years.
4. The form sets how tax is paid and which steps below apply.

steps.title: Register for a business licence (营业执照)
prepare: Proof of the premises: lease or property certificate
conditions: Only if you register an individual business or a company
steps.howTo:
1. Apply to the local market regulation bureau (市场监督管理局), in most places online.
2. The licence carries a unified social credit code; tax registration comes with it (多证合一).
3. Individual business registration charges no fee.
4. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Get any trade permits the business needs
documents: Permit, e.g. food business licence (食品经营许可证)
conditions: Only if the trade needs a permit, e.g. food, medicine, education, transport
steps.howTo:
1. Some trades need a permit beyond the licence; the market regulation bureau and the relevant department list which.
2. Permits are often checked on site before issue.
3. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Set up tax: electronic tax bureau and invoices
documents: Electronic tax bureau (电子税务局) login
prepare: Mobile number in your own name
conditions: Only if you register an individual business or a company
steps.howTo:
1. After the licence, confirm the tax details on the electronic tax bureau of the province; the tax office sets which taxes and periods apply.
2. Most new small businesses start as small-scale VAT taxpayers (小规模纳税人); the monthly or quarterly sales below which VAT is exempt is set by current notices, so check current.
3. Electronic invoices (数电发票) are issued through the same system.

steps.title: Open a business bank account
prepare: Legal representative's or owner's ID card
conditions: Only if you register an individual business or a company
steps.howTo:
1. A company opens a basic account (基本存款账户) for its main transactions and tax payments.
2. An individual business can open a business account; banks set their own documents and checks.
3. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Join basic pension insurance as a flexible worker
conditions: Only if no employer pays your social insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Individual business owners and flexible workers can join basic pension insurance on their own account, through the social insurance office, the tax app or the national platform.
2. The contribution base is chosen within the local range, usually 60% to 300% of the local average wage; the whole amount is paid by you.
3. Many cities now accept flexible workers where they work without a local hukou; check current.
4. Keeping contributions unbroken counts for the pension and, in some cities, for home purchase, hukou and school places.
5. Payments recur monthly, quarterly or yearly as chosen.

steps.title: Keep medical insurance going
conditions: Only if no employer pays your medical insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Flexible workers can join employee medical insurance on their own account, or resident medical insurance (城乡居民医保) paid yearly.
2. A gap can bring a waiting period before benefits restart, set locally.
3. Leaving a job for self-employment is the usual moment for a gap; paying the next month avoids one.

steps.title: Check voluntary housing provident fund contributions
prepare: Existing provident fund account, if any
conditions: Only if you want to keep paying into the provident fund
steps.howTo:
1. The provident fund regulations as revised in 2026 let the self-employed and flexible workers pay in voluntarily; the local fund centre sets how, and some cities had pilots before.
2. Contributions can later be used for rent, a home purchase or a provident fund loan, under local rules.
3. Check current with the local fund centre.

steps.title: Hire staff: contracts, social insurance and provident fund
documents: Staff social insurance and provident fund registrations
conditions: Only if you hire employees
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Labour Contract Law, a written contract is signed within a month of each start date.
2. Under the Social Insurance Law, the employer registers each employee for social insurance within 30 days of hiring, and does the same with the provident fund.
3. Income tax on wages is withheld each month through the electronic tax bureau or the natural person tax management system (自然人电子税务局).

steps.title: File the first quarterly business income tax return (经营所得预缴)
prepare: Income and costs for the quarter
conditions: Only if you have business income as an individual business, sole proprietor or partnership
steps.howTo:
1. Business income (经营所得) of an individual business is taxed under individual income tax; tax is prepaid within 15 days after each quarter ends.
2. Many small individual businesses are taxed on an assessed basis (核定征收) set by the tax office.
3. Companies file VAT and corporate income tax on their own periods instead.
4. This date assumes the first quarter ends about 90 days in; it repeats every quarter.

steps.title: Consider a private pension account (个人养老金)
conditions: Only if you pay into basic pension insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Open through a bank or the national social insurance platform; contributions up to 12,000 yuan a year are deducted from taxable income.
2. It has been open nationwide since December 2024.
3. Contributions for a year are made by December 31; the step repeats each year.

steps.title: File the annual business income reconciliation (经营所得汇算)
prepare: Special additional deductions, if there is no wage income
conditions: Only if you have business income as an individual business, sole proprietor or partnership
steps.howTo:
1. Business income for a year is reconciled by March 31 of the following year.
2. Wage income is reconciled separately, from March 1 to June 30.
3. Where there is no wage income, the basic 60,000 yuan a year and special additional deductions can be claimed against business income.
4. This date assumes a mid-year start; move it to March 31 of the year after. It repeats each year.

steps.title: Submit the annual report (年度报告)
prepare: Operating figures for the past year
conditions: Only if you registered an individual business or a company
steps.howTo:
1. Each registered business reports on the past year through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System between January 1 and June 30.
2. A business that misses it is listed as abnormal (经营异常名录), which can affect loans and contracts.
3. This date assumes a mid-year start; move it to June 30 of the year after. It repeats each year.

title: Self-employed or starting a business · Ontario
summary: Paperwork plan for a sole proprietorship or partnership in Ontario, from the business name and CRA accounts to HST, workers, EI special benefits and the first self-employed tax return.
conditions: You are starting to work for yourself in Ontario, as a sole proprietor or in a partnership; the event date is when you start trading
Incorporating a company follows different steps and filings

steps.title: Register the business name in the Ontario Business Registry
conditions: Only if you trade under a name other than your own full name
prepare: Business name and a name search
steps.howTo:
1. Register online in the Ontario Business Registry; the registration is issued as a Master Business Licence.
2. A sole proprietor trading only under their own full name does not need to register.
3. The registration lasts 5 years and is renewed in the same registry; check current.

steps.title: Get a CRA business number and program accounts
conditions: Only if you will register for HST, open a payroll account, or import or export
steps.howTo:

steps.howTo:

steps.title: Check for a municipal business licence
prepare: Zoning or home-based business rules for your city
steps.howTo:

2. BizPaL lists the permits and licences for your type of business and location.
3. Licences are usually renewed every year.

steps.title: Register with the WSIB
conditions: Only if you hire workers, work in construction, or want optional coverage for yourself
prepare: Type of work and expected payroll
steps.howTo:
1. Most employers in Ontario register with the WSIB within 10 days of hiring their first worker; check current.
2. Independent operators in construction generally need their own coverage.
3. Other sole proprietors can buy optional insurance for themselves.

steps.title: Open a payroll account before the first payday
conditions: Only if you hire employees
prepare: Each employee's SIN and TD1 and TD1ON forms
steps.howTo:
1. Add an RP program account to the business number before the first payday.
2. Deduct CPP, EI and income tax from each pay; most new employers remit by the 15th of the next month.

steps.title: Decide whether to opt in to EI special benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Self-employed people can opt in to EI maternity, parental, sickness and caregiving benefits; regular EI is not included.
2. Claims can be made 12 months after registering, and need a minimum of self-employed earnings in the previous calendar year; check current amounts.
3. Once a benefit is paid, premiums continue for as long as you stay self-employed.

steps.title: Watch the $30,000 small supplier limit and register for HST
conditions: Only if taxable sales pass $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters, or you choose to register earlier
prepare: Business number, if you have one
steps.howTo:
1. Check total taxable sales every quarter; the limit counts the last four calendar quarters together.
2. Passing $30,000 in a single quarter means registering within 29 days, with HST charged from the sale that went over.
3. Ontario has no separate provincial sales tax; the 13% HST covers both parts.
4. Registering early lets you claim input tax credits on business costs.

steps.title: File the first self-employed tax return (T2125)
prepare: Income and expense records for the year
steps.howTo:
1. Report business income and expenses on form T2125 with your T1 return.
2. Self-employed people pay both the employee and employer shares of CPP (Schedule 8).
3. The return is due June 15, but any balance owing is due April 30; interest runs from April 30.
4. This date is an estimate; move it to the year after your first business year. It repeats every year.

steps.title: Pay tax instalments
conditions: Only if net tax owing is more than $3,000 this year and in either of the two previous years
steps.howTo:
1. Instalments are due March 15, June 15, September 15 and December 15.
2. The CRA mails reminders with suggested amounts; paying those avoids instalment interest.
3. This is the first one after tax is owed; they repeat every quarter.

title: Moving home · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for moving to a new home in a British Columbia city, from within B.C. or from another province: lease, mail, utilities, ICBC, MSP, voting, tax and settling in.
conditions: You are moving to a new home in a British Columbia city, from elsewhere in B.C. or from another province
Some steps apply only to people new to B.C., drivers, renters or families with children
The moving day is the anchor date; steps before it are counted back from it

sources.title: Moving to B.C. — ICBC
Moving from within Canada — ICBC
Moving to B.C. (insurance and registration) — ICBC
Address Change BC — Province of British Columbia
Change your personal information on a BC Services Card — Province of British Columbia
MSP: How to enrol — Province of British Columbia
