Elections Ontario
Register to vote — Elections Canada

steps.title: Give notice at the old rental and plan the move-out
documents: Form N9, Tenant's Notice to End the Tenancy
prepare: Check the lease: monthly, or a fixed term still running
Pick a termination date on the last day of a rental period
Photos of the unit when leaving
steps.howTo:
1. A monthly tenant gives at least 60 days' written notice, usually on the Landlord and Tenant Board's form N9, ending on the last day of a rental period.
2. On a fixed-term lease the date can't be earlier than the end of the term, unless the landlord agrees in writing.
3. The last month's rent deposit pays for the last month; a refundable key deposit comes back when the keys are returned.
4. Ontario has no formal move-out inspection; dated photos are a useful record if damage is raised later.
conditions: Only if you rented the old home in Ontario

steps.title: Sign the standard lease or complete the purchase
prepare: View the unit in person or by live video before paying anything
Check the landlord owns or manages the unit
Note the move-in date, rent, what is included and the deposit amount
steps.howTo:
1. Most private residential tenancies that began on or after April 30, 2018 use Ontario's standard lease form.
2. If a landlord doesn't provide it after a written request, the tenant can withhold one month's rent; the landlord has 21 days to comply.
3. A rent deposit can be at most one month's rent (or one week's, if paid weekly) and only goes toward the last rental period; the landlord pays interest on it each year at the rent increase guideline rate.
4. Disputes go to the Landlord and Tenant Board.
5. For a purchase, the lawyer handles the transfer; the timing here is an estimate.

steps.title: Register the children at the new school
prepare: Find the school for the new address with the school board's locator
Child's birth certificate or other proof of age
Latest report card and immunization record
Choose between the public and Catholic boards, English or French, if eligible
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario school boards assign schools by home address.
2. Registration is done with the school or the board; each board sets its own list of papers.
3. Public health units ask for the child's immunization record.
conditions: Only if you have school-age children

steps.title: Order mail forwarding from Canada Post
prepare: Canada Post account, if ordering online
steps.howTo:
1. For a move, forwarding comes in 4-month and 12-month terms, with a fee.
2. Ordered online, it starts 5 days after purchase; at a post office, 3 days after.
3. Forwarding gives time to update the bank, employer, insurers and subscriptions.

steps.title: Set up electricity, gas, water and internet
prepare: Check which utilities the lease includes
The local electricity utility, or Hydro One in many rural areas
Enbridge Gas for natural gas in most of Ontario
Close or move the accounts at the old home
steps.howTo:
1. Start dates are set online or by phone with each provider.
2. Water is billed by the municipality or through the landlord.
3. Internet installs can take a week or more to book.

steps.title: Start tenant or home insurance at the new address
prepare: Check whether the lease asks for tenant insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Tenant insurance covers belongings and liability; the building's own policy usually does not.
2. The standard lease has a section where the landlord can ask for proof of tenant insurance.
3. Moving an existing policy is usually a call to the insurer.

steps.title: Record the unit's condition on moving day
prepare: Photos or video of every room
A list of existing damage, sent to the landlord by email
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario has no set move-in inspection form.
2. A dated record sent to the landlord helps if a question about damage comes up at the Landlord and Tenant Board later.
conditions: Only if you rent

steps.title: Update the address for the licence, vehicle permit and health card
prepare: Driver's licence number and issue date
Health card number and version code
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario gives 6 days after moving to update the driver's licence and the vehicle permit, and 30 days for the health card.
2. All three are free and can be done online through a ServiceOntario account or in person.
3. A new licence arrives by mail in 4 to 6 weeks; no new health card is issued, only the record.
4. Check with ServiceOntario how the updated vehicle permit is delivered.
conditions: Only if you moved within Ontario

steps.title: Apply for OHIP at ServiceOntario
prepare: Three separate original documents: citizenship or immigration status, Ontario residency, identity
Tell the old province's health plan the moving date and ask when its coverage ends
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario removed the 3-month OHIP waiting period in 2020; eligible people are covered once eligibility is accepted.
2. The application is made in person with original documents.
3. Eligibility includes making Ontario the primary home and being physically present 153 days in any 12-month period.
4. Check the end date of the old province's plan so there is no gap.
conditions: Only if you moved to Ontario from another province

steps.title: Change the address with the Canada Revenue Agency
steps.howTo:
1. A change in CRA My Account takes effect right away; by phone it is also immediate, by mail 4 to 6 weeks.
2. The CRA does not pass the new address to other departments, so each one is told separately.
3. Benefit payments depend on current details, so updating before tax season avoids gaps.
4. The province lived in on December 31 is the one used for that year's provincial tax.

steps.title: Update the voter registration with Elections Ontario and Elections Canada
prepare: Ticking the Elections Canada box on the tax return also shares the address with them
steps.howTo:
1. Elections Ontario and Elections Canada keep separate lists; each has an online registration service.
2. Being registered at the current address avoids extra steps at the polls.
conditions: Only if you are a Canadian citizen

steps.title: Register the vehicle in Ontario
prepare: Safety Standards Certificate from an Ontario inspection station
steps.howTo:
1. Vehicles brought from another province are registered at ServiceOntario.
2. A Safety Standards Certificate is usually asked for first.
3. The 30 days here is an estimate; check the current deadline with ServiceOntario.
conditions: Only if you moved to Ontario from another province
Only if you own a vehicle

steps.title: Register with Health Care Connect for a family doctor
steps.howTo:
1. Health Care Connect refers people without a family doctor or nurse practitioner to one accepting patients.
2. Register online or by calling 8-1-1 with a valid health card.
3. The mailing address given has to match the health card record, so the health card address is updated first.
4. Waits vary by area.

steps.title: Get a card at the local library
prepare: Proof of the new address, such as a utility bill or the lease
steps.howTo:
1. Public library cards are free for residents of the library's area.
2. Cards from the old area often still work, but the home library changes with the address.

steps.title: Exchange the driver's licence
prepare: Original accepted identity documents with legal name and date of birth
Proof of driving experience, if the licence doesn't show it
steps.howTo:
1. New residents have 60 days to exchange a valid licence from another province for an Ontario licence.
2. Licences from other Canadian provinces can be exchanged; a vision, knowledge or road test may apply depending on the class and driving history.
3. Since May 11, 2026, applicants declare that Ontario is their primary residence.
conditions: Only if you moved to Ontario from another province
Only if you drive

steps.title: Claim the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit on rent (ON-BEN)
prepare: Addresses and rent paid for each home in the year
steps.howTo:
1. The credit is part of the Ontario Trillium Benefit; renters apply by filling in the ON-BEN form in the tax return, due April 30; move this step to that date.
2. It counts people resident in Ontario on December 31 whose landlord paid property tax on the home; rent at both Ontario addresses is listed.
3. Payments depend on where you live on the 1st of each month, so the CRA address matters. It repeats each year.
conditions: Only if you rent
Only if you live in Ontario on December 31

title: Buying a home · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for buying a home in British Columbia, from mortgage pre-approval and the down payment to completion, property transfer tax, title registration, and the yearly grants and declarations after.
conditions: You are buying a home in British Columbia to live in; the event date is the completion date
You are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, or fall under an exception to the federal ban on non-Canadians buying residential property in urban areas
Foreign nationals buying in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, the Capital Region, Central Okanagan or Nanaimo also pay the 20% additional property transfer tax

sources.title: Buying a home — CMHC
Home buyer rescission period — BC Financial Services Authority
Property transfer tax — Province of British Columbia
First time home buyers' program — Province of British Columbia
Newly built home exemption — Province of British Columbia
Additional property transfer tax — Province of British Columbia
Home owner grant — Province of British Columbia
Apply for the home owner grant — Province of British Columbia
Speculation and vacancy tax — Province of British Columbia
Empty Homes Tax — City of Vancouver
Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Withdrawals and transfers out of your FHSAs — Canada.ca
What is the Home Buyers' Plan — Canada.ca
How to participate in the Home Buyers' Plan — Canada.ca
Line 31270 – Home buyers' amount — Canada.ca
Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Regulations (SOR/2022-250) — Justice Laws
Renewing your mortgage — Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
Appeals — BC Assessment

steps.title: Get a mortgage pre-approval
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: Recent pay stubs and an employment letter
Notices of assessment for the last 2 years
Bank and investment statements showing the down payment
steps.howTo:
1. A lender or mortgage broker checks income, debts and credit and states how much it may lend and at what rate.
2. Pre-approval is not a final approval; the lender still reviews the specific property once an offer is accepted.
3. The rate hold usually lasts 90 to 120 days; check the letter.
4. Federal rules set a minimum down payment by price, and mortgage insurance with less than 20% down; the stress test applies to most mortgages.

steps.title: Plan the down payment from savings, FHSA and RRSP
conditions: Only if part of the down payment comes from an FHSA or RRSP
prepare: Check the current Home Buyers' Plan limit ($60,000 at review)
steps.howTo:
1. A First Home Savings Account (FHSA) allows a tax-free qualifying withdrawal for a first home; it can be combined with the Home Buyers' Plan (HBP) for the same home.
2. The HBP lets each first-time buyer withdraw from their RRSPs without tax, then repay it over 15 years.
3. RRSP contributions made within 90 days before an HBP withdrawal may not be deductible.
4. Both need a written agreement to buy or build before the money comes out; the withdrawal itself is a later step.
5. Not financial advice; the date here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Make an offer and sign the contract of purchase and sale
prepare: Subjects to include, such as financing, inspection and strata documents
steps.howTo:
1. The offer is usually written on the standard contract of purchase and sale through a licensed realtor.
2. Subjects (conditions) protect the buyer until they are removed; the contract lists a date for each.
3. The completion date is when money and title change hands; possession is often a day later.
4. Keep a signed copy; the lender, lawyer or notary and FHSA and RRSP issuers all ask for it.

steps.title: Know the 3-business-day rescission period
prepare: The date and time the offer was accepted
The purchase price, to work out the fee
steps.howTo:
1. Since January 3, 2023, buyers of most residential property in B.C. can cancel an accepted contract within 3 business days, without giving a reason.
2. Cancelling costs a fee of 0.25% of the purchase price, paid to the seller.
3. Notice is given in writing to the seller within the period; the right cannot be waived.
4. Some sales are excluded, such as property on leasehold land, sales by auction and sales under a court order; check the BCFSA page for the current list.

steps.title: Review the strata documents
conditions: Only if the home is a strata unit (condo or townhouse)
prepare: Ask the seller or the strata manager for the documents
steps.howTo:
1. The information certificate (Form B) from the strata corporation shows strata fees, special levies, the contingency reserve fund, bylaw issues and any lawsuits.
2. Minutes and the depreciation report show upcoming repairs and how they may be paid for.
3. Rental and pet bylaws are in the bylaws; check them against your plans.
4. The strata corporation can charge a capped fee for Form B.

steps.title: Remove subjects and pay the deposit
prepare: The lender's appraisal and final mortgage approval
steps.howTo:
1. Before the subject removal date, the buyer checks each subject: financing approval, inspection, strata documents, insurance and any others.
2. Home inspectors are licensed by Consumer Protection BC.
3. Once subjects are removed in writing, the contract is firm.
4. The deposit is often due within 24 hours of subject removal; the contract sets the timing.
5. It is held in trust, usually by the seller's brokerage, and counts toward the down payment.

steps.title: Hire a lawyer or notary, and arrange title insurance
prepare: The contract of purchase and sale
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. a lawyer or notary public handles the conveyance: the title search, the property transfer tax return, the mortgage documents and the transfer.
2. They order title insurance, which most lenders ask for, or confirm a survey.
3. For strata units they also get a Form F certificate of payment from the strata corporation.
4. Book early; they are busy near month-end.

steps.title: Finalize the mortgage
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: Anything the lender still needs, such as an updated pay stub
Proof of down payment for the last 90 days
steps.howTo:
1. The lender sends mortgage instructions to the lawyer or notary.
2. Mortgages are signed at the lawyer's or notary's office, usually in the week before completion.
3. Mortgage default insurance (CMHC or a private insurer) is added when less than 20% is put down.

steps.title: Withdraw from the FHSA and RRSP
conditions: Only if part of the down payment comes from an FHSA or RRSP
prepare: The signed contract of purchase and sale
steps.howTo:
1. FHSA: fill in Form RC725 and give it to the FHSA issuer; the home is to be acquired before October 1 of the year after the withdrawal.
2. HBP: fill in Form T1036 for each RRSP withdrawal; the home is to be bought or built before October 1 of the year after the withdrawal.
3. Issuers can take several business days; allow for that before the money is due at the lawyer or notary.
4. The plan is to live in the home as your principal residence within one year of buying it.

steps.title: Arrange home insurance from the completion date
prepare: For strata: the strata corporation's insurance summary and deductibles
steps.howTo:
1. Lenders ask for proof of insurance before they release mortgage funds.
2. For strata units, the strata corporation insures the building; owners insure contents, improvements and the strata deductible.
3. Coverage starts on the completion date.

steps.title: File the property transfer tax return and claim exemptions
prepare: Citizenship or permanent residence status for each buyer
Proof of living in B.C. for a year, or 2 B.C. tax returns in the last 6 years
steps.howTo:
1. Property transfer tax is paid when title is registered. General rates: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million, 3% above, and a further 2% on residential property over $3 million.
2. First time home buyers' program: at review, a full exemption on the first $500,000 for homes worth up to $835,000, partial up to $860,000.
3. Newly built home exemption: at review, a full exemption up to $1,100,000, partial up to $1,150,000.
4. Both exemptions need citizenship or permanent residence, use as the principal residence, and moving in within 92 days and staying through the first year.
5. Foreign nationals in the five listed regional districts add the 20% additional property transfer tax.
6. The lawyer or notary files the return; a missed exemption can be claimed as a refund between the first anniversary and 18 months after registration.

steps.title: Complete the purchase and register title
prepare: The balance of the down payment and closing costs, sent to the lawyer or notary
steps.howTo:
1. On completion day the lawyer or notary files the transfer and mortgage with the Land Title and Survey Authority (LTSA) and pays the seller.
2. The statement of adjustments splits property tax and strata fees between buyer and seller by date.
3. Keys are usually handed over on the possession date in the contract.
4. Keep the reporting letter from the lawyer or notary; it lists what was registered.

steps.title: Change your address
prepare: Account numbers for utilities, bank and insurers
steps.howTo:
1. Update the CRA in My Account, ICBC for the driver's licence and vehicle, and Health Insurance BC for MSP and the BC Services Card.
2. Set up BC Hydro, FortisBC gas or other utilities, and city water and garbage where billed separately.
3. Canada Post mail forwarding covers the gap.

steps.title: Apply for GST new housing rebates
conditions: Only if you bought a newly built or substantially renovated home
prepare: Check whether the builder already credited the rebate on the statement of adjustments
steps.howTo:
1. The GST/HST new housing rebate returns part of the GST on new homes below a price limit; builders often credit it at closing and claim it themselves.
2. The federal first-time home buyers' GST rebate, for agreements from May 27, 2025, can refund up to $50,000 on new homes up to $1 million, phasing out to $1.5 million; check the current rules and dates on canada.ca.
3. Apply through the builder or directly to the CRA; deadlines run from the completion date, typically 2 years.

steps.title: Claim the home owner grant, every year
conditions: Only if the home is your principal residence
prepare: Jurisdiction and roll number from the notice
Check the current assessed value threshold
steps.howTo:
1. The home owner grant lowers the property tax on a principal residence; it is claimed every year, not renewed automatically.
2. Property tax notices arrive in late spring; the grant is claimed online through the province, by phone or at Service BC, before the tax due date and no later than December 31.
3. Above the assessed value threshold ($2,075,000 for 2026) the grant shrinks and then stops; seniors and some others get a higher grant.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to your first property tax notice.

steps.title: Declare occupancy for Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax, every year
conditions: Only if the home is in the City of Vancouver
prepare: Folio number and access code from the notice
Who lived in the home in the past year
steps.howTo:
1. Every residential owner in the City of Vancouver declares the property's status each year, even when living in it.
2. The deadline is early in the year, usually early February; a late or missing declaration can make the home deemed empty and taxed.
3. Check the current rate and dates on vancouver.ca.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the next declaration window.

steps.title: Declare for the speculation and vacancy tax, every year
conditions: Only if the home is in a speculation and vacancy tax area
prepare: Letter ID and declaration code from the letter
Social Insurance Number for each owner
steps.howTo:
1. Owners in the taxed areas of B.C. get a declaration letter each year and declare online or by phone by March 31, even with no change.
2. Most owners living in their home as a principal residence are exempt, but only after declaring.
3. Each owner on title declares separately.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to when the letter arrives.

steps.title: Pay the property tax by the city's due date, every year
prepare: Whether the lender collects property tax with the mortgage
Claim the home owner grant before paying
steps.howTo:
1. Each municipality sets its own due date; many B.C. cities set it in early July.
2. A late payment adds a penalty set by the city; check the notice.
3. Most cities offer monthly pre-authorized payments, and some owners can defer the tax through the province's property tax deferment program.
4. This repeats every year; the date here is an estimate, so move it to the due date on the notice.

steps.title: Claim the home buyers' amount and report withdrawals on your tax return
prepare: Receipts for the lawyer or notary
steps.howTo:
1. The first-time home buyers' amount (line 31270) is up to $10,000, a federal credit of up to $1,500; it is for buyers who did not live in a home they or a spouse owned in the year or the 4 years before.
2. FHSA and HBP withdrawals are reported on the return for the year they happened.
3. The principal residence exemption is designated when the home is later sold, on the return for that year.
4. File for the year of the purchase by April 30 of the next year.

steps.title: Check the assessment notice and appeal by January 31 if it looks wrong
prepare: Recent sales of similar homes nearby
Anything wrong in the property details
steps.howTo:
1. BC Assessment mails notices early in January, valuing the home as of July 1 the year before.
2. Talk to BC Assessment first; a formal complaint to the Property Assessment Review Panel is filed by January 31 (moved to the next business day when it falls on a weekend).
3. The assessed value sets the property tax share and the home owner grant threshold.
4. This repeats every year; the date here is an estimate, so move it to when the notice arrives.

steps.title: Review and renew home insurance, every year
prepare: Changes to the home, renovations or valuables
For strata: the current strata deductible
steps.howTo:
1. Policies usually renew yearly; the insurer sends the renewal terms before the end date.
2. Check the coverage amount, deductibles, and whether earthquake or water damage cover is included.
3. The lender asks for proof of insurance to continue.
4. This repeats every year.

steps.title: Start repaying the Home Buyers' Plan
conditions: Only if you withdrew from an RRSP under the Home Buyers' Plan
documents: Notice of assessment showing the HBP balance
prepare: The amount due this year from My Account
steps.howTo:
1. Repayments usually start in the second year after the year of the withdrawal, and run over 15 years.
2. Temporary relief has pushed the start to the fifth year for first withdrawals in certain years; check the current rule on canada.ca.
3. A repayment is an RRSP contribution designated as an HBP repayment on Schedule 7; any amount not repaid is added to income for that year.
4. The date here is an estimate; the notice of assessment shows the real schedule.

steps.title: Renew or switch the mortgage before the term ends
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: The term end date on the mortgage
Quotes from other lenders or a broker
steps.howTo:
1. Move this date to about a month before the real term end; a 5-year term is assumed here.
2. A federally regulated lender sends a renewal statement at least 21 days before the term ends; other lenders follow provincial rules.
3. Since November 2024 a straight switch of the same balance and amortization to another lender at renewal generally skips the stress test; check current rules. Switching can bring legal, appraisal or discharge fees.
4. Left alone, some lenders renew automatically into a term and rate they choose, so compare before the date.

title: Buying a home · China
summary: Paperwork plan for buying a home in mainland China, from purchase eligibility and the online-signed contract to the down payment, mortgage, deed tax, property registration, handover and moving in.
conditions: You are buying a home in mainland China; the event date is the handover or registration date
The steps are for a mainland resident; buyers from Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan or abroad face other rules on eligibility and payment
Purchase limits, loan terms and fees are set city by city; check the local housing and urban-rural development bureau (住建局)

sources.title: Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration (不动产登记暂行条例) — gov.cn
State Council decision amending the Housing Provident Fund Regulations (住房公积金管理条例, State Council Order No. 844, effective September 20, 2026; check current) — gov.cn
Interim Measures for Individual Income Tax Special Additional Deductions (国发〔2018〕41号) — State Taxation Administration
Household Registration Regulations of the PRC (户口登记条例)
Tax policy library (契税 deed tax rules) — State Taxation Administration
Civil Code of the PRC (中华人民共和国民法典) — National People's Congress

steps.title: Check purchase eligibility in the city
prepare: Resident ID card and hukou book
Social insurance or tax records in the city, if you have no local hukou
steps.howTo:
1. Purchase eligibility (购房资格) is set by each city; many cities have relaxed or ended purchase limits (限购) since 2024, while some core districts of the largest cities still count homes per family and ask non-locals for months of local social insurance or tax.
2. The check is usually done through the local housing bureau (住建局) portal or by the developer or agent.
3. The family counted is usually you, your spouse and minor children.
4. Check the current local rule; it changes often.

steps.title: Plan the down payment and choose the loan type
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: Housing provident fund balance and contribution history
Ask the local fund centre (公积金中心) about loan limits
steps.howTo:
1. Loans are a commercial loan (商业贷款), a housing provident fund loan (公积金贷款) at a lower rate, or a combined loan (组合贷款).
2. The minimum down payment (首付) is set nationally and locally, and differs for a first and second home; check the current ratio in your city.
3. Provident fund loan limits depend on your balance, contribution years and the city cap.
4. Not financial advice; the date here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Sign the reservation and pay the earnest money
documents: Reservation agreement (认购书) or intention agreement
prepare: The unit or home details and price
steps.howTo:
1. A reservation agreement (认购书) with a developer, or an intention agreement through an agent for a resale home, holds the home before the formal contract.
2. Earnest money (定金) is usually lost if the buyer backs out, and returned double if the seller does; read the terms.
3. Check the developer's pre-sale permit (商品房预售许可证) or, for a resale home, the seller's property certificate and any mortgage on it.

steps.title: Sign the purchase contract online (网签)
prepare: Resident ID cards for all buyers
Names to go on the title
steps.howTo:
1. The purchase contract is signed and filed on the local housing bureau's online system (网签备案); this stops the same home being sold twice.
2. New homes use the standard commodity housing sale contract; resale homes use the local resale contract.
3. The contract sets the price, payment method, handover date and what happens if either side is late.
4. Many cities hold the buyer's funds in a supervised account (资金监管) until registration.

steps.title: Pay the down payment (首付)
prepare: Funds in your own bank account
steps.howTo:
1. The down payment goes to the developer or into the supervised account named in the contract.
2. Banks check the source of the down payment; borrowed money for it may not be accepted.
3. Some cities allow provident fund withdrawals toward the down payment; ask the local fund centre.

steps.title: Pay the special maintenance fund
conditions: Only if you bought a new home, or the resale home has no fund yet
documents: Maintenance fund receipt (维修基金缴存凭证)
prepare: The floor area in the contract
Ask the local rate per square metre
steps.howTo:
1. The residential special maintenance fund (住宅专项维修资金) pays for major repairs to shared parts of the building, such as roofs, lifts and pipes.
2. It is paid by the buyer of a new home, by area or as a share of the price; the rate is set locally.
3. Proof of payment is usually needed before handover or registration.

steps.title: Apply for the mortgage
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: Resident ID cards and marriage certificate
The online-signed purchase contract and down payment receipt
steps.howTo:
1. The bank, or the fund centre for a provident fund loan, reviews the application and signs the loan and mortgage contracts.
2. Fund centres decide on a loan within 10 days of accepting the application under the regulations as amended from September 20, 2026 (check current); banks set their own times.
3. The loan is released after the mortgage is registered or a pre-registration (预告登记) is made.
4. The 30 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Pay the deed tax (契税)
documents: Deed tax payment receipt (完税凭证)
prepare: Proof of how many homes the family owns
steps.howTo:
1. The buyer pays deed tax (契税) before the property is registered; many cities handle it in the same hall as registration.
2. From December 1, 2024, for a family's only home: 1% for 140 square metres or less, 1.5% above; for a second home: 1% for 140 square metres or less, 2% above. Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen may follow these rates for second homes once they drop the ordinary-housing standard. Check the current rule.
3. Without these reliefs the rate is set by each province within 3% to 5%.
4. For a resale home the seller may also owe VAT and income tax; the contract says who pays.

steps.title: Register the property and collect the property certificate
documents: Real estate title certificate (不动产权证书)
prepare: Resident ID cards for all buyers
Purchase contract, deed tax receipt and maintenance fund receipt
steps.howTo:
1. Property is registered at the local real estate registration centre (不动产登记中心); ownership passes on registration, not on payment.
2. For a resale home, transfer registration (转移登记) and mortgage registration are often done the same day, and many cities offer it online.
3. For a new home, the developer first registers the building; buyers' certificates can follow months after handover. Move this date to match.
4. The registration centre issues the real estate title certificate (不动产权证书); with a mortgage the bank may hold the mortgage certificate.

steps.title: Inspect the home and take the keys
documents: Residential quality warranty and user manual (住宅质量保证书, 住宅使用说明书)
prepare: Tools or an inspector for the handover check (验房)
The contract's area and fittings list
Meter readings for water, power and gas
steps.howTo:
1. At handover (交房) the buyer inspects the home (验房): walls, windows, water, power, drainage and measured area against the contract.
2. Defects are written on the handover form for the developer to fix; the developer's warranty periods are set in the residential quality warranty (住宅质量保证书).
3. For a new home, the developer shows the completion acceptance filing (竣工验收备案) before handover.
4. For a resale home, the seller settles utilities and property fees up to the handover date.

steps.title: Sign up with the property management company
documents: Property service contract (物业服务合同)
prepare: Ask the property fee rate and what it covers
steps.howTo:
1. The property management company (物业) runs shared areas, security and repairs; its fee is usually charged by floor area.
2. For new homes, a preliminary property contract signed by the developer binds buyers until an owners' committee (业主委员会) chooses otherwise.
3. Register access cards, parking and renovation plans here.

steps.title: Transfer water, power, gas and internet into your name
prepare: Real estate title certificate or purchase contract
steps.howTo:
1. Water, power and gas accounts are transferred (过户) at each supplier's office or online; many cities combine them with property registration (水电气联动过户).
2. Settle the seller's balances first for a resale home.
3. Internet and TV are signed up directly with a provider.

steps.title: Withdraw the housing provident fund for the purchase
conditions: Only if you or your spouse pay into a housing provident fund
prepare: Purchase contract, invoice or title certificate
Marriage certificate, for a spouse's withdrawal
steps.howTo:
1. The provident fund (住房公积金) can be withdrawn to buy or build a home, or to repay the loan on it.
2. Fund centres decide on a withdrawal within 3 days of accepting the application under the regulations as amended from September 20, 2026 (check current).
3. Whether a spouse or parents can withdraw for the same home, and time limits after the purchase, are set by the local centre.
4. Many centres offer the withdrawal in an app or online.

steps.title: Claim the housing loan interest deduction
conditions: Only if the home is your first home bought with a loan
steps.howTo:
1. Interest on a first-home loan can be claimed as a special additional deduction (住房贷款利息专项附加扣除), up to 1,000 yuan a month for up to 240 months.
2. A couple agrees which one of them claims it; the choice cannot change within a tax year.
3. Claim it in the 个人所得税 app through your employer or at the annual reconciliation.
4. Housing rent and housing loan interest cannot both be claimed for the same months.

steps.title: Move your hukou to the new home
conditions: Only if you want your hukou at the new address
prepare: Ask the local police station (派出所) about moving hukou by home purchase (购房落户)
steps.howTo:
1. Owning a home does not move your hukou; moving it is optional.
2. Many cities now let owners move hukou by home purchase; some set limits on area, time lived there or social insurance.
3. Apply at the police station for the new address, or online where offered; the 30 days is an estimate.
4. Hukou can matter for school places; check the local school district rules.

steps.title: Set up monthly loan repayment from the provident fund (公积金按月还贷 / 冲还贷)
conditions: Only if you borrowed and pay into a housing provident fund
steps.howTo:
1. Many fund centres let the balance repay the home loan automatically each month (按月提取还贷), or offset a provident fund loan directly (冲还贷).
2. It works for provident fund loans and, in many cities, commercial loans too; a spouse's account can often be added.
3. It is set up in the fund centre app, at the centre or at the lending bank; rules are local.
4. The date is only a prompt; it can be set up any time during the loan.

steps.title: Check for a local home purchase or deed tax subsidy (购房补贴 / 契税补贴)
prepare: Talent, family or hukou proof, if the subsidy asks for it
steps.howTo:
1. Many cities and districts pay a purchase subsidy (购房补贴) or refund part of the deed tax (契税补贴), often for first homes, families with several children, graduates or talent programmes.
2. Each has its own window, usually counted from the deed tax payment or registration date.
3. Check the city housing bureau or district government notices; schemes start and end often.

steps.title: Claim the income tax refund for replacing a home (换购住房个税退税)
conditions: Only if you sold your own home within a year before this purchase, in the same city, and paid income tax on the sale
documents: Tax payment certificate for the sale
prepare: Both contracts and deed tax receipt
steps.howTo:
1. A national policy lets a person who sells their home and buys another in the same city within a year have the income tax paid on the sale refunded, in full or in proportion to the new price.
2. The policy has a set end date and has been extended before; check current whether it covers your sale and purchase dates.
3. Apply at the tax office or in the 个人所得税 app.

steps.title: Check the school place rules tied to the home (学位 / 学区)
conditions: Only if you have or plan children who may use the home for a school place
prepare: The catchment (划片) the home falls in
Whether the home's school place has been used, and when
steps.howTo:
1. Many cities tie a public school place to the home and hukou, and limit how often one home can be used, e.g. one place per home per 6 years in some districts (学位占用).
2. For a resale home, a place already used by the seller's child can block a new one for years; ask the school or education bureau.
3. Catchments are redrawn; check the current year's rules.

steps.title: File the renovation plan with property management (装修备案)
conditions: Only if you plan to renovate
documents: Renovation filing (装修备案) and agreement
steps.howTo:
1. Before renovating, the owner files the plan with the property management company and signs its renovation rules; some ask for a deposit.
2. Load-bearing walls and shared parts cannot be changed; structural or gas work may need approval.
3. Work hours and waste removal follow the management rules.

steps.title: Pay the heating fee (供暖费) before the heating season
conditions: Only if the home has central heating, mostly in northern cities
steps.howTo:
1. In northern cities with central heating, the heating season usually starts around November 15; the fee is paid before it, by floor area.
2. It is paid to the heating company, often online; new owners may need to open or transfer the account.
3. It repeats every year; move this date to the local deadline.

steps.title: Check the property tax pilot (房产税试点)
conditions: Only if the home is in Shanghai or Chongqing
prepare: Hukou and number of homes the family owns
steps.howTo:
1. Shanghai and Chongqing run pilot property taxes on some personal homes; the rest of the mainland has none on personal homes for now.
2. Who pays depends on local rules such as hukou, the number of homes and price; check the local tax bureau.
3. It repeats yearly if it applies.

steps.title: Add a spouse to the title after marriage (不动产加名)
conditions: Only if you marry after buying and both want to be on the title
prepare: Bank consent, if the home is mortgaged
steps.howTo:
1. Spouses can be added to the title through a change registration at the real estate registration centre.
2. Changes of ownership between spouses during a marriage are exempt from deed tax.
3. A mortgaged home usually needs the bank's consent; the date is only a prompt.

steps.title: Get the loan settlement certificate and cancel the mortgage (结清证明 / 抵押注销登记)
conditions: Only if you borrowed to buy
documents: Loan settlement certificate (贷款结清证明)
prepare: Mortgage certificate held by the bank
steps.howTo:
1. After the final or an early full repayment, the bank issues a settlement certificate.
2. The mortgage is then cancelled at the real estate registration centre (抵押注销登记); many banks and cities do it online together.
3. Until it is cancelled, selling or re-mortgaging is harder.
4. This date assumes a 30-year loan; move it to the real payoff date.

title: Buying a home · Ontario
summary: Paperwork plan for buying a home in Ontario, from mortgage pre-approval and the down payment to closing, land transfer tax, title registration, and the warranty, tax and declarations after.
conditions: You are buying a home in Ontario to live in; the event date is the closing date
You are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, or fall under an exception to the federal ban on non-Canadians buying residential property in urban areas
Foreign nationals pay Ontario's 25% Non-Resident Speculation Tax, and in Toronto a further 10% municipal tax

sources.title: Buying a home — CMHC
Land transfer tax — Ontario.ca
Land transfer tax refunds for first-time homebuyers — Ontario.ca
Non-Resident Speculation Tax — Ontario.ca
Municipal Land Transfer Tax — City of Toronto
MLTT rebate opportunities — City of Toronto
Vacant Home Tax — City of Toronto
Homeowners — Tarion
Withdrawals and transfers out of your FHSAs — Canada.ca
What is the Home Buyers' Plan — Canada.ca
How to participate in the Home Buyers' Plan — Canada.ca
Line 31270 – Home buyers' amount — Canada.ca
Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Regulations (SOR/2022-250) — Justice Laws
Renewing your mortgage — Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
Request for Reconsideration — MPAC
Province of Ontario benefit programs — Canada Revenue Agency

steps.title: Get a mortgage pre-approval
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: Recent pay stubs and an employment letter
Notices of assessment for the last 2 years
Bank and investment statements showing the down payment
steps.howTo:
1. A lender or mortgage broker checks income, debts and credit and states how much it may lend and at what rate.
2. Pre-approval is not a final approval; the lender still reviews the specific property once an offer is accepted.
3. The rate hold usually lasts 90 to 120 days; check the letter.
4. Federal rules set a minimum down payment by price, and mortgage insurance with less than 20% down; the stress test applies to most mortgages.

steps.title: Plan the down payment from savings, FHSA and RRSP
conditions: Only if part of the down payment comes from an FHSA or RRSP
prepare: Check the current Home Buyers' Plan limit ($60,000 at review)
steps.howTo:
1. A First Home Savings Account (FHSA) allows a tax-free qualifying withdrawal for a first home; it can be combined with the Home Buyers' Plan (HBP) for the same home.
2. The HBP lets each first-time buyer withdraw from their RRSPs without tax, then repay it over 15 years.
3. RRSP contributions made within 90 days before an HBP withdrawal may not be deductible.
4. Both need a written agreement to buy or build before the money comes out; the withdrawal itself is a later step.
5. Not financial advice; the date here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Sign the agreement of purchase and sale
prepare: Conditions to include, such as financing, inspection and a condo status certificate
steps.howTo:
1. Offers are usually written on the standard OREA agreement of purchase and sale through a registered realtor.
2. Conditions protect the buyer until they are waived or fulfilled by the dates in the agreement.
3. Resale homes have no cooling-off period once the agreement is firm.
4. A new condo bought from a builder has a 10-day cooling-off period under the Condominium Act, counted from receiving the signed agreement or the disclosure statement, whichever is later.

steps.title: Review the condo status certificate
conditions: Only if the home is a resale condominium unit
prepare: Ask the condo corporation or the seller for the certificate
steps.howTo:
1. The status certificate from the condo corporation shows common expenses, arrears, special assessments, the reserve fund and any lawsuits.
2. The corporation has 10 days to deliver it, for a capped fee.
3. A lawyer usually reviews it as a condition of the offer.

steps.title: Waive conditions and pay the deposit
prepare: The lender's appraisal and final mortgage approval
steps.howTo:
1. Before each condition date, the buyer checks financing, inspection, the status certificate and any other conditions.
2. Once conditions are waived in writing, the agreement is firm.
3. The deposit is often due within 24 hours of acceptance; the agreement sets the timing. It is held in trust, usually by the listing brokerage.
4. For new builds, deposits are paid on a schedule set by the builder.

steps.title: Hire a real estate lawyer and arrange title insurance
prepare: The agreement of purchase and sale
steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario a lawyer handles the closing: title search, requisitions, land transfer tax, the mortgage and registration.
2. They order title insurance, which most lenders ask for, or confirm a survey.
3. They also decide how co-owners hold title, as joint tenants or tenants in common; ask them what fits.

steps.title: Finalize the mortgage
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: Anything the lender still needs, such as an updated pay stub
Proof of down payment for the last 90 days
steps.howTo:
1. The lender sends mortgage instructions to the lawyer.
2. Mortgage documents are signed at the lawyer's office in the week before closing.
3. Mortgage default insurance (CMHC or a private insurer) is added when less than 20% is put down.

steps.title: Withdraw from the FHSA and RRSP
conditions: Only if part of the down payment comes from an FHSA or RRSP
prepare: The signed agreement of purchase and sale
steps.howTo:
1. FHSA: fill in Form RC725 and give it to the FHSA issuer; the home is to be acquired before October 1 of the year after the withdrawal.
2. HBP: fill in Form T1036 for each RRSP withdrawal; the home is to be bought or built before October 1 of the year after the withdrawal.
3. Issuers can take several business days; allow for that before the money is due at the lawyer.
4. The plan is to live in the home as your principal residence within one year of buying it.

steps.title: Arrange home insurance from the closing date
prepare: For condos: the corporation's insurance summary and deductibles
steps.howTo:
1. Lenders ask for proof of insurance before they release mortgage funds.
2. For condos, the corporation insures the building; owners insure contents, improvements and their share of deductibles.
3. Coverage starts on the closing date.

steps.title: Pay land transfer tax and claim first-time buyer refunds
prepare: Citizenship or permanent residence status for each buyer
Whether you or your spouse ever owned a home anywhere
Check the current rates and refund limits
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario land transfer tax is paid when the deed is registered, by graduated rates on the price.
2. First-time buyers can get a refund of up to $4,000 at registration; the conditions include being 18 or older, never having owned a home anywhere, citizenship or permanent residence, and living in it within 9 months.
3. In Toronto the Municipal Land Transfer Tax is added on top, with a first-time buyer rebate of up to $4,475; higher graduated rates apply to high-value homes from April 1, 2026.
4. Foreign nationals add the 25% Non-Resident Speculation Tax across Ontario and, in Toronto, the 10% Municipal Non-Resident Speculation Tax.
5. The lawyer usually claims the refunds on registration; a missed refund can be applied for within 18 months.

steps.title: Close and register the deed
prepare: The balance of the down payment and closing costs, sent to the lawyer
steps.howTo:
1. On closing day the lawyer registers the transfer and mortgage electronically in the Ontario land registry and pays the seller.
2. The statement of adjustments splits property tax, utilities and condo fees between buyer and seller by date.
3. Keys are released once the funds and registration are done.
4. Keep the reporting letter; it lists what was registered.

steps.title: Change your address
prepare: Account numbers for utilities, bank and insurers
steps.howTo:
1. Update the CRA in My Account, ServiceOntario for the driver's licence, health card and vehicle.
2. Set up hydro, gas, water and internet in your name from the closing date.
3. Canada Post mail forwarding covers the gap.

steps.title: Send the Tarion warranty forms
conditions: Only if you bought a newly built home from a builder
prepare: A list of defects found since moving in
MyHome account on the Tarion website
steps.howTo:
1. New homes in Ontario carry a statutory warranty backed by Tarion: 1 year for workmanship and materials, 2 years for items such as water leaks and electrical, 7 years for major structural defects.
2. The 30-Day Form is sent within the first 30 days of possession; a Year-End Form can be sent in the last 30 days of the first year.
3. Submit through MyHome, and keep copies.

steps.title: Apply for HST new housing rebates
conditions: Only if you bought a newly built or substantially renovated home
prepare: Check whether the builder already credited the rebates on the statement of adjustments
steps.howTo:
1. The federal and Ontario HST new housing rebates return part of the HST on a new home used as a principal residence; builders usually credit them at closing and claim them from the CRA.
2. The federal first-time home buyers' GST rebate, for agreements from May 27, 2025, can refund up to $50,000 on new homes up to $1 million, phasing out to $1.5 million; Ontario has announced matching relief on its portion. Check the current rules on canada.ca and ontario.ca.
3. Apply through the builder or directly to the CRA; deadlines run from closing, typically 2 years.

steps.title: Set up property tax payments
prepare: Whether the lender collects property tax with the mortgage
steps.howTo:
1. The municipality bills property tax from the value set by MPAC; an interim bill early in the year and a final bill later are common.
2. Tell the municipality of the new owner if the lawyer has not; the first bill may still be in the seller's name.
3. Pre-authorized payment plans are offered by most municipalities.
4. The Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit is claimed on the income tax return for low- and moderate-income owners.

steps.title: Declare occupancy for Toronto's Vacant Home Tax, every year
conditions: Only if the home is in the City of Toronto
prepare: Assessment roll number and customer number from the bill
Who lived in the home in the past year
steps.howTo:
1. Every residential owner in Toronto declares the property's occupancy status each year, even when living in it.
2. A missing declaration makes the home deemed vacant and taxed at 3% of its assessed value; false declarations can also bring a fine.
3. The declaration window opens early in the year; check the current deadline on toronto.ca.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the next declaration window.

steps.title: Claim the home buyers' amount and report withdrawals on your tax return
steps.howTo:
1. The first-time home buyers' amount (line 31270) is up to $10,000, a federal credit of up to $1,500; it is for buyers who did not live in a home they or a spouse owned in the year or the 4 years before.
2. FHSA and HBP withdrawals are reported on the return for the year they happened.
3. The principal residence exemption is designated when the home is later sold, on the return for that year.
4. File for the year of the purchase by April 30 of the next year.

steps.title: Check the MPAC assessment notice and ask for reconsideration if it looks wrong
prepare: Recent sales of similar homes nearby
Anything wrong in the property details on AboutMyProperty
steps.howTo:
1. MPAC sends a property assessment notice when values are updated or the property changes, such as a new owner.
2. A Request for Reconsideration is free and is filed by the deadline printed on the notice, often 120 days from the notice date; check the notice.
3. After MPAC's answer, an appeal can go to the Assessment Review Board.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to when a notice arrives.

steps.title: Claim the property tax part of the Ontario Trillium Benefit
conditions: Only if your income is low or moderate
documents: Property tax bills for the year
prepare: Property tax paid on the principal residence for the year
steps.howTo:
1. The Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit counts property tax paid on a principal residence in Ontario.
2. It is applied for on Form ON-BEN with the income tax return; the CRA pays it as part of the Ontario Trillium Benefit, usually monthly from July.
3. Owners 65 or older may also get the Ontario Senior Homeowners' Property Tax Grant on the same form.
4. This repeats every year with the return; move the date to April 30.

steps.title: Review and renew home insurance, every year
prepare: Changes to the home, renovations or valuables
For condos: the condo corporation's deductible
steps.howTo:
1. Policies usually renew yearly; the insurer sends the renewal terms before the end date.
2. Check the coverage amount, deductibles, and whether sewer backup or overland water cover is included.
3. The lender asks for proof of insurance to continue.
4. This repeats every year.

steps.title: Start repaying the Home Buyers' Plan
conditions: Only if you withdrew from an RRSP under the Home Buyers' Plan
documents: Notice of assessment showing the HBP balance
prepare: The amount due this year from My Account
steps.howTo:
1. Repayments usually start in the second year after the year of the withdrawal, and run over 15 years.
2. Temporary relief has pushed the start to the fifth year for first withdrawals in certain years; check the current rule on canada.ca.
3. A repayment is an RRSP contribution designated as an HBP repayment on Schedule 7; any amount not repaid is added to income for that year.
4. The date here is an estimate; the notice of assessment shows the real schedule.

steps.title: Renew or switch the mortgage before the term ends
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
prepare: The term end date on the mortgage
Quotes from other lenders or a broker
steps.howTo:
1. Move this date to about a month before the real term end; a 5-year term is assumed here.
2. A federally regulated lender sends a renewal statement at least 21 days before the term ends; other lenders follow provincial rules.
3. Since November 2024 a straight switch of the same balance and amortization to another lender at renewal generally skips the stress test; check current rules. Switching can bring legal, appraisal or discharge fees.
4. Left alone, some lenders renew automatically into a term and rate they choose, so compare before the date.

title: Selling a home · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for selling a home in British Columbia, from listing and the mortgage payout to completion, the home flipping tax, non-resident clearance and the principal residence designation on the tax return.
conditions: You are selling a home in British Columbia; the event date is the completion date
Some steps apply only if the home was owned for a short time, was not your principal residence, or you are not a resident of Canada

sources.title: BC home flipping tax — Province of British Columbia
BC home flipping tax exemptions — Province of British Columbia
Principal residence and other real estate — Canada.ca
Form T2091(IND), Designation of a Property as a Principal Residence — Canada.ca
Residential property flipping rule — Canada.ca
Disposing of or acquiring certain Canadian property — Canada.ca
Breaking your mortgage contract — Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
Mortgage fees: prepayment penalties — Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
Home buyer rescission period — BC Financial Services Authority
Speculation and vacancy tax — Province of British Columbia
Empty Homes Tax — City of Vancouver
Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia

steps.title: List the home and prepare the seller's documents
documents: Recent property tax notice and assessment
prepare: Purchase date and price, and records of improvements
For strata: bylaws, minutes and the depreciation report, and a Form B from the strata corporation
steps.howTo:
1. Most sellers list with a real estate brokerage licensed by the BC Financial Services Authority; the listing agreement sets commission and term. Commission is subject to GST.
2. A property disclosure statement describes what the seller knows about the home; it is common but not mandatory in B.C.
3. Strata sellers are often asked for an information certificate (Form B) and recent strata documents.
4. Keep the original purchase papers and improvement receipts; they set the cost base if tax applies.

steps.title: Ask the lender for the payout amount and any prepayment penalty
conditions: Only if there is a mortgage or line of credit secured on the home
prepare: Whether you will port the mortgage to a new home
steps.howTo:
1. Paying off a mortgage before the term ends can trigger a prepayment penalty: often 3 months' interest on a variable rate, or the greater of that and an interest rate differential on a fixed rate. The contract sets the method.
2. Porting the mortgage to a new home, or having the buyer assume it, can avoid the penalty where the lender allows it.
3. Lenders also charge a discharge fee.
4. The payout statement is ordered for the completion date; the lawyer or notary usually requests it.

steps.title: Accept an offer and follow the subject dates
steps.howTo:
1. The contract of purchase and sale sets the price, subjects, and completion and possession dates.
2. Buyers of most residential property in B.C. can cancel within 3 business days of acceptance; they pay the seller 0.25% of the price if they do.
3. The sale is firm once the buyer removes subjects in writing; the deposit is then held in trust.
4. Keep a signed copy; the lawyer or notary, lender and tax filings all use it.

steps.title: Hire a lawyer or notary for the sale
prepare: Photo ID for each owner on title
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. a lawyer or notary public prepares the transfer and the seller's statement of adjustments, and pays out the mortgage from the sale money.
2. Sellers sign the transfer and a residency declaration in the days before completion.
3. The mortgage discharge is registered at the Land Title and Survey Authority (LTSA) after payout.
4. For strata units, a Form F certificate of payment shows strata fees are paid up.

steps.title: Complete the sale
prepare: All keys, fobs and remotes for the buyer
steps.howTo:
1. On completion day the buyer's lawyer or notary registers the transfer at the LTSA and the sale money is released.
2. The statement of adjustments splits property tax and strata fees between seller and buyer by date.
3. Keys are handed over on the possession date in the contract.
4. Keep the reporting letter and statement; they record the sale price and date for tax.

steps.title: Notify the CRA and ask for a clearance certificate
conditions: Only if you are not a resident of Canada for tax purposes
prepare: The contract and statement of adjustments
steps.howTo:
1. A non-resident seller notifies the CRA on Form T2062 within 10 days after the sale; the CRA then issues a certificate of compliance once tax is paid or secured.
2. Until the certificate arrives, the buyer's lawyer usually holds back 25% of the price (50% on certain property).
3. Late notice carries a penalty of $25 a day, minimum $100, maximum $2,500.
4. It is usually started before completion so the holdback is released sooner.

steps.title: Cancel insurance and utilities and change your address
prepare: Account numbers for BC Hydro, FortisBC, internet and insurer
steps.howTo:
1. Home insurance is cancelled from the day after completion, not before.
2. BC Hydro, FortisBC and other utilities close on the possession date with final readings.
3. Update the CRA in My Account, ICBC, and Health Insurance BC; the B.C. address change service updates several at once.
4. Canada Post mail forwarding covers the gap.

steps.title: File the BC home flipping tax return
conditions: Only if you owned the home for less than 730 days
documents: Contract of purchase and sale for both the purchase and the sale
prepare: Proof of any life circumstance for an exemption
steps.howTo:
1. From January 1, 2025, B.C. taxes the profit from selling a home owned for less than 730 days: 20% for up to 365 days, reducing to zero at 730.
2. A principal residence deduction of up to $20,000 applies if you owned it at least 365 days and lived in it.
3. Exemptions for life circumstances such as death, separation, illness, job loss or relocation still need a return to claim them.
4. The return is filed online through eTaxBC within 90 days after the sale.

steps.title: Check the last speculation and vacancy tax and Empty Homes declarations
conditions: Only if the home was in a speculation and vacancy tax area or the City of Vancouver
prepare: Who lived in the home during the year
steps.howTo:
1. The speculation and vacancy tax and Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax are declared once a year by owners; a letter can still arrive for a year you owned part of.
2. Declare if a letter arrives, even after selling, so no tax is charged by default.
3. The home owner grant is claimed each year only for a home you still own.
4. Check current rules on each page; the date here is an estimate.

steps.title: Report the sale and designate the principal residence on your tax return
documents: Statement of adjustments for the purchase and the sale
prepare: Years you owned and lived in the home
Purchase price, sale price and selling costs
Any other property you own that could also be designated
steps.howTo:
1. The sale of a principal residence is reported on Schedule 3, and the designation on Form T2091(IND), on the return for the year of the sale.
2. A late designation may be accepted, but a penalty can apply.
3. Under the federal flipping rule, a home held less than 365 days is taxed as business income with no principal residence exemption, unless a life event such as death, separation, a new job or illness applies.
4. Years it was not your principal residence, such as a rental or second home, can leave a taxable capital gain.
5. File by April 30 of the year after the sale (June 15 if self-employed, with any balance still due April 30).

title: Selling a home · China
summary: Paperwork plan for selling a home in mainland China, from ownership papers and the mortgage to the online-signed contract, supervised funds, seller taxes, the title transfer, handover and a possible tax refund on buying again.
conditions: You are selling a home in mainland China; the event date is the title transfer (过户) date
The steps are for an individual seller of a residential home
Taxes, fees and transfer procedures are set nationally and city by city; check the local housing bureau (住建局) and tax office

sources.title: Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration (不动产登记暂行条例) — gov.cn
Tax policy library (individual income tax, VAT and 换购住房 refund rules) — State Taxation Administration
Interim Measures for Special Additional Deductions of Individual Income Tax (2018) — gov.cn
Civil Code of the PRC (中华人民共和国民法典) — National People's Congress
Household Registration Regulations of the PRC (户口登记条例)

steps.title: Gather ownership papers and co-owner consent
documents: Real estate title certificate (不动产权证书)
Deed tax receipt (契税完税凭证)
prepare: Resident ID cards of all owners
steps.howTo:
1. Every registered owner signs, or signs a notarised power of attorney (委托公证); under the Civil Code a spouse's share in marital property usually needs consent too.
2. The original purchase invoice and deed tax receipt show the cost, which matters for income tax.
3. If a child in the family uses the home's school place (学位), selling can affect it; check the local education bureau rule.

steps.title: Pay off the mortgage or arrange a transfer with it (带押过户)
documents: Mortgage cancellation registration (抵押注销登记), or the lender's 带押过户 agreement
prepare: Funds for early repayment, or the buyer's loan approval
conditions: Only if the home still has a mortgage
steps.howTo:
1. The usual route is to repay the loan early, get the settlement certificate and cancel the mortgage at the registration centre.
2. Since 2023, transfer with the mortgage still on it (带押过户) has been promoted nationwide; the buyer's lender and yours coordinate so the title passes without paying off first. Availability depends on the city and banks; check current.
3. Banks often ask for early repayment to be booked weeks ahead.

steps.title: Sign the online contract and set up supervised funds (网签, 资金监管)
documents: Funds supervision agreement (资金监管协议)
prepare: Agreed price, payment schedule and handover date
Clauses on hukou move-out and school place
steps.howTo:
1. Second-hand sales are signed and filed in the city's online contract system (网签), usually through an agent or the housing bureau.
2. Many cities route the buyer's payments through a supervised account (资金监管) released to the seller after the title transfer.
3. The contract often sets a deadline and penalty for moving the hukou out.

steps.title: File and pay the seller's taxes
documents: Tax payment receipts or exemption record
prepare: Original purchase invoice and deed tax receipt
Renovation and loan interest receipts, if counted as costs
Proof it is the family's only home, if claiming the exemption
steps.howTo:
1. Income tax: exempt if the home was held for 5 years or more and is the family's only home (满五唯一); otherwise 20% of the gain with costs proven, or a deemed rate on the price (核定征收, often 1% for ordinary homes) where the city allows.
2. VAT: individuals selling a home held 2 years or more have been exempt; check current rules under the VAT Law in force from 2026.
3. Individuals selling a home are currently exempt from land appreciation tax and stamp duty; check current.
4. The buyer pays deed tax.
5. Taxes are usually paid at the tax window in the registration hall before the transfer.

steps.title: Complete the title transfer (过户)
documents: New title certificate issued to the buyer
prepare: Resident ID cards of all sellers and buyers
steps.howTo:
1. Buyer and seller apply together at the real estate registration centre (不动产登记中心); many cities combine registration and tax in one window.
2. The title passes when the registration is entered.

steps.title: Receive the sale money
documents: Bank record of the released funds
prepare: Seller's bank account named in the supervision agreement
steps.howTo:
1. Supervised funds and the buyer's loan are usually released within days of the transfer.
2. Timing depends on the bank and the contract.

steps.title: Hand over the home and settle the bills
documents: Handover record (交房确认书) with meter readings
prepare: Water, electricity, gas and heating accounts
steps.howTo:
1. Water, electricity, gas, heating and property management fees are paid up to the handover date, and the accounts are moved to the buyer.
2. The housing maintenance fund (维修基金) stays with the home.
3. Both sides sign a handover record with meter readings.

steps.title: Move the hukou out of the sold home (户口迁出)
prepare: Address and proof for the new registration
conditions: Only if anyone's hukou is registered at the sold home
steps.howTo:
1. The hukou is moved at the police station to a new home, a relative's household or a collective household (集体户).
2. The sale contract usually sets the deadline.

steps.title: Update mortgage or rent deductions in the tax app
conditions: Only if you claimed the mortgage interest deduction on this home, or now rent
steps.howTo:
1. The mortgage interest deduction (住房贷款利息) stops after the loan is repaid.
2. The rent deduction (住房租金) can apply once renting in a city of work, but not in the same month as mortgage interest.

steps.title: Claim the income tax refund on buying another home (换购住房退税)
documents: New home's purchase contract and deed tax receipt
prepare: Income tax receipt from this sale
conditions: Only if you paid income tax on this sale and buy a home in the same city within a year
steps.howTo:
1. A national policy refunds income tax paid on selling a home when a new home is bought in the same city within a year before or after the sale.
2. The refund is the full tax paid if the new home costs at least as much as the sold one, otherwise in proportion.
3. The policy has been extended before; check the current end date.
4. It is applied for at the tax office or online.

title: Selling a home · Ontario

Some steps apply only if the home was owned for a short time, was not your principal residence, or you are not a resident of Canada

prepare: Purchase date and price, and records of improvements
For condos: ask the condo corporation about a status certificate for buyers
steps.howTo:

2. Condo buyers usually make the offer conditional on the status certificate; the corporation has 10 days to deliver it, for a capped fee.
3. Keep the original purchase papers and improvement receipts; they set the cost base if tax applies.

steps.title: Ask the lender for the payout amount and any prepayment penalty
