3. Lenders also charge a discharge fee.
4. The payout statement is ordered for the closing date; the lawyer usually requests it.

steps.title: Accept an offer and follow the condition dates
documents: Waiver or notice of fulfillment of conditions
steps.howTo:
1. The agreement of purchase and sale sets the price, conditions and closing date.
2. Resale homes in Ontario have no general cooling-off period; the agreement is firm once the buyer waives or fulfils the conditions in writing.
3. The deposit is held in trust, usually by the listing brokerage.
4. Keep a signed copy; the lawyer, lender and tax filings all use it.

steps.title: Hire a real estate lawyer for the sale
prepare: Photo ID for each owner on title
steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario a lawyer answers the buyer's requisitions, prepares the seller's statement of adjustments, and pays out the mortgage from the sale money.
2. Sellers sign closing documents, including a declaration of residency and possession, in the days before closing.
3. The transfer and mortgage discharge are registered electronically in the land registry system.

steps.title: Close the sale
prepare: All keys, fobs and remotes for the buyer
steps.howTo:
1. On closing day the lawyers exchange documents and money, and the transfer is registered.
2. The statement of adjustments splits property tax and condo fees between seller and buyer by date.
3. Keys are released to the buyer's lawyer or agent once the deal closes.
4. Keep the reporting letter and statement; they record the sale price and date for tax.

steps.title: Notify the CRA and ask for a clearance certificate
conditions: Only if you are not a resident of Canada for tax purposes
prepare: The agreement and statement of adjustments
steps.howTo:
1. A non-resident seller notifies the CRA on Form T2062 within 10 days after the sale; the CRA then issues a certificate of compliance once tax is paid or secured.
2. Until the certificate arrives, the buyer's lawyer usually holds back 25% of the price (50% on certain property).
3. Late notice carries a penalty of $25 a day, minimum $100, maximum $2,500.
4. It is usually started before closing so the holdback is released sooner.

steps.title: Cancel insurance and utilities and change your address
prepare: Account numbers for hydro, gas, water, internet and insurer
steps.howTo:
1. Home insurance is cancelled from the day after closing, not before.
2. Hydro, gas and water accounts close on the closing date with final readings; rental water heaters are transferred to the buyer.
3. Update the CRA in My Account, and ServiceOntario for the driver's licence, vehicle permit and health card within 6 days of moving.
4. Canada Post mail forwarding covers the gap.

steps.title: Make the last Vacant Home Tax declaration
conditions: Only if the home was in Toronto or another city with a vacant home tax
prepare: Who lived in the home during the year
steps.howTo:
1. Toronto owners declare each property's occupancy status every year; a missing declaration can make the home deemed vacant and taxed.
2. A declaration can still be due for a year you owned the home, even after selling; check the city's page for who declares after a sale.
3. Ottawa and some other cities run similar taxes; check current rules.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the next declaration window.

steps.title: Report the sale and designate the principal residence on your tax return
documents: Statement of adjustments for the purchase and the sale
prepare: Years you owned and lived in the home
Purchase price, sale price and selling costs
Any other property you own that could also be designated
steps.howTo:
1. The sale of a principal residence is reported on Schedule 3, and the designation on Form T2091(IND), on the return for the year of the sale.
2. A late designation may be accepted, but a penalty can apply.
3. Under the federal flipping rule, a home held less than 365 days is taxed as business income with no principal residence exemption, unless a life event such as death, separation, a new job or illness applies. Ontario has no separate provincial flipping tax at review.
4. Years it was not your principal residence, such as a rental or second home, can leave a taxable capital gain.
5. Property tax paid for the part of the year you owned it can count toward the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit through ON-BEN.
6. File by April 30 of the year after the sale (June 15 if self-employed, with any balance still due April 30).

title: Buying a car · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for buying a car in British Columbia, from the history report and lien search to the transfer, PST and Autoplan insurance at a broker, and the recalls and renewals after.
conditions: You are buying a car, new or used, to register and drive in British Columbia; the event date is the purchase or delivery date
Steps marked for a private sale do not apply when buying from a licensed dealer

sources.title: Buy a used vehicle — ICBC
Steps to buying a used vehicle — ICBC
Vehicle history reports — ICBC
PST on vehicles — ICBC
Import a vehicle into B.C. — ICBC
Sell a used vehicle — ICBC
Buy, renew, update, or estimate your insurance — ICBC
Personal Property Registry — BC Registries
Vehicle Sales Authority of British Columbia
Defects and recalls — Transport Canada

steps.title: Get a vehicle history report and an inspection
conditions: Only if the car is used
prepare: The seller's vehicle registration (APV250), to match the VIN and owner
steps.howTo:
1. ICBC sells a vehicle claims history report for B.C. vehicles; private reports also cover other provinces and the U.S.
2. The report shows past claims, damage, and whether the car was ever branded rebuilt, salvage or flood-damaged; some flood-damaged vehicles cannot be licensed in B.C.
3. A mechanic's pre-purchase inspection finds what the report cannot.
4. Check that the name and VIN on the seller's registration match the seller and the car.

steps.title: Search for liens on the car
conditions: Only if you are buying from a private seller
prepare: A BC Registries account, or a card for the search fee
steps.howTo:
1. A lien is a debt registered against the car, such as an unpaid loan; it can stay with the car after the sale.
2. A serial number search in the B.C. Personal Property Registry, by VIN, shows registered liens; some private history reports include it.
3. If a lien shows, the seller pays it off and has it discharged before the money changes hands.
4. Licensed dealers are regulated by the Vehicle Sales Authority and clear liens themselves.

steps.title: Get an out-of-province inspection
conditions: Only if the car was last registered outside B.C.
documents: For imports from the U.S.: customs Form 1 and the RIV inspection record
steps.howTo:
1. A car coming from another province or country usually passes an inspection at a Designated Inspection Facility before it can be licensed in B.C.
2. Cars imported from outside Canada also go through the federal Registrar of Imported Vehicles (RIV) process first.
3. See ICBC's import page for what applies; the step here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Sign the Transfer/Tax Form and pay
documents: For a dealer sale: the purchase agreement
steps.howTo:
1. In a private sale, buyer and seller both fill in and sign the Transfer/Tax Form (APV9T) with original signatures; electronic signatures are not accepted.
2. The seller also signs the original registration (APV250) over.
3. Write the true price; PST is worked out on the price or the Canadian Black Book wholesale value, whichever is greater.
4. A dealer prepares the paperwork, collects GST and PST, and often registers the car for you.

steps.title: Transfer, register and insure at an Autoplan broker
prepare: Odometer reading, and the previous car's odometer if you had one, for usage-based discounts
Money for PST and the first insurance payment
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C., registration, licence plates and Autoplan basic insurance are all done together at an Autoplan broker; driving the car on the road needs valid insurance first.
2. New purchases are registered in the name of the licence holder within 10 days of purchase.
3. PST on a private sale is paid here. At review: 12% up to $124,999.99, 15% from $125,000, 20% from $150,000; from a dealer 7% under $55,000, rising in steps. Zero-emission vehicles have different thresholds; check the current ICBC PST page.
4. Some gifts between family members are PST-exempt; ask the broker.
5. Plates from a car you just sold or traded can often be moved to the new one; the broker explains the conditions.
6. Optional coverage (collision, comprehensive, higher liability) can come from ICBC or a private insurer.

steps.title: Wrap up the car you sold or traded in
conditions: Only if this car replaces one you sold or traded in
documents: Your copy of the Transfer/Tax Form
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. plates stay with the owner, not the car; the seller removes them before the buyer drives away.
2. The insurance is cancelled or moved to the new car at a broker; unused premium is usually refunded.
3. Keep a copy of the signed transfer form and the date and time of sale.

steps.title: Check for recalls and register with the manufacturer
steps.howTo:
1. Transport Canada's recall database lists safety recalls by make, model and year.
2. Registering with the manufacturer, or updating the owner on file, means recall notices reach you.
3. Recall repairs are done by the brand's dealers at no charge.

steps.title: Renew the insurance and registration, every year
prepare: Any change in drivers or use
steps.howTo:
1. Autoplan insurance and the vehicle licence renew together each year, at a broker or online.
2. ICBC sends a reminder before expiry; driving with expired insurance is an offence.
3. It repeats every year; the date here is the first renewal.

title: Buying a car · China
summary: Paperwork plan for buying a private car in mainland China, from a plate quota and trade-in subsidy to purchase tax, insurance, registration, inspections and licence points.
conditions: You are buying a private passenger car in mainland China; the event date is the purchase or delivery date
Plate quotas, subsidies and fees are set city by city; check the local traffic police and commerce bureau

sources.title: Announcement on continuing and optimising the NEV vehicle purchase tax reduction (财政部 税务总局 工业和信息化部公告2023年第10号) — gov.cn
Tax policy library (车辆购置税法, 车船税法) — State Taxation Administration
Traffic Safety Integrated Service Platform (交管12123) — Ministry of Public Security
Civil Code of the PRC (中华人民共和国民法典) — National People's Congress

steps.title: Get a plate quota in a quota city (摇号, 竞拍, 新能源指标)
documents: Vehicle quota certificate (指标确认通知书)
prepare: Hukou, or residence permit and months of local social insurance or tax
conditions: Only if you live in a city that limits new plates (e.g. Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Tianjin)
steps.howTo:
1. Some large cities limit plates: Beijing uses a lottery (摇号) with a separate new-energy queue, Shanghai auctions plates for fuel cars (竞拍), others mix lottery and auction.
2. New-energy cars often get plates more easily, but rules change; check current.
3. Applicants without local hukou usually show a residence permit and continuous local social insurance or tax.
4. A quota is valid for a limited time; the time here is an estimate and a lottery can take years.

steps.title: Check the scrappage or trade-in subsidy (以旧换新)
documents: Scrappage certificate (报废机动车回收证明) or used-car sale invoice
prepare: Old car's registration certificate and ID card
conditions: Only if you are scrapping or selling an old car in your name
steps.howTo:
1. National and local trade-in programmes pay a subsidy for scrapping an old car or replacing it with a new one.
2. Applications go through the national car trade-in platform (汽车以旧换新 platform, in the commerce ministry app) or the local one.
3. The amounts, eligible cars and deadlines are set each year and budgets can run out; check current.

steps.title: Collect the sales invoice and vehicle papers
documents: Unified motor vehicle sales invoice (机动车销售统一发票)
steps.howTo:
1. The dealer issues the unified sales invoice in the buyer's name; it is used for purchase tax, registration and any subsidy.
2. Check the VIN on the invoice, certificate and car match.

steps.title: Buy compulsory traffic insurance and pay vehicle tax (交强险, 车船税)
documents: Compulsory traffic accident insurance policy (交强险)
Vehicle and vessel tax receipt (车船税)
steps.howTo:
1. Compulsory traffic accident liability insurance (交强险) is bought before the car is registered or driven.
2. Commercial insurance (third-party, own damage) is optional and priced by the insurer.
3. The insurer collects the yearly vehicle and vessel tax (车船税) with 交强险; new-energy cars are exempt or reduced.
4. Both renew yearly.

steps.title: Pay vehicle purchase tax (车辆购置税)
steps.howTo:
1. Purchase tax is 10% of the price excluding VAT, declared within 60 days of buying; dealers often file it for the buyer.
2. New-energy cars bought in 2024–2025 were exempt up to 30,000 yuan per car; those bought in 2026–2027 pay half, with the reduction capped at 15,000 yuan per car.
3. Only models on the government's eligible list qualify.
4. The tax is paid before registration.

steps.title: Sign the car loan and register the mortgage on the car
documents: Mortgage registration on the vehicle (抵押登记)
conditions: Only if you are borrowing to buy
steps.howTo:
1. The lender records a mortgage on the car at the vehicle office, usually at or right after registration.
2. After the last payment, the lender gives the release papers and the mortgage is cancelled (解除抵押) at the vehicle office or through 12123.

steps.title: Register the car and get plates (上牌)
documents: Motor vehicle registration certificate (机动车登记证书)
prepare: Resident ID card, or residence permit if not local
Plate quota, in a quota city
steps.howTo:
1. Registration is done at the vehicle management office (车管所) or a dealer service point; many cities allow choosing a number in the 交管12123 app.
2. Most new cars skip a pre-registration inspection.
3. Temporary plates (临时号牌) cover driving before registration, for a limited time.
4. New-energy cars get green plates.

steps.title: Set up an ETC tag for tolls
conditions: Only if you use toll expressways
steps.howTo:
1. ETC (电子不停车收费) is issued by banks or the provincial expressway operator, often free.
2. Toll discounts for ETC vary by province.

steps.title: Install a home charger (充电桩)
conditions: Only if the car is electric or plug-in hybrid and you have a fixed parking space
steps.howTo:
1. The property management company (物业) usually confirms the space and wiring; the local grid company handles the meter.
2. Carmakers often include installation.
3. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Check licence points at the end of the scoring cycle (记分周期)
steps.howTo:
1. Each driving licence has 12 points per 12-month cycle, counted from the licence's first issue date.
2. Violations and fines show in the 交管12123 app; unpaid fines can block inspection.
3. Reaching 12 points leads to study and a test.
4. It repeats yearly.

steps.title: Get the inspection sticker or book an inspection (年检)
steps.howTo:
1. For a private car with up to 9 seats, the current pattern is: in-person inspection exempt in years 2, 4 and 8, with the mark applied for online in 12123; in-person inspection in years 6 and 10; then yearly after 10 years, and twice a year after 15 (check current).
2. It can be done within 3 months before the due date.
3. It repeats on that cycle.

title: Buying a car · Ontario
summary: Paperwork plan for buying a car in Ontario, from the Used Vehicle Information Package and safety certificate to insurance, registration and retail sales tax at ServiceOntario, and the recalls and renewals after.
conditions: You are buying a car, new or used, to register and drive in Ontario; the event date is the purchase or delivery date
Steps marked for a private sale do not apply when buying from a registered dealer

sources.title: Buy or sell a used vehicle in Ontario — Ontario.ca
Renew your licence plate sticker — Ontario.ca
Change your address on your driver's licence, vehicle permit and health card — Ontario.ca
Ontario Motor Vehicle Industry Council (OMVIC)
Defects and recalls — Transport Canada

steps.title: Get a vehicle history report and an inspection
conditions: Only if the car is used
prepare: The seller's vehicle permit, to match the VIN and owner
steps.howTo:
1. A private history report shows accidents, past registrations and whether the car was branded rebuilt, salvage or irreparable.
2. A mechanic's pre-purchase inspection finds what the report cannot.
3. Check that the name and VIN on the seller's vehicle permit match the seller and the car.

steps.title: Get the Used Vehicle Information Package from the seller
conditions: Only if you are buying from a private seller
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Highway Traffic Act, a private seller in Ontario gives the buyer a Used Vehicle Information Package (UVIP); the seller buys it from ServiceOntario.
2. It shows the registration history, any liens registered in Ontario, and the wholesale value used for tax.
3. If a lien shows, the seller pays it off and gets a discharge letter before the money changes hands.
4. The bill of sale on the back is filled in and signed by both.
5. Registered dealers are regulated by OMVIC, disclose history and clear liens themselves.

steps.title: Get a Safety Standards Certificate
conditions: Only if the car is used and needs a safety certificate to be plated
prepare: Book a Motor Vehicle Inspection Station (Ontario DriveON sign)
Agree with the seller who pays for repairs
steps.howTo:
1. A used car needs a Safety Standards Certificate before plates go on it in the buyer's name; the seller or buyer can get one, as agreed.
2. Only a licensed Motor Vehicle Inspection Station can issue it.
3. It is valid for a short time after the inspection (36 days at review; check current).
4. Ownership can be transferred without one, but the car is not plated for the road until it has one.

steps.title: Arrange car insurance before driving
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario auto insurance comes from private insurers or brokers; it is mandatory before the car is driven on the road.
2. The liability slip is shown at registration and carried in the car.
3. Optional coverages such as collision and comprehensive are extra; compare quotes.

steps.title: Register the car and pay retail sales tax at ServiceOntario
prepare: UVIP with the signed bill of sale
The vehicle portion of the seller's permit, signed
steps.howTo:
1. A private buyer registers the transfer at ServiceOntario within 6 days of the purchase.
2. Retail sales tax of 13% is paid at registration, not to the seller; it is worked out on the purchase price or the wholesale value, whichever is greater.
3. Some gifts between close family members are tax-exempt with a sworn statement; ask ServiceOntario.
4. Plates stay with the driver, not the car; use your own plates or get new ones.
5. A dealer collects HST and usually registers the car for you.

steps.title: Wrap up the car you sold or traded in
conditions: Only if this car replaces one you sold or traded in
documents: Plate portion of the vehicle permit
steps.howTo:
1. In Ontario the seller keeps the plates and the plate portion of the permit, and gives the buyer the vehicle portion and the UVIP.
2. The insurance is cancelled or moved to the new car; ask the insurer about any refund.
3. Plates not put on another car can be returned to ServiceOntario.

steps.title: Check for recalls and register with the manufacturer
steps.howTo:
1. Transport Canada's recall database lists safety recalls by make, model and year.
2. Registering with the manufacturer, or updating the owner on file, means recall notices reach you.
3. Recall repairs are done by the brand's dealers at no charge.

steps.title: Renew the insurance and check the plate renewal, every year
documents: Renewed insurance policy and liability slip
prepare: Any change in drivers, use or address
steps.howTo:
1. Insurance renews with the insurer each year; compare quotes before the renewal date.
2. Plates on passenger cars renew automatically each year for free if insurance is valid and there are no unpaid fines or tolls; others renew manually.
3. Address changes go to ServiceOntario within 6 days of moving.
4. It repeats every year; the date here is the first renewal.

title: Separation and divorce · British Columbia
summary: The paperwork after separating in British Columbia, counted from the date of separation: taxes and benefits, parenting and support, dividing property, wills, and divorce.
conditions: You and your spouse or partner have separated, and you live in British Columbia
Married, or unmarried and living in a marriage-like relationship
General information about the process, not legal advice

sources.title: Family justice — Province of British Columbia
Separation and divorce — Province of British Columbia
Parenting apart — Province of British Columbia
Child support — Province of British Columbia
Spousal support — Province of British Columbia
Dealing with property and debt — Province of British Columbia
How do I get my divorce certificate? — Province of British Columbia
Online Divorce Assistant — B.C. Ministry of Attorney General
BC Family Maintenance Agency
Change your name after marriage or divorce — Province of British Columbia
Family Law Act, S.B.C. 2011, c. 25
Wills, Estates and Succession Act, S.B.C. 2009, c. 13
Divorce and separation — Department of Justice Canada
Federal Child Support Guidelines — Department of Justice Canada
Spousal Support Advisory Guidelines — Department of Justice Canada
Change your marital status with the CRA — Canada.ca
Recommended consent letter for children travelling abroad — Travel.gc.ca

steps.title: Find free family justice help
prepare: Nearest Family Justice Centre or Justice Access Centre
Whether you qualify for Legal Aid BC
steps.howTo:
1. Family Justice Centres and Justice Access Centres offer free in-person and virtual help: information on options, parenting, support and property, and mediation with family justice counsellors.
2. Legal Aid BC publishes family law guides, and some people qualify for a legal aid lawyer.
3. If anyone is at risk, the province has safety planning resources and protection orders through the courts.
4. Many people also see a lawyer before signing anything.

steps.title: Gather financial records around the separation date
prepare: Last 3 years of tax returns and notices of assessment
Bank, investment, RRSP, TFSA and pension statements
Mortgage, loan and credit card statements
Proof of what each of you owned when the relationship began
steps.howTo:
1. Support and property both rely on income and asset records, and financial disclosure is part of both agreements and court cases.
2. Statements close to the separation date help show what existed then.
3. The date of separation matters for time limits, taxes and the divorce, so keep a note of it and anything that shows it.

steps.title: Review your will, beneficiaries and incapacity documents
prepare: Beneficiaries on RRSPs, TFSAs, pensions and life insurance
Who is named in your enduring power of attorney and representation agreement
Who is covered on your workplace health plan
steps.howTo:
1. Under B.C.'s Wills, Estates and Succession Act, once spouses separate in the legal sense, gifts to the former spouse in a will, and their appointment as executor, are revoked as if they had died first.
2. Beneficiary designations on registered plans and insurance are separate documents; each one is checked with the plan.
3. An enduring power of attorney or representation agreement naming the other person stays in place until changed; check each one.
4. Workplace plans have their own rules for how long a separated spouse stays covered.

steps.title: Consent letters for children travelling
conditions: Only if you have children who may travel with one parent
steps.howTo:
1. Canada recommends a consent letter signed by the other parent for a child travelling abroad without them; border officers may ask for it.
2. A parenting order or agreement may already say how travel and passports are handled.
3. A child's passport application asks about custody and parenting documents.

steps.title: Work out parenting arrangements
conditions: Only if you have children together
prepare: Parenting After Separation course certificate, if taken
steps.howTo:
1. B.C. uses the terms guardianship, parenting arrangements (parental responsibilities and parenting time) and contact.
2. Arrangements can be set out in a written agreement, worked out in mediation or with a family justice counsellor, or decided by the Provincial Court or Supreme Court.
3. The free online Parenting After Separation course is offered by the province; some court registries expect it before a first appearance.
4. Decisions are based only on the best interests of the child.

steps.title: Work out child support
conditions: Only if you have children together
prepare: Both parents' income for the last year
Costs of child care, health, school and activities
steps.howTo:
1. Child support in B.C. follows the Federal Child Support Guidelines: a table amount based on the paying parent's income and the number of children, plus a share of special expenses.
2. Shared or split parenting time changes the calculation.
3. The B.C. Child Support Recalculation Service can update the amount each year from new income, without going back to court.

steps.title: Look at spousal support
conditions: Only if either of you may ask for spousal support
prepare: Length of the relationship and of living together
steps.howTo:
1. Spousal support depends on each person's situation; there is no automatic right to it.
2. The federal Spousal Support Advisory Guidelines give ranges that courts and lawyers commonly refer to.
3. Under B.C.'s Family Law Act, a claim is made within 2 years after a divorce order, or 2 years after separation for unmarried spouses. Check current.
4. Spousal support paid periodically under a written agreement or order generally has tax effects for both people; child support does not.

steps.title: Tell the CRA you are separated
steps.howTo:
1. The CRA treats you as separated once you have lived apart for more than 90 days because of the breakdown of the relationship; the change dates back to the first day apart.
2. Tell the CRA by the end of the month after the month your status changed.
3. Update in CRA My Account or by phone (processed straight away), or mail form RC65 (4 to 6 weeks).
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the real deadline.

steps.title: Set up the Canada Child Benefit for the new arrangement
conditions: Only if you have children under 18
prepare: Which parent the children mainly live with
Parenting schedule, if time is shared
steps.howTo:
1. The Canada Child Benefit goes to the parent mainly responsible for the child's care.
2. When the children live with each parent 40% to 60% of the time, each parent can get half.
3. A parent not already receiving it applies through CRA My Account or form RC66.
4. Payments are recalculated on your own income from the month after the status change; BC Family Benefit follows automatically.

steps.title: Divide family property and debt
prepare: List of family property and debt, with values
Property each of you brought in, inherited or received as a gift
steps.howTo:
1. Under B.C.'s Family Law Act, married spouses and unmarried spouses who lived together in a marriage-like relationship for at least 2 years generally share family property and family debt equally.
2. Property one person had before the relationship, gifts and inheritances are generally excluded, though growth in value during the relationship may be shared.
3. Spouses can agree on a different split in writing.
4. Workplace pensions can be divided under the Family Law Act; the plan administrator has its own forms.

steps.title: Put the arrangements in writing
steps.howTo:
1. A written separation agreement records parenting, support and property terms.
2. An agreement can be filed with the court so parenting or support terms can be enforced like an order.
3. Terms that cannot be agreed can go to mediation, arbitration, or the Provincial Court (parenting and support) or Supreme Court (property and divorce).
4. Many people get independent legal advice before signing.

steps.title: Enrol support with the BC Family Maintenance Agency
conditions: Only if child or spousal support is payable under an agreement or order
prepare: Contact details for the other person
steps.howTo:
1. The BC Family Maintenance Agency (formerly FMEP) collects support and passes it on, and can enforce missed payments.
2. Either the person paying or the person receiving can enrol a filed agreement or court order.
3. Enrolment is voluntary; check current enrolment steps with the agency.

steps.title: Apply to split CPP credits
conditions: Only if either of you paid into the Canada Pension Plan during the relationship
prepare: Dates you lived together and separated
steps.howTo:
1. CPP pension credits earned while living together can be divided equally between the two of you (a credit split).
2. Divorced spouses can apply after the divorce; married spouses after living apart for at least 12 months; common-law partners after 12 months apart, with a time limit to apply.
3. Apply to Service Canada; check the current form and time limits.

steps.title: Apply for a divorce
conditions: Only if you were married and want a divorce
prepare: Original marriage certificate or registration of marriage
Parenting and support arrangements for any children
Check the current court filing fees
steps.howTo:
1. Divorce comes under the federal Divorce Act; the usual ground is living apart for at least 1 year.
2. In B.C. divorces go through the Supreme Court. A joint application can be prepared with the Online Divorce Assistant when both agree on everything.
3. An uncontested divorce is usually decided on the paperwork alone, without a hearing (a desk order divorce).
4. The court checks that reasonable arrangements are in place for child support before granting it.
5. The divorce takes effect 31 days after the order.

steps.title: Get the divorce certificate
conditions: Only if you were married and a divorce order was made
steps.howTo:
1. Once the divorce takes effect, a certificate of divorce can be requested from the Supreme Court registry where the file is.
2. Keep a copy; it is asked for when remarrying, changing a name back, and for CPP credit splitting.

steps.title: Go back to a previous last name
conditions: Only if you want to use a previous last name again
prepare: Documents linking the previous and current last names
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. a birth surname or a surname from an earlier marriage can be used again without a legal change of name.
2. Start with MSP and the BC Services Card and driver's licence; updated provincial ID makes other changes easier.
3. Then update the SIN record, passport, banks and employer; each has its own document list.

steps.title: Time limit for property and support claims
conditions: Only if property, debt or spousal support is not yet settled
steps.howTo:
1. Under B.C.'s Family Law Act, unmarried spouses apply to divide property within 2 years of separating.
2. Married spouses apply within 2 years after the divorce order.
3. The date here is 2 years after separation; for married spouses, move it to 2 years after the divorce order. Check current.

title: Divorce · China
summary: Paperwork plan for a divorce in mainland China, counted from the day the joint application is made at a marriage registration office: the agreement, the 30-day cooling-off period, the divorce certificate, and then hukou, property, children, tax, insurance and beneficiaries. A court route is noted for when there is no agreement.
conditions: You are ending a marriage registered in mainland China, and both of you are mainland residents
The dates assume a divorce by registration (协议离婚) with the application made on the plan date; a court divorce follows its own timetable
With a foreign, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan spouse, other offices and documents apply

sources.title: Marriage Registration Regulations (婚姻登记条例), State Council Decree No. 804 — gov.cn
Marriage registration "全国通办" policy Q&A (Ministry of Civil Affairs officials) — Luohu District Civil Affairs Bureau, Shenzhen
Civil Code of the PRC (中华人民共和国民法典) — National People's Congress
Civil Code, Book Five: Marriage and Family — Suixi County Government
Household Registration Regulations of the PRC (户口登记条例)
Interim Measures for Individual Income Tax Special Additional Deductions (国发〔2018〕41号) — State Taxation Administration
Employee medical insurance personal accounts can be used for close relatives — gov.cn
State Taxation Administration

steps.title: Draw up the divorce agreement (离婚协议书)
documents: Divorce agreement signed by both, several copies
prepare: List of joint property, savings, vehicles and debts
Arrangements for any children: who they live with, support, visits
steps.howTo:
1. Divorce by registration needs both to agree to divorce and on the children, property and debts; the agreement sets these out.
2. The registry checks that it covers children and property; many offices have a template.
3. Under the Civil Code, a child under 2 generally lives with the mother; for a child of 8 or older, the child's own wishes are respected.
4. Some people have the agreement reviewed by a lawyer or a legal aid centre; the time here is an estimate.

steps.title: Gather the documents for the registry
prepare: Ask the office about photos, copies and booking
steps.howTo:
1. Under the 2025 Marriage Registration Regulations, each side brings a resident ID card and the marriage certificate, plus the signed agreement.
2. A lost marriage certificate can be reissued first (补领) at a registry.
3. Offices usually take bookings through the local civil affairs app or mini-program.

steps.title: Apply together at the marriage registration office
documents: Application receipt (离婚登记申请受理回执单)
prepare: ID cards, marriage certificates and the agreement
steps.howTo:
1. Both apply in person at a county-level marriage registration office (婚姻登记处).
2. Since May 10, 2025, two mainland residents can apply at any registry in the country (全国通办); the certificate is then collected at the same office that took the application.
3. The office gives a receipt with the date; the cooling-off period counts from it.

steps.title: Cooling-off period ends (离婚冷静期)
steps.howTo:
1. Under Civil Code Article 1077, within 30 days of the registry receiving the application, either side can withdraw it.
2. Withdrawing is done at the same office.
3. Nothing else is filed in this period.

steps.title: Return together for the divorce certificate (离婚证)
prepare: ID cards, marriage certificates, the agreement and the receipt
steps.howTo:
1. Within 30 days after the cooling-off period ends, both return in person to the same office.
2. If neither goes back within that window, the application is treated as withdrawn and the process starts again.
3. The office checks the agreement and issues the certificates on the spot; the marriage ends on that date.
4. The certificate and agreement are needed for most of the steps below.

steps.title: Court divorce (诉讼离婚), if there is no agreement
prepare: Evidence on property, children and grounds
conditions: Only if one side does not agree to divorce, or on the terms
steps.howTo:
1. The suit is filed at the basic people's court, usually where the defendant lives; the court tries mediation first.
2. Under Civil Code Article 1079, divorce is granted where mutual affection has broken down, e.g. after two years living apart, domestic violence or bigamy; if a divorce is refused and the couple live apart for another year after the judgment, a later suit is granted.
3. The cooling-off period does not apply to court divorces.
4. The divorce takes effect when the judgment or mediation document becomes effective; it takes the place of the registry steps above.
5. Ordinary procedure is set at about 6 months and the simplified procedure 3 months; these are estimates.

steps.title: Update the hukou: marital status, splitting or moving it (分户/迁户)
prepare: Proof of a new home, if moving
conditions: Only if the two of you share a household register, or you want to update your marital status there
steps.howTo:
1. Marital status on the household register is updated at the local police station.
2. Someone registered in the other spouse's household can move out or set up a separate household (分户); the conditions are local.
3. Moving the hukou elsewhere follows the receiving city's rules.
4. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Set up child support and custody arrangements
documents: Agreement or judgment terms on the children
prepare: Payment method and dates for support
conditions: Only if you have children under 18 or not yet self-supporting
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Civil Code, both parents keep their rights and duties toward the children after divorce.
2. The parent the child does not live with pays support as agreed or ordered; either side can later ask the court to change it.
3. The parent not living with the child has a right to visit.
4. A bank transfer with a note keeps a record of each payment.

steps.title: Reassign tax deductions for the children (子女教育)
documents: Updated deduction declaration in the individual income tax app
prepare: Which parent claims, and the share
conditions: Only if either of you claims deductions for children or a home loan
steps.howTo:
1. The children's education and infant care deductions are claimed 100% by one parent or 50% by each.
2. Mortgage interest and rent deductions also follow who holds the loan or lease after the divorce.
3. Changes are made in the individual income tax app and confirmed each December for the next year.

steps.title: Unlink medical insurance family sharing (医保共济)
prepare: Medical insurance app or local medical insurance office
conditions: Only if one of you shared an employee medical insurance personal account with the other
steps.howTo:
1. Employee medical insurance personal accounts can be shared with close relatives (家庭共济), linked through the medical insurance app.
2. A former spouse is no longer a close relative; the link is removed in the same app.

steps.title: Transfer the home and other registered property
documents: New real estate certificate (不动产权证书)
Vehicle registration, if a car moves
conditions: Only if a home, car or other registered property changes hands
steps.howTo:
1. Real estate is re-registered at the local real estate registration centre (不动产登记中心), using the certificate and the agreement or judgment.
2. Under a 2021 Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration announcement, a change in home ownership from splitting joint property on divorce is exempt from deed tax.
3. Vehicles are transferred at the vehicle management office (车管所).
4. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Change the mortgage or provident fund loan
documents: Lender's written consent or new loan contract
prepare: Income proof of the person keeping the loan
conditions: Only if there is a bank mortgage or housing provident fund loan on a shared home
steps.howTo:
1. The divorce agreement does not change the loan contract; the lender decides whether to remove a borrower or change the loan.
2. Provident fund loans are handled by the local fund centre, bank loans by the bank.
3. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Update the will, beneficiaries and emergency contacts
documents: Updated will or insurance beneficiary forms
steps.howTo:
1. After divorce, a former spouse is no longer a statutory heir under the Civil Code.
2. A named beneficiary on an insurance policy stays until changed with the insurer.
3. Employers, schools and banks may hold a former spouse as an emergency contact.

title: Separation and divorce · Ontario
summary: The paperwork after separating in Ontario, counted from the date of separation: taxes and benefits, parenting and support, dividing property, wills, and divorce.
conditions: You and your spouse or partner have separated, and you live in Ontario
Married, or unmarried and living together
General information about the process, not legal advice

steps.title: Find free family law help
prepare: Nearest family court and its Family Law Information Centre
Whether you qualify for Legal Aid Ontario
steps.howTo:
1. Family Law Information Centres at family courts offer free information on separation and divorce, referrals, and Legal Aid Ontario duty counsel who explain the law that applies.
2. Government-funded family mediation is offered at family courts, with fees based on income.
3. If anyone is at risk, restraining orders are available through the courts, along with victim support services.
4. Many people also see a lawyer before signing anything.

steps.title: Gather financial records as of the separation date
prepare: Last 3 years of tax returns and notices of assessment
Bank, investment, RRSP, TFSA and pension statements on the separation date
Mortgage, loan and credit card statements
Values of what each of you owned on the date of marriage
steps.howTo:
1. Support and property both rely on income and asset records, and financial disclosure is part of both agreements and court cases.
2. For married spouses, the separation date is usually the valuation date for dividing property, so statements from that date matter.
3. The date of separation also affects time limits, taxes and the divorce, so keep a note of it and anything that shows it.

steps.title: Review your will, beneficiaries and powers of attorney
prepare: Beneficiaries on RRSPs, TFSAs, pensions and life insurance
Who is named in your powers of attorney for property and personal care
Who is covered on your workplace health plan
steps.howTo:
1. Since January 1, 2022, under Ontario's Succession Law Reform Act, a separated married spouse is treated as having died first for gifts and appointments in a will, once the spouses have lived apart for 3 years, or have a separation agreement, court order or family arbitration award settling their rights.
2. Beneficiary designations on registered plans and insurance are separate documents; each one is checked with the plan.
3. Powers of attorney naming the other person stay in place until changed; check each one.
4. Workplace plans have their own rules for how long a separated spouse stays covered.

steps.title: Consent letters for children travelling
conditions: Only if you have children who may travel with one parent
steps.howTo:
1. Canada recommends a consent letter signed by the other parent for a child travelling abroad without them; border officers may ask for it.
2. A parenting order or agreement may already say how travel and passports are handled.
3. A child's passport application asks about custody and parenting documents.

steps.title: Work out parenting arrangements
conditions: Only if you have children together
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario uses the terms decision-making responsibility, parenting time and contact.
2. Arrangements can be set out in a written parenting plan or separation agreement, worked out in mediation, or decided by the Ontario Court of Justice or the Superior Court of Justice.
3. In a court case about parenting or support, both people usually attend the Mandatory Information Program early on; check current rules.
4. Decisions are based only on the best interests of the child.

steps.title: Work out child support
conditions: Only if you have children together
prepare: Both parents' income for the last year
Costs of child care, health, school and activities
steps.howTo:
1. Child support in Ontario follows the child support guidelines, which use the federal tables: a table amount based on the paying parent's income and the number of children, plus a share of special expenses.
2. Shared or split parenting time changes the calculation.
3. Parents exchange income information each year so the amount can be updated.

steps.title: Look at spousal support
conditions: Only if either of you may ask for spousal support
prepare: Length of the relationship and of living together
steps.howTo:
1. Spousal support depends on each person's situation; there is no automatic right to it.
2. Under Ontario's Family Law Act, unmarried partners can claim if they lived together for at least 3 years, or had a child together in a relationship of some permanence.
3. The federal Spousal Support Advisory Guidelines give ranges that courts and lawyers commonly refer to.
4. Time limits can apply, especially for unmarried partners; check current.
5. Spousal support paid periodically under a written agreement or order generally has tax effects for both people; child support does not.

steps.title: Tell the CRA you are separated
steps.howTo:
1. The CRA treats you as separated once you have lived apart for more than 90 days because of the breakdown of the relationship; the change dates back to the first day apart.
2. Tell the CRA by the end of the month after the month your status changed.
3. Update in CRA My Account or by phone (processed straight away), or mail form RC65 (4 to 6 weeks).
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the real deadline.

steps.title: Set up the Canada Child Benefit for the new arrangement
conditions: Only if you have children under 18
prepare: Which parent the children mainly live with
Parenting schedule, if time is shared
steps.howTo:
1. The Canada Child Benefit goes to the parent mainly responsible for the child's care.
2. When the children live with each parent 40% to 60% of the time, each parent can get half.
3. A parent not already receiving it applies through CRA My Account or form RC66.
4. Payments are recalculated on your own income from the month after the status change; the Ontario Child Benefit follows automatically.

steps.title: Divide property and debt
prepare: Each spouse's property and debts on the separation date and on the marriage date
Gifts and inheritances received during the marriage
steps.howTo:
1. Married spouses in Ontario share the growth in wealth during the marriage through an equalization of net family property: the spouse with the higher net family property generally pays the other half the difference.
2. The matrimonial home has special rules: both spouses have an equal right to live in it whatever the title says, and neither can sell or mortgage it without the other's consent.
3. Unmarried partners have no automatic property division under the Family Law Act; property generally stays with the owner unless a court finds otherwise.
4. Spouses can agree on a different split in a written domestic contract.
5. Workplace pensions have a family law value that the plan administrator calculates on request.

steps.title: Put the arrangements in writing
steps.howTo:
1. A separation agreement is a domestic contract under Ontario's Family Law Act; it is in writing, signed by both people and witnessed.
2. Support terms in an agreement can be filed with the court so they can be enforced like an order.
3. Terms that cannot be agreed can go to mediation, arbitration or family court.
4. Many people get independent legal advice before signing.

steps.title: Register support with the Family Responsibility Office
conditions: Only if child or spousal support is payable under an agreement or order
prepare: Court order, or agreement filed with the court
Contact details for the other person
steps.howTo:
1. The Family Responsibility Office (FRO) collects support and passes it on, and can enforce missed payments.
2. Support orders made by an Ontario court generally go to FRO automatically; an agreement is first filed with the court and then registered.
3. Once registered, the first payment usually reaches the recipient within 30 to 60 days.
4. Both people can jointly choose to withdraw from FRO in some cases; check current.

steps.title: Apply to split CPP credits
conditions: Only if either of you paid into the Canada Pension Plan during the relationship
prepare: Dates you lived together and separated
steps.howTo:
1. CPP pension credits earned while living together can be divided equally between the two of you (a credit split).
2. Divorced spouses can apply after the divorce; married spouses after living apart for at least 12 months; common-law partners after 12 months apart, with a time limit to apply.
3. Apply to Service Canada; check the current form and time limits.

steps.title: Apply for a divorce
conditions: Only if you were married and want a divorce
prepare: Original marriage certificate or registration of marriage
Parenting and support arrangements for any children
Check the current court filing fees
steps.howTo:
1. Divorce comes under the federal Divorce Act; the usual ground is living apart for at least 1 year.
2. In Ontario divorces go through the Superior Court of Justice, including its Family Court Branch.
3. A simple divorce (one spouse applies) or a joint divorce (both apply together) can be filed online.
4. The court checks that reasonable arrangements are in place for child support before granting it.
5. The divorce takes effect 31 days after the order.

steps.title: Get the certificate of divorce
conditions: Only if you were married and a divorce order was made
steps.howTo:
1. Once the divorce takes effect, a certificate of divorce can be requested from the court office where the file is.
2. Keep a copy; it is asked for when remarrying, changing a name back, and for CPP credit splitting.

steps.title: Go back to a previous last name
conditions: Only if you want to use a previous last name again
prepare: Documents linking the previous and current last names
steps.howTo:
1. If the married name was legally changed through the old Election to Change Surname service, the Election to Resume Former Surname (Form 2) goes to the ServiceOntario Office of the Registrar General; the fee is $25 and processing takes 6 to 8 weeks. Check current.
2. If the married name was only used, not legally changed, ask each office which documents it accepts to go back.
3. Update the health card and driver's licence at ServiceOntario, then the SIN record, passport, banks and employer.

steps.title: Time limit for property claims
conditions: Only if you were married and property is not yet settled
steps.howTo:
1. Under Ontario's Family Law Act, a married spouse applies for an equalization of net family property by the earliest of 2 years after the divorce and 6 years after separation.
2. The date here is 6 years after separation; if a divorce came earlier, move it to 2 years after the divorce. Check current.

title: Caring for a family member · British Columbia
summary: Paperwork plan for caring for a seriously ill family member from British Columbia: the medical certificate, job-protected leave, EI caregiving benefits, legal authority, home and long-term care, and tax credits.
conditions: You live in British Columbia and are caring for or supporting a family member, or someone like family, who is seriously ill, injured or near the end of life
The event date is when the care starts or you stop working to give it

steps.title: Get a medical certificate for the person you care for
documents: Medical certificate for EI caregiving benefits
prepare: The person's written consent to share medical information
Name of their doctor or nurse practitioner
steps.howTo:
1. A medical doctor or nurse practitioner certifies that the person is critically ill or injured, or needs end-of-life care (a significant risk of death within 26 weeks).
2. The same certificate supports the EI claim and the leave from work.
3. Service Canada has its own certificate forms; ask the doctor to use the one for the benefit you apply for.

steps.title: Arrange job-protected leave with your employer
conditions: Only if you are an employee covered by the BC Employment Standards Act (not federally regulated work)
prepare: Medical certificate, once you have it
steps.howTo:
1. Compassionate care leave: up to 27 weeks in a 52-week period, for a family member expected to die within 26 weeks.
2. Critical illness or injury leave: up to 36 weeks for a child, or up to 16 weeks for a family member 19 or older.
3. Family responsibility leave: up to 5 days each employment year for a child or immediate family member.
4. These leaves are unpaid; EI benefits can replace part of the income.

steps.title: Apply for EI caregiving benefits
conditions: Only if you stopped or cut back work and have enough insured hours, or opted in as self-employed
prepare: Details of the person cared for
steps.howTo:
1. Compassionate care benefits: up to 26 weeks. Family caregiver benefit for adults: up to 15 weeks. Family caregiver benefit for children: up to 35 weeks.
2. Apply online as soon as you stop working; waiting more than 4 weeks after the last day of work can cost benefits.
3. Eligibility usually needs 600 insured hours in the last 52 weeks; check current.
4. Several family members can share the weeks, at the same time or one after another.

steps.title: Set up legal authority to act for them
conditions: Only if the person may need someone to handle their money, health or personal care decisions
prepare: The person's wishes, while they can still give them
Who will act, and an alternate
steps.howTo:
1. An enduring power of attorney covers financial and legal matters.
2. A representation agreement covers health and personal care; a standard one (section 7) can be made even when capacity is reduced.
3. An advance directive records the person's own health care instructions.
4. The person makes these while capable; if they can no longer do so, a court committeeship or the Public Guardian and Trustee may be involved.
5. Not legal advice; a lawyer or notary can help.

steps.title: Ask the health authority for a home and community care assessment
prepare: What help is needed each day
steps.howTo:
1. Contact the home and community care office of the regional health authority; a doctor or hospital can also refer.
2. A case manager assesses needs for home support, nursing, adult day programs, respite or assisted living.
3. Long-term care is also arranged through the health authority; publicly funded care costs are based on income.

steps.title: Check their Fair PharmaCare registration
conditions: Only if the person lives in British Columbia and has MSP coverage
prepare: Their notice of assessment, for income
steps.howTo:
1. Fair PharmaCare helps with prescription costs based on family net income, not age.
2. Registration is free and done online or by phone.
3. Income is checked each year from the tax return, so their return needs filing.

steps.title: Apply for the disability tax credit for them
conditions: Only if the person has a severe and prolonged impairment
prepare: Name of the medical practitioner who will certify
steps.howTo:
1. Part A of form T2201 is filled in by the person or their representative; Part B by a medical practitioner (can be submitted digitally).
2. If approved, an unused disability amount can be transferred to a supporting relative.
3. The DTC also opens the Registered Disability Savings Plan and the Child Disability Benefit.

steps.title: Claim caregiver and medical expense credits on your return
steps.howTo:
1. The Canada caregiver amount is for supporting a spouse, partner or dependant with a physical or mental impairment.
2. A provincial caregiver amount, where it applies, is claimed on the BC428; check current.
3. Medical expenses paid for a dependant can be claimed, subject to income limits.
4. This date is an estimate; move it to the next April 30. It repeats every year while you give care.

steps.title: Set up powers of attorney to act for them

prepare: The person's wishes, while they can still give them

steps.title: Ask Ontario Health atHome for a care assessment
prepare: What help is needed each day
steps.howTo:
1. Contact Ontario Health atHome (formerly Home and Community Care Support Services); a doctor or hospital can also refer.
2. A care coordinator assesses needs for home care, nursing, personal support, respite or community programs.
3. Applications for long-term care homes also go through Ontario Health atHome; the resident pays a co-payment for accommodation.

steps.title: Check their prescription drug coverage
conditions: Only if the person lives in Ontario and has OHIP coverage
documents: Trillium Drug Program approval, if applied
prepare: Their notice of assessment, for income
steps.howTo:
1. From 65, the Ontario Drug Benefit covers most listed drugs automatically.
2. Under 65, OHIP+ covers people 24 and under without a private plan; others with high drug costs can apply to the Trillium Drug Program, based on household income.
3. Trillium runs on a benefit year from August 1; it is renewed each year.

title: A parent turns 60 · China
summary: Paperwork plan for when a parent turns 60 in mainland China: the elderly support tax deduction, carer leave, medical insurance sharing, senior benefits, a parent moving in, and planning ahead with a chosen guardian.
conditions: A parent of yours turns 60; the event date is their 60th birthday
The steps are for an adult child who lives or pays tax in mainland China
Carer leave, senior benefits and hukou rules are set by each province or city; check the local rule

sources.title: Interim Measures for Special Additional Deductions of Individual Income Tax (2018) — gov.cn
Tax policy library (special additional deduction amounts, current) — State Taxation Administration
Civil Code of the PRC (中华人民共和国民法典) — National People's Congress
National Healthcare Security Administration

National Social Insurance Public Service Platform

steps.title: Declare the elderly support deduction (赡养老人专项附加扣除)
documents: Deduction declaration in the individual income tax app
Written split agreement, if shared with siblings
prepare: Siblings' names and ID numbers, if any
How the amount is split between siblings
conditions: Only if you pay individual income tax in China
steps.howTo:
1. The deduction starts from the month a parent turns 60; it is counted per taxpayer, not per parent.
2. An only child deducts the full amount, 3,000 yuan a month since 2023 (check current).
3. Siblings share the same total, split equally, by agreement or as the parent designates; each sibling deducts at most 1,500 yuan a month. An agreed or designated split is put in writing.
4. It is declared in the individual income tax app (个人所得税 app), either through the employer each month or in the annual reconciliation (年度汇算).
5. Declarations are confirmed again each December for the next year.

steps.title: Check the only-child carer leave in your province (独生子女护理假)
prepare: Proof of being an only child (e.g. 独生子女证 or household register)
conditions: Only if you are an only child and employed
steps.howTo:
1. Many provinces give paid carer leave (护理假) to an only child when a parent aged 60 or over is in hospital.
2. The number of days, and whether it applies to non-only children, differs by province; check the current provincial regulation on the elderly.
3. Hospital admission papers are usually shown to the employer.

steps.title: Check the parent's retirement date and pension status
prepare: Parent's social security card or the 12333 app
conditions: Only if the parent's own retirement plan doesn't already cover this
steps.howTo:
1. Under the reform from 2025, the statutory retirement age rises gradually; a man turning 60 may retire a few months later than 60.
2. The national social insurance platform or the 12333 app shows the retirement date and contribution years.
3. A parent already drawing a pension usually confirms eligibility (领取资格认证) once a year, often by face check in an app.

steps.title: Set up medical insurance family sharing (医保家庭共济)
documents: Family sharing binding in the national medical insurance app
prepare: Parent's ID card and insurance details
conditions: Only if you have employee medical insurance (职工医保)
steps.howTo:
1. The personal account of employee medical insurance can pay close relatives' resident medical insurance contributions and their medical costs.
2. Binding is done in the national medical insurance app (国家医保服务平台) or the local app.
3. Sharing across provinces is being rolled out; check current local support.

steps.title: Check local senior benefits (老年人优待)
documents: Senior card or benefit card, if the city issues one (老年人优待证)
steps.howTo:
1. Cities give people over 60 or 65 free or cheaper public transport, park and museum entry and priority services.
2. Some benefits work with the ID card alone; others need a local card.
3. The age and what is covered are set locally; check with the street or community office (街道/社区).

steps.title: Register the parent's medical care in your city (异地就医备案)
prepare: Your address in the new city
conditions: Only if the parent is moving in with you in another city or province
steps.howTo:
1. Registering for medical care away from the insured city (异地就医备案) lets hospital bills be settled directly where the parent lives.
2. It is done online in the national medical insurance app, often by selecting "long-term residence" or "living with family".
3. Reimbursement rates can differ from the home city.

steps.title: Decide where the parent keeps resident medical insurance
documents: Resident medical insurance enrolment (城乡居民医保)
conditions: Only if the parent is moving in with you and has resident, not employee, insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Resident medical insurance is usually paid yearly where the hukou is; some cities let holders of a residence permit enrol locally.
2. Payment usually opens in the autumn for the next year; a gap can bring a waiting period.
3. Check the current local rule before stopping insurance in the home city.

steps.title: Move the parent's hukou to your city (投靠子女落户)
prepare: Your hukou book and ID card
Parent's hukou book and ID card
Proof of your home or residence
conditions: Only if the parent wants to move their hukou to live with you
steps.howTo:
1. Many cities let parents move their hukou to join a child (投靠子女), often from a set age and with conditions on the child's hukou, home and years in the city.
2. The local public security bureau or police station handles it.
3. Moving the hukou can change the parent's resident insurance, land rights in the home village and local benefits; check before applying.
4. The date and time taken are estimates.

steps.title: Set up a chosen guardian or a will, if wanted (意定监护, 遗嘱)
conditions: Only if the parent wants to plan ahead
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Civil Code, an adult with full capacity can choose in writing, with the person's agreement, who becomes their guardian if they later lose capacity (意定监护).
2. A notary office (公证处) can notarise the agreement and a will; notarisation is common but a will has other valid forms under the Civil Code.
3. The parent decides; this step is only a prompt.

steps.title: Book the free yearly health check at 65
prepare: Nearest community health centre (社区卫生服务中心)
steps.howTo:
1. Under the national basic public health services, people 65 and over can get a free health check once a year at the community health centre or township clinic.
2. It is usually registered where the parent lives; check what the local centre needs.
3. It repeats yearly.
