steps.title: Medical certification of death
prepare: Name of the doctor, nurse practitioner or coroner involved
steps.howTo:
1. A medical practitioner, nurse practitioner or coroner completes and signs the Medical Certification of Death within 48 hours and sends it to the funeral director.
2. If the death was sudden, unexpected or unexplained, the BC Coroners Service may be involved first; the funeral director and coroner coordinate the timing.
3. The family does not file this form themselves.

steps.title: Choose a funeral home; it registers the death
prepare: The deceased's full legal name, date and place of birth
Parents' names, marital status, usual address and occupation
Social Insurance Number and Personal Health Number
Any written wishes about burial or cremation, or a pre-paid funeral plan
steps.howTo:
1. The funeral director gathers the personal details from an informant, usually the next of kin, and registers the death with the B.C. Vital Statistics Agency.
2. Once registered, the funeral director issues the disposition permit for burial or cremation.
3. When the death happens in B.C., Vital Statistics passes it on to Health Insurance BC (MSP), Elections BC, Service Canada and the CRA.
4. If the death happened outside B.C., these offices are not told automatically; each one is contacted directly.

steps.title: Look for the will and other papers
prepare: Home files, safety deposit box, lawyer or notary the person used
Life insurance policies, pension and bank statements
Recent tax returns and notices of assessment
steps.howTo:
1. The original will is often with a lawyer or notary, or kept at home or in a safety deposit box.
2. The will usually names the executor, who handles the rest of this plan; with no will, a close family member can apply to administer the estate.
3. A list of accounts, debts, insurance and property now makes the probate and tax steps easier.

steps.title: Order death certificates
prepare: How many originals banks, insurers and pension plans want
steps.howTo:
1. Funeral homes often order certificates for the family; more can be ordered from the Vital Statistics Agency online, by mail or at Service BC once the death is registered.
2. Banks, insurers, pension plans, ICBC and the Land Title Office each tend to ask for one; some accept a certified copy.
3. The 7 days is an estimate; courier orders are faster.

steps.title: Confirm Service Canada and the CRA know
prepare: List of federal payments they received (CPP, OAS, CRA benefits)
steps.howTo:
1. For a death in B.C., Vital Statistics tells Service Canada and the CRA; a phone call confirms they have it.
2. CPP and Old Age Security stop after the month of death; payments sent for later months are usually returned. Check with Service Canada.
3. The CRA cancels or transfers benefit payments such as the Canada Child Benefit and the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB).
4. The executor can register as the legal representative with the CRA to deal with the tax file.

steps.title: Move child and family benefits to the survivor
conditions: Only if the deceased received the Canada Child Benefit or had a spouse or partner
steps.howTo:
1. If the deceased received the Canada Child Benefit for children now in your care, apply for it in your own name through CRA My Account or form RC66.
2. A surviving spouse or partner reports the change in marital status to the CRA; family benefits are recalculated on the survivor's income.
3. BC Family Benefit comes with the Canada Child Benefit, so no separate application.

steps.title: Tell banks, insurers, employers and pension plans
prepare: Utilities, phone, subscriptions and credit cards
steps.howTo:
1. Banks freeze accounts in the deceased's sole name until the executor shows authority; joint accounts usually pass to the surviving owner.
2. Life insurance and workplace benefits have their own claim forms; claims can start before probate.
3. Contact BC Pension Corporation or the employer's plan about any survivor pension.
4. Credit bureaus (Equifax, TransUnion) can mark the file as deceased to limit identity fraud.
5. B.C. publishes an after-a-death checklist to track who has been told.

steps.title: Cancel passport, driver's licence and other ID
steps.howTo:
1. Health coverage (MSP) ends automatically for a death registered in B.C.
2. Tell ICBC to cancel the driver's licence; a combined BC Services Card is cancelled with it.
3. Return or report the Canadian passport to the Passport Program; IRCC also handles a PR card or citizenship record.
4. The SIN record is updated by Service Canada once the death is reported.

steps.title: Apply for CPP death, survivor's and children's benefits
conditions: Only if the deceased paid into the Canada Pension Plan
prepare: Survivor's and children's SINs and birth certificates
Proof of marriage or common-law relationship
steps.howTo:
1. The death benefit is a one-time payment of up to $2,500 (up to $5,000 with the top-up in some cases, since January 2025). The executor applies within 60 days of the death; after that, whoever paid for the funeral, then the spouse or next of kin, can apply.
2. The survivor's pension is a monthly payment for a legal spouse or common-law partner.
3. The children's benefit is monthly for dependent children under 18, or 18 to 25 in full-time school.
4. Apply online through My Service Canada Account or by mail; processing takes about 6 to 12 weeks.
5. A surviving spouse aged 60 to 64 with low income may also qualify for the Old Age Security Allowance for the Survivor; check current rules.

steps.title: Register the death on a jointly owned home
conditions: Only if the deceased owned land or a home in joint tenancy with someone who survives them
prepare: Legal description or PID of the property
A lawyer or notary, if using one
steps.howTo:
1. Joint tenancy passes the property to the surviving owner outside the estate; it does not need probate.
2. The survivor applies to the Land Title Office through the LTSA to remove the deceased's name, with a death certificate.
3. Most people use a lawyer or notary, since filings are made electronically.
4. A home held in the deceased's sole name, or as tenants in common, goes through the estate instead.

steps.title: Transfer or cancel the vehicle and insurance
conditions: Only if the deceased owned a vehicle
steps.howTo:
1. Visit an Autoplan broker to transfer the vehicle to the survivor or beneficiary, or to cancel the insurance.
2. The broker asks for the death certificate and proof of who is entitled to the vehicle, such as the will or a grant of probate.
3. Check current ICBC rules on tax exemptions for transfers to family.

steps.title: Settle RRSPs, RRIFs and TFSAs
conditions: Only if the deceased had registered accounts
prepare: Named beneficiaries or successor holders on each account
Survivor's own RRSP or RRIF account details
steps.howTo:
1. A named beneficiary or successor holder deals with the financial institution directly, usually without probate.
2. An RRSP or RRIF left to a spouse or common-law partner can roll into the survivor's own plan without tax at death; otherwise its value is generally income on the final return.
3. A spouse named as TFSA successor holder takes over the account as their own.
4. Other TFSA beneficiaries receive the value; some amounts can go into a survivor's TFSA within a set period. Check the current CRA rules.

steps.title: Search the B.C. Wills Registry
conditions: Only if the estate needs a grant of probate or administration
steps.howTo:
1. The Vital Statistics Agency holds wills notices: where a will was kept and when it was signed, not the will itself.
2. Apply by mail or in person at Service BC (not the Vancouver, Burnaby or Surrey offices); the fee is $20 plus $5 for each extra name. Check current.
3. Standard orders take about 20 business days plus mail; courier is faster.
4. The search result goes in with the probate application.

steps.title: Send the probate notice to beneficiaries
conditions: Only if the estate needs a grant of probate or administration
prepare: Names and addresses of everyone named in the will, and anyone who would inherit if there were no will
steps.howTo:
1. Banks and the Land Title Office usually ask for a grant when there is land, or larger accounts, in the deceased's sole name.
2. The executor delivers a Notice of Proposed Application (Form P1) with a copy of the will to beneficiaries and intestate successors, and to others the probate rules list.
3. The application cannot be filed until 21 days after the notice is delivered.

steps.title: Apply to the Supreme Court for the grant
conditions: Only if the estate needs a grant of probate or administration
prepare: List of assets and debts at the date of death
Affidavits, sworn before a lawyer, notary or commissioner
steps.howTo:
1. File the probate application forms with a B.C. Supreme Court registry, including the affidavit of assets and liabilities.
2. Probate fees are paid at filing, based on the estate's B.C. assets: none up to $25,000, then $6 per $1,000 up to $50,000 and $14 per $1,000 above. Check the current fee schedule.
3. The court issues the grant once the registry is satisfied; the 60 days here is an estimate and registries vary.

steps.title: File the final tax return
prepare: Income slips from January 1 to the date of death
Any tax returns from earlier years not yet filed
Values of property and registered accounts at the date of death
steps.howTo:
1. For a death from January 1 to October 31, the final return is due April 30 of the next year; from November 1 to December 31, 6 months after the death.
2. If the deceased or their spouse ran a business, the filing date is June 15 (or 6 months after a death in late December), but any balance is still due by the regular date.
3. Capital property and registered accounts are generally treated as sold at death, unless they pass to a spouse.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the real deadline.

steps.title: File the estate's trust return (T3)
conditions: Only if the estate earns income, such as interest, rent or gains, after the death
prepare: Income and distributions after the death
steps.howTo:
1. The estate is a separate taxpayer from the day after death.
2. The T3 return is due 90 days after the estate's tax year-end; the first year can end up to 1 year after the death.
3. The date here is an estimate; set it from the year-end the executor chooses.

steps.title: Ask the CRA for a clearance certificate
prepare: Notices of assessment for every return filed
Draft plan for distributing the estate
steps.howTo:
1. A clearance certificate confirms that all taxes the deceased and the estate owe are paid.
2. Send form TX19 once every return has been assessed.
3. An executor who distributes without one can be personally liable for tax still owing.
4. Processing takes several months; the 120 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Distribute the estate and close it
steps.howTo:
1. Under B.C. law, a spouse or child who feels left out can ask the court to vary a will within 180 days after the grant; executors usually wait at least 210 days after the grant before distributing, unless the beneficiaries consent or a court orders otherwise. Check current rules.
2. The executor pays debts and taxes, gives beneficiaries an accounting, and hands out what remains.
3. Close the estate bank account once everything is paid out.

title: Death in the family · China
summary: The practical matters after a family member dies in mainland China, in the order they usually come: the death certificate, the funeral, cancelling the hukou, pension and insurance claims, the provident fund, bank accounts, property and vehicles. There is no rush for most of them; the dates are gentle reminders.
conditions: A family member has died, and they lived or had their hukou in mainland China
Many steps apply only to some estates: a pension, a home, a car, a work-related death

sources.title: Household Registration Regulations of the PRC (户口登记条例)
Social Insurance Law of the PRC — State Taxation Administration law library
Housing Provident Fund Regulations, consolidated text — Ministry of Justice regulations database
Civil Code of the PRC (中华人民共和国民法典) — National People's Congress
Order of statutory succession (Civil Code, Article 1127) — Shenzhen Justice Bureau
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
National Healthcare Security Administration
People's Bank of China
Traffic management online service platform (交管12123)

steps.title: Get the medical certificate of death (死亡医学证明书)
documents: Medical certificate of death (死亡医学证明书), several copies
steps.howTo:
1. In a hospital, the hospital issues it.
2. At home, the community health service centre or township hospital usually issues it after a doctor's check; the local police can also be called.
3. Where the cause is not natural or not known, the police handle the case and issue their own proof of death.
4. Copies are asked for by the funeral home, the police station, the social insurance office and banks; the hospital can say how many it issues.

steps.title: Arrange the funeral and cremation
steps.howTo:
1. Contact the funeral home (殡仪馆), which collects the body in its own vehicle and sets the date.
2. In areas where cremation is the rule, the funeral home issues a cremation certificate afterwards; it is needed for the hukou cancellation and pension claims.
3. Many cities give a basic funeral fee waiver or subsidy for local hukou holders; ask the funeral home or civil affairs bureau.
4. The timing here is only a placeholder; families set their own.

steps.title: Cancel the hukou (户口注销)
documents: Hukou cancellation record (注销户口证明)
prepare: Medical certificate of death or police proof
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Household Registration Regulations, death is reported to the police station holding the hukou: in cities before burial, in rural areas within a month.
2. The station cancels the hukou and takes back the ID card; ask for a cancellation record, which banks, the social insurance office and the property registry often ask for.
3. Some places cancel it together with the death certificate or at the funeral home; check with the local station.

steps.title: Gather the will and a list of what they left
documents: List of accounts, property and debts
prepare: Documents showing each heir's relationship: household register, marriage and birth certificates
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Civil Code, a valid will comes first; without one, the first order of heirs is the spouse, children and parents, sharing equally in general.
2. A will may be handwritten, typed, recorded or notarised, each with its own witnessing rules.
3. Debts and taxes are paid from the estate, up to its value.
4. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Stop the pension and claim the survivors' benefits (丧葬补助金, 抚恤金)
prepare: Hukou cancellation record or death certificate
Claimant's bank card and ID card
conditions: Only if they were in basic pension insurance, working or retired
steps.howTo:
1. Tell the local social insurance office; pension paid for months after the death is usually reclaimed.
2. Under the Social Insurance Law, the family of an insured person who died of illness or a non-work cause can claim a funeral grant (丧葬补助金) and a survivors' benefit (抚恤金) from the pension fund; amounts are set by the province.
3. The balance of the pension personal account (个人账户) can be inherited and is claimed at the same time.
4. Civil servants and public institution staff follow their own rules through the employer.
5. Many places accept the claim online or through the social insurance app.

steps.title: Claim the medical insurance personal account balance
prepare: Hukou cancellation record or death certificate
Claimant's bank card and ID card
conditions: Only if they had employee medical insurance
steps.howTo:
1. The balance of an employee medical insurance personal account can be inherited.
2. Apply to the local medical insurance office (医保经办机构); the documents asked for are set locally.

steps.title: Withdraw their housing provident fund (住房公积金)
prepare: Hukou cancellation record or death certificate
Proof of being an heir or legatee
Claimant's bank card and ID card
conditions: Only if they had a provident fund account
steps.howTo:
1. Under the provident fund regulations, heirs or legatees can withdraw the balance when an account holder dies.
2. The local fund centre sets the proof of heirship it accepts; where there are several heirs, it may ask for all of them or a notarised or agreed division.

steps.title: Claim life and accident insurance
prepare: Beneficiary's ID card and bank card
conditions: Only if they had life, accident or employer group insurance
steps.howTo:
1. The named beneficiary claims from the insurer; without one, the payout joins the estate.
2. Under the Insurance Law, life insurance claims can be made within 5 years of knowing of the death; other insurance within 2 years.
3. Employer group policies are claimed through the employer.

steps.title: Apply for work-related death benefits (工亡待遇)
documents: Work-injury recognition decision (工伤认定决定书)
prepare: Labour contract or proof of employment
conditions: Only if the death happened at or because of work
steps.howTo:
1. Under the Work-Related Injury Insurance Regulations, the employer applies for recognition within 30 days; if it does not, the family can apply within one year.
2. Benefits include a funeral grant of 6 months of the local average monthly wage, a pension for dependants, and a one-off death grant of 20 times the previous year's national urban per capita disposable income.
3. Without work-injury insurance, the employer pays these itself.
4. Disputes go to labour arbitration or the courts.

steps.title: Close or transfer bank deposits
prepare: Death certificate or hukou cancellation record
steps.howTo:
1. Close relatives can ask banks whether the person held deposits, with proof of death and relationship, under simplified rules from the central bank.
2. For small balances, banks have a simpler withdrawal process; the threshold is set by the regulators and banks, so check current.
3. Larger balances usually need a notarised inheritance certificate, a court document, or all heirs present at the bank.
4. Securities, funds and online payment balances each have their own process with the provider.

steps.title: Register the inherited home (不动产继承登记)
documents: New real estate certificate (不动产权证书)
prepare: Death certificate or hukou cancellation record
Proof of relationships of all heirs
conditions: Only if they owned a home or land rights
steps.howTo:
1. Apply at the local real estate registration centre (不动产登记中心).
2. Notarisation is no longer the only route: many centres accept the heirs applying together with proof of relationship, checked by the centre; a notarised document or court judgment also works.
3. Under the Deed Tax Law, statutory heirs inheriting a home are exempt from deed tax.
4. A mortgage on the home stays with it; talk to the lender.
5. The time taken is an estimate.

steps.title: Transfer their vehicle and cancel the driving licence
prepare: Vehicle registration certificate (机动车登记证书)
conditions: Only if they owned a car or held a driving licence
steps.howTo:
1. A car passes to an heir through a transfer at the vehicle management office (车管所), with proof of inheritance.
2. A driving licence is cancelled on the holder's death; family can report it at the office or through 交管12123.
3. Compulsory traffic insurance (交强险) moves with the car or is cancelled for a refund.

steps.title: Close phone, utility and online accounts
prepare: Death certificate or hukou cancellation record
steps.howTo:
1. Phone numbers, utilities, memberships and subscriptions can be closed or moved into another name.
2. Online platforms such as WeChat and Alipay have their own processes for a deceased user's account and balance.
3. Keeping the phone number active for a while can help with verification codes during other steps.

title: Death in the family · Ontario

conditions: A family member died, and they lived in Ontario
You are the estate trustee (executor), the next of kin, or helping the person who is

steps.title: Medical Certificate of Death
prepare: Name of the doctor, nurse practitioner or coroner involved
steps.howTo:
1. A doctor, nurse practitioner or coroner completes the Medical Certificate of Death.
2. If the death was sudden, unexpected or unexplained, the coroner may investigate first; the funeral director coordinates the timing.
3. The family does not file this form themselves.

steps.title: Choose a funeral home; it registers the death

Parents' names, marital status, usual address and occupation
Social Insurance Number and Ontario health card number
Any written wishes about burial or cremation, or a pre-paid funeral plan
steps.howTo:
1. The funeral director and a family member complete the Statement of Death (Form 15).
2. The funeral director submits it with the Medical Certificate of Death to the municipal clerk where the death happened; families can also register it themselves.
3. The death is registered before a burial permit is issued.
4. Ontario does not say that federal offices are told automatically, so the Service Canada and CRA step below covers them.

steps.title: Look for the will and other papers

Life insurance policies, pension and bank statements
Recent tax returns and notices of assessment
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario has no central wills registry. The original is often with a lawyer, at home, or in a safety deposit box.
2. A will deposited with the court can be found through the estates office of the Superior Court of Justice where the deceased lived.
3. The will usually names the estate trustee, who handles the rest of this plan; with no will, a close family member can apply to administer the estate.
4. A list of accounts, debts, insurance and property now makes the probate and tax steps easier.

steps.title: Order death certificates
prepare: How many originals banks, insurers and pension plans want
steps.howTo:
1. Order from ServiceOntario online, by mail or in person once the death is registered; there is no limit on who can apply or how many copies.
2. The funeral home also gives a proof-of-death statement that some organizations accept.
3. The 7 days is an estimate; check current ServiceOntario processing times.

steps.title: Tell Service Canada and the CRA
prepare: List of federal payments they received (CPP, OAS, CRA benefits)
steps.howTo:
1. Call Service Canada and the CRA with the date of death; the funeral home may already have sent a notice, so the call confirms it.
2. CPP and Old Age Security stop after the month of death; payments sent for later months are usually returned. Check with Service Canada.
3. The CRA cancels or transfers benefit payments such as the Canada Child Benefit and the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB).
4. The estate trustee can register as the legal representative with the CRA to deal with the tax file.

steps.title: Move child and family benefits to the survivor
conditions: Only if the deceased received the Canada Child Benefit or had a spouse or partner
steps.howTo:
1. If the deceased received the Canada Child Benefit for children now in your care, apply for it in your own name through CRA My Account or form RC66.
2. A surviving spouse or partner reports the change in marital status to the CRA; family benefits are recalculated on the survivor's income.
3. The Ontario Child Benefit comes with the Canada Child Benefit, so no separate application.

steps.title: Tell banks, insurers, employers and pension plans
prepare: Utilities, phone, subscriptions and credit cards
steps.howTo:
1. Banks freeze accounts in the deceased's sole name until the estate trustee shows authority; joint accounts usually pass to the surviving owner.
2. Life insurance and workplace benefits have their own claim forms; claims can start before probate.
3. Contact the employer's pension plan about any survivor pension.
4. If the deceased paid or received support through the Family Responsibility Office, tell FRO.
5. Credit bureaus (Equifax, TransUnion) can mark the file as deceased to limit identity fraud.

steps.title: Cancel passport, driver's licence and other ID
steps.howTo:
1. Return the driver's licence to ServiceOntario with the death certificate or another proof of death.
2. Mail an accessible parking permit to ServiceOntario within 30 days of the death.
3. Ask ServiceOntario to cancel the health card too; check current steps.
4. Return or report the Canadian passport to the Passport Program; IRCC also handles a PR card or citizenship record.
5. The SIN record is updated by Service Canada once the death is reported.

steps.title: Apply for CPP death, survivor's and children's benefits
conditions: Only if the deceased paid into the Canada Pension Plan
prepare: Survivor's and children's SINs and birth certificates
Proof of marriage or common-law relationship
steps.howTo:
1. The death benefit is a one-time payment of up to $2,500 (up to $5,000 with the top-up in some cases, since January 2025). The estate trustee applies within 60 days of the death; after that, whoever paid for the funeral, then the spouse or next of kin, can apply.
2. The survivor's pension is a monthly payment for a legal spouse or common-law partner.
3. The children's benefit is monthly for dependent children under 18, or 18 to 25 in full-time school.
4. Apply online through My Service Canada Account or by mail; processing takes about 6 to 12 weeks.
5. A surviving spouse aged 60 to 64 with low income may also qualify for the Old Age Security Allowance for the Survivor; check current rules.

steps.title: Register the death on a jointly owned home
conditions: Only if the deceased owned land or a home as joint tenants with someone who survives them
steps.howTo:
1. Joint tenancy passes the property to the surviving owner outside the estate; it does not need an estate certificate.
2. A survivorship application is registered in the Ontario land registry with proof of death to remove the deceased's name.
3. Registration is electronic, so it is usually done by a lawyer.
4. A home held in the deceased's sole name, or as tenants in common, goes through the estate instead.

steps.title: Transfer or cancel the vehicle and insurance
conditions: Only if the deceased owned a vehicle
steps.howTo:
1. At ServiceOntario, transfer the vehicle permit to the survivor or beneficiary, with the death certificate and proof of who is entitled, such as the will or the estate certificate.
2. Tell the insurer; the policy is cancelled or moved to the new owner.
3. Check current ServiceOntario rules on retail sales tax for transfers to family.

steps.title: Settle RRSPs, RRIFs and TFSAs
conditions: Only if the deceased had registered accounts
prepare: Named beneficiaries or successor holders on each account
Survivor's own RRSP or RRIF account details
steps.howTo:
1. A named beneficiary or successor holder deals with the financial institution directly, usually without probate.
2. An RRSP or RRIF left to a spouse or common-law partner can roll into the survivor's own plan without tax at death; otherwise its value is generally income on the final return.
3. A spouse named as TFSA successor holder takes over the account as their own.
4. Other TFSA beneficiaries receive the value; some amounts can go into a survivor's TFSA within a set period. Check the current CRA rules.

steps.title: Send the estate application to beneficiaries
conditions: Only if the estate needs a Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee or a Small Estate Certificate
prepare: Names and addresses of everyone entitled to a share of the estate
steps.howTo:
1. Banks and the land registry usually ask for a certificate when there is land, or larger accounts, in the deceased's sole name.
2. Estates worth $150,000 or less can use the simpler Small Estate Certificate forms (Form 74.1A and others); larger estates apply for a Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee, with or without a will.
3. Before filing, a copy of the application is sent to everyone entitled to a share; email or mail is accepted.
4. A bond may be needed, for example when there is no will or the applicant lives outside Canada.

steps.title: File with the Superior Court and pay Estate Administration Tax
conditions: Only if the estate needs a Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee or a Small Estate Certificate
documents: Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee
prepare: Value of real and personal property in the estate
Affidavits, sworn before a commissioner for taking affidavits
steps.howTo:
1. File at the Superior Court of Justice in the county or district where the deceased lived.
2. Estate Administration Tax is paid at filing: none on estates of $50,000 or less, then $15 for every $1,000 or part of it above $50,000. Check current.
3. Applications are typically processed within 15 business days; small estates in about 5; longer if something is missing.

steps.title: File the Estate Information Return
conditions: Only if a certificate was issued
documents: Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee
prepare: Values of each asset at the date of death
steps.howTo:
1. The estate trustee files the Estate Information Return with the Ministry of Finance within 180 calendar days after the certificate is issued.
2. It is filed even when the estate owes no tax.
3. The date here is an estimate; set it from the date on the certificate.

steps.title: Married spouse's 6-month election
conditions: Only if the deceased was married and the spouse survives them
prepare: Values of both spouses' property at the date of death
A family or estates lawyer, if using one
steps.howTo:
1. Under Ontario's Family Law Act, a surviving married spouse chooses between what the will (or the intestacy rules) gives them and an equalization of net family property.
2. The election is filed with the Estate Registrar for Ontario within 6 months after the death; with no election filed, the spouse takes under the will or intestacy.
3. Common-law partners do not have this election.
4. The estate trustee generally waits for this period to pass before distributing.

steps.title: File the final tax return
prepare: Income slips from January 1 to the date of death
Any tax returns from earlier years not yet filed
Values of property and registered accounts at the date of death
steps.howTo:
1. For a death from January 1 to October 31, the final return is due April 30 of the next year; from November 1 to December 31, 6 months after the death.
2. If the deceased or their spouse ran a business, the filing date is June 15 (or 6 months after a death in late December), but any balance is still due by the regular date.
3. Capital property and registered accounts are generally treated as sold at death, unless they pass to a spouse.
4. The date here is an estimate; move it to the real deadline.

steps.title: File the estate's trust return (T3)
conditions: Only if the estate earns income, such as interest, rent or gains, after the death
prepare: Income and distributions after the death
steps.howTo:
1. The estate is a separate taxpayer from the day after death.
2. The T3 return is due 90 days after the estate's tax year-end; the first year can end up to 1 year after the death.
3. The date here is an estimate; set it from the year-end the estate trustee chooses.

steps.title: Ask the CRA for a clearance certificate
prepare: Notices of assessment for every return filed
Draft plan for distributing the estate
steps.howTo:
1. A clearance certificate confirms that all taxes the deceased and the estate owe are paid.
2. Send form TX19 once every return has been assessed.
3. An estate trustee who distributes without one can be personally liable for tax still owing.
4. Processing takes several months; the 120 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Distribute the estate and close it
documents: Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee
steps.howTo:
1. Dependants can claim support from an estate, generally within 6 months after the certificate is issued, and a married spouse has the 6-month election; estate trustees usually wait these out unless everyone consents or a court orders otherwise. Check current rules.
2. The estate trustee pays debts and taxes, gives beneficiaries an accounting, and hands out what remains.
3. Close the estate bank account once everything is paid out.

conditions: You are retiring from work in Canada, fully or mostly
The date is the last day of work; the age-based CPP, OAS and RRIF steps are in the retirement plans for British Columbia and Ontario
Some steps apply only to people with a workplace pension, group savings or group benefits

steps.title: Apply for CPP and OAS if not already done
conditions: Only if you plan to start CPP or OAS around the time you stop work
steps.howTo:
1. CPP can start from 60 and is applied for online up to 12 months before the chosen start month.
2. OAS starts from 65; many people are enrolled automatically, others apply up to 11 months ahead.
3. Stopping work does not force either to start; waiting raises the monthly amount, up to 70.
4. The age-based steps are in the retirement plan for your province.

steps.title: Choose how to take the workplace pension
documents: Spousal waiver, if a joint pension is declined
prepare: Lifetime pension amounts for each option
conditions: Only if you belong to a workplace defined benefit pension plan
steps.howTo:
1. The plan administrator sends a statement with the options: a lifetime pension (single, or joint and survivor), and sometimes a lump-sum commuted value.
2. A commuted value usually moves to a locked-in account (LIRA or LIF) up to a tax limit, with any excess paid as taxable cash.
3. Declining a joint and survivor pension usually needs the spouse's signed waiver.
4. The election window is set by the plan, often 60 to 90 days; the choice is usually final.

steps.title: Move group RRSP or defined contribution savings
conditions: Only if you have a group RRSP, DPSP or defined contribution pension
steps.howTo:
1. Group plans usually ask for a decision within a set time after leaving; otherwise money may be moved to a default option.
2. Group RRSP money can move to an individual RRSP or straight to a RRIF or annuity; locked-in pension money moves to a LIRA, LIF or annuity.
3. A direct transfer avoids withholding tax.
4. RRSPs convert to a RRIF or annuity by the end of the year of turning 71; see the retirement plan for your province.

steps.title: Replace group health and dental benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Group benefits usually end on or soon after the last day of work; some employers offer retiree benefits.
2. Insurers often let people convert to an individual plan without a medical questionnaire if they apply within a short window, often about 31 days; the booklet has the real deadline.
3. The Canadian Dental Care Plan covers residents without dental insurance and with adjusted family net income under $90,000.
4. Drug costs: British Columbia's Fair PharmaCare is income-based at any age; the Ontario Drug Benefit covers most people 65 and over.

steps.title: Check the final pay, vacation pay and Record of Employment
steps.howTo:
1. Final pay includes earned wages and unused vacation pay; provincial employment standards set the deadline.
2. The employer issues a Record of Employment, viewable in My Service Canada Account.
3. Any retiring allowance can be partly transferred to an RRSP only for service years before 1996.

steps.title: Set tax withholding on pension income
documents: Request for voluntary federal income tax deductions (ISP-3520)
prepare: Expected total income for the year
conditions: Only if you receive a workplace pension, CPP, OAS or RRIF payments
steps.howTo:
1. Each payer withholds as if it were the only income, so several pensions together can leave tax owing.
2. A TD1 to the pension payer, or a request for extra deductions, raises withholding; for CPP and OAS, Service Canada takes form ISP-3520 or a request in My Service Canada Account.
3. Without enough withheld, the CRA may send instalment reminders the next year.

steps.title: Note CPP contributions if working again after starting CPP
conditions: Only if you draw CPP and keep or take up paid work before 70
steps.howTo:
1. Working while receiving CPP between 60 and 70 means paying CPP contributions, which build a Post-Retirement Benefit added to the pension the next year.
2. From 65 to 70, contributions can be stopped with form CPT30 given to the employer.
3. The Post-Retirement Benefit is paid automatically.

steps.title: File the first return with pension income
steps.howTo:
1. The return is due April 30 of the next year; slips arrive by the end of February.
2. Eligible pension income can give the pension income amount and, with a spouse, pension splitting on form T1032.
3. If tax owing is over $3,000, the CRA may ask for quarterly instalments afterwards.
4. This date is an estimate; move it to April 30.

conditions: You live in Canada; the drug, supplement and property tax programs are for British Columbia residents
You paid into the Canada Pension Plan, or expect OAS from living in Canada

steps.title: Sign up for My Service Canada Account
prepare: GCKey, or online banking for a Sign-In Partner
steps.howTo:
1. Register with a GCKey or through a Sign-In Partner (online banking).
2. Identity may be confirmed with a Personal Access Code sent by mail.
3. The account is where CPP and OAS are applied for and tracked.
4. The 14 days is an estimate, to allow for a mailed code.

steps.title: Check your CPP Statement of Contributions
prepare: Notices of assessment for self-employed years
steps.howTo:
1. In My Service Canada Account, open Canada Pension Plan and view contributions and benefit estimates.
2. Compare each year with your T4 slips; report errors straight away with T4s, an employer letter, or a T1 and notice of assessment.
3. It can also be requested by mail.

steps.title: Choose when to start CPP
prepare: Health, other income and work plans
steps.howTo:
1. CPP can start any time from age 60 to 70.
2. Before 65 it drops 0.6% a month, up to 36% less at 60.
3. After 65 it rises 0.7% a month, up to 42% more at 70.
4. There is no gain in waiting past 70.
5. Not financial advice; the Service Canada estimates help compare.

steps.title: Apply for the CPP retirement pension
prepare: Children's details, for the child-rearing provision
steps.howTo:
1. Apply up to 12 months before the chosen start date, in My Service Canada Account.
2. Online applications get a decision by mail within 28 days; paper within 120 days.
3. This date assumes a start at 65; move it to about 6 months before the start age you chose.

steps.title: Watch for the OAS enrolment letter
prepare: Check the mail around your 64th birthday
steps.howTo:
1. Most people get a letter around their 64th birthday saying they are enrolled automatically for OAS at 65.
2. OAS needs at least 10 years living in Canada after age 18 (20 years if living abroad).
3. You can delay OAS to as late as 70: it rises 0.6% a month, up to 36% at 70. If you qualify for GIS, there is no gain in waiting.
4. From 75, OAS is 10% higher; the increase is automatic.

steps.title: Apply for Old Age Security
conditions: Only if no enrolment letter came a month after your 64th birthday
steps.howTo:
1. If a month has passed since your 64th birthday with no letter, contact Service Canada or apply.
2. Online applications open once you are at least 1 month past your 64th birthday, in My Service Canada Account.
3. The 30 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Check the Guaranteed Income Supplement
conditions: Only if your income is low
steps.howTo:
1. GIS is for people 65 or older who get OAS and have a low income.
2. Service Canada enrols most people automatically if it has their information.
3. Unfiled taxes can stop or reduce GIS.
4. GIS does not increase if you delay OAS.

steps.title: Register for Fair PharmaCare
conditions: Only if your family is not registered yet
prepare: Social Insurance Numbers for the adults
Net income from the tax return of 2 years ago
steps.howTo:
1. Fair PharmaCare is open to anyone enrolled in MSP; coverage depends on family net income, not age, and there is no separate drug plan that starts at a set age.
2. Register online, by phone with Health Insurance BC, or on paper.
3. Return the CRA consent form within 30 days, or the temporary coverage ends.
4. Once registered you stay covered as long as income can be checked with the CRA each year, so keep filing taxes.
5. Age 55 here is only a prompt; register any time.

steps.title: Look into the property tax deferment program
conditions: Only if you own and live in your home in B.C.
prepare: Mortgage and other charges on the property
Check the current interest rate and fees
steps.howTo:
1. The regular program is for owners 55 or older in the current year, surviving spouses and people with disabilities; only one owner needs to be 55.
2. You need to have lived in B.C. at least one year, live in the home as your principal residence, have paid earlier taxes, and keep at least 25% equity.
3. It is a loan: interest accrues and the deferred taxes are repaid when the home is sold or transferred.
4. Apply online through eTaxBC between May 1 and December 31; automatic renewal can carry it to later years.
5. Not financial advice; the date here is an estimate for the first spring after you turn 55.

steps.title: Update the will, enduring power of attorney and representation agreement
prepare: Who should decide on money and on care
Beneficiaries on RRSPs, pensions and insurance
steps.howTo:
1. In B.C. an enduring power of attorney covers financial affairs, and a representation agreement covers health and personal care.
2. A section 9 representation agreement covers personal and health care; a section 7 one can also cover routine finances and legal services.
3. An advance directive gives or refuses consent to health care directly; without a representative, providers turn to a temporary substitute decision maker from a set list.
4. The standard provincial forms are optional, and the My Voice guide walks through advance care planning.
5. Not legal advice; age 60 here is only a prompt; review after any big change.

steps.title: Claim the senior home owner grant
conditions: Only if you own and live in your home in B.C.
prepare: Check the current assessed value limit
steps.howTo:
1. Owners who are 65 or older in the current year can claim the higher additional grant on their principal residence.
2. The grant is claimed every year: after the property tax notice arrives and before the tax due date, and no later than December 31.
3. Apply online through eTaxBC, by phone or at Service BC.
4. Above the assessed value limit, a low-income grant supplement may still apply.
5. The date here is an estimate; move it to your next property tax notice.

steps.title: Check the BC Senior's Supplement
conditions: Only if you get the Guaranteed Income Supplement
steps.howTo:
1. The Senior's Supplement tops up low-income B.C. residents who get OAS and GIS.
2. There is no application; it starts one month after your first OAS and GIS payment.
3. The amount is based on your OAS and GIS, which use last year's tax return.

steps.title: Check income against the OAS recovery tax threshold
prepare: Expected CPP, workplace pension and RRSP or RRIF income
steps.howTo:
1. OAS is reduced by 15% of net income above a yearly threshold (a little over $90,000 at review; check current), and stops at a higher level.
2. The timing of CPP, RRSP withdrawals, RRIF conversion and pension splitting all change net income in the OAS years.
3. Income in one year sets the recovery tax taken from monthly OAS from July of the following year.
4. Not financial advice; the date here is only a prompt before the CPP and OAS start.

steps.title: Replace workplace health and dental benefits at retirement
conditions: Only if you had health or dental benefits through work
prepare: Drugs, dental and travel cover you use now
Whether the employer offers retiree benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Workplace health and dental plans often end on the last day of work or soon after, unless the employer offers retiree benefits.
2. Many group insurers offer a conversion plan without medical questions if applied for within a short window after coverage ends, often 30 to 60 days; check the plan booklet.
3. Individual plans with medical questions are another route, and travel medical cover usually needs its own policy.
4. Moving this date to the real retirement date keeps the window in view.

steps.title: Apply for the Canadian Dental Care Plan
conditions: Only if you have no dental insurance and your adjusted family net income is under $90,000
prepare: Tax returns filed for you and any spouse
Check that no retiree or pension plan still gives dental cover
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Dental Care Plan is for residents with no access to dental insurance, an adjusted family net income under $90,000, and tax returns filed by you and any spouse; there is no upper age limit.
2. Dental cover still available through a pension or retiree plan usually rules it out, even if you do not take it.
3. Apply online or by phone through Service Canada; co-payments depend on income.
4. Eligibility is confirmed every year from the tax return, so keep filing.

steps.title: Split pension income with a spouse and claim the pension income amount
conditions: Only with a spouse or common-law partner and pension or RRIF income
prepare: Pension, annuity and RRIF income for the year
steps.howTo:
1. Up to half of eligible pension income can be moved to a spouse or common-law partner on Form T1032, filed with both returns each year.
2. From 65, RRIF and annuity income counts; before 65, mainly life annuity payments from a workplace pension plan.
3. The pension income amount gives a federal credit on up to $2,000 of eligible pension income.
4. CPP and OAS cannot be split this way; CPP can be shared through Service Canada instead.
5. This repeats every year with the return.

steps.title: Send in the driver's medical examination report
conditions: Only if you hold a B.C. driver's licence
prepare: An appointment with a doctor or nurse practitioner
The fee the clinic charges; MSP does not cover it
steps.howTo:
1. RoadSafetyBC asks for a Driver's Medical Examination Report at 80, at 85, and every 2 years after that.
2. The doctor or nurse practitioner fills it in and sends it; the clinic sets the fee.
3. RoadSafetyBC only makes contact if it needs more information or a further assessment; a report not sent on time can lead to a licence suspension.
4. Decisions rest on medical fitness to drive, not age alone.

steps.title: Ask the health authority for a home support or long-term care assessment
conditions: Only if daily living at home is getting harder
prepare: Income from the latest notice of assessment, for the fee
steps.howTo:
1. Home support, adult day programs, assisted living and long-term care in B.C. go through the regional health authority's home and community care office.
2. A case manager assesses needs; a doctor, hospital or family member can also make the referral.
3. Client rates for home support and long-term care are based on after-tax income.
4. Age 80 here is only a prompt; ask whenever daily living gets hard.

steps.title: Convert the RRSP to a RRIF or annuity
conditions: Only if you have an RRSP
steps.howTo:
1. By the end of the year you turn 71, choose to withdraw the RRSP, transfer it to a RRIF, or buy an annuity.
2. December 31 of that year is also the last day to contribute to your own RRSP.
3. Direct transfers to a RRIF or annuity have no tax withheld; a withdrawal does.
4. This date is your 71st birthday, a safe point before the December 31 deadline.

steps.title: Take the first RRIF minimum withdrawal
conditions: Only if you have a RRIF
prepare: Minimum amount from the RRIF carrier
Spouse's date of birth, if using their age
steps.howTo:
1. Minimum payments start the year after the RRIF is set up, and continue every year.
2. The carrier sets the minimum from your age at the start of the year; you can elect your spouse's age instead.
3. You can take more than the minimum, but not less.
4. RRIF payments are taxable income in the year received.

title: Retirement · China
summary: Paperwork plan for the basic pension in mainland China from 45 to 80: the rising retirement age and contribution years, flexible retirement, the pension claim, yearly certification, the housing fund, medical insurance and later-life services.
conditions: You are insured in mainland China, in the employee basic pension (职工基本养老保险) or the urban and rural residents' pension
Retirement ages differ for men and women and by original job type; the dates here assume 60, so move them to your own
Women whose original retirement age was 50 now retire between about 50 and 55; their first checks come at 45

steps.title: Check your social insurance contribution record
prepare: Social security card or electronic social security card
A list of employers and cities you paid in, with dates
steps.howTo:
1. Look up your contribution record (参保缴费记录) on the National Social Insurance Public Service Platform (国家社会保险公共服务平台) or the 掌上12333 app, or at the local social insurance office.
2. Compare each year with your work history; gaps and years paid in other cities are easier to fix now than at retirement.
3. If you paid in several places, ask about transferring the pension record (转移接续) so it is counted together.
4. The 14 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Look up your statutory retirement age
prepare: Whether your original retirement age was 50, 55 or 60
steps.howTo:
1. From January 1, 2025, the statutory retirement age (法定退休年龄) rises gradually over 15 years: men from 60 to 63, and women from 50 to 55 or from 55 to 58.
2. For men and women whose original age was 55, it rises 1 month every 4 months; for women whose original age was 50, 1 month every 2 months.
3. The official retirement age calculator on the national platform and 掌上12333 gives your exact age and month from your birth month, sex and original type.
4. Every date in this plan assumes 60; move them to the month the calculator gives.

steps.title: Check you will reach the minimum contribution years
prepare: Years left until your statutory retirement age
steps.howTo:
1. A monthly basic pension needs a minimum number of contribution years, now 15.
2. From January 1, 2030, the minimum rises by 6 months each year until it reaches 20 years; the calculator shows the minimum for your retirement year.
3. If you reach retirement age short of the minimum, you can extend contributions or pay a lump sum as the rules allow.
4. Not financial advice; the local social insurance office can confirm your count.

steps.title: Check your medical insurance years for retirement
conditions: Only if you have employee medical insurance
prepare: The local medical insurance office's rule
steps.howTo:
1. Retirees with enough employee medical insurance years stop paying premiums and keep coverage for life.
2. The minimum number of years is set locally, not nationally; ask the local medical insurance office for its rule.
3. If you will fall short, ask the local medical insurance office (医保局) whether you can keep paying after retirement or pay the gap in one sum.
4. Age 55 here is only a prompt, to leave time to close a gap.

steps.title: Decide on flexible early or late retirement
steps.howTo:
1. Flexible retirement (弹性退休) is voluntary, and employers may not force a choice.
2. Early: once you reach the minimum contribution years, you can retire up to 3 years early, but not below the original age of 60 for men, or 50 or 55 for women. Tell your employer in writing at least 3 months before the date you choose.
3. Late: with your employer's agreement, you can retire up to 3 years late; agree the date in writing at least 1 month ahead.
4. For early retirement, move this step to at least 3 months before your chosen date. Not financial advice.

steps.title: Apply for the basic pension
prepare: Bank account on your social security card for payments
Personnel file (档案) and proof of any special job type, if your employer keeps them
Confirm with HR who submits the claim
steps.howTo:
1. For employees, the employer applies to the social insurance agency for the basic pension (基本养老金) no later than the month of the retirement date.
2. Without an employer, e.g. as a flexible worker, ask the local social insurance office how to apply.
3. The pension starts the month after the approved retirement date.
4. The 30 days is an estimate; this date assumes retirement at 60.

steps.title: Withdraw the housing provident fund
conditions: Only if you have a housing provident fund account
steps.howTo:
1. Retirement is one of the grounds for withdrawing the whole housing provident fund (住房公积金) balance, and the account can be closed at the same time.
2. The fund centre decides within 3 days of accepting the application (as amended from September 20, 2026; check current).
3. Apply online or at the local fund centre; ask how any outstanding provident fund loan is handled.
4. The date is an estimate, once retirement is approved.

steps.title: Complete the yearly pension qualification check
prepare: Smartphone with the 掌上12333 app or the national platform
steps.howTo:
1. Pension recipients confirm their eligibility (领取资格认证) once in each 12-month period, at any time within 12 calendar months of the last one.
2. Face recognition works on the national platform or 掌上12333; people abroad can use the 中国领事 app; older or housebound people can ask for a home visit.
3. Many people are now confirmed automatically by data matching; check the app to see if you are.
4. If the check lapses, payment is suspended until you complete it.

steps.title: Claim the residents' pension at 60
conditions: Only if you have no employee basic pension
steps.howTo:
1. The urban and rural residents' pension (城乡居民养老保险) is paid monthly from age 60 to people who have paid in for at least 15 years in total and get no other state basic pension.
2. It has a basic part set by government and a personal account part; the account balance can be inherited.
3. Apply through the village or community service point, or the local social insurance office.
4. If you also paid into the employee pension, ask how the two records are combined.

steps.title: Make a will and choose a guardian in advance
prepare: Who should decide for you if you cannot
A notary office (公证处) near you
steps.howTo:
1. Without a will, the Civil Code gives the estate first to the spouse, children and parents (Article 1127).
2. A will (遗嘱) can change that; the Civil Code allows handwritten, witnessed, printed, audio or video, and notarised wills.
3. Voluntary guardianship (意定监护) lets an adult choose in writing, in advance, who will be their guardian if they lose capacity.
4. For information only, not legal advice; age 60 here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Check your social insurance record early (original retirement age 50)
conditions: Only for women whose original retirement age was 50
prepare: A list of employers and cities you paid in, with dates
steps.howTo:
1. Women whose original retirement age was 50 now retire between about 50 and 55, depending on birth month; the calculator on the national platform or 掌上12333 gives the exact month.
2. Look up the contribution record now and compare it with your work history; gaps and records in other cities are easier to fix years ahead.
3. The later steps in this plan assume 60; move them to your own dates.

steps.title: Check the minimum contribution years for your retirement date
conditions: Only for women whose original retirement age was 50
prepare: Your statutory retirement month from the calculator
steps.howTo:
1. A monthly basic pension needs 15 contribution years now; from January 1, 2030 the minimum rises by 6 months a year to 20.
2. With retirement only a few years away, a shortfall may mean extending contributions or paying as the rules allow.
3. Not financial advice; the local social insurance office can confirm your count.

steps.title: Apply for chronic and special disease outpatient cover (门诊慢特病认定)
conditions: Only if you have a long-term condition such as high blood pressure, diabetes or another listed illness
steps.howTo:
1. Medical insurance pays more for outpatient care of listed chronic and special diseases (门诊慢特病) once the condition is approved.
2. The list, the approving hospitals and the cover are set locally; many places approve online or at a named hospital.
3. It can be applied for at any age; 60 here is only a prompt.

steps.title: Get the senior citizen card (老年人优待证)
documents: Senior citizen card (老年人优待证) or its electronic version
steps.howTo:
1. From 60, many places issue a senior card for free or reduced fares, park and museum entry and other local benefits; in many cities the ID card alone works.
2. Benefits and the age for each are set locally.
3. Apply at the community or street office, or online.

steps.title: Draw the personal pension (个人养老金领取)
conditions: Only if you have a personal pension account
prepare: Bank holding the personal pension account
steps.howTo:
1. The personal pension (个人养老金) can be drawn once you reach the basic pension retirement age, as a lump sum, in instalments or monthly.
2. Payouts are taxed at 3% and go to your social security card's bank account.
3. Apply through the bank that holds the account.

steps.title: Draw the enterprise or occupational annuity (企业年金 / 职业年金领取)
conditions: Only if you have an enterprise or occupational annuity
prepare: Annuity account details from HR or the plan manager
steps.howTo:
1. An enterprise annuity (企业年金) or occupational annuity (职业年金) pays out after retirement, monthly, in instalments or as a lump sum as the plan allows.
2. Payouts are taxed as income; the choice of method changes the tax.
3. Ask HR or the plan manager how to apply.

steps.title: Book the free yearly health check for people 65 and over
prepare: The community health service centre (社区卫生服务中心) or village clinic
steps.howTo:
1. Under the national basic public health service (国家基本公共卫生服务), residents aged 65 and over get a free health check once a year, with lifestyle, blood and other basic tests.
2. The community or township health centre books it and keeps a health record.
3. It repeats every year.

steps.title: Check long-term care insurance (长期护理保险)
conditions: Only if you live in a city that runs long-term care insurance
prepare: The local long-term care insurance rules
steps.howTo:
1. Long-term care insurance (长期护理保险) pays for care for people who have lost the ability to look after themselves; it runs in pilot cities, usually linked to employee medical insurance.
2. It usually needs an assessment of care needs; the benefits and who is covered are local.
3. Ask the local medical insurance bureau whether your city has it.

steps.title: Driving from 70: yearly health report and the three-ability test (三力测试)
conditions: Only if you drive
documents: Health condition certificate (身体条件证明)
prepare: Health check at a qualified hospital
steps.howTo:
1. From 70, drivers of small cars submit a health condition certificate every year, often online through 交管12123.
2. Drivers of 70 and over also take a test of memory, judgement and reaction (记忆力、判断力、反应力, 三力测试); check current when it is due.
3. The licence classes allowed from 70 are limited, mainly to small cars and motorcycles; check current.

steps.title: Apply for the old-age allowance at 80 (高龄津贴)
steps.howTo:
1. Most provinces pay an old-age allowance (高龄津贴) from 80, some from an earlier or later age; the amount rises with age and is set locally.
2. Apply at the community or street office, or it is paid automatically in some places.
3. Many provinces have extra benefits on the senior card at this age.

steps.title: Sign up for My Service Canada Account
prepare: GCKey, or online banking for a Sign-In Partner
steps.howTo:
1. Register with a GCKey or through a Sign-In Partner (online banking).
2. Identity may be confirmed with a Personal Access Code sent by mail.
3. The account is where CPP and OAS are applied for and tracked.
4. The 14 days is an estimate, to allow for a mailed code.

steps.title: Check your CPP Statement of Contributions
prepare: Notices of assessment for self-employed years
steps.howTo:
1. In My Service Canada Account, open Canada Pension Plan and view contributions and benefit estimates.
2. Compare each year with your T4 slips; report errors straight away with T4s, an employer letter, or a T1 and notice of assessment.
3. It can also be requested by mail.

steps.title: Choose when to start CPP
prepare: Health, other income and work plans
steps.howTo:
1. CPP can start any time from age 60 to 70.
2. Before 65 it drops 0.6% a month, up to 36% less at 60.
3. After 65 it rises 0.7% a month, up to 42% more at 70.
4. There is no gain in waiting past 70.
5. Not financial advice; the Service Canada estimates help compare.

steps.title: Update the will and powers of attorney
documents: Continuing power of attorney for property
Power of attorney for personal care
prepare: Who should decide on money and on care
Beneficiaries on RRSPs, pensions and insurance
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario has two powers of attorney: a continuing power of attorney for property and one for personal care.
2. Without an attorney for property, family, including a spouse, cannot automatically step in; they may need to go to court.
3. You can make one yourself for free or with a lawyer.
4. Not legal advice; age 60 here is only a prompt; review after any big change.

steps.title: Apply for the CPP retirement pension
prepare: Children's details, for the child-rearing provision
steps.howTo:
1. Apply up to 12 months before the chosen start date, in My Service Canada Account.
2. Online applications get a decision by mail within 28 days; paper within 120 days.
3. This date assumes a start at 65; move it to about 6 months before the start age you chose.

steps.title: Watch for the OAS enrolment letter
prepare: Check the mail around your 64th birthday
steps.howTo:
1. Most people get a letter around their 64th birthday saying they are enrolled automatically for OAS at 65.
2. OAS needs at least 10 years living in Canada after age 18 (20 years if living abroad).
3. You can delay OAS to as late as 70: it rises 0.6% a month, up to 36% at 70. If you qualify for GIS, there is no gain in waiting.
4. From 75, OAS is 10% higher; the increase is automatic.

steps.title: Apply for Old Age Security
conditions: Only if no enrolment letter came a month after your 64th birthday
steps.howTo:
1. If a month has passed since your 64th birthday with no letter, contact Service Canada or apply.
2. Online applications open once you are at least 1 month past your 64th birthday, in My Service Canada Account.
3. The 30 days is an estimate.

steps.title: Check the Guaranteed Income Supplement
conditions: Only if your income is low
steps.howTo:
1. GIS is for people 65 or older who get OAS and have a low income.
2. Service Canada enrols most people automatically if it has their information.
3. Unfiled taxes can stop or reduce GIS.
4. GIS does not increase if you delay OAS.

steps.title: Start using the Ontario Drug Benefit
conditions: Only if you live in Ontario
prepare: Bring the health card to the pharmacy
steps.howTo:
1. You join the Ontario Drug Benefit automatically on the first day of the month after you turn 65; a letter comes about 3 months before.
2. Lower-income seniors can apply to the Seniors Co-Payment Program to pay less.

steps.title: Apply to the Ontario Seniors Dental Care Program
conditions: Only if you live in Ontario, your income is under the program limit and you have no other dental benefits apart from the CDCP
steps.howTo:
1. For Ontario residents 65 or older with low income and no other dental benefits apart from the Canadian Dental Care Plan.
2. Apply online, or on paper from the local public health unit; income is checked from your tax return.
3. Coverage ends every July 31 and most people are renewed automatically if they keep filing taxes.

steps.title: Check income against the OAS recovery tax threshold
prepare: Expected CPP, workplace pension and RRSP or RRIF income
steps.howTo:
1. OAS is reduced by 15% of net income above a yearly threshold (a little over $90,000 at review; check current), and stops at a higher level.
2. The timing of CPP, RRSP withdrawals, RRIF conversion and pension splitting all change net income in the OAS years.
3. Income in one year sets the recovery tax taken from monthly OAS from July of the following year.
4. Not financial advice; the date here is only a prompt before the CPP and OAS start.

steps.title: Replace workplace health and dental benefits at retirement
conditions: Only if you had health or dental benefits through work
prepare: Drugs, dental and travel cover you use now
Whether the employer offers retiree benefits
steps.howTo:
1. Workplace health and dental plans often end on the last day of work or soon after, unless the employer offers retiree benefits.
2. Many group insurers offer a conversion plan without medical questions if applied for within a short window after coverage ends, often 30 to 60 days; check the plan booklet.
3. Individual plans with medical questions are another route, and travel medical cover usually needs its own policy.
4. Moving this date to the real retirement date keeps the window in view.

steps.title: Apply for the Canadian Dental Care Plan
conditions: Only if you have no dental insurance and your adjusted family net income is under $90,000
prepare: Tax returns filed for you and any spouse
Check that no retiree or pension plan still gives dental cover
steps.howTo:
1. The Canadian Dental Care Plan is for residents with no access to dental insurance, an adjusted family net income under $90,000, and tax returns filed by you and any spouse; there is no upper age limit.
2. Dental cover still available through a pension or retiree plan usually rules it out, even if you do not take it.
3. Apply online or by phone through Service Canada; co-payments depend on income.
4. Eligibility is confirmed every year from the tax return, so keep filing.

steps.title: Split pension income with a spouse and claim the pension income amount
conditions: Only with a spouse or common-law partner and pension or RRIF income
prepare: Pension, annuity and RRIF income for the year
steps.howTo:
1. Up to half of eligible pension income can be moved to a spouse or common-law partner on Form T1032, filed with both returns each year.
2. From 65, RRIF and annuity income counts; before 65, mainly life annuity payments from a workplace pension plan.
3. The pension income amount gives a federal credit on up to $2,000 of eligible pension income.
4. CPP and OAS cannot be split this way; CPP can be shared through Service Canada instead.
5. This repeats every year with the return.

steps.title: Check the Ontario GAINS top-up
conditions: Only if you get the Guaranteed Income Supplement
steps.howTo:
1. GAINS, the Ontario seniors income top-up, adds to the income of low-income Ontario seniors who get OAS and GIS.
2. There is no application when OAS and GIS are already paid; Ontario works it out from Service Canada information.
3. It also asks for 10 years in Canada and 12 months living in Ontario; payments run from July to June and are paid monthly.
4. Check the current maximum on ontario.ca.

steps.title: Claim the Ontario Senior Homeowners' Property Tax Grant
conditions: Only if you own and live in your home in Ontario
documents: Property tax bills for the year
prepare: Property tax paid on your principal residence
steps.howTo:
1. Owners 65 or older who pay property tax on their Ontario principal residence and have low to moderate income can get up to $500 a year.
2. It is claimed on Form ON-BEN with the income tax return, alongside the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit.
3. This repeats every year with the return; move the date to April 30.

steps.title: Renew the driver's licence under the senior driver program
conditions: Only if you hold an Ontario driver's licence
prepare: The renewal notice mailed before your 80th birthday
Glasses or contacts for the vision test
steps.howTo:
1. From 80, Ontario drivers renew every 2 years through the senior driver licence renewal program; the notice comes by mail before the birthday.
2. It usually includes a vision test, a driver record review and short in-class screening exercises; a road test or medical report may also be asked for. Check the current steps on ontario.ca.
3. Book a DriveTest or ServiceOntario appointment early, before the licence expires on the birthday.

steps.title: Contact Ontario Health atHome about home care or long-term care
conditions: Only if daily living at home is getting harder
steps.howTo:
1. Ontario Health atHome arranges home care and assesses eligibility for long-term care homes; call 310-2222 or ask a doctor or hospital for a referral.
2. A care coordinator assesses needs and helps choose long-term care homes and join their waitlists.
3. Long-term care has a set accommodation charge; a rate reduction may be available on low income.
4. Age 80 here is only a prompt; ask whenever daily living gets hard.

steps.title: Convert the RRSP to a RRIF or annuity
conditions: Only if you have an RRSP
steps.howTo:
1. By the end of the year you turn 71, choose to withdraw the RRSP, transfer it to a RRIF, or buy an annuity.
2. December 31 of that year is also the last day to contribute to your own RRSP.
3. Direct transfers to a RRIF or annuity have no tax withheld; a withdrawal does.
4. This date is your 71st birthday, a safe point before the December 31 deadline.

steps.title: Take the first RRIF minimum withdrawal
conditions: Only if you have a RRIF
prepare: Minimum amount from the RRIF carrier
Spouse's date of birth, if using their age
steps.howTo:
1. Minimum payments start the year after the RRIF is set up, and continue every year.
2. The carrier sets the minimum from your age at the start of the year; you can elect your spouse's age instead.
3. You can take more than the minimum, but not less.
4. RRIF payments are taxable income in the year received.

summary: Paperwork plan for hosting relatives or friends from abroad, from checking whether they need a visa or eTA to the invitation letter, arrival, extensions and leaving on time.
conditions: You live in Canada and are hosting someone coming from abroad
They are visiting, not moving to Canada for work, study or permanent residence
The date is the day they arrive in Canada
